items.lead: Opens related sections of content as they are needed.

docs.name: Accordion
docs.summary: A list of disclosures. Compound: Item, Trigger, Panel. Single-open by default, with a card variant and a height-animated panel that can hold anything, including form controls.

anatomy.notes: The list. Owns the variant and heading level, and passes both by context so every part cannot be told twice.

One disclosure. The ONLY part the variant changes: card gives it a raised tile, its 8px vertical padding and — in the card variant only — the HOVER fill, so the whole tile lights rather than a rectangle inset inside it. Plain gives it nothing.
The heading element the trigger sits inside, at headingLevel. Rendered by Trigger — it carries nothing of its own.
The button. Holds the icon slot, the label lane and the chevron.
The title lane. Clamped to one line so a long title cannot push the chevron out of the row.
The chevron. aria-hidden — aria-expanded already says the same thing. Rotates from the trigger's state via a group variant.
The animating element. Clips, and takes its height from the behaviour layer's measurement.
Carries the padding. Padding on the animating element would be added to every intermediate height and the content would jump at the end.

docs.composition:
Accordion                       variant, headingLevel, value/defaultValue, isMultiple
└─ Accordion.Item               value, isDisabled
   ├─ Accordion.Trigger         icon? — renders the heading AND the button
   └─ Accordion.Panel           any content, including form controls

variant.notes: Only the ITEM differs: card adds rounded-md, bg-elevated, py-sm and the hover fill. Header, trigger and panel are identical in both, which is why this travels by context rather than being threaded through every part. The hover fill is the one place the variant reaches the trigger too — plain paints it on the trigger's own rounded-sm box, card paints the tile and the trigger paints nothing.

headingLevel.notes: The element each trigger's heading renders as. A prop with no clever default, for the same reason Card's is: the right level depends on what surrounds the accordion and a component cannot see that. 3 is the common case, not a guess about yours.

value.notes: Controlled open set. An ARRAY in both modes including single, where it holds at most one value. Restated rather than re-exported — no behaviour-layer type may appear in a public signature (§9).

onValueChange.notes: Fires with the full open set. The behaviour layer hands back a second event-details argument; it is deliberately not forwarded, so nothing third-party reaches a consumer's callback signature.

isMultiple.notes: Allow more than one panel open. Off is what the sheet draws and what the behaviour layer defaults to — asserted, not assumed.

isDisabled.notes: Disables the whole list. See a11y: this is aria-disabled, not the native attribute.

Item.value.notes: Identifies the item in value/defaultValue. Defaults to the item's index when omitted.

Trigger.icon.notes: Slot: the leading mark, never wrapped (§3). The sheet puts an icon here in two rows and a numbered step badge in the third. The component only reserves the 16px lane — griddy renders width/height="24" as attributes, so an unsized slot would ship 24px.

do: Set headingLevel to whatever is correct beneath the surrounding heading — the default is a common case, not a guess about your page.
Put real content in the panel, including form controls; the panel is a normal container and its height follows what is inside it.
Give each Item a stable value when you control the open set; the index fallback shifts if the list reorders.
Use variant="card" when items need to read as separate objects, plain when they are one list.
Expect a card to inset its content 20px on all four sides — pinned by design/paper/specs/accordion.geometry.json and measured in the geometry browser test, not asserted from the class list.
dont: Do not set a height on the panel; it is measured from the content and a fixed value would clip whatever does not fit.
Do not use disabled: or enabled: variants on the trigger — the behaviour layer marks it aria-disabled and keeps it focusable, so those match nothing.
Do not put padding on the panel itself; it belongs on the inner container, or every intermediate height gains it and the content jumps.
Do not rely on arrow keys to move between headers — they are not implemented. See knownGaps.
Do not restyle a card Item's padding to close the gap between rows; the item's py-sm is one of the three paddings that add up to the 20px lane, and the geometry test measures the sum.

a11y.role: A heading per row containing a button, each controlling its panel (the APG accordion pattern).

keyboard.does: Moves to the next trigger, and into an open panel's own controls.
Toggles the panel. Native — the trigger is a real button.
Toggles the panel.
NOTHING. Optional in the APG pattern and not implemented by the behaviour layer — see knownGaps.

a11y.labelling: Each trigger sits inside a real heading at headingLevel, so the list is navigable by heading. aria-expanded reports the row's state, aria-controls points at the panel and the panel points back with aria-labelledby — asserted in both directions.
a11y.disabled: isDisabled sets aria-disabled and KEEPS the trigger focusable (tabindex 0) rather than using the native attribute. That is deliberate: a control removed from the tab order cannot tell anyone why it is unavailable. Styling therefore hangs off aria-disabled variants.
a11y.landmarks: Each panel is a role=region LANDMARK labelled by its trigger, which the behaviour layer applies unconditionally. Two panels whose triggers READ THE SAME therefore produce two landmarks with the same accessible name, and axe fails that as landmark-unique. It is a COMPOSITION rule the component cannot enforce — it cannot see the rest of your page — and it bit this component's own Matrix story, which rendered three copies of one FAQ. Keep trigger text distinct across every accordion on a page. The APG also warns against landmark proliferation for long accordions; see knownGaps.
a11y.indicator: The chevron is aria-hidden. It repeats what aria-expanded already says, and motion is never the only channel — the panel's presence is the static cue.

contrastPairs.role: a trigger label on the plain variant
a trigger label on a card
panel copy on the plain variant
panel copy on a card
the chevron on a card
a trigger label on a HOVERED card — the fill is the item's, so the whole tile's ink sits on this ground, panel copy included
panel copy inside an open card while its trigger is hovered
the chevron on a hovered card
the keyboard focus ring

contrastPairs.why: WCAG 1.4.3 exempts disabled controls, and a disabled row has to READ as unavailable — holding it to 4.5:1 would make it indistinguishable from an available one, which is the real failure.

forwarding.ref: Item forwards to the item element, Trigger to the button, Panel to the animating element. Trigger's ref reaches the BUTTON rather than the heading, because the button is the thing a caller wants to focus or measure.
forwarding.className: Each part takes its own className. Panel's lands on the INNER container, not the animating element, so a consumer restyling the content cannot accidentally break the height transition.
forwarding.rest: Not spread. The parts take an explicit prop list rather than passing native props through, which keeps behaviour-layer props from being reachable by accident.

needsDesign: CLOSED. Resting, hover, focus and disabled are now drawn on the sheet's `Accordion Card States` section. Hover is --ui-bg-hover on the ITEM, which is the review's finding: a fill on the trigger is inset 8px by the header's px-sm and 8px by the item's own padding, so a hovered card showed a smaller rounded rectangle floating inside it.

The card's hover fills the tile while its FOCUS ring still hugs the trigger — an inset rounded-sm box, 2px offset, drawn on the sheet. That is correct in ARIA terms (the button is what receives focus) but the two indicators now have different shapes on the same control. Decide whether the card variant's ring should hug the tile instead; if it should, it needs a radius and an offset chosen against --ui-radius-md rather than reusing the trigger's.

The sheet's leading icon frame carries a raw 8px gap and an 8px radius, both off the token layer and both inert (it holds one 16px glyph and nothing to round). Harmless as drawn, but it means the frame is not the icon lane it appears to be.

The numbered step badge in the Rich Content row is drawn as a 20px --ui-bg-sunken circle and exists nowhere else in the system. It is passed through the icon slot here, so it is the caller's element — if numbered steps recur it wants a name of its own rather than being rebuilt per call site.
No divider between items in the plain variant, and no drawn state for the last item's bottom edge. At gap-xs the rows read as one block; confirm that is intended rather than a missing rule.

The sheet is light only. Paper cannot hold a light-dark() pair, so the hover ramp was checked against the resolver instead: elevated #F6F3F0 → hover #EDE8E3 in light and #2A2724 → #2E2B28 in dark (1.15 → 1.22 against the surface since the 2026-11-03 warm-ink ramp), which moves one direction in each scheme. A dark half of this sheet would make that legible to a reader rather than to a script.
knownGaps: The two variants differ by more than a fill, and the difference is the whole choice. PLAIN has no border, no dividers and NO hover — grouping is spacing alone, which is CONVENTIONS' own rule that a rule is usually a spacing problem solved with ink. CARD is a radius-md tile on bg-elevated whose hover moves the WHOLE tile to bg-hover, never the trigger. So a surface with several PRESSABLE section headers wants card: plain gives the pointer nothing to answer. Confirmed against the sheet's own Card States section 2026-08-25, after Sheet's record panel was first drawn as plain with invented hairlines between the sections.

NO ARROW-KEY NAVIGATION between headers. `loopFocus` is accepted as a prop by the behaviour layer but no key handler exists — confirmed in its source and then in the browser. Arrow keys are OPTIONAL in the APG accordion pattern so this conforms, and Tab does move between triggers. It is pinned by a test so it is not rediscovered as a bug.

A closed panel is not mounted at all, so its content is invisible to find-in-page and to a consumer querying the DOM. The behaviour layer offers hiddenUntilFound and keepMounted for exactly this; neither is exposed yet because neither is drawn, and hiddenUntilFound changes what find-in-page does on the page.
The panel animates height only. Content that reflows while open — an image loading, a textarea being dragged — will not re-measure, because the measurement is taken at the transition.
No horizontal orientation. The behaviour layer supports it; nothing draws it.

The trigger's hover fill is NOT guarded by `@media (hover: hover)`, unlike every other hover in this library. Read out of the compiled stylesheet: a plain `hover:bg-hover` emits inside that media query, but composing it as `not-aria-disabled:hover:bg-hover` — which is required here, because the behaviour layer marks a disabled trigger aria-disabled rather than natively disabled — emits the rule bare. Reordering to `hover:not-aria-disabled:` does not restore it either. The consequence is touch-only and small: a tapped row keeps its hover fill until the next tap, where other components drop theirs. Kept as-is because the alternatives (a separate aria-disabled override racing on equal specificity, or pointer-events-none, which §10 forbids) are worse than the artifact.

Every panel is a role=region landmark, applied by the behaviour layer and not currently suppressible through this wrapper. The APG advises AGAINST the region role once panels are numerous, precisely because it proliferates landmarks — a 12-row FAQ adds 12 of them to the page's landmark list. Two consequences worth knowing before that becomes a problem: duplicate trigger text across a page fails axe's landmark-unique (see a11y.landmarks), and there is no opt-out here yet because none is drawn and removing a role the behaviour layer sets deliberately is not a change to make casually.
docs.motion: The chevron rotates 180 degrees and the panel's height animates between 0 and `--accordion-panel-height` — the measurement Base UI publishes, because `height: auto` cannot be transitioned and a constant would clip whatever does not fit. Trigger background and chevron at --ui-duration-fast, the panel at --ui-duration-base, both --ui-ease-out. `rotate` and `height` are named individually: Tailwind v4 writes `rotate-*` as the standalone `rotate` property, so a list naming `transform` would animate nothing.

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

A record-panel composition is drawn on the Sheet sheet: the variant that pushed this component past a navigation drawer. A row in a table opened beside it — Sheet.Header carrying Close plus record pagination and an open-the-full-record control, then Sheet.Body holding an identity block, a completeness hero, and an Accordion of field groups at size md. Nothing in it is a new part, which is the point: it exercises the size axis and the scrolling body the same day they shipped. Four decisions are recorded on the sheet with their evidence. The band stays CHROME and the identity scrolls, checked against the field rather than asserted — of six CRM detail panels surveyed on Mobbin, four pin one compact row and put the identity in the scrolling body (Twenty, Apollo, Lightfield, HubSpot) and one scrolls everything (folk); pinning a taller identity block is the minority pattern, and it would also miss the body's 16px lane by the 8 the band is inset. The hero is a COMPOSITION, not a component: Banner is the nearest thing and does not fit, being items-center with one text slot where this stacks a label row, a Progress at size sm, a consequence sentence and two controls. Field rows sit at px-xs inside the panel's px-sm, which is 4 + 8 = 12 and therefore the trigger's p-md exactly, so a group name and its fields share one lane; an empty value is an em dash in --ui-text-placeholder because a missing field and an unexamined one are different things and the meter above counts on the difference. And the chips are two different components that look alike: Disciplines and Tools are Badge neutral md (labels), while the hero's missing-field chips are Button secondary sm shape-full (controls) at 24px, which meets SC 2.5.8 exactly where Badge sm at 22px would not. CORRECTED on review: the field groups were first drawn as Accordion's PLAIN variant with hairline dividers between them, and both halves of that were wrong. A standard accordion has no border and no dividers — grouping is spacing alone, which is CONVENTIONS' own rule that a rule is a spacing problem solved with ink — so the hairlines were an invention. And plain has no hover either: the bg-hover step belongs to CARD, on the whole tile rather than the trigger, exactly as the Accordion sheet's Card States section labels it. Six pressable section headers on one surface is the case that needs it, so the panel is card now, radius-md tiles on bg-elevated at the root's own gap-xs, with Disciplines drawn hovered. That in turn took the fill off the hero: bg-elevated was the obvious answer and the card variant already owns it on the same surface, so the hero sits on the panel ground at the Body's own inset, where its text lane and the tiles' outer edges agree. The needsDesign row filed against Accordion is withdrawn — plain is not missing anything — and the two variants' real difference is recorded in accordion.doc.ts knownGaps instead: plain has no border, no dividers and no hover, card is a tile whose WHOLE surface answers the pointer, and a surface with pressable section headers wants card.

Two design-review findings against the card variant, both of them arithmetic nobody could see in the source. FIRST: the hover fill belonged to the TRIGGER, which is inset 8px horizontally by the header's px-sm and 8px vertically by the item's py-xs -- so hovering a card painted a smaller rounded rectangle floating inside it rather than lighting the card. The fill moves to the ITEM, where the tile's own rounded-md bounds it. It hangs off `:has([data-slot=accordion-trigger]:hover)` rather than the item's own :hover, deliberately: an open card can hold a form, and tinting the tile because the pointer is in a text field claims that pixel toggles the panel. The guard is `not-data-disabled:`, the item's own attribute -- the behaviour layer sets it alongside the trigger's aria-disabled, so no attribute-value match is needed. The trigger keeps the fill ONLY in the plain variant, where there is no tile to light, and its transition-[background-color] goes with it: a transition on a property nothing changes reads in review as a decision and animates nothing. SECOND: the card's content sat 20px from the left and right edges and 16px from the top and bottom, because three components author that lane and only two of them are vertical -- header/panel px-sm (8) plus trigger/inner p-md (12) horizontally, against item py-xs (4) plus p-md (12) vertically. py-xs becomes py-sm and every side reads 20. RATCHET: the item had no geometry spec, so the asymmetry could only ever be found by eye. design/paper/specs/accordion.geometry.json now carries the closed and open card as measured cases (uniform-inset, track-is-the-sum-of-its-parts), with inset-is-declared and concentric-radius recorded as NOT declared and why -- the horizontal inset has a second, intended author, and an unpainted radius is not a fact about the design. Seven of the eight new assertions fail against the previous component, checked by reverting it.

migration.manual: A card row is 8px taller than before (py-xs to py-sm), so a list of them is taller by 8px per item; nothing about the API changes. If you were overriding the trigger's hover through className on variant="card", it no longer paints there -- style the Item instead, or the fill will sit under the tile's own. The plain variant is untouched.

changes.summary: check:motion joins the gate list, and every animating component now documents its motion. The gate rejects a literal duration or easing in registry/ (a discipline that was already perfect — zero hard-coded durations across 26 files — and had nothing keeping it that way), transition-all (CONVENTIONS section 6 has said this since the beginning and nothing enforced it), a keyframe with no reduced-motion guard, and an animating component with no top-level motion: note in its doc. It reads lib recipes alongside components as check:overlays does, so Header's motion is found in @/lib/chrome-control where it actually lives rather than reported as absent. 27 doc files gain a motion: note describing what moves, what drives it and what reduced motion does to it; Sheet's and ImageUpload's existing notes are PROMOTED out of a11y to the top level, where Button already had its, because motion is a description of what a component does rather than solely an accessibility concern and a field meaning one thing at two depths stops being findable. ImageUpload's note is corrected while being promoted: it credited the token layer with stopping its spinner, and what actually stops it is the motion-safe: variant. Two findings are recorded in the notes rather than fixed: Sidebar's collapsible section snaps via the hidden attribute where Accordion animates the identical interaction against Base UI's published height, and Banner reaches for transition-colors where the rest of the library enumerates properties. No component's rendered motion changes; no .tsx is touched.

migration.manual: Documentation only — every change is inside a *.doc.ts, and no component's classes or rendered motion moved. If you consume the doc files and read `a11y.motion`, it has moved to the top-level `motion` key on Sheet and ImageUpload; Button was already there and the other 27 are new.

changes.summary: Accordion, from the 'Component --- Accordion' sheet. Compound: Item, Trigger, Panel, with plain and card variants and a panel whose height animates. Unusually, the DESIGN was drawn against the behaviour layer's anatomy -- the sheet's layers are named Accordion Root / Item / Header / Trigger / Panel / Panel Inner Container, which are Base UI's parts exactly -- so the DOM here is that structure one-for-one and every value on the sheet has a single place to land. Trigger renders the Header AND the button as one part, because the header carries nothing of its own; both data-slots are present so the DOM still matches the sheet layer for layer. WHY NOT <details>/<summary>, since the platform does a real share of this: summary is not a button and its ARIA mapping is inconsistent across screen readers, while the sheet's row is a heading CONTAINING a control; the panel height has to animate, and the behaviour layer publishes --accordion-panel-height where the native route needs ::details-content plus interpolate-size (one engine today); single/multiple has to be driven from state, where `name` is markup-level; and hiddenUntilFound exists for find-in-page. NOT one of the reasons, though it was the first one written down: arrow-key navigation between headers does NOT exist -- `loopFocus` is accepted as a prop and no key handler is implemented, confirmed in the source and then in the browser. Arrow keys are OPTIONAL in the APG accordion pattern so Tab-only conforms; the claim was removed and the actual behaviour is pinned by a test rather than left to be rediscovered as a bug. Three things the behaviour layer does that a wrapper must not assume away, each found by testing rather than by reading: `multiple` defaults to false (which is what the sheet draws); a disabled trigger is marked aria-disabled and KEPT FOCUSABLE rather than given the native attribute, so `disabled:` and `enabled:` variants match nothing and both shipped here as dead classes until the test caught them; and the chevron's rotation has to hang off the TRIGGER's data-panel-open through a group variant, since a child never has that attribute itself. headingLevel is a prop with no guessed default, for the same reason Card's is. onValueChange is re-wrapped so the behaviour layer's second event-details argument never reaches a consumer's signature.

migration.manual: New item, nothing to migrate. Two notes for anyone extending it. `@base-ui/react/accordion` was added to optimizeDeps.include in apps/storybook/vitest.config.ts -- the list must grow with every new behaviour-layer subpath or the first run after adding a story flakes. And do not reach for `disabled:`/`enabled:` variants on the trigger: the behaviour layer uses aria-disabled and keeps the control focusable, so style it with aria-disabled variants.

items.name: aspect-ratio
items.title: AspectRatio
items.lead: Keeps media in a predictable frame as the layout changes.

docs.lead: Keeps media in a predictable frame as the layout changes.
docs.name: AspectRatio
docs.summary: A media frame whose height comes from its width. Six named ratios from the sheet — square, story, portrait, landscape, card, screen — over a recessed well, clipped to the soft radius. Sizes and crops a child from the outside, so the call site is just src and alt.

anatomy.notes: The only node. Owns the ratio, the radius, the clip, the well, className and the ref. Width-driven: it takes its column and the ratio supplies the height.

docs.composition: AspectRatio ├─ ratio? "square" | "story" | "portrait" | "landscape" | "card" | "screen" └─ children the media — typically a bare

ratio.notes: 1:1, 9:16, 3:4, 4:3, 1.586:1 and 16:9 — the sheet's six rows, in its order. A vocabulary rather than a number (§2): 'story' means the same shape wherever it is written, and nobody has to remember which way round 9/16 goes. Anything outside the six goes through className — `aspect-[21/9]` displaces the default cleanly, because tailwind-merge classifies both in the aspect-ratio group.

children.notes: The media. A child is sized and cropped from the outside (size-full, object-cover) rather than wrapped, so the call site writes src and alt and nothing else. Anything that is not an img is left alone.

do: Put a bare inside; the frame sizes and crops it.
Let the frame take its width from the column it sits in — that is what a ratio box is for.
Reach for className with an arbitrary aspect utility when the shape is genuinely outside the six.
Pass alt="" for a decorative image rather than omitting it.
dont: Do not wrap the image in a sizing div — the frame already does it, and two sizing layers is how object-fit stops applying.
Do not give the frame a fixed height; the ratio owns the height and a height would silently win.
Do not use it for a 48px attachment tile — that is Thumbnail, which adds the remove control and the stack.

a11y.role: none — a plain div. The frame is presentation; the media inside it carries its own semantics.
a11y.name: None of its own. An child carries the alt text, which is where an accessible name for a picture belongs.

contrastPairs.why: The well behind the media, measured 1.22:1 light / 1.50:1 dark (on the 2026-11-03 warm-ink ramp sunken is a fill above the page in dark, not a recess). It is not a boundary anything depends on identifying: once an image has loaded it is invisible, and when one has not the frame communicates nothing that the missing picture does not already communicate. Declared rather than omitted so the number is visible — a well this quiet against the page is worth a designer knowing about, and it is in needsDesign.

forwarding.ref: Goes to the frame — the only node, and not a form control, so the §5 default applies.
forwarding.className: Lands on the frame. Because it merges last it is also the escape hatch for a ratio outside the six, and for turning the well or the radius off.
forwarding.rest: Native div props go to the frame.

needsDesign: The AspectRatio sheet draws its frames with no fill, while the Image Thumbnail sheet draws the same frame over --ui-bg-sunken. Shipped WITH the well, because a frame that clips shows the page through it until the image loads and the two sheets should not disagree about one frame. Confirm.
The 'card' row is labelled 1.586:1 and drawn 304x192, which is 1.583:1. Shipped at the label, since 1.586 is the ID-1 card ratio and 1.583 is what a whole-pixel artboard could reach. Confirm.
No loading, empty or broken-media state is drawn. The well is the whole of the fallback today; a frame that has failed to load looks identical to one that is still trying.
No hover or focus state is drawn, and a media frame is very often a link or a button (it opens the asset). Nothing here is interactive; a consumer wrapping one gets the wrapper's states.
knownGaps: The frame is `w-full`, so it needs a parent with a resolved width. Inside a shrink-to-fit parent — a bare flex or inline-block, and Storybook's docs cells — `w-full` is circular and collapses to the content, which for an with no intrinsic size is nothing. Every story here wraps the frame in a fixed width for exactly this reason. If a frame renders at zero, look at its parent before looking at the component.
The ratio vocabulary is closed. An arbitrary shape is reachable only through className, which works but is not type-checked — `aspect-[16/10]` and `aspect-[16-10]` are equally valid to the compiler.
Only a direct child is sized from the outside. A

migration.manual: New item — nothing to migrate. `npx shadcn add @bydiorama/aspect-ratio`; it pulls in the `cn` lib item and expects react as a peer.

items.title: Avatar
items.lead: Represents a person or team, with an image or their initials.

docs.lead: Represents a person or team, with an image or their initials.
docs.name: Avatar
docs.summary: A person or entity as a photo or their initials, in two shapes and three sizes, with an optional status dot. Avatar.Group stacks several with an overflow counter.

anatomy.notes: The outermost node. Owns the box, className and the ref, and is the positioning context for the status dot. It does NOT clip.

The clipped tile: well and radius. Everything that must take the radius lives inside it. It carries NO edge — a lone avatar has nothing behind it to separate from, and the seam between stacked avatars is the group's job.
A real , so alt text exists and a broken URL degrades to it.
The abbreviation. aria-hidden — the full name is exposed separately.
The dot. aria-hidden; statusLabel carries the meaning. A sibling of the frame, not a child, because the frame clips.

The stack. Applies BOTH the 4px overlap and the seam from the container rather than by rewriting children — the seam is an offset box-shadow on every child but the first, so it lands on the avatar beneath and never on the ground.
The '+N' tile. Deliberately the same tile as an avatar with no photo, and a child of the group like any other, so it gets its seam from the same rule.

docs.composition:
Avatar
├─ name          string (required) — alt text, and the source of the initials
├─ src?          string — a photo; omit for initials
├─ initials?     string — override the derived pair
├─ status?       "success" | "neutral" | "danger"
└─ statusLabel   string — REQUIRED whenever status is set

Avatar.Group
├─ children      Avatar elements, as direct siblings
├─ max?          number — show this many, the rest become "+N"
└─ overflowLabel string — REQUIRED whenever max is set

name.notes: Required in both forms: it is the image's alt text and, without an image, the source the initials are derived from. An avatar with no name is decoration wearing a person's face.

src.notes: A photo. Omit for the initials form — the two are a discriminated union, so `initials` and `src` cannot both be passed.

initials.notes: Override the derived pair — non-Latin names, mononyms, brand marks. Only available in the initials form.

size.notes: 48 / 32 / 24px. md is the sheet's size verbatim; lg and sm are derived from the same scale so avatars match the control heights they sit beside.

shape.notes: Button's two words for the same two shapes (§2), and the two the sheet's own layers are named after. The soft radius per size is Button's soft radius per size, so a row of both is concentric. RENAMED from circle|rounded — see the ledger.

status.notes: A dot on the corner. Intent vocabulary, as everywhere else. The fills are the intent ROLES rather than the sheet's values — see needsDesign for the two the sheet got wrong.

statusLabel.notes: REQUIRED by the type whenever status is set, the same shape isIconOnly uses for aria-label. A dot is colour and position only, so on its own it tells a screen-reader user nothing — WCAG 1.4.1 exactly. Rendered sr-only next to the name so the two are announced together.

max.notes: Avatar.Group only. How many to show before the rest become a '+N' tile. Counts DIRECT children, so a component that returns three avatars counts as one — pass them as siblings.

overflowLabel.notes: Avatar.Group only, REQUIRED whenever max is set. '+4' is a glyph and a number; a screen reader needs the sentence. A prop rather than a derived string — there is no i18n runtime here (§9) and pluralisation is not guessable.

cssVars.name: --ui-avatar-ring-color
cssVars.notes: The colour of the two things that still paint an edge: the seam between stacked avatars, and the status dot's ring. It used to govern a full-perimeter hairline on EVERY avatar — which is what shadcn, MUI, Atlassian and Flowbite all ship, and which is wrong on any ground but one (MUI has it on file as #21700). It no longer does: the frame carries no edge, the seam is painted only on the leading edge of a stacked child where it lands on the avatar beneath, and neither reaches the ground. Rebinding is therefore rarely needed — do it on the CONTAINER (`style={{ "--ui-avatar-ring-color": "var(--ui-bg-elevated)" }}`) when you want the seam to read as a cut through the stack on a non-surface ground. Declared as a var() fallback rather than as a declaration on the avatar, so an ancestor's binding wins.

do: Always pass the full name, even with a photo — it is the alt text.
Drop an avatar on any ground you like — a card, a menu panel, a table row, a photograph. It carries no edge of its own, so there is nothing to reconcile.
Pass statusLabel with every status; the type will insist, and the reason is that a colour is not a message.
Pass Avatar children to Avatar.Group as direct siblings, and give the group the same size and shape the children carry.
Use initials for brand marks and mononyms rather than faking a two-word name.
dont: Do not pass initials as name; the accessible name must be the full name.
Do not use the disabled ink for initials — it measures 1.76:1 on the well. Initials identify a person and must clear AA.
Do not put anything inside the frame that must escape the radius; the frame clips, which is why the status dot is a sibling.
Do not wrap Avatar.Group's children to space them — the overlap comes from the container so slot contents are never rewritten (§3).

Do not put a ring back on the avatar to 'separate it from the page'. Nothing is behind a lone avatar; a ring there can only ever be a claim about the ground, and that claim is what every library in this space gets wrong.

a11y.role: img (native, when src is present) / plain text otherwise
a11y.name: The `name` prop. With a photo it is the alt text; without one, the visible initials are aria-hidden and the full name is rendered in an sr-only span, so a screen reader announces the person rather than spelling out 'M V'.
a11y.status: The dot is aria-hidden and statusLabel is rendered sr-only inside the same element as the name, so the two are announced as one thing. The label is type-required, not documented — colour alone would fail WCAG 1.4.1.
a11y.group: The counter's '+N' glyph is aria-hidden and overflowLabel is announced instead. The group is a plain container with no role: each avatar already carries its own name, and a role=group with no accessible name adds a landmark that says nothing.

contrastPairs.role: initials on the well — the pair the component actually renders
the success dot against its ring, at the ring's default colour
the neutral dot against its ring, at the ring's default colour
the danger dot against its ring, at the ring's default colour

contrastPairs.why: The 1.5px SEAM between two overlapping avatars, against the initials well it most often lands on — 1.19:1 light / 1.41:1 dark (the sunken fill sits above the surface on the 2026-11-03 warm-ink ramp). Decorative rather than a boundary anything depends on identifying: a photo avatar's own fill separates it, and the stack reads as a stack from the offset alone. Declared rather than omitted so the number is visible; a seam this quiet is worth a designer knowing about, and it is in needsDesign. Rebinding --ui-avatar-ring-color moves this pair and the dots' 3:1 floor above with it, which is why the property takes a surface ROLE and not an arbitrary colour.

a11y.imageFallback: A broken src degrades to the alt text rather than an empty box, because the image is a real and not a background.

forwarding.ref: Goes to the outermost node — Avatar is not a form control, so the §5 default applies.
forwarding.className: Lands on the outermost node, so sizing or positioning an avatar works. The clipped tile is data-slot="avatar-frame".
forwarding.rest: Native span props go to the outermost node.

needsDesign: The sheet's group rows disagree on the overlap: the plain stack uses -4px and the stack-with-counter uses -12px, which clips the initials illegibly ('MV' renders as 'M'). Shipped as -4px, the value that keeps the initials readable. Confirm one number for both.

The status dot's ring. The sheet rings each dot with a lighter step of its OWN hue (green-60 under green-40, and a raw --ui-red-60 palette step under the red) rather than with the surface. A same-hue ring does not separate the dot from a photo behind it, and the raw palette step is off the role layer entirely. Shipped with a --ui-bg-surface ring, matching the avatar's own hairline. Confirm.

The 1.5px seam measures 1.19:1 against the initials well it separates, so two overlapping initials-avatars are divided by a nearly invisible line. Against a photograph it reads; against another `bg-sunken` tile it barely does. Worth a role of its own rather than the ground colour.

The seam is not RTL-tested. A box-shadow offset has no logical form, so the leading edge is handled with an `rtl:` variant rather than by the same mechanism `-space-x-*` uses. Nothing in this library renders RTL yet.

No hover, focus or pressed state is drawn, and an avatar is frequently a button or a link (it opens a profile). Nothing here is interactive yet; a consumer wrapping one in a Button gets Button's states, which may or may not be what is wanted.

The intent family has no NEUTRAL solid. The neutral dot reuses --ui-text-muted, which is what Banner's neutral variant uses, but it is an ink role serving as a fill. If neutral status is going to recur, --ui-intent-neutral-fg is the role that is missing.
No image-loading or image-error state is drawn; a slow photo shows an empty frame rather than the initials it could fall back to.
knownGaps: The status dot has no size of its own at sm: 4px is a floor, not a scale point, because 3px is a mark nobody can see and the dot is the only visual carrier of the state.
Avatar.Group counts DIRECT children. `{cond && <Avatar/>}` is handled (Children.toArray drops it), but a component that returns several avatars counts as one and `max` will not see through it.

Stacking order is DOM order, so a later avatar paints over an earlier one. The sheet draws the reverse (earlier on top). At a 4px overlap with the hairline the difference is one seam's direction; reproducing it would mean cloning children to assign z-index, which §3 rules out.

outline-width AND outline-offset both snap to whole device pixels, so the 1.5px hairline computes to 1px inset 1px at dPR 1 and is exact at dPR 2. Pinned in border-hairline.browser.test.tsx rather than re-investigated.

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

Avatar stops carrying an edge at all, and Avatar.Group paints a seam only where one is needed. The frame used to draw a full-perimeter 1.5px hairline in --ui-bg-surface — the industry-standard implementation (shadcn `*:ring-2 *:ring-background`, MUI `2px solid background.paper`, Atlassian's 'surface-coloured ring', Flowbite's `ring-white dark:ring-gray-800`) and the industry-standard bug with it, filed against MUI as #21700: 'Avatar group uses the background colour set for the app for the Avatar borders, but doesn't pick up on the background colour of the div it's within.' Three of that ring's four sides never touch another avatar: they sit on the ground claiming to BE the ground, so on a Card, a Menu panel or a Table row it painted a visible mismatched rim (#FDFCFB on #F6F3F0) — and a LONE avatar, which is most call sites in an app, wore it for nothing at all. The component's own comment always said the ring existed 'so two overlapping avatars read as two rather than as one shape'. So it is now painted only there. Primer is the one library that gets this right — a directional `border-right` instead of a ring — and this takes its insight with a better mechanism: an offset box-shadow on the LEADING edge of every group child but the first. A shadow copies the border-box SHAPE, so it follows `soft` and `full` with no per-shape geometry and stays resolution-independent; the leading edge means DOM order already puts the seam on top of the avatar beneath, where Primer has to invert the z-index to get its trailing border there. The seam is 1.5px inside a 4px overlap, so by construction it never reaches the ground. Verified by rendering both shapes at all three sizes over four grounds in Chromium, plus a 5x magnification confirming the seam follows the radius. NOT a mask: a cut-out is the only truly ground-independent answer and it clips tightly enough that an outer focus ring becomes impossible (Vaadin #26 — and an avatar is going to become a control), lands on fractional pixels and jitters on resize, and the radial-gradient form everyone ships is a circle trick while `soft` is this component's default. --ui-avatar-ring-color survives for the two things that still paint — the seam and the status dot's ring — and the dot keeps an opaque ring because it separates a 4px mark from the photograph beneath it, which is the one case a hole cannot serve.

migration.manual: A lone Avatar no longer paints a hairline. If your layout depended on that 1.5px ring to separate an avatar from a same-coloured ground, give the container the contrast instead — the ring was never a boundary, it was a claim about the page. Anything that bound --ui-avatar-ring-color to fix a mismatched rim can drop the binding: there is no rim. Keep the binding only if you want the SEAM inside a stack to read as a cut through it on a non-surface ground. Any local `outline-*` override on avatar parts should be removed.

changes.summary: Four values on the Avatar sheet measured wrong and were reconciled to the code (flow stays repo -> Paper). (1) INITIALS INK. The sheet drew initials in --ui-text-disabled, which measures 1.76:1 on the --ui-bg-sunken well -- initials identify a person and have to clear AA. The code already used --ui-text-muted (4.87 light / 7.11 dark) and the sheet now does too, across all 17 initials and the +4 counter. (2) NEUTRAL STATUS DOT. The sheet drew --ui-bg-emphasis-active, which measures 10.34:1 in light and 1.31:1 in DARK -- a state indicator invisible in the scheme nobody opened. Now --ui-text-muted, which is what Banner's own neutral variant uses and which holds in both (5.78 / 6.47). (3) SUCCESS DOT. The sheet drew --ui-data-transactional-fg, a data-visualisation category role that happens to be the same green; now the intent role it always should have been. (4) DOT RINGS. Each dot was ringed with a lighter step of its OWN hue, and the error dot's ring was a RAW PALETTE STEP (--ui-red-60) -- off the role layer entirely, and a same-hue ring does not separate the dot from a photo behind it. All three now ring with --ui-bg-surface, matching the avatar's own hairline. Also fixed: the sheet's two group rows disagreed on the overlap, -4px for the plain stack and -12px for the stack-with-counter, and the tighter one clipped the initials illegibly ('MV' rendered as 'M'). Both are now -4px, the value that keeps them readable. Note for whoever edits this sheet next: `update_styles` silently DROPS a margin change -- it reports success and the value does not move -- so the counter row had to be rebuilt with x-paper-clone. All three dot fills are now declared as contrast pairs in avatar.doc.ts and measured by check:contrast in both schemes.

migration.manual: No code change -- the code was the source for three of the four. The sheet now carries no raw palette step and no role that fails in dark.

changes.summary: Avatar expanded to the redrawn sheet, which grew from one row to three sections. THE BREAKING PART: `shape` is now "soft" | "full" and defaults to "soft". It was "circle" | "rounded" defaulting to "circle" -- a synonym pair for two shapes that already had names on Button (CONVENTIONS §2 says variant values are shared vocabulary where the meaning is shared), and the sheet's own layers are named "Avatar Rounded Soft" and "Avatar Rounded Full". The soft radius per size is now Button's soft radius per size, so a row of both is concentric. The default flip is a VISUAL change at every existing call site: avatars that were circles are now soft squares. It is the right way round -- the Header sheet's own User Avatar is radius-md, so the old default disagreed with the composition that uses it -- but it is a change, and the old values are a type error rather than a silent no-op. NEW: `status` + `statusLabel`, a corner dot in success/neutral/danger, with the label REQUIRED BY THE TYPE whenever status is set (the isIconOnly/aria-label shape) because a dot is colour and position only and WCAG 1.4.1 is not satisfiable by documentation. NEW: `Avatar.Group`, a stack overlapping by the sheet's 4px with an optional "+N" tile; `max` and `overflowLabel` are likewise a union, since "+4" is a glyph and a number. The overlap comes from the container (`-space-x-xs`) rather than by rewriting children, so slot contents are never touched (§3). REFACTOR: the component is now two nodes. The root holds the box, className, ref and the positioning context; a new `avatar-frame` holds the well, radius, the sheet's 1.5px inset hairline and the clipping. The dot is a SIBLING of the frame, not a child, because the frame is overflow-clip and a corner dot inside it would be cut in half by the radius. Three of the sheet's own values were NOT transcribed, because each measured wrong -- see the design entry.

migration.manual: REQUIRED: replace shape="circle" with shape="full" and shape="rounded" with shape="soft". Both old values now fail to compile, deliberately -- a silently-ignored shape prop would be worse. THEN DECIDE THE DEFAULT: any <Avatar> with no shape prop changes from a circle to a soft square. If a surface wants circles, pass shape="full" explicitly. In this repo the only call sites were the Header and Sidebar stories and the visual matrix; the Header sheet draws radius-md, so the new default matches it. Also note the doc previously declared a contrast pair the component never rendered (--ui-text-primary on the well, while the code renders --ui-text-muted); the declared pair is now the rendered one, so the generated figure changes from 14.11:1 to the real 4.87:1.

changes.summary: Twelve defects fixed in the Avatar, Badge and Multiselect sheets rather than transcribed. Accessibility: Avatar initials used --ui-text-disabled, measuring 1.8:1 on the sunken well — initials identify a person and are not disabled content, so they now use --ui-text-muted at 4.9:1. Type floor: Badge labels were 11px in all twelve places, below the system's own 12px floor (ADR 0009) and the THIRD component to ship this defect — now --ui-text-label-sm. Token discipline: Badge's selected fill and border used the raw palette step --ui-blue-80 instead of --ui-bg-accent; Badge's danger ink used --ui-bg-danger-solid, a BACKGROUND token used as a foreground, now --ui-text-on-danger-subtle; Avatar gaps were raw 8px; Multiselect's trigger carried raw 16px padding, 8px radius and 8px gap; its label used the raw palette step --ui-neutral-20; its dropdown shadow was a raw hex instead of --ui-shadow-sm.

migration.manual: Design-side only; both implementations were built from the corrected values.

changes.summary: Avatar and Badge, both built through add-component and needing no new tokens. Avatar: photo or derived initials, circle/rounded, `name` required in both forms because it is simultaneously the alt text and the initials source; the visible initials are aria-hidden with the full name in an sr-only span, so a screen reader announces the person rather than spelling letters; a real means a broken URL degrades to alt text instead of an empty box. Badge: four variants, two sizes, pill/rounded, rendering a with NO interaction props — the sheet's x and check variants are composed by passing a real button into iconEnd, which keeps the accessible name at the call site and avoids the commonest tag-component defect (a click handler on a span with no role, focus or keyboard path). 12 design bugs fixed in Paper across both, plus Multiselect (see the design-fixes entry).

migration.manual: New items. `npx shadcn add @bydiorama/avatar @bydiorama/badge`; both pull in `cn` and expect react as a peer.

items.name: badge
items.title: Badge
items.lead: Gives a status a name, so colour does not have to explain it alone.

docs.lead: Gives a status a name, so colour does not have to explain it alone.
docs.name: Badge
docs.summary: A short status or selection label. Seven variants, two sizes, pill or rounded, with an optional trailing slot.

anatomy.notes: A <span>. Carries data-variant and data-size.
children.
Trailing mark. Pass a real <button> here when it should be actionable.

docs.composition:
Badge
├─ children   ReactNode — the label
└─ iconEnd?   ReactElement — arrow, check, or a real <button> for remove

variant.notes: selected is the brand fill; unselected is outlined; neutral, info, success, warning and danger are tinted labels with no border, so a row of them reads as data rather than controls. NEUTRAL is for status data with no intent — an industry, a type, a plan tier — which is the commonest badge in an admin table and had no answer before: `unselected` is a choice state wearing an outline, and tinting a category green teaches nothing when the value never varies. Same two roles as Banner's own neutral (§2 — one vocabulary per concept).

size.notes: 22px and 28px tall. Both carry the same 12px label and the same padding — the difference is height alone, pinned with min-h because the spacing scale cannot express 28 (py-xs gives 22, py-sm 30). md pairs with a 16px icon, sm with 12px. These two were previously identical apart from the icon, so a badge with no icon rendered the same at either size.

shape.notes: One vocabulary with Button (§2). `full` is rounded-full; `soft` is the component's own smaller radius — radius-sm here, Button's per-size soft radius there. Was `pill`/`rounded`, which named the same two shapes differently from the only other component that has them.

iconEnd.notes: Slot. A decorative mark should be aria-hidden; an interactive one must be a real button with its own accessible name.

do: Keep the label to one or two words — a badge is a label, not a sentence.
Pass a real <button aria-label="Remove X"> into iconEnd for removable tags.
Use success/warning/danger for state, neutral for categorical data with no state, selected/unselected for choice; do not mix the meanings.
dont: Do not try to make the Badge itself interactive — onClick, onKeyDown and tabIndex are removed from the prop type, because a click handler on a <span> has no role, no focus and no keyboard path. Put the control in iconEnd, or wrap the badge in a real button.
Do not use a badge as a button substitute for primary actions.
Do not convey status by colour alone — the label carries the meaning (WCAG 1.4.1).
Do not colour a category that never varies. An industry badge that is always blue teaches nothing — that is what `neutral` is for. The sheet's own don't-list, verbatim.

a11y.role: none (plain text). Deliberate: a label with no interaction should not claim one — and the prop type removes the interaction handlers so it cannot acquire one by accident.

keyboard.does: Not focusable. Interactivity lives in the iconEnd slot's own control.

Declared because it is the channel that makes `neutral` legible in dark at all: 1.434 light, 1.391 dark, against a fill that manages 1.188 and 1.098.

needsDesign: `neutral` and `unselected` now look close: a quiet fill plus a `border-edge-subtle` hairline, differing only in the fill (`sunken` against `base`). They are different jobs — `unselected` is one half of a choice pair and `neutral` is a static category label — and the fill still separates them, but a caller reading the two side by side has to know which is which. Worth checking whether the pair wants a sharper difference or whether `unselected` should simply be documented as the interactive one.
knownGaps: No dedicated removable-tag component. The sheet draws a `×` variant; today that is composed by passing a button into iconEnd, which keeps the accessible name at the call site where it belongs.

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

ChatTasks: the plan the agent works to, written, ticked off and revised in place. A chat-widget card with a disclosure header; proposed plans show numbered rows with Run / Change it and a per-row drop; running, complete and stopped plans show six row statuses (done, current, pending, needsYou, failed, skipped) and fold to a header whose glyph is the plan's status. The current task holds StatusMatrix Working's key frame — the plan never moves.

Badge gains variant="info" (--ui-intent-info-bg fill, --ui-intent-info-fg ink, transparent hairline), so Badge's statuses are exactly Banner's five intents (#9). The same pair Banner info paints: 4.82:1 light, 5.64:1 dark. Distinct from `selected`, which is also blue: selected is a choice (accent fill), info a status (tint).

`neutral` gains a `border-edge-subtle` hairline; its fill and ink are unchanged. The fill alone was level with the status tints in light — 1.188 against a table row where success and warning sit at 1.201 and 1.176 — and less than a third of their weight in DARK, 1.098 against their 1.629. Six category chips down a dark table read as faint holes beside status chips that read fine, which is what a full-width specimen in both schemes made visible; the numbers had been recorded for a while and nobody had seen them. Raising the FILL in dark was the obvious fix and the wrong one: the nearest role that lands near 1.63 drops `--ui-text-muted` on it to 3.86:1, under AA, so ground and ink would both have had to move and neither has a role for where they land. The edge does the same job in both schemes instead — 1.434 light, 1.391 dark — leaves the ink at 7.11:1, and introduces no new value: `unselected` already pairs a quiet fill with a hairline, so this is the family's existing vocabulary applied to the variant that needed it. It also makes the split structural rather than tonal, which is the better end state: a CATEGORY is outlined, an INTENT is tinted, and that reads the same way in both schemes.

migration.manual: `<Badge variant="neutral">` now renders a 1.5px `--ui-border-subtle` edge where the border was transparent. The box does not change size — the border box already reserved 1.5px on every variant, which is why `min-h-5.5` still measures 22px. If you pinned the neutral border colour in a test or a visual baseline, it is now the subtle role rather than transparent. Nothing to change at a call site.

changes.summary: The intent GROUNDS (--ui-intent-success-bg, -warning-bg, -danger-bg, -info-bg and -danger-bg-hover) are composited at derivation instead of shipped as translucent tints. Contrast against a translucent value is only defined once something flattens it, and here that something is whatever a consumer puts the label on — while the audit flattens every pair over --ui-bg-base. So the measured number was the number you got ON THE PAGE and nowhere else. Measured on the pale-yellow stress brand in light: warning ink 4.87:1 on the page, 4.57 on a Table's bg-elevated mat, 4.47 on a bg-sunken well; danger 4.75 / 4.45 / 4.36; info 4.80 / 4.50 / 4.39. Nothing was wrong with the ink — the ground moved under it, and no gate could see it because a contrast pair names two tokens and cannot say 'over elevated'. It is the same rule --ui-border-control already follows ('opaque, not an alpha hairline: it must MEASURE at 3:1, so it is composited by construction'), applied to the fills that carry intent ink. Theme zero's authored LIGHT intents were already opaque ramp-90 steps; its authored DARK ones were rgba literals — a transcription convenience, because a flat Paper file cannot hold a light-dark() pair — and are now composited over the dark page, which is what the audit already reported for them. --ui-intent-danger-border stays translucent: it is a border on a tinted surface, not a ground carrying ink. A resolver test asserts an intent ink measures the same on bg-base, bg-surface, bg-elevated and bg-sunken, in every stress brand and both schemes. Surfaced by the elevated-ramp fix moving a stress brand's light bg-elevated off pure white, which pushed one of these under AA where axe could finally see it.

migration.manual: A tinted Badge or Banner no longer shows the surface beneath it through its fill — it paints the same colour on a page, a card, a row or a well, which is the colour the audit always reported. Theme zero's light values are byte-identical; its dark values become the opaque equivalent of what they composited to on the page. If you deliberately layered a tinted surface over an image or another tint expecting it to show through, it no longer will.

changes.summary: Badge gains a `neutral` variant: status data that carries no INTENT — an industry, a type, a plan tier. It is the commonest badge in an admin table and the set had no answer for it, so a consumer carried a documented local fork of Badge through two checkpoint syncs. `unselected` is a CHOICE state wearing an outline, and tinting a category green or blue teaches nothing when the value never varies — the Patterns index sheet draws exactly this and says so in its own don't-list ('Don't colour a category that never varies. An industry badge that is always blue teaches nothing'). Ships as `bg-sunken text-ink-muted` with no border: the same two roles Banner's own `neutral` variant uses, because it is the same concept and §2 gives a concept one vocabulary. Measured 4.87:1 light and 7.11:1 dark, Banner's own numbers. The sheet drew it as --ui-bg-active, which is an INTERACTION role — a resting badge would then be the exact colour of a pressed table row, and a row of them would change meaning under the pointer — so the role is corrected and the WEIGHT is recorded as an open question in needsDesign: against a table row (bg-surface) sunken measures 1.188:1 light but only 1.098:1 dark, where the tinted status variants sit at 1.201 and 1.629. A story renders the real composition — neutral and status badges on bg-surface rows inside a bg-elevated mat, in both schemes — so that difference is a thing you look at rather than a number in a doc.

migration.manual: Additive; no existing variant changes. If you forked Badge locally to add a neutral variant, delete the fork and pass variant="neutral" — check the fill first, since this ships bg-sunken and a fork transcribed from the sheet would be bg-active.

changes.summary: One shape vocabulary across Button and Badge: `full` and `soft`. Button's `pill` becomes `full` and Badge's `pill`/`rounded` become `full`/`soft` — the same two shapes had two different names in the only two components that have them, and `pill` named the DRAWING where every other value in this system names the token. The redrawn Button sheet settles it in its own legend: 'Button variants: Default (soft border radius), Rounded Full'. Both type-test files keep a compile-time assertion that the old names no longer compile, so they cannot drift back in quietly.

migration.manual: Rename `shape="pill"` to `shape="full"` on Button and Badge, and `shape="rounded"` to `shape="soft"` on Badge. Defaults are unchanged in behaviour: Button still defaults to soft, Badge still defaults to the fully rounded shape (now spelled `full`).

changes.summary: Badge gains the `warning` variant the sheet now draws in all three size rows, completing the intent set the token layer already carried — success, warning and danger all existed as roles and only two had been drawn. The browser test asserts the three status variants are three DIFFERENT colours rather than checking three literals, because a copy-paste in the VARIANT map would leave every literal assertion passing while warning painted the success tint; Badge has been here before, with two sizes that were pixel-identical while every test passed. The type test's `@ts-expect-error unknown variant` sat on `variant="warning"`, so the directive reporting as UNUSED is what said the sheet had grown a third tint — it now sits on `caution`, a synonym the system deliberately does not have.

Badge md and sm rendered identically, reported from Storybook. Two independent defects stacked. First, the SIZE map differed ONLY by icon size, so a badge with no icon was pixel-identical at both sizes. Second — and the reason even the sm height was wrong — tailwind-merge was deleting `leading-flat`: our type roles are registered in its `font-size` group, whose built-in conflict clears `leading` because stock `text-sm` bundles a line height. Ours never do (ADR 0009 pairs every role with its own leading token), so `text-label-sm` silently removed the leading and both sizes fell back to the font's normal 1.42, rendering at 28px instead of the designed 22px. Fixed by overriding conflictingClassGroups so font-size no longer clears leading — a knowing trade documented in cn.ts and pinned by a test: a consumer writing stock `leading-6 text-sm` now keeps both and the cascade decides, which is a far smaller failure than a component losing its own leading, and affects only stock classes this library never emits. Sizes are now pinned with min-h-5.5 and min-h-7 (22/28) rather than transcribing the sheet's off-scale 145% md leading, which put a control's height at the mercy of font metrics; the padding scale cannot express 28 (py-xs gives 22, py-sm 30). Design corrected in Paper to match: md leading moved to --ui-leading-flat with an explicit 28px min-height, md gained the tracking-tight the sm rows already had, and the md status variants lost a 1px border drawn in their own background colour that sm did not have.

migration.manual: cn() no longer lets a font size clear a preceding leading. If consumer code relied on stock `text-sm` overriding an earlier `leading-*`, set the leading after the size instead. `pnpm test` now also runs registry/**/*.test.ts, which had never been globbed — registry-level unit tests, including the first cn() tests, were silently not running.

changes.summary: Badge's doc said 'do not attach onClick' while its props extended HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>, which permits onClick, onKeyDown and tabIndex — the doc and the types disagreed, and the types are what callers actually obey. Same class of defect as the phantom render slot found on Button. onClick/onDoubleClick/onMouseDown/onMouseUp/onKeyDown/onKeyUp/tabIndex are now Omitted from BadgeProps, so faking interactivity on a span is a compile error rather than a review comment. `role` is deliberately kept: role="status" on a live badge is legitimate. Two @ts-expect-error assertions added. Also added computed-style tests for the trailing-icon size, since the arbitrary variant [&_svg]:size-* compiles to a descendant rule and a class existing proves nothing about which element it reaches.

migration.manual: Re-add @bydiorama/badge. Any call site passing onClick to a Badge must move the handler into an iconEnd button or wrap the badge in a real control.

changes.summary: Twelve defects fixed in the Avatar, Badge and Multiselect sheets rather than transcribed. Accessibility: Avatar initials used --ui-text-disabled, measuring 1.8:1 on the sunken well — initials identify a person and are not disabled content, so they now use --ui-text-muted at 4.9:1. Type floor: Badge labels were 11px in all twelve places, below the system's own 12px floor (ADR 0009) and the THIRD component to ship this defect — now --ui-text-label-sm. Token discipline: Badge's selected fill and border used the raw palette step --ui-blue-80 instead of --ui-bg-accent; Badge's danger ink used --ui-bg-danger-solid, a BACKGROUND token used as a foreground, now --ui-text-on-danger-subtle; Avatar gaps were raw 8px; Multiselect's trigger carried raw 16px padding, 8px radius and 8px gap; its label used the raw palette step --ui-neutral-20; its dropdown shadow was a raw hex instead of --ui-shadow-sm.

migration.manual: Design-side only; both implementations were built from the corrected values.

changes.summary: Avatar and Badge, both built through add-component and needing no new tokens. Avatar: photo or derived initials, circle/rounded, `name` required in both forms because it is simultaneously the alt text and the initials source; the visible initials are aria-hidden with the full name in an sr-only span, so a screen reader announces the person rather than spelling letters; a real means a broken URL degrades to alt text instead of an empty box. Badge: four variants, two sizes, pill/rounded, rendering a with NO interaction props — the sheet's x and check variants are composed by passing a real button into iconEnd, which keeps the accessible name at the call site and avoids the commonest tag-component defect (a click handler on a span with no role, focus or keyboard path). 12 design bugs fixed in Paper across both, plus Multiselect (see the design-fixes entry).

migration.manual: New items. `npx shadcn add @bydiorama/avatar @bydiorama/badge`; both pull in `cn` and expect react as a peer.

items.lead: Puts a message and its next action where they can be seen together.

docs.lead: Puts a message and its next action where they can be seen together.
docs.name: Banner
docs.summary: An inline message attached to the surface it belongs to — not a toast, not a dialog. Five intents, an optional leading glyph, title, action (Banner.Action, which takes the banner's role) and dismiss control. Composes inside a Popover panel as a boxed child.

anatomy.notes: A <div>. Carries data-variant. radius-md, p-lg, gap-sm.
Leading glyph slot. Decorative — pass it aria-hidden.
Present only with a title or an action: the column holding title and message, gap-xs.

title, as a

at label-md in the intent ink — not a heading: a banner is an annotation, not a section of the document outline.

children, as a

. Takes the remaining width.

Banner.Action — a Button md that takes the banner's role: primary on info, a 1.5px outline in the banner's own ink on every other intent. Centred on the block; under the message, in the text column, when the banner is narrower than 480px.
A real <button> with a required accessible name, in a 24px target around a 16px glyph.

docs.composition:
Banner
├─ children       ReactNode (required) — the message
├─ variant?       neutral | info | success | warning | danger
├─ icon?          ReactElement — leading glyph, never wrapped
├─ title?         ReactNode — a label-md line above the message
├─ action?        <Banner.Action onClick | render>Label</Banner.Action>
├─ isLive?        announce on appearance
└─ onDismiss? + dismissLabel?   — the two travel together at the type level

children.notes: A slot rather than a string so the message can carry a link.

variant.notes: Intent ROLES, never palette steps — the sheet drew --ui-blue-90 and --ui-red-40 directly, which do not re-skin with a brand.

icon.notes: Leading glyph. Decorative: the message carries the meaning, so never rely on the glyph or the colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1). The component sizes the slot at 16px, the size the sheet draws at every control size. Without that the glyph arrives at whatever the icon library defaults to — griddy hard-codes width/height="24" as attributes — which rendered every icon 50% oversize.

title.notes:
A line above the message, label-md 13/600 in the intent ink. A

, not a heading — a heading would put an annotation into the page outline between the headings around it. With a title the row aligns to the top and the glyph sits on the title's line; without one the banner is the single centred row it always was.

action.notes: Slot, never wrapped. Fill it with Banner.Action, which takes the banner's ROLE (owner's redesign, 2026-11-02): Button primary on info; a 1.5px outline in the banner's own ink on neutral, success and warning (4.87 / 5.05 / 5.03:1 light, 7.11 / 5.68 / 4.92:1 dark); and on danger the same outline in --ui-text-on-danger-subtle (8.52 / 5.93:1), the ink Button danger uses. Hover and press are a 10% / 15% tint of that ink. A filled accent on every intent was the first proposal and measured 1.22-1.26:1 against the tinted grounds in light. In a container under 480px the action moves under the message, into the text column; the dismiss stays top-right. Banner.Action is always md (32px) and takes Button's other props, including render={<a href />} for a link.

isLive.notes: Adds role=status + aria-live=polite. OFF by default on purpose: a banner rendered with the page is not news, and a live region that fires on mount talks over whatever the user was reading. Turn it on when the banner appears in response to something.

onDismiss.notes: Renders the dismiss button. Requires dismissLabel at the type level.

dismissLabel.notes: The button's accessible name — 'Dismiss export notice', not 'Close'. Cannot be omitted when onDismiss is set; the type is a discriminated union.

do: Write a dismissLabel that names what is being dismissed, since it is read out of context.
Use isLive for a banner that appears after an action, and leave it off for one rendered with the page.
Fill the action slot with Banner.Action so its emphasis follows the banner's role — one action, a verb ("Review layouts"), never a second CTA.
Put a Banner inside a Popover panel as a plain child — it is boxed, so it sits flush at the panel's padding rather than taking the unboxed inset.
dont: Do not convey the meaning through variant colour alone — the message text must say it (WCAG 1.4.1).
Do not use a Banner for something requiring acknowledgement; that is a Modal.
Do not pass a bare glyph as children to make an icon-only banner — the message is the point.
Do not set onDismiss without dismissLabel; it will not compile, which is the point.
Do not pass a plain <Button variant="primary"> as the action on a tinted banner — its fill measures 1.22-1.26:1 against the tint. Banner.Action picks the right treatment per role.

a11y.role: none by default — a static banner is part of the page, not an announcement. role=status + aria-live=polite only when isLive is set.
a11y.name: The message itself. The dismiss button carries its own required aria-label.

keyboard.does: Reaches the dismiss button when present; the banner itself is not focusable.
Activates dismiss — it is a real <button>, so this is native.

a11y.target: The dismiss control is a 24px box around a 16px glyph, clearing SC 2.5.8; the glyph alone would be a 16px target.

contrastPairs.role: neutral banner ink
info banner ink
success banner ink
warning banner ink
danger banner ink
danger banner action — label and 1.5px ring (Button danger's own ink)

knownGaps: The sheet draws three variants — neutral, info and danger. success and warning are DERIVED from the existing intent roles for completeness and are not in the design; confirm with design.
The sheet gives the neutral variant a leading glyph and the danger variant a dismiss control, and neither the reverse; the component allows any combination.

Title and action are CLOSED (2026-11-02, #9): drawn on the #9 Proposals sheet in every intent, narrow and dark, with the action's treatment set by the owner's Audit #9 redesign. Neutral and success actions were not drawn by the owner and follow the same rule (an outline in the banner's ink).
Banner.Action knows the narrow placement; a caller who puts some other element in the action slot gets the wide layout only (it does not carry the container-query classes).
docs.motion: Only the dismiss control moves — a colour transition at --ui-duration-fast with --ui-ease-out. The banner itself has no enter or exit animation: it is placed inline by the page rather than portalled, so its appearance is a layout change the consumer owns and can animate in context. This is the one component using Tailwind's `transition-colors` group where the rest of the library enumerates properties; the group is a fixed set rather than `all`, so it is legal, but it names more properties than actually change here.
