info banner ink
success banner ink
warning banner ink
danger banner ink
danger banner action — label and 1.5px ring (Button danger's own ink)

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

Banner gains title (a

at label-md in the intent ink, not a heading) and an action slot filled with the new Banner.Action, which takes the banner's ROLE per the owner's Audit #9 redesign: Button primary on info; a 1.5px outline plus label in the banner's own ink on neutral, success and warning (4.87/5.05/5.03:1 light, 7.11/5.68/4.92:1 dark); on danger the same outline in --ui-text-on-danger-subtle (8.52/5.93:1). Hover/press are a 10%/15% tint of that ink. A filled accent on every intent was the first proposal and measured 1.22-1.26:1 against the tinted grounds. A banner with a title or an action lays out as a grid whose root is a @container: under 480px the action moves under the message, into the text column, and the dismiss stays on the title's line. A message-only banner is the unchanged single flex row. Banner now depends on Button.

lib/motion — the three timings this library animates at, as class-name constants: motionMicro (interaction feedback, --ui-duration-fast), motionStandard (a surface arriving or leaving, --ui-duration-base) and motionDeliberate (an unfolding, --ui-duration-slow). The duration/easing pair had been hand-assembled 49 times across 28 files, identically. The property list deliberately STAYS at the call site rather than becoming a parameter, and that is a constraint rather than a preference: Tailwind compiles the class names it finds by scanning source TEXT, so a recipe built as `transition-[${properties}]` produces a string the scanner never saw, generates no rule, and the element silently does not animate. The split chosen is the one that keeps every class name a literal in a file Tailwind reads. Writing it surfaced two things worth recording. The library uses --ui-ease-out in FIFTY cases out of fifty, while the token layer offers four easings and four --ui-motion-* intent tokens with zero consumers between them — including --ui-motion-standard, which pairs --ui-duration-base with --ui-ease-default, an easing nothing here has ever reached for. So the constants are named for the intents but do not read them, which records a disagreement between the token layer and the components rather than papering over it; which side is right is a design question and motion sign-off is still open. Banner's dismiss control is also corrected in the same pass, from Tailwind's `transition-colors` group to `transition-[background-color]`: the group covers colour, background, border, fill, stroke and text-decoration, and the comment directly above it explains that the glyph must hold full strength because dimming it measured under the 3:1 floor — a group naming `color` invites exactly the change the comment forbids.

migration.manual: New lib item, and 28 items now list it in registryDependencies — `npx @bydiorama/ui add <component>` pulls it in automatically. No rendered motion changes: the constants expand to the exact strings they replaced, asserted by the browser suite and by 70 unchanged visual baselines. If you have forked a component, the import is `import { motionMicro } from "@/lib/motion"` and the alias needs registering wherever your build resolves `@/lib/*`.

changes.summary: check:motion joins the gate list, and every animating component now documents its motion. The gate rejects a literal duration or easing in registry/ (a discipline that was already perfect — zero hard-coded durations across 26 files — and had nothing keeping it that way), transition-all (CONVENTIONS section 6 has said this since the beginning and nothing enforced it), a keyframe with no reduced-motion guard, and an animating component with no top-level motion: note in its doc. It reads lib recipes alongside components as check:overlays does, so Header's motion is found in @/lib/chrome-control where it actually lives rather than reported as absent. 27 doc files gain a motion: note describing what moves, what drives it and what reduced motion does to it; Sheet's and ImageUpload's existing notes are PROMOTED out of a11y to the top level, where Button already had its, because motion is a description of what a component does rather than solely an accessibility concern and a field meaning one thing at two depths stops being findable. ImageUpload's note is corrected while being promoted: it credited the token layer with stopping its spinner, and what actually stops it is the motion-safe: variant. Two findings are recorded in the notes rather than fixed: Sidebar's collapsible section snaps via the hidden attribute where Accordion animates the identical interaction against Base UI's published height, and Banner reaches for transition-colors where the rest of the library enumerates properties. No component's rendered motion changes; no .tsx is touched.

migration.manual: Documentation only — every change is inside a *.doc.ts, and no component's classes or rendered motion moved. If you consume the doc files and read `a11y.motion`, it has moved to the top-level `motion` key on Sheet and ImageUpload; Button was already there and the other 27 are new.

changes.summary: The intent GROUNDS (--ui-intent-success-bg, -warning-bg, -danger-bg, -info-bg and -danger-bg-hover) are composited at derivation instead of shipped as translucent tints. Contrast against a translucent value is only defined once something flattens it, and here that something is whatever a consumer puts the label on — while the audit flattens every pair over --ui-bg-base. So the measured number was the number you got ON THE PAGE and nowhere else. Measured on the pale-yellow stress brand in light: warning ink 4.87:1 on the page, 4.57 on a Table's bg-elevated mat, 4.47 on a bg-sunken well; danger 4.75 / 4.45 / 4.36; info 4.80 / 4.50 / 4.39. Nothing was wrong with the ink — the ground moved under it, and no gate could see it because a contrast pair names two tokens and cannot say 'over elevated'. It is the same rule --ui-border-control already follows ('opaque, not an alpha hairline: it must MEASURE at 3:1, so it is composited by construction'), applied to the fills that carry intent ink. Theme zero's authored LIGHT intents were already opaque ramp-90 steps; its authored DARK ones were rgba literals — a transcription convenience, because a flat Paper file cannot hold a light-dark() pair — and are now composited over the dark page, which is what the audit already reported for them. --ui-intent-danger-border stays translucent: it is a border on a tinted surface, not a ground carrying ink. A resolver test asserts an intent ink measures the same on bg-base, bg-surface, bg-elevated and bg-sunken, in every stress brand and both schemes. Surfaced by the elevated-ramp fix moving a stress brand's light bg-elevated off pure white, which pushed one of these under AA where axe could finally see it.

migration.manual: A tinted Badge or Banner no longer shows the surface beneath it through its fill — it paints the same colour on a page, a card, a row or a well, which is the colour the audit always reported. Theme zero's light values are byte-identical; its dark values become the opaque equivalent of what they composited to on the page. If you deliberately layered a tinted surface over an image or another tint expecting it to show through, it no longer will.

changes.summary: Banner added, and Popover/Checkbox refined against the updated sheets. Banner is an inline message with five intents; the dismiss control's accessible name is a DISCRIMINATED UNION with onDismiss rather than a doc note, so an unnamed icon-only dismiss cannot compile. It does not announce by default: role=status/aria-live=polite is opt-in via isLive, because a banner rendered with the page is not news and a live region firing on mount talks over whatever the user was reading. The sheet's info well inside the Popover panel IS this component, so Popover's stories now compose Banner instead of a hand-rolled box, and its glyph is griddy's InfoCircle — byte-identical to the path the sheet drew. Popover moves to radius-xl (24), which is concentric exactly against a Banner's radius-md (8) plus the panel's p-lg (16); the earlier 32px panel was concentric too but read as too round. Popover.Description is respecced from the actions sheet — the only place a description is actually drawn — to body-md at the relaxed leading in secondary ink with its own py-xs. Checkbox's label alignment fixed: the 24px minimum added for SC 2.5.8 had been combined with items-start, so a 17px label sat at the top of the row with 6px of dead space beneath it instead of beside the box; items-center matches the sheet, and a geometric regression test pins the label's centre to within 1px of the row's (it was 3.55px off, confirmed by probing the fix away).

migration.manual: Popover panel radius changes from 32px to 24px and Popover.Description from body-sm/muted to body-md/secondary at a 600 weight — both transcribed from the updated sheet. check:utilities gained a catch-all namespace for intent inks (text-danger, text-success, text-info), which had gone unchecked since Badge shipped: a `text-dangr` typo emitted no CSS and nothing reported it. Coverage went 248 to 255.

docs.name: Button
docs.summary: The primary action control. Five types, three sizes, two shapes, five content arrangements. Theme zero defaults to soft; a brand may choose full: the design's Rounded Full is the alternative, not the baseline, and having that inverted is why three components appeared to need a button nobody had defined.

anatomy.notes: The <button>. Carries variant, size and state data attributes.
Leading icon. Passed as an element, never wrapped by the button.
children. Absent when isIconOnly.
Trailing icon — chevrons for menu triggers.

docs.composition:
Button
├─ icon?        ReactElement — griddy-icons only
├─ children     ReactNode — omitted when isIconOnly
└─ iconEnd?     ReactElement

variant.notes: primary uses the brand fill for the main action. secondary provides a quiet decorative edge; use outline when the boundary must identify the control. ghost stays unboxed until hover. danger uses a subtle danger surface for destructive actions. inverse is designed for inverse-background bands, such as a footer or call to action, and follows that band's colors when the scheme changes.

size.notes: 44 / 32 / 24px tall at default density (--ui-control-*-height). lg is the touch target for primary page actions. Under [data-ui-density="compact"] every size is 4px shorter, floored at 24 — so lg is 40px and gives up the 44px touch target; under comfortable they are 4px taller (ADR 0020 §4).

shape.notes: Omitted follows the brand's controlShape (soft in theme zero). Explicit soft or full overrides the brand. Soft uses radius-sm for sm, radius-md for md/lg; full uses radius-full. The default control radii are independent of panel radii and never change control height or density.

isDisabled.notes: Non-interactive, removed from the tab order. The disabled treatment is PER VARIANT: primary, secondary, outline and danger flatten to the --ui-bg-elevated chip the sheet's Disabled frame draws; ghost keeps no fill and no ring and takes only the disabled ink (--ui-text-disabled), because a control with no chrome at rest turned into a grey slab — the heaviest thing in its row — the moment it disabled (#27).

isBusy.notes: BUSY SWALLOWS ACTIVATION (maintainer decision 2026-10-05, #8). Keeps focus and its place in the tab order, but a click, Enter or Space does nothing: onClick is not called, and a type="submit" button does not submit its form — by click, by Enter on the button, or by Enter in a text field (implicit submission fires a synthetic click at the form's default button, and that click is cancelled). So isBusy is the double-submit guard ON ITS OWN; do not pair isDisabled with it for that. It is still not isDisabled: no disabled styling, no lost focus. Sets aria-busy and aria-disabled="true" (aria-busy alone is not announced on a button by most screen readers, and the control genuinely cannot be activated). The cursor is `progress` and the press-scale is off, because both would acknowledge a press nothing acts on. Shows a 16px spinner IN PLACE OF the leading icon rather than beside it, so the button keeps its width and does not shift the layout under a pointer still resting on it; the spinner is aria-hidden because aria-busy already carries the meaning, and it stops turning under prefers-reduced-motion while staying visibly different from the resting icon. DERIVED — the sheet draws no busy state; it shipped as a prop that announced to assistive tech and showed sighted users nothing, which is worse than not having it.

isIconOnly.notes: Requires aria-label — enforced by the prop types, not by review.

staticTap.notes: Opts out of the press-scale feedback.

icon.notes: Slot. Icons come from griddy-icons only. The component sizes the slot at 16px, the size the sheet draws at every control size. Without that the glyph arrives at whatever the icon library defaults to — griddy hard-codes width/height="24" as attributes — which rendered every icon 50% oversize.

render.notes: Slot: render as this element instead of a <button> — `render={<a href="/contact" />}` or the app's own `<Link>` — for a call to action that navigates (#31). Classes, data attributes and handlers merge onto it. On a rendered element `type` is not set; `isDisabled` becomes aria-disabled + tabIndex -1 + a cancelled click, because an <a> has no disabled attribute.

do: Give every icon-only button an aria-label describing the action, not the glyph.

For a CTA that navigates, pass render={<a href=… />} (or the router's Link). In .astro or server templates, put buttonClassName({ variant, size }) on the <a> and add data-disabled/aria-disabled yourself if it can be disabled.

Use isBusy for in-flight submits: it refuses a second activation AND keeps focus on the button for the round trip. It is the whole double-submit guard — migrating from a `loading` prop that implied disabled is a straight rename.
Pass icons as slots so usage is visible at the call site.
Reach for size="lg" on primary page actions — it is the only size at the 44px touch target.
dont: Do not use isDisabled to indicate loading; the control disappears from the tab order.
Do not pair isDisabled with isBusy to stop a double submit — busy already refuses activation, and adding disabled only throws the keyboard user's focus away mid-submit.
Do not rely on a click reaching onClick while busy (to cancel, say). A busy button swallows activation; a cancel action is a separate button.
Do not add pointer-events-none to a disabled control — it blocks the tooltip that explains why it is disabled, and the disabled attribute already prevents activation.

Do not nest a Link inside a Button, and do not wrap a Button in an <a> — nested interactive elements are invalid HTML and double-announce to screen readers. For a navigation styled as a button, use `render={<a href=…/>}` (or `buttonClassName()` in markup React does not own) — one element, one role.
Do not add a second filled primary to the same view; the brand fill is the one loudest thing on a screen.
Do not restyle a variant with className to invent a fifth one; add it here instead.

a11y.role: button (native element)

keyboard.does: Activates — unless busy, when it does nothing (and does not submit a form). Native implicit activation, verified in a real browser (button.browser.test.tsx) — not re-implemented. Note the UA applies `:active` only instantaneously for Enter, so the press-scale is not perceptible; the focus ring is the static cue and the resulting action is the acknowledgement.
Activates on release, and holds the `:active` press-scale while down. Busy: does nothing, and no press-scale.
Moves in and out. isDisabled removes it from the sequence; isBusy does not.

keyboard.key: Enter (in a field of the same form)
keyboard.does: Implicit submission targets the form's default button. If that is a busy submit Button, nothing is submitted — the synthetic click it receives is cancelled.

a11y.pointer: cursor: pointer is set explicitly. A <button> has no pointer cursor by default — the UA default is the arrow and Tailwind's preflight adds nothing — so omitting it silently costs the only pre-click affordance. Disabled shows not-allowed.
a11y.hover: Each type's own step: primary and danger deepen their fill, secondary and outline firm their edge, inverse fills the band's -hover step. ghost FILLS — with the sheet's --ui-bg-elevated on the page, and with --ui-bg-hover inside any ancestor that paints bg-elevated (a card, a dock, a panel), because there the sheet's fill is the ground's own colour and the hover vanished. The surface declares its ground by painting it; no prop. The token test holds bg-hover a step past bg-elevated in every seed and both schemes.
a11y.pressed: PAINTS NO NEW FILL on the edge-on-nothing types. secondary firms its ring (default -> strong) and takes its ink to primary; outline takes its ink to primary; ghost keeps the fill hover already painted and darkens its ink. A pointer press is necessarily also a hover, so :hover's treatment is already applied and :active adding a second, darker fill is what produced a neutral chip on a control the design draws with no fill in any state. primary and danger are FILLS by definition and keep theirs. The ink step is required, not decorative: §8 forbids motion being the only feedback channel, and the press-scale is the motion.
a11y.disabled: PER VARIANT. primary, secondary, outline and danger fill and ring with --ui-bg-elevated, which is what the sheet's Disabled frame draws — the control flattens rather than becoming a filled chip. It shipped one step darker (bg-sunken). ghost keeps its absence of chrome — no fill, a transparent ring — and takes only --ui-text-disabled, so an unavailable quiet action stays the quietest thing in its row (#27). Uses the native disabled attribute only; pointer-events are deliberately left alone so a tooltip can still explain why the control is unavailable. Hover and press states are gated behind `not-data-disabled:` — Button stamps data-disabled on whatever element it renders, because `:enabled` never matches an <a> and gated every link's hover away (#31).
a11y.busy: aria-busy="true" plus aria-disabled="true", focusable, in the tab order, activation refused. aria-disabled is deliberate: activation really is unavailable, and aria-busy on a button is silently ignored by most screen readers, so without it AT would present a control that does nothing as operable. The label ("Saving…") carries the why. Note for consumers' tests: Playwright treats aria-disabled as not-enabled, so `userEvent.click` on a busy button waits forever — dispatch `.click()` to assert that it refuses.
a11y.focus: focus-visible only, drawn as a 2px outline offset 2px in --ui-focus-ring-color (5.6:1 against the page). Sits on the outline layer so no variant's resting ring can be mistaken for it, and forced-colors mode keeps it.

a11y.hitArea: sm is exactly 24px, the WCAG 2.5.8 floor, at every density — compact cannot go under it. lg is 44px, the recommended touch target, at default and comfortable density only: compact lg is 40px, so a compact screen meant for touch should reach for comfortable instead. md sits between at 32px — pair it with generous surrounding space on touch surfaces.

needsDesign: Every button COMPOSED in the file is fully rounded, while the stated model makes soft the default. The compositions and the model disagree, and one of them needs updating — the model is now explicit in the sheet's own legend, so the compositions are the side that is out of date.

TWO SHEETS NOW EXIST and they disagree. The handoff sheet (Handoff - Components, XK7-0) was rebuilt to match this implementation: all five types against rest, hover, pressed, focus-visible and disabled, plus busy, full width, a token map and a dark matrix. The older component sheet (Components, E3V-0) is what the earlier notes here described. Retire E3V-0 or reconcile it — a handoff with two spec sheets is a handoff with none.

E3V-0 draws NO pressed row at all: eleven frames, five variants, their five hovers, and disabled. Every active treatment was therefore derived, and what the derivation reached for was --ui-bg-active, a value appearing ZERO times in that artboard. The handoff sheet now draws pressed as shipped — no new fill, a firmer ring and darker ink. Confirm.

E3V-0's Outline and Outline Hover rows disagree with what ships in two ways. Its hover edge is border-default, which measures 2.14:1 and fails the 3:1 SC 1.4.11 asks of the boundary this variant exists to provide, so border-control ships instead. And its hover LIGHTENS the ink (text-primary at rest, text-muted on hover), the opposite direction from every other variant; ours keeps the ink and firms the ring. Both need a decision.

E3V-0's Secondary Hover fills with --ui-bg-sunken and rings itself with that same value. What ships has no hover fill at all: the ring firms and the ink darkens. Two different pictures of one state, and only one can be right. The handoff sheet draws the shipped version.
The soft radius at lg is derived from md (8px). The sheet draws soft only at sm.
No busy state is drawn; the spinner is ours. So is the `progress` cursor busy now shows, since busy refuses activation (#8).

The component sheet draws ONE Disabled frame — the elevated chip — for every type. The ghost exception (no fill, no ring, disabled ink only; #27) comes from a product frame (service-portal, Brand Profile › Fonts, each style's Delete), not from the sheet. Draw a disabled ghost in the handoff sheet so the two agree.
Ghost Large draws paddingInline xl where the other three large buttons draw lg. Corrected to lg in Paper — confirm.
docs.motion: Press feedback is scale(--ui-press-scale) with a staticTap opt-out; colour and ring transitions use --ui-duration-fast with --ui-ease-out. Scale is excluded from the transition list so the press snaps. prefers-reduced-motion collapses durations at the token layer and cancels the scale here.

changes.summary: Clarify public variant guidance without maintenance history
Suppress native button appearance so the library ring owns the edge without platform decoration.

Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

ChatSources: inline citation markers, a hover/focus preview anchored to each, and a sources block under the answer — folded to kind discs and a count, open to numbered link rows, or led by source cards. Numbers are list positions shared through ChatSources.Provider; a working StatusMatrix while sources gather; a disabled marker while the answer streams. The marker is allowlisted in check:controls as an inline pill no Button size describes.

ChatRunDock and ChatRunMark: background runs that outlive their turn. The dock sits behind the composer's pill (bg-elevated, radius-lg, inset space-xl), one 32px row per run with a 14px StatusMatrix (Progress when measured, Working otherwise), name, truncating activity, a 40px tabular clock and a named Stop; the mark is the run's line in the thread — started, finished with an action, failed with Retry, or stopped. A named region, never a toast. The rows' matrices hold while the thread has a live edge (`isHeld`), and even when the thread is idle only the FIRST row moves — one live matrix per region, however many runs.

Chat Progress rebuilt on StatusMatrix with ONE moving mark per turn. The CSS ring spinner is gone. New forms: waiting and streaming status rows (the thinking row's matrix hands over in place to its ending — failed and stopped keep the same element); reasoning under a five-line capped, faded body; a thought chain on a 16px node lane with kind glyphs, chips, prose, one level of branches, a failed status with Retry and a 40px tabular clock; parallel lanes drawn as the activity pill's box (glyph, 104px name, activity, clock, chevron) that open to their own chain. Only the deepest running node moves — the root when parallel or folded, none when isHeld — and a run that finishes while mounted folds to its receipt. Stop past ~30 s and a stoppedText ending. The geometry spec now measures the lane pill (sheet 4040-0) instead of the old step list.

migration.manual: BREAKING: steps take `status: "done" | "current" | "pending" | "failed"` with optional icon, duration, chips, detail and one level of `steps`; the spinner and its data-slot are gone (the row's mark is a StatusMatrix with data-slot="status-matrix"). Pass isHeld to every ChatProgress in a turn except the live edge. Rows are 17.55px at the body-sm role's leading rather than the old 16px.

changes.summary: A ghost Button's hover is visible on an elevated surface. Its hover fill is the sheet's --ui-bg-elevated, drawn on the page, so inside any surface that already paints bg-elevated — a Card, a Chat Tasks card, the run dock, a lane pill, a popover panel — the hover was the ground's own colour (1.00:1) and nothing happened. Inside an ancestor that paints bg-elevated the ghost now steps to --ui-bg-hover, the next rung of the interaction ramp that the token test holds past elevated in every seed and both schemes; on the page it is unchanged. Asserted in a real hover, both schemes, as the hovered fill DIFFERING from its ground, which failed on the old code. The class reader shared by check:utilities, check:strokes, check:type-roles and check:token-consumers did not know Tailwind's `in-*` variant and skipped such classes whole — probed with a typo that stayed green — and now strips it.

Button variant="inverse" draws its focus outline in --ui-text-inverse, the band's own ink, instead of --ui-border-focus. The page's focus colour measured 2.88:1 against --ui-bg-inverse in light and 1.37:1 in dark (blue-80 on the paper band of the warm-ink dark ramp), so a keyboard-focused inverse button had no visible ring in dark. The band's ink is 15.53:1 in both schemes and needs no new token. Closes the Measured gap on the Inverse grounds sheet (#36) for Button; other controls placed on an inverse band still take the page's focus colour. Browser test added.

Button's hover, press and disabled styles are gated on a `data-disabled` attribute Button stamps itself, not on `:enabled`/`:disabled` — `:enabled` never matches an <a>, so a link-rendered Button had no hover at all (#31). The native disabled attribute is still set on <button>. Same specificity as before.

migration.manual: A consumer className that overrides Button's disabled look with `disabled:…` no longer wins; write it as `data-disabled:…` (ChatComposer's send control did exactly this and was updated). Overrides of hover/press written as `enabled:hover:…` should become `not-data-disabled:hover:…`.

changes.summary: Button takes a `render` slot (`render={<a href=…/>}` or the router's Link) so a CTA that navigates is one element with every state intact, and exports `buttonClassName()` — the identical recipe — for markup React does not own, such as .astro templates (#31). On a rendered element isDisabled becomes aria-disabled + tabIndex -1 + a cancelled click.

variant="inverse": outline's shape for --ui-bg-inverse bands (footer, dark CTA band) — ring and label in --ui-text-inverse, hover/press on --ui-bg-inverse-hover/-active, disabled in --ui-text-inverse-muted. Follows the band when the scheme flips; not for media grounds (#36).

A disabled ghost Button keeps no fill and no ring and takes only the disabled ink. Closes #27. Every disabled Button flattened to the same chip — bg-elevated with a matching elevated ring — which is right for primary, secondary, outline and danger, the types that have a fill or an edge to flatten. A ghost has neither at rest, so the shared chip turned it into a grey block the moment it disabled: in service-portal's Brand Profile › Fonts, the ghost Delete that is disabled for the sole heading/body provider read as a solid slab on bg-base, the heaviest thing in its row, for an action that is unavailable. The product's Paper frame draws it as ghost text in --ui-text-disabled with no fill and no ring, and that is now the ghost's disabled treatment; the ring stays the ring-transparent it rests with. The disabled treatment is a per-variant map in button.tsx rather than one string. The four chip variants are unchanged.

migration.manual: Visual only — no API change. Disabled ghost buttons lose their grey chip and show only the disabled ink. If you patched this locally (service-portal carried a temporary rule on `[data-slot="button"][data-variant="ghost"]:disabled` in globals.css), delete the patch.

changes.summary: A busy Button now swallows activation, so isBusy is the double-submit guard on its own. Closes #8. Busy used to be 'visual only': it set aria-busy, drew a spinner and stayed fully operable, and its doc said never to swap it for isDisabled during submit. That left a gap the first real migration fell straight into: a legacy `loading` prop implied disabled, and an audit of service-portal found ~87 of 93 `loading=` call sites relied on that implication (57 passed no `disabled` at all, 29 bound it to an unrelated validity check) — so a mechanical `loading` -> `isBusy` rename would have reopened double-submit across save, delete, create and publish flows. Maintainer decision (2026-10-05): while isBusy is true the button keeps focus and its tab stop and takes no disabled styling, but a click, Enter or Space does nothing — onClick is not called, and a type="submit" button does not submit its form. That includes implicit submission: Enter in a text field submits through the form's default button by firing a synthetic click at it, and the guard cancels that click, which is the one thing the native `disabled` attribute would otherwise be needed for. The guard is an unconditional wrapper, not composeEventHandlers — a safety invariant a consumer cannot opt out of (CONVENTIONS §5). A busy button now also carries aria-disabled="true": activation genuinely is unavailable, and most screen readers ignore aria-busy on a button, so without it assistive tech would present a control that does nothing as operable. The cursor is `progress` rather than a pointer promising a click, and the press-scale is off while busy. CONVENTIONS §4 is amended to match.

migration.manual: Migrating a legacy `loading` prop that implied disabled: rename `loading` -> `isBusy` and STOP there — do not add `isDisabled={<same pending var>}` beside it. Busy already refuses a second activation and a second submit, and pairing disabled with it throws away the keyboard user's focus mid-submit, which is exactly what busy exists to avoid. Keep an `isDisabled` that is bound to something else (a validity check, a permission): that is a different state and still wanted. Existing isBusy call sites: if anything relied on a click reaching onClick WHILE busy (a cancel-by-clicking-again pattern, say), move that to a separate cancel button — it no longer fires. Tests: Playwright/vitest-browser treat aria-disabled="true" as not-enabled, so `userEvent.click` on a busy button now waits until timeout; dispatch `button.click()` inside act() to assert that it refuses, and assert `aria-disabled` rather than the absence of `disabled`.

changes.summary: Pressing secondary, outline or ghost no longer paints a neutral fill. The Button sheet draws eleven frames — five variants, their five hovers, and disabled — and NO pressed row, so every active treatment was derived; what the derivation reached for was --ui-bg-active (#DAD4CE), a value that appears zero times in the whole Button artboard. An edge-on-nothing control therefore grew a grey chip under the pointer, heavier than any fill the design draws for a button. Press now firms the channels each type already uses and keeps whatever hover painted, because a pointer press is necessarily also a hover: secondary steps its ring default -> strong and its ink to primary, outline takes its ink to primary, ghost keeps hover's fill and darkens its ink. primary and danger are fills by definition and keep theirs. The ink step is required rather than cosmetic — CONVENTIONS §8 forbids motion being the only feedback channel, and the press-scale is the motion. Two RESTING fills were also a step darker than drawn and are corrected the same way: ghost's hover moves from bg-hover (neutral-90) to bg-elevated (neutral-95), and DISABLED moves from bg-sunken to bg-elevated with a matching ring, which is what the sheet's Disabled frame draws. Disabled is the state seen most — a form disables its secondary actions while it submits, so a whole column of them goes grey at once, and at neutral-90 they read as filled chips rather than as flattened controls. The handoff sheet was then rebuilt from this implementation rather than the other way round: anatomy, the three sizes with both shapes, all five types against rest/hover/pressed/focus-visible/disabled, busy, full width, a token map carrying both schemes, and the states matrix again in dark on bg-surface so the interaction ramp can be read as a sequence. Six roles Paper was missing were added to the file so every cell on it is a token rather than a literal: --ui-bg-accent-hover, --ui-bg-accent-active, --ui-bg-accent-subtle-hover, --ui-intent-danger-border, --ui-intent-danger-bg-hover and --ui-text-on-danger-subtle.

migration.manual: Visual only — no API change. Pressed secondary and outline buttons lose their grey fill and gain a firmer edge and darker ink; pressed ghost keeps the hover fill it already had. Hovered ghost buttons and ALL disabled buttons are one step lighter, matching the sheet. If you relied on the pressed fill as a selected-looking state, that was never a designed state: use Badge's `selected` variant or a real toggle.

changes.summary: One shape vocabulary across Button and Badge: `full` and `soft`. Button's `pill` becomes `full` and Badge's `pill`/`rounded` become `full`/`soft` — the same two shapes had two different names in the only two components that have them, and `pill` named the DRAWING where every other value in this system names the token. The redrawn Button sheet settles it in its own legend: 'Button variants: Default (soft border radius), Rounded Full'. Both type-test files keep a compile-time assertion that the old names no longer compile, so they cannot drift back in quietly.

migration.manual: Rename `shape="pill"` to `shape="full"` on Button and Badge, and `shape="rounded"` to `shape="soft"` on Badge. Defaults are unchanged in behaviour: Button still defaults to soft, Badge still defaults to the fully rounded shape (now spelled `full`).

changes.summary: Labelled Button sizes now own the 44/32/24px heights promised by the component documentation and approved design. Padding plus line-height previously computed to 40/28/20px, leaving every size four pixels short and the small control below the 24px WCAG 2.5.8 target-size floor. Explicit heights make the geometry and hit area invariant while preserving the existing inline padding, label metrics, variants and icon-only sizes.

migration.manual: No API change. Review dense layouts and visual baselines: every labelled Button is four pixels taller. Icon-only Button dimensions are unchanged.

changes.summary: Protect button state contracts

Button rebuilt against the stated model — five types, three sizes, two shapes, five content arrangements — and the single most consequential correction is that SOFT IS THE DEFAULT. The shape axis shipped inverted, with pill as the default and soft opt-in, so every Button placed anywhere came out fully rounded and the soft control the design actually draws looked like an invention each time it was needed. That one inversion is the whole reason Header, Sheet, Calendar and Card Sorting each hand-rolled a control: none of them could have got it from Button. The soft radius SCALES rather than being one value — 4px at small (the sheet's own Small Rounded column) and 8px at medium and large (as Header, Sheet and Calendar draw their 32px controls); only large is derived, and it follows medium rather than inventing a third step. `outline` joins the type list as a stronger edge on the same transparent ground as secondary, DERIVED because the sheet draws no Outline row: secondary keeps border-subtle and outline takes border-default, the next step up ADR 0010's stack. Two further divergences found by measuring the sheet rather than reading it: the outline is 1.5px at EVERY size and md/sm shipped at ring-1, and large draws paddingInline space-lg where we shipped space-xl (three of the four large buttons agree on lg; Ghost's xl was the outlier and is corrected in Paper). The 32px fill-with-no-edge control is NOT a button type — every button is either a fill with a matching edge or an edge on nothing — so it becomes `@/lib/chrome-control`, one exported recipe replacing four independent reinventions, and Calendar's version gains the --ui-bg-elevated fill it had simply been missing. Card Sorting's grip becomes a real ghost Button (its bespoke radius was the medium soft value at a small size, matching nothing). Banner's dismiss stays bespoke and is allowlisted with its reason: it inherits the banner's intent ink, which every Button variant would override.

migration.manual: BREAKING: `shape` defaults to `soft` instead of `pill`, and the value `"rounded"` is renamed `"soft"`. Any button that should stay fully rounded must now say shape="pill" explicitly. Buttons also gain a 1.5px ring at md and sm (was 1px) and large loses 8px of horizontal padding.

changes.summary: Storybook 10 lands as an isolated workspace app (apps/storybook) with addon-a11y configured to FAIL rather than warn. It renders the same output a consumer gets: styles/tokens.generated.css is emitted from @bydiorama/tokens (toCss + toTailwindTheme), never hand-authored, so a token change moves every story. Stories live beside their components in registry/ and are kept out of consumers by check:manifest, which now rejects any attempt to list a story/test file as distributable. Button ships Matrix, States, WithIcons and the mandatory BrandThemed story (AGENTS.md step 4). Verified end to end: the built stylesheet contains .bg-accent{background-color:var(--ui-bg-accent)} — a live custom-property reference, not a baked hex — which is what lets a brand scope re-skin utilities with no rebuild.

migration.manual: None for consumers — Storybook is a devDependency of this repo and can never be installed by `shadcn add`, because distribution is driven by ui.manifest.json rather than by the folder tree.

changes.summary: cn() now runs an extended tailwind-merge configuration that knows the system's own utility namespaces. Unconfigured, the merger guessed at custom classes and silently DELETED some: text-button-sm (a font size) was treated as conflicting with text-ink-on-accent (a colour), so every md/sm button label rendered at the body's 16px instead of the design's 12px — no build error, no missing CSS, the class simply never reached the DOM. The same gap also broke the CONVENTIONS §5 forwarding guarantee for spacing: a consumer's px-6 failed to displace a component's px-md. The config registers the type roles as font-size, ink-* as text-colour, the spacing step names on the shared scale, and the custom weight/leading names. Regression-pinned by computed-style browser tests (16/12/12px per size). Separately diagnosed from the same report: declared weights matched the design exactly — the perceived weight difference was macOS subpixel rendering; app roots now set antialiased smoothing + font-synthesis: none (new CONVENTIONS §6 rule).

migration.manual: Re-add @bydiorama/cn (and re-check any local copy): without the merge config, any component mixing the system's text sizes and text colours loses one of them at runtime. Apps should also add the §6 root smoothing/synthesis declarations.

changes.summary: Button had no pointer cursor: a <button> defaults to the UA arrow and Tailwind v4's preflight adds nothing, so the compiled stylesheet contained no cursor rule at all. Adds cursor-pointer and disabled:cursor-not-allowed, asserted against COMPUTED style in a real browser. Also drops disabled:pointer-events-none — the native disabled attribute already blocks activation and removes the control from the tab order, while suppressing pointer events only makes the control unhoverable and kills the tooltip explaining why it is unavailable; hover/press states are now gated behind `enabled:` instead. Investigated alongside a report that Enter did not activate: a browser test proves Enter DOES activate (no functional defect). The perceived failure was the absence of an observable response — the Playground story had no handler, and Enter's activation is instantaneous so the :active press-scale is imperceptible, unlike pointer-press and Space-hold. Stories now log every activation and a dedicated Activation story demonstrates all three routes.

migration.manual: Re-add @bydiorama/button to pick up the cursor and disabled-state changes. Anything that relied on disabled buttons being unhoverable should note they are now hoverable by design, so a tooltip can explain the disabled state.

changes.summary: Code review of the compiled stylesheet found two invisible-at-runtime bugs. (1) The focus ring never rendered: `outline-none` set --tw-outline-style to none, which `focus-visible:outline-2` then inherited — a 2px ring drawn in style:none, i.e. a WCAG 2.4.7 failure at a perfect contrast ratio. The base outline-none is removed entirely; the UA outline needs no suppressing because our focus-visible rules override it. (2) Motion tokens were disconnected: the bracket arbitrary-value syntax `duration-[--x]` emits the bare property name (`transition-duration: --ui-duration-fast`), which is invalid CSS — transitions ran at 0s and the press-scale never applied. Switched to the parens syntax `duration-(--x)` which compiles to var(--x). Both regressions are pinned by computed-style browser tests (transitionDuration 0.12s, easing curve, outline solid/2px/opaque on focus), added failing-first.

migration.manual: Re-add @bydiorama/button. Any local component using `duration-[--x]`/`ease-[--x]`/`scale-[--x]` has dead CSS — switch to the parens form. Any component pairing `outline-none` with a focus-visible outline has an invisible focus ring.

changes.summary: Repo-local `add-component` skill distills the validated Button pipeline into the standard order of operations for every future component: Paper spec via computed values, tokens before component, the API/a11y checklist, typed doc, mandatory BrandThemed story, type tests plus real-browser interaction tests, manifest/ledger, and the probe discipline (a gate is not evidence until it has been watched failing). Codifies the ratchet rule: review findings graduate to a type, then a CI gate, then a lint rule, and only last to prose. CI extended to run the utilities gate, Playwright browser tests and the Storybook build (a11y at error severity). Validation fixes alongside: button.doc.ts no longer references the not-yet-existing render slot and now records the isBusy visual-treatment gap explicitly instead of implying one exists.

migration.manual: None for consumers. Contributors: invoke the add-component skill at the start of any component work; AGENTS.md §Adding a component now points at it.

changes.summary: First component. Four variants (primary/secondary/ghost/danger), three sizes (44/32/24px), pill or rounded, icon-only and full-width forms, transcribed from the approved Buttons sheet. isIconOnly requires aria-label at the type level; isBusy is visual-only and keeps focus where isDisabled does not. Resting ring is an inset ring so focus keeps the outline layer (survives forced-colors). Ships with a typed doc file and compile-time contract tests. Prerequisites landed with it: Tailwind v4 @theme inline emitter (the remaining Phase 1 emitter), React devDependencies, and an @/ path alias so registry items type-check through the same import specifiers a consumer uses.

migration.manual: New item — nothing to migrate. Consumers install with `npx shadcn add @bydiorama/button`; it pulls in the `cn` lib item and expects react and griddy-icons as peers.

items.name: calendar
items.title: Calendar
items.lead: Browses dates and makes a selection with a pointer or keyboard.

docs.lead: Browses dates and makes a selection with a pointer or keyboard.
docs.name: Calendar
docs.summary: A month grid for picking one date, with month and year selects in its header. Ours rather than a library's (ADR 0012): the hard parts are the ARIA grid and the keyboard contract, and both are decisions this system has to own. Month and weekday names come from Intl, so a consumer in another locale gets their own without this library shipping a translation table.

anatomy.notes: The card: w-80, p-lg, radius-lg, bg-surface with shadow-sm. Sets --ui-calendar-view-height (292px), the height all three panels share.
Previous button, the two selects, next button. mb-lg.
The visible month and year, VISUALLY HIDDEN and aria-live: the two triggers name themselves, so without it an arrow press changes the date silently.
32px chrome controls. They step whatever panel is open — a month, a year, or a page of years — and their names change with it.
The month and year triggers, gap-xs.
Disclosures at h-6. aria-expanded plus a chevron that flips; the open one is inked text-link, so state is never colour alone. data-open for styling.
role=listbox replacing the grid IN PLACE, at the grid's own height. Months are one column, years are three.
role=option, min-h-8. Carries data-selected and data-current, drawn exactly as the day grid draws selected and today.
role=grid, 7 columns, gap-xs. Rows and cells use display:contents so the grid template reaches the days.

role=columnheader. Shows 'Sun', named 'Sunday'. Carries mb-sm, which with the grid's 4px gap makes the 12px separation the sheet draws — the row is display:contents, so the margin cannot live on the row.
A square button on bg-elevated. Carries data-selected and data-today.
A leading or trailing empty cell. aria-hidden — there is no date there to announce.

docs.composition:
Calendar   label (required)
           value? / defaultValue? / onValueChange?
           month? / defaultMonth? / onMonthChange?
           isDateDisabled? / weekStartsOn?

label.notes: Required — the grid is otherwise announced as 'grid'.

value.notes: Controlled selection. null means nothing is selected; clicking the selected day again clears it.

onValueChange.notes: One callback for select and clear (§1).

month.notes: Controlled visible month — any date within it will do. Omit and the calendar owns it, starting at the selection or today.

onMonthChange.notes: Fires for the arrows, PageUp/PageDown, and an arrow that walks off the edge of the month.

isDateDisabled.notes: Marks a date unselectable. It sets aria-disabled and stays FOCUSABLE, so a screen-reader user can still read it — a date they cannot reach is one they cannot be told the reason for.

today.notes: Which day is marked as today. The clock is an input this component reads without being asked, and an untestable one — the visual baseline pinned month and value and still failed the next morning, because the ring had moved a cell overnight. Also the honest hook for a server render or a non-local timezone.

weekStartsOn.notes: 0 = Sunday, as the sheet draws it. Changing it re-lays the leading blanks, not just the header row.

do: Give the calendar a label describing what the date is for.
Use isDateDisabled for ranges rather than filtering days out — a missing cell breaks the grid's geometry and the arrow keys with it.
Let the arrows walk off the edge of a month; the grid follows, which is what stops the last week being a dead end.
dont: Do not use the `disabled` attribute for unavailable dates. aria-disabled keeps them readable; `disabled` removes them from the keyboard entirely.
Do not hard-code weekday or month names — Intl already knows them, in the user's locale.
Do not give every day a tab stop. One roving stop is the whole point of the grid pattern.

a11y.role: grid, with columnheader cells for the weekdays and one gridcell per date. Blank cells are aria-hidden.
a11y.name: The `label` prop. Each day is named in FULL ('Monday, 3 August 2026') — a bare '3' locates nothing.

keyboard.does: Enters the grid at exactly one day — a roving tabindex, not 31 stops.
Moves by a day, crossing into the previous or next month when it runs off the edge.
Moves by a week.
First and last day of the WEEK, not of the month.
Previous and next month, keeping the day of the month.

Selects the focused day, or clears it if it was already selected. Native — every day is a real button. In a month or year list it chooses the option; role=option cannot contain a button, so activation is implemented rather than inherited.
Closes the month or year list and returns focus to the trigger that opened it.

Up/Down by a row — one month, or three years — and Left/Right by one. Clamped at the ends rather than wrapped: a year grid that jumps from 2039 to 2013 reads as a bug, and the header arrows page the window anyway.

a11y.focus: The roving stop follows ACTUAL focus, not only clicks: a screen reader can move into any cell without clicking, and the arrows must continue from where the user really is. Opening a select moves focus into it at the current value and centres that row; closing it returns focus to the trigger, so no panel swap ever drops focus on the body.

needsDesign: Today is now drawn (Paper, Components - Handoff, Audit #9): a 1px outline in --ui-border-control, which clears 3:1 against the calendar's surface (3.04:1 light / 4.28:1 dark on the 2026-11-03 warm-ink ramp). It was --ui-border-default at 2.09:1 light / 1.72:1 dark. Carries to the month and year lists.

The month list fills June while its own header reads August, so the sheet does not say whether the fill marks the VISIBLE month or the selected date's month. Shipped as the visible one, mirroring the day grid where the fill is the selection and the outline is today.

The year grid's window is 27 years centred on the visible year, and the header arrows page it a screenful at a time. The sheet draws one static screenful, so the range and the paging step are both derived.
The month and year triggers are 24px tall — SC 2.5.8's floor exactly, because the sheet's header row is 32px overall and a taller trigger would push the arrows out of line.
knownGaps: The month and year lists replace the grid IN PLACE rather than opening a Select. Inside DatePicker the calendar is already a popover, and a popover over a popover is two surfaces where the sheet draws one.

The sheet draws a 1.5px border on the selected month row on top of its fill. Not shipped: --ui-bg-accent on --ui-bg-accent-subtle measures 1.3:1, so it identifies nothing the fill and the bold weight do not already carry, and the day grid draws no such border.

An open month or year list is closed by Escape or by its own trigger, not by clicking elsewhere in the card. It is a disclosure that swaps content in place rather than an overlay, and outside-press dismissal on one would be surprising — but the card's padding is a dead zone, which is worth knowing.
One date only. No range, no multiple selection; the sheet draws neither.
One month at a time. No two-up view.
Today is marked with an outline rather than anything the sheet draws — it draws no today state at all, and a calendar without one is disorienting. DERIVED; confirm with design.
No min/max props. `isDateDisabled` covers the same ground and is the more general of the two, but a range would be more convenient.

Day cells are square and fill the column, so their size follows the card's width rather than a token. At the sheet's 320px card they are 38px, comfortably over SC 2.5.8's floor, but a narrower container would shrink them.
docs.motion: Day cells and the weekday header transition `background-color` and `color` at --ui-duration-fast with --ui-ease-out; the previous/next month arrows take theirs from `@/lib/chrome-control` rather than declaring their own. The month CHANGE is not animated — a new grid replaces the old one in place, so nothing slides between months.

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

useControllableState no longer reads or writes refs during render, so it passes eslint-plugin-react-hooks@7 `recommended` (react-hooks/refs) in consumer apps (#35). onChange is synced in an insertion effect; the controlled/uncontrolled switch warning moved to an effect; the setter depends on isControlled instead of a ref, so it is stable for every caller that does not switch modes (which already warns). The library now lints its own registry/ with the same preset, which also moved Calendar's focused-date correction from an effect to render-time derivation, useIsStuck's reset to its cleanup, and three ref-through-helper call sites (DatePicker, MultiSelect, CardSorting) to direct attributes.

Calendar's today marker (and the current month/year in the pickers) is outlined in --ui-border-control instead of --ui-border-default, which measured 2.09:1 — under the 3:1 SC 1.4.11 asks of a state indicator. Now 3.04:1 light / 4.05:1 dark (#9 audit sheet).

check:motion joins the gate list, and every animating component now documents its motion. The gate rejects a literal duration or easing in registry/ (a discipline that was already perfect — zero hard-coded durations across 26 files — and had nothing keeping it that way), transition-all (CONVENTIONS section 6 has said this since the beginning and nothing enforced it), a keyframe with no reduced-motion guard, and an animating component with no top-level motion: note in its doc. It reads lib recipes alongside components as check:overlays does, so Header's motion is found in @/lib/chrome-control where it actually lives rather than reported as absent. 27 doc files gain a motion: note describing what moves, what drives it and what reduced motion does to it; Sheet's and ImageUpload's existing notes are PROMOTED out of a11y to the top level, where Button already had its, because motion is a description of what a component does rather than solely an accessibility concern and a field meaning one thing at two depths stops being findable. ImageUpload's note is corrected while being promoted: it credited the token layer with stopping its spinner, and what actually stops it is the motion-safe: variant. Two findings are recorded in the notes rather than fixed: Sidebar's collapsible section snaps via the hidden attribute where Accordion animates the identical interaction against Base UI's published height, and Banner reaches for transition-colors where the rest of the library enumerates properties. No component's rendered motion changes; no .tsx is touched.

migration.manual: Documentation only — every change is inside a *.doc.ts, and no component's classes or rendered motion moved. If you consume the doc files and read `a11y.motion`, it has moved to the top-level `motion` key on Sheet and ImageUpload; Button was already there and the other 27 are new.

changes.summary: Clamp calendar month navigation

The weekday header row was separated from the first week by the grid's 4px gap, where both artboards draw `margin-bottom: var(--ui-space-md)` — 12px — on that row (DZO-0 and JNV-0). Shipped since Calendar did, invisible to every gate: the utilities all resolved, the contrast was right, and the visual baseline recorded the defect as the reference. Found by measuring the gap in Chromium while reviewing the month/year selects, because the missing 8px was also what made a select panel resize the card by 9px on open. Fixed with mb-sm on the weekday CELLS — the row is display:contents, so a margin on the row itself would do nothing — giving 4 + 8 = 12. The card is 8px taller and both baselines were re-recorded and looked at.

Calendar takes a `today` prop, defaulting to the real clock. Found by the visual gate failing on two Calendar baselines after a change that touched neither Calendar nor anything it imports: the date had rolled over at midnight and the today ring had moved one cell. The visual case already pinned `defaultMonth` and `defaultValue` with a comment saying a baseline of 'this month' fails tomorrow — the pin was simply incomplete, because the clock is an input the component read without being asked and no prop could override it. That is a scheduled failure, not a flake: it would have turned CI red every single day once the visual project moved onto a runner, and a baseline that rots on a schedule is worse than one that is wrong, because it trains people to re-record without looking. The prop is also the honest hook for a server render or a non-local timezone, where the browser's midnight is not the user's. Tests assert all three behaviours: the prop decides the marked cell, omitting it still tracks the real clock, and a pinned today does not follow the visible month — paging to September clears the ring entirely rather than landing it on another cell.

Calendar's header is now the sheet's two dropdowns rather than a heading, closing the gap recorded when it shipped ('there is no Select yet, and a control that looks interactive and is not is worse than plain text'). They do not open a Select: they replace the day grid IN PLACE at its own height, because inside DatePicker this card is already a popover and a popover over a popover is two surfaces where the sheet draws one. Each is a listbox with its own roving tab stop — role=option cannot contain a button, so Enter and Space are implemented rather than inherited — opening moves focus to the current value and centres it, Escape and choosing both return focus to the trigger, and the ends clamp rather than wrap. The month list is one column, the year grid three, 27 years centred on the visible year with the header arrows paging a screenful; those arrows now step whatever panel is open and their accessible names change with it, because a button labelled 'Previous month' that moves a year is a lie a screen reader cannot catch. The month/year heading survives as a visually-hidden aria-live region: the two triggers name themselves, so without it an arrow press would change the date in silence. The grid is UNMOUNTED rather than `hidden` when a select is open — the attribute's UA rule loses to the author-origin `display: grid`. Selected and current are drawn as the day grid draws selected and today (fill, outline) rather than as the sheet's two 1.5px borders: accent on accent-subtle measures 1.3:1 and identifies nothing the fill and bold weight do not. Trigger type is text-button-lg, NOT the sheet's title-sm, which is a fluid clamp() role and computes to ~12px inside this fixed 320px card.

migration.manual: calendar-heading is now visually hidden and no longer an <h2> — it is a live region, not a document heading. Anything styling or querying it as visible text needs the two trigger slots instead. The prev/next aria-labels are no longer always 'Previous month'/'Next month'; they follow the open panel.

changes.summary: Calendar — a month grid for picking one date, built here rather than on a date library (ADR 0012) because the hard parts are the ARIA grid and the keyboard contract, and both are decisions this system has to own. One roving tab stop rather than 31; arrows by day and by week; Home and End across the WEEK, not the month; PageUp and PageDown by month; and an arrow that walks off the edge carries the grid with it, so the last week of a month is not a dead end. The roving stop follows ACTUAL focus rather than clicks alone — a screen reader can move into any cell without clicking, and the first version's arrows carried on from wherever the component last thought it was: focus day 10, press Right, land on 16. Caught by a test that focused a day and pressed an arrow. Date arithmetic runs at 12:00 local: midnight plus 24 hours is not reliably the next day across a DST transition, and noon has twelve hours of slack in both directions. addMonths normalises to day 1 first, so the 31st plus a month is February rather than the 3rd of March. Month and weekday names come from Intl, so a consumer in another locale gets their own without this library shipping a translation table it would have to maintain; weekday headers show 'Sun' and are NAMED 'Sunday'. Unavailable dates take aria-disabled and stay focusable, because a date a screen-reader user cannot reach is one they cannot be told the reason for. Design defects corrected in Paper: weekday headers were drawn in --ui-text-disabled, which is not only the wrong role for a label that is not a disabled control but measures under 2:1 on that surface; the selected day was a raw --ui-blue-90; letter-spacing was a raw positive 0.26px where the system tracks -0.02em; and three margins and two gaps were raw pixels. One contract gap the component exposed: --ui-text-primary on --ui-bg-accent-subtle had never been audited, because nothing had put ink on that fill before — it is now in CONTRAST_PAIRS at 13.88:1 light and 6.66:1 dark. The sheet draws month and year as dropdown buttons; there is no Select in this system yet, so they render as a heading rather than shipping a control that looks interactive and is not.

items.title: Card
items.lead: Groups related content and its actions on a surface.

docs.lead: Groups related content and its actions on a surface.
docs.name: Card
docs.summary: A titled surface that groups related controls. Renders a <section> with a real heading, so a card is navigable structure rather than a styled div. Its surface is deliberately identical to Popover's panel.

anatomy.notes: A <section>. radius-lg, p-lg, gap-lg, bg-elevated, a border-subtle hairline, and shadow-md unless surface="outlined". No minimum width — the container decides. data-surface names the surface. className lands here (§5).
Title plus optional actions. Takes the unboxed inset.
A real heading element, level chosen by the caller. Truncates rather than wrapping.
Wraps title and subtitle. Takes pt-xs when a subtitle is present, so the title line sits near the centre of a 32px action.

Optional line under the title: body-sm in --ui-text-muted, gap-xs below the title, wraps while the title truncates. A

OUTSIDE the heading, so the heading's name stays the title; the card points aria-describedby at it.
collapsible only. Button ghost, icon-only md, ChevronDown rotating 180° when open; LAST in the actions slot. Named by the title (aria-labelledby), with aria-expanded and aria-controls → the body.

Optional region between header and footer, and what collapsible collapses (hidden, kept in the DOM). Cap its height with className and it scrolls under a bottom Fade (md, ground elevated) bound to the scroller: full while there is more below, easing out over the last 48px of scroll, and inset off a classic scrollbar instead of veiling it.
Slot for controls acting on the whole card. Never wrapped, so each keeps its own accessible name.
The action row, justify-between, inset on all sides. No rule above it — long content is separated by Card.Body's Fade (#10, decided in review). Stays visible when collapsed.

docs.composition:
Card
Card  surface? collapsible? isOpen? onOpenChange?
├─ Card.Header  subtitle? actions? headingLevel?   (+ trigger, when collapsible)
├─ Card.Body    optional; capped → scrolls under a Fade; collapses
│  └─ <boxed children>   flush at p-lg — an Input, a Banner
└─ Card.Footer

surface.notes: raised = hairline + shadow-md. outlined = hairline only, for a house rule of "a border OR a shadow, never both" (issue #10). The hairline stays in both: it is what carries the boundary against the page (bg-elevated alone is 1.11:1).

className.notes: SANCTIONED for adjusting padding, radius, border and shadow, not just for layout. `cn()` is `clsx` + `tailwind-merge` (CONVENTIONS §5), so a conflicting utility in className wins over the root's own — `className="p-md rounded-lg border-0 shadow-none"` produces a smaller, squarer, borderless, flat surface with no source change. This is how a consumer reaches a shape Card does not (yet) expose a dedicated prop for — e.g. a denser inset, or a minimum width (`min-w-80`) where the container does not already set one. Prefer a real prop once a shape is common enough to need one (see knownGaps); until then, this is not a workaround, it is the mechanism.

Header.actions.notes: Slot: an Edit or delete control. Passed through, never wrapped (§3).

collapsible.notes: Makes Card.Body a disclosure (CONVENTIONS §3's boolean-or-config shape). Requires a Card.Header — the trigger's name is the title. Open by default. The footer stays visible when collapsed.

isOpen.notes: Controlled open state, with onOpenChange(isOpen). Only meaningful with collapsible.

Header.subtitle.notes: A line under the title. Kept out of the heading so the accessible name stays the title alone; the card is aria-describedby it. With a subtitle the header aligns items-start.

Header.headingLevel.notes: A prop rather than a guess: a card nested in a page section is rarely an <h2>, and only the page knows its own outline. A wrong level is worse than a plain one.

do: Set headingLevel to match the page outline rather than accepting the default everywhere.
Let boxed children (Input, Banner) sit flush; Header and Footer already carry the inset.
Pass aria-labelledby pointing at the title when the card should be a navigable region.
Use surface="outlined" for a border-only card rather than className="shadow-none".
Reach for className overrides (a different p-*/rounded-*, a min-w-*) when the default surface is the wrong shape — see the className prop entry. This is sanctioned, not a hack.
dont: Do not nest a Card in a Card to get a second surface — that is a Banner or a plain well.
Do not add padding to the header or footer; they already carry the inset, and doubling it breaks the alignment with boxed children.
Do not put the primary action anywhere but the footer's right side; the sheet separates dismiss from commit deliberately.

a11y.role: section. It becomes a named REGION only when the consumer supplies aria-labelledby — an unnamed <section> is generic, so a page full of cards adds no landmark noise.
a11y.name: None by default, deliberately. The heading provides navigable structure on its own.

keyboard.does: The card itself is not focusable; its contents carry their own contracts.

Only while a capped Card.Body actually scrolls: focuses the body, a region named by the card's title, so arrow keys and Page Up/Down can scroll content that has no focusable child of its own (SC 2.1.1). A body that fits is never a tab stop.

contrastPairs.role: title on the card surface
the card surface against the page
contrastPairs.why: the boundary is the border-subtle hairline plus shadow-md, not the fill (ADR 0010)

knownGaps: ALIGNMENT GAP, open: Header and Footer take the unboxed inset, but an Input's own label does not — an Input placed directly in a Card has its label 8px to the left of the card title. The sheet wraps each field label in its own inset frame. Either Input grows an inset-aware mode or Card grows a field wrapper; a wrapper that only re-declares flex-col was tried and removed for earning nothing.
No media/image region — not drawn.
Collapsible open/close has no motion yet: the body toggles with `hidden`. The sheet defers to Accordion's motion and does not draw it.

CONCENTRICITY, accepted: radius-lg (16) over a radius-md (8) boxed child at p-lg (16) is not concentric — §6 would ask for 24. The 2026-10-29 owner review chose 16 for cards, popovers and dialogs platform-wide (issue #40).
The sheet's icon-only action button carries a raw 8px radius and a 16px padding on a 32px box; that is Button's territory and was not transcribed.
docs.motion: The collapsible chevron rotates 180° over --ui-duration-fast (motionMicro, the standalone `rotate` property, as Accordion's). The body itself toggles with `hidden` and does not animate. Card.Body's Fade appears and disappears by opacity (Fade's own motion). Reduced motion collapses both durations at the token layer.

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

A capped Card.Body that scrolls is now a tab stop: a region named by the card's title, with an inset focus outline, so static content past the cap can be scrolled from the keyboard (SC 2.1.1). It is a tab stop only while it actually overflows, which is Sheet.Body's and Table's rule. Found by CI rather than locally: Linux fonts set the States story a few pixels taller than macOS, and only there did the body overflow and axe report scrollable-region-focusable.

A ghost Button's hover is visible on an elevated surface. Its hover fill is the sheet's --ui-bg-elevated, drawn on the page, so inside any surface that already paints bg-elevated — a Card, a Chat Tasks card, the run dock, a lane pill, a popover panel — the hover was the ground's own colour (1.00:1) and nothing happened. Inside an ancestor that paints bg-elevated the ghost now steps to --ui-bg-hover, the next rung of the interaction ramp that the token test holds past elevated in every seed and both schemes; on the page it is unchanged. Asserted in a real hover, both schemes, as the hovered fill DIFFERING from its ground, which failed on the old code. The class reader shared by check:utilities, check:strokes, check:type-roles and check:token-consumers did not know Tailwind's `in-*` variant and skipped such classes whole — probed with a typo that stayed green — and now strips it.

Fade's two-stop linear ramp is replaced by a perceptual one (new lib item fade-ramp): a Gaussian penumbra sampled at seventeen stops, so there is no corner at either end to read as a stripe or a start line, plus a dark-scheme table that leaves the same perceptual fraction of ink visible as light does (light ink under a dark veil kept 53% of its lightness at 0.5 alpha against 46% in light, so dark trails lingered). Depths move one step to 24/48/96 (sm/md/lg) because the eased ramp's first quarter is under 9% alpha — md 48 covers about what linear 32 did, and dissolves where that one ghosted a single line. fadeMask uses the same profile as the paint's complement. Chosen by rendering six curves at four depths over the shipped copy in both schemes (fade.doc.ts, knownGaps 'Ramp research').

migration.manual: Callers that sized a layout around the band's depth (an action slot placed relative to a 32px ramp, a sticky region offset by -32px) re-check against 48px for md, 24px for sm and 96px for lg. To keep an old depth, set --ui-fade-band-depth on the band's style.

changes.summary: Fade gains scrollContainer and ground="affix". Bound to a scroller, the band's strength follows how much content runs past its edge, easing out over the last band-depth of scroll instead of popping off at the last pixel; it insets itself off a classic scrollbar (right, left in RTL, or bottom) instead of veiling the track; and it renders hidden until measured, server-side too. The strength is written to the band's own style, so scrolling re-renders nothing. ground="affix" paints in the translucent pinned-bar role, so the ramp starts at the bar's own alpha. useScrollEdges exports the measurement under it as scrollDistances(). Card.Body, Combobox and ChatWidget now bind their fades this way.

Card, Popover's panel and Modal's surface draw at --ui-radius-lg (16px), not radius-xl (24) — the 2026-10-27/29 owner decision, platform-wide (#40). Modal's radius half of #23 is reversed; its hairline, shadow and title are unchanged. A radius-md boxed child at p-lg is no longer concentric; accepted in review.

migration.manual: Remove any consumer patch that forced [data-slot=card|popover-panel|modal-surface] to --ui-radius-lg (e.g. service-portal's `Registry patch (TEMPORARY)` block).

changes.summary: Card additions from the #10 handoff: `surface="outlined"` (hairline, no shadow), Card.Header `subtitle` (body-sm muted, outside the heading, aria-describedby on the card), Card.Body (a region that scrolls under a bottom Fade when its height is capped — the answer to the footer-divider ask), and `collapsible` / isOpen / onOpenChange (a ghost chevron trigger last in the header actions, named by the title, controlling Card.Body). Card now depends on Button, Fade, motion, use-controllable-state and use-scroll-edges.
Card no longer sets min-w-80 (320px). It takes its container's width, so it fits narrow chat columns and minmax(280px, 1fr) grids instead of overflowing them (#10).

migration.manual: A call site whose parent was narrower than 320px and relied on the card holding 320 should add className="min-w-80" (or set the width on the layout).

changes.summary: Documented, for the first time, that Card's className is sanctioned for overriding padding/radius/border/shadow via tailwind-merge conflict resolution (CONVENTIONS SS5), not just for layout. This mechanism already worked -- nothing in card.tsx changed -- but card.doc.ts never said so, and a consumer-side audit (service-portal, ~105 hand-rolled card surfaces) found real blockers this documents a path around: a whole component family whose house style is border-only (no shadow), and a grid with a track minimum narrower than Card's default 320px. Added a knownGaps entry noting a first-class prop may still be worth it if enough consumers reach for the same override -- tracked as issue #10, not resolved by this entry.

migration.manual: No code change. Consumers who were already using className to override Card's surface were doing something sanctioned, not a hack; card.doc.ts now says so.

changes.summary: Card — a titled surface that groups related controls. Renders a <section> with a real heading rather than a styled div, so a card is navigable structure; the heading LEVEL is a prop with no default guess beyond 3, because only the page knows its own outline and a wrong level is worse than a plain one. It becomes a named region only when the consumer supplies aria-labelledby, so a page full of cards adds no landmark noise. The surface is deliberately identical to Popover's panel and the browser test asserts that as a RELATIONSHIP — radius, padding and border compared between a Card and a Popover rendered together — rather than as numbers that would pass while the two drifted apart. Header and Footer carry the unboxed inset; boxed children sit flush. One wrapper was written and removed: a CardField that only re-declared flex-col gap-sm earned nothing, and the inset question it pretended to answer is a real composition gap, now recorded honestly — an Input dropped into a Card has its own label 8px left of the card title, because Input's label carries no inset and the sheet wraps each field label in its own inset frame. Design defects not transcribed: the title's raw 16px/135%/-0.02em became title-sm plus leading and tracking roles, and the sheet's icon-only action button carries a raw 8px radius and 16px padding on a 32px box, which is Button's territory.

migration.manual: None — new component.
