items.title: CardSorting
items.lead: Reorders items with a pointer or keyboard.

docs.lead: Reorders items with a pointer or keyboard.
docs.name: CardSorting
docs.summary: A reorderable list of cards, with a grip on each row. Reordering works three ways and all three are first-class: a pointer drag, a keyboard lift-and-move, and a no-drag pointer path of click-to-lift then click-to-place. Built here rather than on a drag library (ADR 0012) — the accessible half of this pattern is the half a drag library does not solve, and it is most of the work.

anatomy.notes: A <ul>, named by its label. gap-sm between rows.
An <li> card: radius-lg, bg-elevated, pl-xs pr-lg py-lg. Carries data-lifted and data-dragging.

A real <button> with a 16px grip in a 24px box. Names the row and its position, and reports aria-pressed while holding it. Renders as the row's leading child by default; render CardSorting.Handle anywhere inside the Item to place it yourself, and the leading grip is not drawn.
The row's slot: flex-1, justify-between. Whatever the caller puts there — the sheet draws a title, a Badge and a Switch.
One sr-only live region for all three input methods. role=status, polite, atomic.

docs.composition:
CardSorting                label (required) / order? / defaultOrder? / onOrderChange? / messages?
└─ CardSorting.Item        id (required) / label (required)
   └─ <your content>       a title, a Badge, a Switch — anything
      └─ CardSorting.Handle?  optional — place the grip yourself (a tile's corner);
                              without one the Item draws it at the leading edge

label.notes: Required — 'list, 4 items' says nothing about what is being sorted, and the name is read out with every announcement.

order.notes: Controlled, as item ids. Omit and the list owns it. Ids that are no longer rendered are dropped and newly rendered ones join the end, so a list whose children change does not lose a row or render a hole.

defaultOrder.notes: Uncontrolled starting order. Defaults to the children's source order.

onOrderChange.notes: One callback for every path — drag, keyboard and click-to-place all go through the same move (§1). A cancelled gesture (Escape, or a pointercancel) calls it once more with the order restored, so a consumer that saves on every change ends on the order the person kept.

messages.notes: Every string the list speaks: { handleLabel, lifted, moved, dropped, cancelled }, each a function of { label, position, total, listLabel } returning the phrase. Functions, not strings, because the word order around a number belongs to the translator. All reach assistive technology only — the reason they are props (§9). English defaults; any key left out stays English, so a localised list should pass all five.

Item.id.notes: Stable identity: this is what `order` is made of, so an array index will break the moment anything moves.

Item.label.notes: What the announcements and the handle call this row. Required, because 'item 3 moved to position 1' is not a reorder anyone can follow.

Handle.notes: The grip, placed by the caller anywhere inside an Item — the Brand Profile specimen tile puts it in the tile's top-right corner. Carries the whole keyboard and pointer contract and the row's accessible name; position it with className. Its name, id and pressed state are the contract and are not accepted. Forwards ref to the <button>. An Item with no Handle draws the leading grip exactly as before.

do: Give every item a stable id — a database key, not an index.
Write Item.label as the row's visible title; it is what a screen reader hears on the handle and in every announcement.
Put the row's own controls in the content slot as real elements: the sheet draws a Badge and a Switch, and both keep their own accessible names.
dont: Do not rely on the drag alone. Dragging is one of three paths and the other two are not fallbacks — a pointer user who cannot drag uses click-to-place, and a keyboard user lifts with Space.
Do not put the only copy of a row's meaning in colour or position; the announcement carries the name and the position because nothing else does.
Do not nest interactive controls inside the handle — it is the drag target, and a button inside a button is neither.
Do not render more than one CardSorting.Handle in an Item — the row is named by its handle's id, and two handles share it.
Do not move the grip with CSS on the default handle's data-slot. Render CardSorting.Handle where the design puts it.

a11y.role: A list of list items. The handle is a button with aria-pressed, not a custom role: aria-grabbed is deprecated, and a real button gets Enter, Space and focus for free.
a11y.name: The list from `label`; each row from its handle via aria-labelledby; the handle itself names the row AND its position, so 'Reorder Brand guidelines, position 1 of 4'.

keyboard.does: Reaches each handle in list order.
Lifts the row, and drops it again. aria-pressed reflects which.
Moves a LIFTED row. Does nothing otherwise — a stray arrow must not silently reorder a list someone is reading, and it would fight the browser's scrolling.
Cancels, restoring the order from before the lift. Not 'drop where it happens to be'. Also cancels a POINTER drag in progress, wherever focus is.

a11y.pointer: SC 2.5.7 (Dragging Movements) requires a single-pointer path for every dragging movement, and a keyboard alternative does not satisfy it. Clicking the handle lifts the row; clicking any other row drops it there. A drag starts on the primary button only and becomes a drag after 4px of travel — a press that moves less is a click and lifts. The click that ends a drag does not lift. A pointercancel (a touch gesture taken over by scrolling or the OS) puts the row back and announces 'cancelled' rather than committing the move.
a11y.live: One polite, atomic region announces lift, move, drop and cancel, each with the row's name, its new position and the list's name. A reorder only sighted mouse users can perceive is not a reorder. Every phrase, and the handle's name, comes from `messages` — English by default.
a11y.target: The handle is the sheet's 24px box around a 16px grip — exactly SC 2.5.8's floor rather than comfortably over it. See knownGaps.

contrastPairs.role: the row's own content
the grip
the outline on a lifted or dragging row

needsDesign: The 24px handle is SC 2.5.8's floor exactly, not a comfortable touch target.
No lifted appearance is drawn for the dragged row beyond the active edge.

A Handle placed on a specimen tile has no designed resting fill. A ghost grip on a saturated swatch has nothing to stand on; the PlacedHandle story gives it bg-base, which is a stand-in, not a decision.
knownGaps: The handle is 24px, which is SC 2.5.8's floor exactly and not a comfortable touch target. The sheet draws 24; a 44px target would need design.

The dragged row does not lift visually — no scale, no tilt, no gap where it came from. The list reorders live underneath the pointer instead, which is honest but plainer than the sheet's shadowed card suggests.
No auto-scroll while dragging near the edge of a scrolling container.
No multi-column or cross-list sorting. One vertical list, one axis.
No drop animation — a moved row appears in its new place rather than sliding there. Under prefers-reduced-motion that is the correct behaviour anyway; for everyone else it is a refinement.
The sheet draws the second card in an active state with a --ui-border-focus edge; that is rendered here as an outline rather than a border, so lifting a row cannot shift the layout by a pixel.
docs.motion: Only the ring moves: `outline-color` and `box-shadow` at --ui-duration-fast with --ui-ease-out. A reordered card does NOT animate to its new position — the row appears where it landed. Under prefers-reduced-motion that is the correct behaviour anyway; for everyone else it is a declared refinement rather than a decision (see needsDesign).

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

useControllableState no longer reads or writes refs during render, so it passes eslint-plugin-react-hooks@7 `recommended` (react-hooks/refs) in consumer apps (#35). onChange is synced in an insertion effect; the controlled/uncontrolled switch warning moved to an effect; the setter depends on isControlled instead of a ref, so it is stable for every caller that does not switch modes (which already warns). The library now lints its own registry/ with the same preset, which also moved Calendar's focused-date correction from an effect to render-time derivation, useIsStuck's reset to its cleanup, and three ref-through-helper call sites (DatePicker, MultiSelect, CardSorting) to direct attributes.

CardSorting takes `messages?: Partial<CardSortingMessages>` for every string it speaks: `handleLabel` (the grip's accessible name), and the live region's `lifted`, `moved`, `dropped` and `cancelled`. Closes #20. All five were hard-coded English, and they reach assistive technology only, which is what made them easy to miss: the portal ships in en, sk, cs and de, and a Slovak screen-reader user reordering a palette heard English for every step while the item names around it were Slovak. Each message is a FUNCTION of `{ label, position, total, listLabel }` rather than a string, because every phrase carries a position and a count and the word order around a number is the part a translator owns; the registry's existing localisable strings (Toast's dismissLabel, Drawer's handleLabel, ImageEdit's seven *Label props) are flat strings because none of them interpolates. One object rather than five `*Label` props because they are one vocabulary, and §3 prefers that to prop explosion. English stays the default and any key left out stays English, so existing lists are unchanged; `cancelled` now also receives the row and the position it went back to, which the English default does not use. A new Localised story speaks Slovak. Browser tests assert the handle's name and all four announcements come from the prop, a pointer cancel included, and that a partial object keeps the rest in English; type tests refuse a string message and an unknown key.

Five defects in CardSorting's pointer path, two of which changed the user's data. Closes #21. (1) `pointercancel` called the same endDrag as `pointerup`, so it announced "dropped" and KEPT the move; on touch, pointercancel is the browser taking the gesture away (a scroll takeover, an OS gesture), and the portal saves on settle, so it persisted a move the person abandoned. It now restores the order from before the gesture, calls onOrderChange once more with that order, and announces cancelled. (2) Escape only cancelled a keyboard/click LIFT; during a pointer drag it did nothing. It now cancels a drag the same way, listened for on the document while a drag is live, because a press does not focus a button in every browser (Safari) and the person pressing Escape mid-drag is not thinking about focus. (3) The handle's onClick always toggled lift, and a comment claimed pointerup had already cleared the drag so it would not; the handler never read that state. With the pointer captured on the grip, the click after pointerup lands on it, so every finished drag also lifted the row. A press now becomes a drag only after 4px of travel; a press that moves less is still a click and still lifts (the SC 2.5.7 single-pointer path), and the click that ends a real drag is swallowed. A side effect worth knowing: a plain click no longer announces "dropped" before "lifted" for a drag that never happened. (4) Any button started a drag, including right and middle clicks; only event.button === 0 does now. (5) setPointerCapture throws NotFoundError for a pointer that is no longer active, which broke the handler before the drag began; it and releasePointerCapture are wrapped in try/catch. Each case has a browser test, and all eight new pointer tests fail against the previous component, checked by swapping it back in.

migration.manual: If you added your own restore-on-pointercancel or settle detection around onOrderChange to work around this, remove it: a cancelled gesture now calls onOrderChange with the restored order itself, and doing both restores twice. A drag now needs 4px of pointer travel before rows move.

changes.summary: Adds `CardSorting.Handle`, the grip as a part the caller places anywhere inside an Item. Closes #19. The grip was always the row's first child with no way to move it, and the portal's Brand Profile collections (Colors, Type styles) put it in the top-right corner of a 240px specimen tile, where it reads as "pick this up" and costs no lane; with the grip forced to the leading edge every block gained a 24px gutter the design does not have, and two consumers shipped it that way in one week rather than fight it with CSS. The Handle is the SAME wired button the default grip is (one internal component behind both), so it carries the whole keyboard contract, the pointer drag, the click-to-lift path, aria-pressed and the row's accessible name, and the row stays aria-labelledby it. An Item that contains a Handle draws no leading grip and takes px-lg instead of the pl-xs that made room for one; an Item without one renders exactly as before, and the card-sorting visual baseline is unchanged. Presence is found two ways: a render-time scan of the Item's JSX, so the first paint and a server's HTML never carry two grips sharing an id, and a layout-effect registration for a Handle rendered from inside the caller's own component, which the scan cannot see. Its name, id, type and pressed state are not props; TypeScript cannot refuse a hyphenated aria-label in JSX, so the browser test asserts the handle's own name wins at runtime instead. New PlacedHandle story draws the specimen-tile layout; browser tests cover placement in the corner, the name, keyboard lift-move-drop and a pointer drag through the placed Handle, and the registration path.

migration.manual: Optional. If you repositioned the grip with CSS on [data-slot=card-sorting-handle], render <CardSorting.Handle className="..." /> where the design puts it instead and delete the override; the Item then drops its leading grip and its pl-xs.

changes.summary: check:motion joins the gate list, and every animating component now documents its motion. The gate rejects a literal duration or easing in registry/ (a discipline that was already perfect — zero hard-coded durations across 26 files — and had nothing keeping it that way), transition-all (CONVENTIONS section 6 has said this since the beginning and nothing enforced it), a keyframe with no reduced-motion guard, and an animating component with no top-level motion: note in its doc. It reads lib recipes alongside components as check:overlays does, so Header's motion is found in @/lib/chrome-control where it actually lives rather than reported as absent. 27 doc files gain a motion: note describing what moves, what drives it and what reduced motion does to it; Sheet's and ImageUpload's existing notes are PROMOTED out of a11y to the top level, where Button already had its, because motion is a description of what a component does rather than solely an accessibility concern and a field meaning one thing at two depths stops being findable. ImageUpload's note is corrected while being promoted: it credited the token layer with stopping its spinner, and what actually stops it is the motion-safe: variant. Two findings are recorded in the notes rather than fixed: Sidebar's collapsible section snaps via the hidden attribute where Accordion animates the identical interaction against Base UI's published height, and Banner reaches for transition-colors where the rest of the library enumerates properties. No component's rendered motion changes; no .tsx is touched.

migration.manual: Documentation only — every change is inside a *.doc.ts, and no component's classes or rendered motion moved. If you consume the doc files and read `a11y.motion`, it has moved to the top-level `motion` key on Sheet and ImageUpload; Button was already there and the other 27 are new.

changes.summary: check:dependencies now resolves every `@/` import in a distributed file against the manifest's INSTALL TARGETS, and it found two shipped items importing paths their consumers do not have: multiselect imported '@/ui/badge/badge.tsx' and card-sorting '@/ui/button/button.tsx' — this repo's folder layout, while the CLI installs those files as 'ui/badge.tsx' and 'ui/button.tsx'. Both declared the right registryDependencies, so the CLI delivered the right FILES under the wrong NAMES; nothing compared the two because the gate skipped `@/` with a comment saying 'the alias ones are what registryDependencies is for'. Fixed to '@/ui/badge' and '@/ui/button', with the alias registered in all four resolvers (root tsconfig, storybook tsconfig, .storybook/main.ts, vitest.config.ts) so the path we ship is the path we type-check. Two keys per item in the Vite configs, longer first: Vite matches a string alias as a prefix, so a lone '@/ui/badge' would turn the folder form tests use into '.../badge.tsx/badge.tsx'. The gate checks both halves — an import that matches no target, and a target imported without its registryDependency — and both were probed failing-first.
Compose card sorting interactions

CardSorting — a reorderable list of cards, and the first component in this system whose whole contract is an interaction rather than a surface. Built without a drag library (ADR 0012, AGENTS.md independence), and that is not stubbornness: the accessible half of this pattern is the half a drag library does not solve, and it is most of the work. Reordering has THREE paths and all three are first-class rather than one real one and two fallbacks. A pointer drag; a keyboard lift-and-move on the handle (Space lifts, arrows move, Space drops, Escape restores the order from before the lift — a cancel that leaves the row where the arrows happened to take it is not a cancel); and a no-drag pointer path of click-the-handle-to-lift then click-a-row-to-place, which is what WCAG 2.5.7 (Dragging Movements) actually requires, since a keyboard alternative satisfies 2.1.1 and not 2.5.7. All three go through one move so they cannot diverge, and all three announce through one polite live region carrying the row's name, its new position, the total and the list's name — a reorder only sighted mouse users can perceive is not a reorder. Arrows deliberately do nothing until a row is lifted, so a stray arrow cannot silently reorder a list someone is reading, and so the keys do not fight the browser's own scrolling. The drag index is computed against the OTHER rows' midpoints rather than all of them: including the dragged row makes the target depend on where that row currently sits, which shifts the instant it moves — the index came out one short and the list juddered between two positions while the pointer stood still, caught by a test that dragged to a known midpoint and got the wrong neighbour. Two contract gaps the component exposed, both the 'an unlisted pair is an unchecked pair' failure: --ui-text-muted and --ui-border-focus had never been audited against --ui-bg-elevated, because nothing had drawn ink or a focus edge on that surface before; both are now in CONTRAST_PAIRS / NONTEXT_CONTRAST_PAIRS and measure 5.36:1 and 5.39:1 in light, 5.19:1 and 5.09:1 in dark. The lifted state is drawn as an OUTLINE rather than the sheet's border, so lifting a row cannot shift the layout by the pixel a resting row does not have.

items.title: Chart
items.lead: Makes a comparison visible, with a written takeaway and a table of the data.

docs.lead: Makes a comparison visible, with a written takeaway and a table of the data.
docs.name: Chart
docs.summary: Bars, lines and areas on a value axis, in a frame that always carries its title, its takeaway, a legend for two or more series and a view-as-table toggle. The plot is one tab stop with arrow-key navigation and polite announcements. BarChart, LineChart, AreaChart, ScatterPlot and Histogram are the presets; Chart with Chart.Bars / .Lines / .Areas / .Dots / .Rule children is the composition they are made of.

anatomy.notes: A <figure> named by the title and described by the takeaway. bg-surface, border-subtle, radius-md, 24px inset, 16px between parts. className lands here.
label-md, primary. The `label` prop.
body-sm, muted. The `description` prop: the takeaway a person wrote, not a restatement of the axes. Visually hidden (still the accessible description) when a `headline` is passed.
Optional, under the title, 4px down: an element the caller passes — ChartCard's figure and change. Takes the description's printed place.
Button secondary md, icon-only (ChartTable), aria-pressed. Swaps the plot for the table.

Only for two or more series. Each entry is a native checkbox in a 24px label (8px inline padding, radius-sm, entries flush in a 24px band): checked is shown. An 8px key in the series' marker SHAPE and slot colour, the shape scaled to fill the box on its longer side so no point is clipped, then the name in label-sm 400, secondary ink; a hidden series keeps its key as a 1.5px round-joined outline, inset half the stroke so it stays inside the box and its name drops to muted. Hover fills the entry bg-hover; keyboard focus draws the focus ring on it. Hovering a shown entry dims every other series' marks to 0.32 (the Bar sheet's Interaction row), instantly.

Unchecking an entry removes its series from the marks, the tooltip and the keyboard; the group closes up. The value axis keeps the domain of EVERY series, so the marks that stay do not move. The table still lists it. The last shown series is aria-disabled — focusable, not hideable.

32px column of ticks, label-sm 400, muted, tabular figures, right-aligned and centred on their gridlines. Horizontal bars: a 168px lane of category names instead, one per row, capped at 40% of the row on a narrow frame, truncated (the full name is the span's title and is in the table view).
The one tab stop. 240px (md) or 160px (sm) tall; holds the SVG, the empty message and the tooltip.
One solid 1px line per tick above zero, border-subtle.
The zero line, border-default — one role stronger than the grid.

At most 24px, 2px apart in a group, radius-sm at the data end and square at the baseline. Stacked: one column, 2px surface gaps, only the outer segment rounds. Horizontal: 24px rows 16px apart on a nice 0-based domain, no grid, no baseline. Forced colours: slot 1 solid CanvasText, slots 2–8 a hatch pattern in system colours inside a 1px CanvasText outline.
stroke-thick (2px), round caps and joins, solid. A missing value breaks the line.

The slot's -bg wash under its line; stacked areas are bands between cumulative lines. `wash="fade"` (overlaid areas only) is the Line sheet's fading area instead: the slot's solid colour at 28% at the top of the area, clear at the baseline.

label-sm 600 primary, 16px right of a ringed end marker, in a 96px lane. Up to four series. A name longer than the lane's 80px drops every direct label and end marker (the legend or the title already names the lines), rather than painting past the frame.

A solid 1px border-strong line at a value, with its required label above its end. The Line sheet sets the label in the direct-label lane; it moved above the rule so it cannot collide with a line ending near the same value. When a shown line runs through that place — a series ending a little over its own target — the label sits under the rule instead (data-placement="below"), if that place is clear and inside the plot. Decided from the data, so the server draws the same side.

Chart.Dots: the slot's marker shape at 4px inside a 2px bg-surface ring. Every shape has the area of the 4px circle and sits on its area centroid, so a square (7.09px) does not outweigh a circle and a triangle's centre is the data point, not its box's, so overlapping dots stay apart. The ring is the mark's own outline stroked 4px in the surface, mitred: 2px off every edge, slants and arms included. With areaKey a circle whose AREA follows the measure, 4px to 16px radius, at 85% fill so a dot under it still shows. Forced colours: the same fills as bars.
Chart.Rule at: a solid 1px border-strong line down the plot at a category, a date or a linear x, its label-sm label at the top, beside the line on the side with room (data-placement start | end).
Bars: the hovered or focused band in bg-hover, under the marks.
Lines and areas: a 1px border-default rule at the category, with each series' ringed marker on it.
Keyboard only: 2px border-focus, 2px off the bar (radius 6) or around the point.

bg-elevated, border-subtle, shadow-md, radius-md, 8/12 inset. The category in label-sm 600, then key · name (400, muted) · value (600, primary, tabular). Follows the pointer and the keyboard. aria-hidden: the announcer speaks. Positioned by the behaviour layer against a virtual anchor (the band, or the crosshair), fixed on the --ui-z-tooltip layer so a clipping ancestor cannot cut it, portalled into the chart's own figure so a brand theme still reaches it, and capped to the space the positioner measured.

Category ticks, centred in their band; on lines the first and last align to the plot edges. Thinned so labels never collide: the spacing is the widest name, measured after paint (a character-count guess before it, so the server agrees), plus 8px. A name thinned away is still in the tooltip, the announcement and the table view.
Horizontal bars: the value 8px past each bar's tip, label-sm 600, primary, tabular. Outside the bar on either side of zero.
The data through Table (size sm): the category column, then one numeric column per series.
A polite live region: "category, series, value" on every keyboard move.

docs.composition:
Chart                         label · description · data · x · xLabel · series
├─ Chart.Bars | Chart.Lines | Chart.Areas     the marks (direct children)
│    Chart.Dots areaKey? · areaLabel?         a scatter (xScale="linear"); bubbles with areaKey
│    Chart.Bars orientation="horizontal"      ranked rows: one series, alone
└─ Chart.Rule                 value · label — a solid, labelled threshold across the plot
                              at · label — or an event down it, at a category or a Date

BarChart / LineChart / AreaChart   = Chart with one mark, same props
ScatterPlot                         = Chart xScale="linear" + Chart.Dots (areaKey for bubbles)
Histogram                           = values binned on nice edges + Chart.Bars isAdjacent
BarChart orientation="horizontal"   series must be a one-element tuple, never stacked

label.notes: The visible title and the accessible name.

description.notes: The takeaway, written by a person. A chart without one leaves the reader to compute the point; a screen-reader user hears it first.

data.notes: One row per category, in axis order. Values may be numbers or numeric strings; anything else is a missing value.

x.notes: The field that names each category.

xFormat.notes: A linear x's ticks and values. The tooltip and announcement prefix the value with xLabel ("Share 42%"), since a number on its own does not say what it measures.

xLabel.notes: The first column's header in the table view ("Year").

series.notes: One to eight. A ninth throws: it is never a generated colour (ADR 0023 §5). `slot` pins a series' colour so a filter that removes others cannot repaint it.

isStacked.notes: Stack instead of grouping (bars) or overlaying (lines, areas). Positives stack up, negatives down. `{ isPercent: true }` stacks every category to 100%: marks and the value axis show shares (0–100%), the tooltip and announcement say the share then the value ("42% (1,234)"), and the table keeps the values. A percent stack refuses negative values — a negative has no share of a whole — and re-shares among the series still shown when one is hidden, as the whole is always 100%.

size.notes: 240px with five ticks, or 160px with three — the two plots the sheets draw.

format.notes: For values and ticks. Never a format string (ADR 0023 §1).

locale.notes: Pass it when the server and the reader may differ, or the server's digits hydrate into the client's.

isLoading.notes: Skeleton columns in bg-sunken, no axis text, aria-busy; the frame keeps its height.

emptyText.notes: Shown over a baseline-only plot when `data` is empty.

orientation.notes: BarChart and Chart.Bars. Horizontal is the Bar sheet's ranked rows: names left, value at each tip, no axis or tooltip. The type takes exactly one series and no isStacked; Chart.Bars throws if given more, a rule or a second mark, because grouped and stacked rows are not designed.

xScale.notes: Lines, areas and dots. `linear` reads numbers on a nice axis that need not reach zero and sorts the rows by x (onSelect still reports the index as given): the scatter's axis. `time` places each point at its date, so 1951, 1953 and 1961 are not equally far apart; the x field must hold Dates in ascending order (the chart parses nothing and throws otherwise). Ticks fall on whole UTC years, months or days — UTC so the server and the reader print the same markup — and need not be data points. The table, tooltip and announcement print each point's own date at the coarsest precision that tells them apart ("1957", "Mar 1957", "Mar 4, 1957"). BarChart refuses it in its type.

onSelect.notes: Enter or Space on the focused point, or a click on a category. `row` is the caller's own row; `series` is the focused series' key from the keyboard, and from a click the only series' key or null when the band holds several. The chart keeps and draws no selected state — no sheet draws one; the caller acts (opens a detail, filters a table). Without it the plot keeps the default cursor and Enter does nothing.

headline.notes: A figure and its change under the title (ChartCard passes StatFigure). The description stops being printed and stays the accessible description — decided 2026-11-11 on the Stat tiles and Chart card sheet, because a printed sentence and a figure compete for the same glance.

wash.notes: AreaChart and Chart.Areas. `fade` grades the wash to clear at the baseline so the line reads first. The AreaChart type refuses it with isStacked; Chart.Areas draws stacked bands flat whatever it is given.

do: Write the description as the finding: 'Posters led books every year and peaked in 1972.'
Pin `slot` on every series when the set of series can change.
Use a Rule with a label for a target or threshold.
Use `Chart.Rule at` for an event in time (a launch, a repositioning) — a solid line down the plot with its name at the top, never a dashed one.
dont: Do not draw a dashed line for a target, forecast or secondary series — the solid-strokes rule holds (ADR 0023 §6).
Do not put two measures with different units on one chart; there is no second axis by design.
Do not pass more than five or six series in practice; slots 7 and 8 exist for the cases that truly need them.

a11y.role: <figure> named by the title and described by the takeaway. The plot is a role=group with one tab stop; the SVG is aria-hidden; the table view carries every value.
a11y.name: `label` via aria-labelledby, `description` via aria-describedby, on the figure and on the plot.

keyboard.does: Each legend entry (two or more series), then the plot (one stop), which focuses the first value and announces it.
Hides or shows that series. On the last shown series, nothing: it is aria-disabled.
Previous / next category.
Next / previous series at the same category.
Next / previous row. ← / → do nothing: there is one series.
First / last category.
Clears the focused value and its tooltip; focus stays on the plot.
With onSelect: selects the focused value. Focus and the announcement stay where they are.

the baseline and crosshair: the ticks carry the scale
contrastPairs.why: Position is read from the tick labels and the table; the baseline orients and carries no value of its own.

contrastPairs.why: Gridlines are reading aids; every value is in the tooltip, the announcement and the table.

forwarding.className: root (the figure)
forwarding.ref: root (the figure)
forwarding.rest: root — every HTML attribute except title, which the `label` prop owns

needsDesign: Histogram (`Chart.Bars isAdjacent`): bars fill their band 2px apart, bins named by en-dash ranges. The library's reading of the Plan's P1 row; drawn from code on the Rules, shares, dots and bins sheet (Gaps: Derived) and waiting for a designer's yes.

Scatter and bubble (`Chart.Dots`, `ScatterPlot`): the library's reading of the Plan's P1 row and the stand-in screen's market map — the Line sheet's ringed markers as dots, a nice x axis that need not reach zero, pointer hit within 24px of a dot, a tooltip naming one reading. Drawn from code on the Rules, shares, dots and bins sheet (Gaps: Derived); not yet designed.

Event rules (`Chart.Rule at`): a solid edge-strong line down the plot, its label-sm name at the top on the side with room. The library's own reading for the stand-in screen's "Repositioned" marker; drawn from code on the Rules, shares, dots and bins sheet (Gaps: Derived).

100% stacks (`isStacked={{ isPercent: true }}`): drawn exactly as an absolute stack on a 0–100% axis, with the share before the value in the tooltip. Drawn from code on the Rules, shares, dots and bins sheet, without its tooltip row (Gaps: Derived).

Two label behaviours added for the market-intelligence stand-in screen are described, not drawn: a rule label UNDER its rule when a line runs through its place above, and a line chart that drops its direct labels and end markers when a name is longer than the lane. No sheet shows either case (Line sheet and the Rules, shares, dots and bins sheet, Gaps: Absent).

Marker shapes for slots 4–8 (diamond, triangle-down, plus, hexagon, pentagon): the Line sheet draws circle, square and triangle; all eight are drawn from code on the Rules, shares, dots and bins sheet (Gaps: Derived).

Grouped and stacked horizontal bars. Long category names on a narrow frame: the name lane is capped at 40% of the row so the bars keep room at 320px, which is the library's reading — no sheet draws a phone-width bar chart.
Forecast as muted ink over a confidence band: drawn on the Line sheet; the band needs its own role (sheet Gaps: Missing).

Focus beside a neighbour: grouped, stacked and histogram marks sit 2px apart, so a ring 2px off the mark lands on the next one, where focus ink measures 1.0–1.9:1 light and 1.9–2.9:1 dark. The Bar sheet proposes a 6px surface halo under the ring, open at the baseline (Bar sheet: Focus in a group; Gaps: Measured). Not built.
knownGaps: A dense scatter (hundreds of dots) is still SVG: the Canvas tier of ADR 0023 §3.2 is not built, and the V0 spike that sets its threshold has not run. No Voronoi: the pointer finds the nearest dot within 24px by brute force, which is fine to a few thousand.
The keyboard walks a scatter in x order, one series at a time (↑/↓ switch series). Dots that share an x are reached by index, not by position.

No tabular figures: Aspekta ships no `tnum` feature and its digits are proportional (367–602 units), so `tabular-nums` is a no-op in this face — figures right-align on their last digit but do not line up digit by digit, and a figure that changes in place changes width. Filed against the face (ADR 0011 item 5); pinned by registry/fonts/aspekta/aspekta.test.ts.
Forced-colours fills for slots 3–8 (135°, cross, horizontal, vertical, grid, outline) extend the anatomy sheet's two; confirmed by the maintainer on 2026-11-10 and not yet drawn back onto the sheet.
Forced colours: bars and legend keys are hatched; lines and areas still rely on marker shape alone, since a hatched stroke is not drawn on any sheet.
Ticks, legend names and tooltip names are label-sm at weight 400, declared as type-role deviations until the sheet's proposed data-tick role exists.

The proposed --ui-data-grid / -axis / -label / -highlight roles are not added: they alias border-subtle, border-default, text-muted and bg-hover, and ADR 0023 §5 keeps aliases out until a chart needs a value none has.
The area wash is the slot's -bg role (14% alpha); the sheet draws 10%.

The fading wash's 28% is a constant in the component, not a token: it is the slot's own solid colour at an opacity, as the Line sheet draws it. In forced colours it relies on the line and marker, like every area.
Light-scheme marks on the hover band fall to about 2.6:1 (sheet Gaps: Measured); the tooltip and the focus ring carry the value then.
The time axis steps no finer than a day (no hours or minutes), and its type does not yet require the x field to be a Date: a string is refused when the chart renders, not when it compiles.
The time axis is not drawn on a sheet: its ticks reuse the category axis's labels and pinning, at calendar boundaries instead of data points.
onSelect draws no selected state: the chart sheets draw none, so a selection the caller keeps is invisible on the plot until one is designed.
Legend emphasis is pointer-only, as drawn: focusing a legend entry or a series (↑/↓) does not dim the others. Dimmed marks fall below 3:1 by design; the emphasised series is the one being read.
Hidden series are the chart's own state: there is no hiddenSeries / onHiddenSeriesChange pair yet, so a caller cannot start with a series hidden or persist the choice.
Each legend entry is its own tab stop, so a chart with eight series puts eight stops before the plot. The plan's single-stop legend is not designed.
Direct labels are not nudged apart when lines converge (sheet Gaps: Absent).
docs.motion: None yet. A data change redraws instantly; the plan's CSS transitions on `d` wait for a reduced-motion test.

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

Paper: a new 'Chart --- Rules, shares, dots and bins' sheet draws the P1 parts no sheet had (event rule, 100% stack, scatter with quadrant rules, bubbles, histogram, marker shapes 1–8, Sparkline xs), copied from the shipped components with colours mapped back to tokens, each badged Derived until a designer approves it. The Bar sheet gains 'Focus in a group': grouped, stacked and histogram marks sit 2px apart, so the focus ring 2px off a mark lands on its neighbour at 1.0–1.9:1 light and 1.9–2.9:1 dark; a 6px surface halo under the ring is proposed, not built. The Heatmap sheet's focus ring moves inside the cell (inset 2px focus ink, then a 2px surface gap), since an outside ring spilled onto neighbouring cells. The Anatomy sheet's series 2 now paints --ui-data-cat-2-solid, closing chart.doc.ts's stale --ui-data-div-neg-2 known gap; Paper's cat-1..8 bg/fg tokens are re-pushed from the repo. chart.doc.ts and sparkline.doc.ts needsDesign rows now point at the new sheet.

Chart: legend and tooltip keys scale each marker shape to fill its 8px box (lib/viz `markerKeyPath`), so the triangle, diamond, triangle-down, hexagon and pentagon no longer lose their points to the key's clipping svg. The 2px surface ring under end, crosshair and scatter markers is now the mark's own outline stroked 4px in the surface, mitred (`RING_GAP`), instead of the shape scaled to r 6, which left the triangle's slants at 1.21px and the plus's arms at 0.8px. A hidden series' outlined key is inset by half its stroke and round-joined, since a mitred apex reached 0.47px past the box. Found by /review-ui; the Marker shapes section, the Line sheet and the Bar sheet's keys were redrawn to match.

Chart: every marker shape has the area of the circle it stands beside and sits on its area centroid (lib/viz markerPoints). Measured at r 4 before: the square was 27% heavier than the circle, the diamond 8%, the triangle 10% lighter and the plus 19%, and the triangle's centroid sat 1px (a quarter of r) below the data point, so on a line the marker read as off the line. Hexagon and pentagon were already equal-area. Legend and tooltip keys are fitted to their box and do not change. Found by /review-ui on the Marker shapes section; the section and the Line sheet were redrawn to match.

Chart grows the P1 forms the V2 stand-in asked for. Chart.Rule takes `at` (a category, date or number) and draws a vertical event rule labelled at the top of the plot. `isStacked={{ isPercent: true }}` normalises each category to 100% (the axis reads 0–100%; the tooltip and announcer say "60% (120)"; negatives throw). `xScale="linear"` gives a numeric x axis, and Chart.Dots draws markers in a 2px surface ring, with `areaKey`/`areaLabel` for bubbles. New presets ScatterPlot and Histogram (bins from lib/viz, adjacent bars). Scatter hit-testing is nearest-dot within 24px; the baseline is clamped to the plot floor when zero is outside the y domain. Not yet drawn in Paper: recorded in the doc's needsDesign.

Legend name ink decided as built: text-secondary. The Bar and Line sheets drew legend names in --ui-data-label (an alias of text-muted), which left the legend toggle no step to mark a hidden series. The sheets' legend specimens (light, dark and stress brand) now draw secondary, the Bar sheet's Gaps row reads Decided and its Legend toggle row Built, and the Anatomy token map splits 'Title and legend names' (which said primary) into Title, primary, and Legend names, secondary. Ticks and category labels stay on --ui-data-label. No code change.

The legend entry joins chart.geometry.json as case chart-legend-entry, extracted from the Legend toggle sheet's Shown entry: 62×24, insets 4 block and 8 inline, an 8px key 4px from the name. To make it measurable the geometry test now looks for a case's children inside its container rather than across the document, which a legend (two entries at least) had made impossible; every existing case still passes. The entry moves from a fixed 24px height to 4px block padding with a 24px floor, so its inset is declared rather than produced by centring, and the key carries data-slot="chart-legend-key".

Charts V2 has no product screen to adopt it yet, so registry/screens/market-intelligence rebuilds the charted parts of the service portal's Market intelligence section (Overview, Share of search, Categories) from library parts only, on placeholder data, as Storybook stories under the axe pass. It maps every Recharts call site the portal has to a library part or a recorded gap (docs/charts-and-graphs-plan.md, 'V2 stand-in'), and surfaced three defects now fixed: direct labels painting past the frame, a rule label crossed by its line, and sparklines in a column exaggerating flat series. The plan's axis geometry case is added (chart-plot-column), and the geometry test now waits for a ResizeObserver re-render before measuring. The stand-in does not close V2's exit; a real screen adopting these does.

Three failures found by checking the market-intelligence stand-in screen at 320px against the better-layout reflow rule. Category names on a chart's x axis ran together ("PostersTypographyWayfinding…"): the axis now spaces its labels by the widest name plus 8px, guessed from the character count so the server agrees and corrected by measurement after paint, and a name thinned away is still in the tooltip, the announcement and the table view. A horizontal bar chart's fixed 168px name lane left the bars 8px: the lane is now capped at 40% of the row, which only binds below a 420px row, and a truncated name carries its full text as a title. And Table's scroll clip was not a containing block, so visually hidden text in a cell (the screen's "Not ranked") was placed against the page and scrolled it 33px sideways; the clip is now relative. Table's knownGaps also records that a fixed table whose declared lanes exceed its frame gives the flexing column 0px — the screen now sets minWidth.

Chart's legend toggles series, as the Bar sheet's new Legend toggle section draws it. Each entry is a native checkbox in a 24px label (checked is shown) with bg-hover on hover and the focus ring on the label. A hidden series leaves the marks, tooltip and keyboard and the group closes up; the value axis keeps every series' domain so the rest do not move; the table still lists it. A hidden key is outlined and its name muted; the last shown series is aria-disabled. Each entry is a tab stop before the plot. The sheet's toggle drawing first padded entries 6px on the belief that the legend gap was 12px; it is 16px, so entries are padded space-sm (8px) and the anatomy specimen's legend band grows to 24px (frame 409 → 417; chart.geometry.json follows).

Two label collisions found by the market-intelligence stand-in screen. A direct label longer than the 96px lane (a domain such as muller-brockmann.example) painted past the chart's frame onto the card beside it; now, when any series name measures wider than the lane's 80px, the chart drops every direct label and end marker and the plot takes the lane back — the legend (two or more series) or the title (one) already names every line. And a Rule's label, always above the rule's end, was crossed by a line ending a little over its own target; it now sits under the rule (data-placement="below") when a shown line runs through its place above and the place below is clear and inside the plot, decided from the data so the server draws the same side.

Chart gains onSelect and xScale="time". onSelect fires on Enter or Space on the focused point (with its series key) and on a click on a category (series null when the band holds several); the plot takes cursor-pointer only when it is set, and the chart keeps and draws no selected state because no sheet draws one. xScale="time" places line and area points at their Dates (ascending, parsed by the caller), with ticks on whole UTC years, months or days from new lib/viz helpers (timeTicks, timePositions, tickDateFormat, pointDateFormat); the table, tooltip and announcement print each point's own date. BarChart refuses the time axis in its type; Chart throws on a non-Date, unsorted rows or bars on a time axis.

Chart gains a headline slot and a fading area. headline: an element under the title (ChartCard's figure and change); when present the description is visually hidden and stays the accessible description. Chart.Areas / AreaChart wash="fade": the slot's solid colour at 28% at the top of the area, clear at the baseline (the Line sheet's Fading area); overlaid areas only — the AreaChart type refuses it with isStacked, and Chart.Areas draws stacked bands flat.

ADR 0011 item 5 checked: Aspekta ships no `tnum` feature and its default digits are proportional (367–602 units), so `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` is a no-op wherever the library uses it. Figures still right-align on their last digit; they do not line up digit by digit, and a figure that changes in place (tooltip, meter reading, slider readout) changes width. Filed against the face as ADR 0011 directs, not answered with a second family. Chart, ChartCard, StatTiles, Meter, Table and RangeSlider list the gap; registry/fonts/aspekta/aspekta.test.ts pins the measurement and fails when a font update adds the feature. No code or visual change.

Chart: the tooltip is positioned by the behaviour layer against a virtual anchor (the band or the crosshair), fixed on --ui-z-tooltip and portalled into the chart's figure, so a clipping ancestor no longer cuts it
Chart: horizontal bars (orientation on BarChart and Chart.Bars, one series as ranked rows) and forced-colours fills for bars and legend keys — slot 1 solid, slots 2–8 distinct system-colour hatches
Chart: bars, lines and areas in a figure with a takeaway, legend, one-tab-stop keyboard navigation, announcements and a table view; BarChart, LineChart and AreaChart presets

Paper: the Chart anatomy sheet's legend and tooltip rows used an off-scale 6px gap, corrected to --ui-space-xs (legend) and --ui-space-sm (tooltip rows); and its specimen frame was typed 784 wide around a 684px plot, leaving 10px of the plot row unfilled, now 774 so the row is the sum of its parts. Both now match the shipped component, whose frame and plot row geometry is extracted into design/paper/specs/chart.geometry.json and asserted in the geometry browser test.

items.title: ChartCard
items.lead: Brings a figure, its change and a chart into the same frame.

docs.lead: Brings a figure, its change and a chart into the same frame.
docs.name: ChartCard
docs.summary: The Chart frame with a stat tile's figure and change under its title, so the card says how much, and whether that is good, before the plot is read. Below the head it is the Chart, untouched. By default one fading area; any Chart mark goes in as children.

anatomy.notes: Chart's <figure>, with data-block="chart-card". className, ref and the rest land here, as on Chart.
Chart's own: label-md, primary.
4px under the title: the figure (stat-value, `figure` role, tabular) and the change line (stat-delta) on one baseline, 12px apart.
Still rendered and still the figure's aria-describedby; visually hidden. The figure has its printed place.

docs.composition:
ChartCard                     value · delta? · label · description · data · x · xLabel · series
└─ children?                  Chart marks; default <Chart.Areas wash="fade" />

value.notes: The headline figure, formatted by the caller — usually the plot's total or latest value. The card does not compute it.

delta.notes: The change and its comparison, exactly as on a StatTiles tile (change, comparison, polarity, format).

description.notes: Still required: it is the chart's accessible description. Not printed — decided 2026-11-11 (sheet Gaps: Conflict, resolved as drawn).

children.notes: The marks. Bars, lines, a rule — anything Chart takes.

…Chart props.notes: label, data, x, xLabel, series, size, format, isLoading, emptyText, tableLabel: as on Chart. `headline` is the card's own.

do: Make the figure summarise the plot it sits on: its total, or its latest value.
Write the description as the takeaway; a screen reader still hears it first.
Use one series for the fading area; overlapping fades go muddy.
dont: Do not put a figure that the plot does not show — the card then makes two claims a reader has to reconcile.
Do not repeat the takeaway as visible text under the figure; the head has one sentence's room and the figure uses it.

a11y.role: Chart's: a <figure> named by the title, described by the description. The figure and change are text in the head, read in order after the title.
a11y.name: `label` via aria-labelledby; `description` via aria-describedby, though not printed.

items.name: chat-composer
items.title: ChatComposer
items.lead: Writes a message, adds context and controls a running response.

docs.lead: Writes a message, adds context and controls a running response.
docs.name: ChatComposer
docs.summary: The message box of the agent chat: one frame holding an attachment tray, an auto-growing text region and a control row. A compact pill at rest, squaring to radius-xl the moment the text wraps — the layout switch is measured, not declared, because a composer cannot know in advance whether a sentence will wrap. Send carries the state of the conversation: disabled while the field is empty, accent when sendable, and an inverse-filled Stop while the agent answers.

anatomy.notes: Column, gap-sm. Carries className and data-layout (inline | stacked) so a consumer or a test can read which arrangement won without inspecting classes.
The tray, ABOVE the frame — a Thumbnail.Group or the file chips beside it. It scrolls horizontally rather than growing the composer; the pill stays a pill however many files are attached.

bg-field on a 1.5px border-subtle hairline (1 device pixel at DPR 1). radius-full while inline, radius-xl while stacked. p-md, gap-sm, and NO declared height — 12 + 32 + 12 is the sheet's 56px compact height, and a height would be a second author of the inset.
The leading control slot — the sheet's Add button, Button ghost · md · full with a Plus glyph, opening the attach menu.
The text region. Flexes inline; spans the frame with the sheet's px-sm py-xs inset while stacked, via order-first rather than a different tree.

The textarea itself, rows=1, resize disabled, height measured from the content and capped at maxRows lines before it scrolls. body-md 400 leading-normal in text-ink-primary; placeholder in text-ink-placeholder.
endActions (the sheet's Dictate) followed by Send or Stop. Pushed to the trailing edge with ms-auto while stacked.

Button primary · md · full with an ArrowUp glyph — the single filled action in the frame (ui-craft 18). Disabled while the value is blank, with the sheet's bg-sunken fill rather than Button's own bg-elevated.
Replaces Send while isGenerating. Button md · full filled --ui-bg-inverse with --ui-text-inverse ink, and a filled SquareRounded glyph — griddy's Stop hard-codes fill="black" and cannot take the ink.
The failure caption, caption size in danger ink, inset px-lg so it clears the pill's curve. Its presence sets aria-invalid and the danger edge together.
The centred caption below the frame — "Diorama Agent can make mistakes…". Outside the frame; omitted (not hidden) in the sidebar context.

docs.composition:
ChatComposer                 label! sendLabel! stopLabel! value onValueChange onSubmitAction
├─ attachments?              <Thumbnail.Group>…</Thumbnail.Group>
├─ (frame)
│  ├─ startAction?           <Button variant="ghost" shape="full" size="md" isIconOnly icon={<Plus/>} aria-label="Add"/>
│  ├─ (text region)          the textarea — auto-grows to maxRows, then scrolls
│  └─ (actions)
│     ├─ endActions?         <Button variant="ghost" shape="full" size="md" isIconOnly icon={<Microphone/>} aria-label="Dictate"/>
│     └─ (Send | Stop)       owned by the component; isGenerating chooses
├─ errorText?
└─ disclaimer?

label.notes: Required. The field's accessible name, ALWAYS visually hidden — the sheet draws no visible label in any of its three contexts, so there is no isLabelHidden to get wrong.

sendLabel.notes: Required. Accessible name of the send control; an icon-only button with no name announces as "button".

stopLabel.notes: Required even for a composer that never generates. isGenerating changes at runtime, so a discriminated union on it cannot be satisfied by a caller holding a boolean — the label would be optional exactly when it is needed.

value.notes: Controlled. Uncontrolled through defaultValue; both go through the shared useControllableState (§4).

onSubmitAction.notes: Enter (without Shift) and the Send button. The composer does NOT clear itself — a send that failed has to be able to put the text back, and only the caller knows whether it did.

isGenerating.notes: Swaps Send for Stop. Typing and Enter still work: the sheet's own placeholder for this state is "Reply to interrupt…".

onStopAction.notes: Runs when Stop is pressed; only reachable while isGenerating.

layout.notes: auto measures the rendered line boxes — the sheet's rule is about the TEXT wrapping, which only layout knows. The literals exist for a story, a visual baseline, or a caller who has already decided.

maxRows.notes: Lines before the field scrolls instead of growing. The frame never exceeds this plus its chrome.

errorText.notes: Sets aria-invalid, the danger edge and the caption together, so the three cannot drift apart.

attachments.notes: Slot: the tray above the frame. Never wrapped (§3), and never moved inside — the pill stays a pill.

startAction.notes: Slot: the Add control. A slot rather than props because what it opens (upload, library, camera) is the caller's.

endActions.notes: Slot: controls between the text and Send. The sheet draws Dictate here and calls it the first thing to drop when the frame is narrow — dropping it is the caller's decision, at their breakpoint.

isDropActive.notes: PRESENTATIONAL. In a chat the drop target is the whole thread, not this pill, so the composer draws the state and the app owns the event — nothing here can detect it.

dropLabel.notes: Replaces the placeholder while isDropActive — "Drop to attach". A string swap rather than a DOM swap: unmounting a focused control is what §10 forbids.

disclaimer.notes: The caption below the frame. Hiding it in the sidebar context means not passing it.

do: Give Add and Dictate as slots filled with Button ghost · md · full — that is exactly what the sheet draws, and it keeps the menu the Add button opens at the call site.
Keep the attachment tray in `attachments`; it belongs above the frame, and putting it inside is what turns the pill into a box.
Drive isGenerating from the stream and let the component swap Send for Stop — the two are one control, not two that must be conditionally rendered by the caller.
Pass errorText rather than styling the frame; it wires aria-invalid, the edge and the message together.
dont: Do not clear the value in onSubmitAction before the send has succeeded — the composer deliberately does not clear itself, so a failure can put the draft back.
Do not set rows or a height: the field measures its own content and caps at maxRows. A declared height would be a second author of the frame's inset.
Do not use this as a general multi-line field. That is Textarea — it has a visible label, helper text and a resize grip, none of which belong in a chat.
Do not add a second filled action to the frame. Send is the single filled control in it (ui-craft 18); everything else is a ghost.

a11y.role: A plain textarea with two or three real buttons beside it — no ARIA composite, because nothing here is a widget the platform does not already have.
a11y.name: The field is named by `label` (required, visually hidden). Send and Stop are named by `sendLabel` / `stopLabel`, both required at the type level. Slot controls carry their own names — Button's isIconOnly requires one.

keyboard.does: Submits the current value, when it is not blank. preventDefault()'d, so no newline is inserted.
Inserts a line break; the field grows a row, and past one row the frame squares to radius-xl.
Commits the candidate and does NOT submit — sending there loses half a sentence in Japanese or Korean.
Walks the frame: the Add slot, the field, the end slots, then Send or Stop. Every one is a real button or a real form control.
Activates it — native, nothing is faked.

contrastPairs.role: the entered message
the placeholder, and the drop label that replaces it
the ArrowUp glyph on the send control
the Stop control's fill against the frame — the only channel telling it from Send, and the pair --ui-bg-emphasis failed at 1:1 in dark
the Stop glyph
the invalid frame edge (SC 1.4.11 — state carried by a boundary)
the error caption, which sits on the page rather than in the frame
the disclaimer caption
the focus ring — the resting hairline is decorative by design, so the ring is what carries SC 1.4.11 here
the ArrowUp glyph while the composer is empty
contrastPairs.why: the control is genuinely disabled and WCAG 2.2 exempts disabled controls (1.4.3, 1.4.11). The state is also carried by the fill dropping out of the accent, not by the glyph alone

contrastPairs.role: the drag-over fill
contrastPairs.why: the drop state is carried by the solid border-focus edge and by the label replacing the placeholder; the tint is the third channel, not the only one

forwarding.ref: The TEXTAREA, not the frame (§5) — a ref to the wrapper could not focus it, could not be read for a value and could not be handed to a form library, which is every reason a caller takes one here.
forwarding.className: The outermost node, so a width sizes the tray, the frame and the captions together.
forwarding.native props: The remaining textarea attributes (name, maxLength, autoFocus, spellCheck, …) go to the textarea, which is the element that owns them. onKeyDown is composed with the Enter contract, consumer first — preventDefault() opts out of submission.

docs.motion: Two layers, one clock each. Interaction feedback is a transition on the frame — border-color, box-shadow and background-color at duration-fast / ease-out. The inline↔stacked flip is a measured FLIP at duration-base / ease-out via the Web Animations API: the frame's height, its border-radius and the start/actions slots are captured before the re-arrangement and animated from where they were to where they land, the frame clipped in flight. The radius rides the FLIP rather than the transition list deliberately: rounded-full computes to 999px and only the painted value is clamped to the box, so a CSS transition from it sits above the clamp for ~99% of its duration and snaps at the end — the FLIP animates measured visual radius to measured visual radius instead. It fires ONLY when measured auto layout crosses arrangements: never on mount (no entrance animation), never for an explicit layout prop (stories and visual baselines stay static), and never on ordinary line growth — the field's height is still set imperatively and deliberately NOT transitioned, because a height that eases behind the caret puts the caret outside the box while it catches up. The text row snaps on the flip for the same reason: its width change re-wraps the draft instantly either way, and glyphs gliding under a still-moving Send button read as a glitch. Reduced motion is handled twice — the WAAPI reads its duration from the computed --ui-duration-base, which the token layer collapses to 1ms, and checks prefers-reduced-motion explicitly besides.
needsDesign: The empty Send control's fill. The sheet draws --ui-bg-sunken; Button's own disabled treatment is --ui-bg-elevated, which measures 1.03:1 against a white field and disappears. Shipped as the sheet's, overriding Button in one place — the two should agree, and this is the third component to want a quieter disabled fill on a light field.

The Stop control is a filled type Button has no variant for (an inverse fill with a matching edge). Written as a local recipe here; if a second component needs it, Button should grow the variant rather than the recipe being copied.

griddy has no Stop glyph that can take the ink — its `Stop` hard-codes fill="black", as `Pause` and every `ChatCircle*` do. Shipped as a filled SquareRounded. The sheet draws griddy's Stop and should be re-drawn with the glyph that can actually ship.
The stacked layout's threshold is one wrapped line, and the 8-row cap is the sheet's own Derived note — neither is a product decision yet.
RTL is not drawn. The frame uses logical properties (ms-auto, px), so it should mirror, but nothing has confirmed which side Send belongs on in RTL.
knownGaps: isDropActive is presentational and the composer registers no drop handler. That is deliberate — the drop target in a chat is the thread — but it means the sheet's drag-over state only appears if the app wires it.
While isDropActive with text already typed, the drop label does not appear: it is the placeholder, and a placeholder is hidden once the field has a value.
The attachment tray's stacked/spread behaviour belongs to Thumbnail.Group; this component does not drive it from focus, which is what the sheet's Derived note describes.

The file chip drawn in the sheet's tray (icon + name + meta + remove) exists nowhere as a component. It is passed in as a slot child today; the sheet flags it as Missing and shares it with Chat Message.
The dictate control does not drop itself below 300px of content width — the sheet's rule is a caller-side breakpoint decision, and the composer has no width knowledge of its own.
