changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

Paper: design fixes pushed back into the chat sheets in Paper, so the sheets match what ships. Chat Progress: the dock's Stop layers are SquareRounded (griddy's Stop hard-codes black and check:licensing rejects it), the dock inset is calc(100% - --ui-space-xl × 2) rather than a raw 48px, the thread marks' glyphs are 16px (the root's metrics, as the caption says), the finished action layer is named Button / secondary / md as drawn, the precedence table's quiet dock row is the dock's own box (14px matrix, radius-lg, p-xs), the reasoning fade is --ui-bg-base rather than #FFFFFF, and the dock annotation states the one-moving-row rule. Chat Sources: the focus ring is var(--ui-bg-base) 2px + var(--ui-focus-ring-color) 4px rather than raw hex; the library card glyph is PdfFile as in the list; the folded discs are the first three distinct kinds in list order (Globe, PdfFile, FileText) and the '+3 more' card draws all three hidden kinds; the gathering row draws a held 14px Working Status matrix where the retired ring spinner stood. The preview panels' shadow already equals --ui-shadow-md's light value — Paper has no shadow token type — so it stays. Rich Turn (dark): the Tasks header gains its chevron, the running task loses a hover fill nothing could cause, and the dock and composer Stop glyphs are SquareRounded. The matching needsDesign notes are removed from the chat-run-dock, chat-sources, chat-progress and chat-tasks docs.

The inline↔stacked flip is animated — a measured FLIP at duration-base / ease-out via the Web Animations API. When the auto measurement crosses arrangements, the pre-flip geometry (frame height, painted border-radius, the start and actions slot rects) is captured in the same pass as the decision, and after the re-arrangement the frame's height and radius animate to their settled values in one track while the control slots translate from their old row to the new one, the frame clipped in flight; a flip reversed mid-flight retargets from the visually held values rather than stacking tracks. border-radius left the frame's transition list in the same change, deliberately: rounded-full computes to 999px and only the painted radius is clamped to the box, so the transition spent ~99% of its duration above the clamp and snapped at the end — it was declared motion that never ran, and the FLIP now animates measured visual radius instead. The choreography fires only on a measured auto crossing: never on mount, never for an explicit layout prop (stories and visual baselines stay static), and never on ordinary line growth, which stays deliberately instant per the doc's caret rationale. Reduced motion is honoured twice — durations are read from the computed --ui-duration-base the token layer collapses to 1ms, plus an explicit prefers-reduced-motion check. Browser tests pin the choreography at the animation layer with getAnimations(): the flip actually runs (height and radius keyframes at the token's duration, a transform slide on the actions slot), a composer mounted with a wrapped draft renders stacked with zero animations, and a keystroke that keeps the arrangement animates nothing.

The auto layout no longer oscillates on drafts in the width band between the two arrangements. The line-box measurement that decides inline vs stacked was taken at whatever width the textarea currently held, and the two arrangements give the text column different widths — inline shares its row with the controls, stacked spans the frame. A draft that wrapped at the inline width but fit on one stacked line flipped the frame on alternate keystrokes, and the field height was set from whichever width was about to lose, so overflow-y hidden could swallow the second line — reported from the agent launch screen. The arrangement is now decided by probing the textarea transiently at the INLINE width, which the current arrangement cannot influence: the frame stacks exactly when the text no longer fits the inline row. The height is then re-measured once more after the arrangement settles, at the width the field actually ends up with, and a ResizeObserver on the frame re-runs the measurement when the container resizes, since a moved wrap point gets no keystroke to announce it. A browser test walks a growing draft through the band one character at a time and pins both halves: once stacked, more text never unstacks it, and below the maxRows cap the field is always tall enough for its own text.

ChatComposer: the agent chat's message box — an attachment tray above a bg-field frame holding an auto-growing textarea and a control row. Two arrangements, ONE DOM: inline is the sheet's radius-full pill, stacked squares to radius-xl the moment the text wraps, and the switch is flex-wrap + `order-first` rather than a different tree, so focus and the caret survive a wrap. `layout` defaults to `auto` and MEASURES the rendered line boxes — the sheet's rule is about the text wrapping, which only layout knows; the two literals exist for stories, baselines and callers who have already decided. Height is measured from scrollHeight and capped at `maxRows` (8) lines, then scrolls. Enter submits, Shift+Enter opens a line, and an Enter committing an IME candidate does neither — dispatched directly in the browser test, because userEvent cannot produce isComposing. The composer never clears itself: a send that failed has to be able to put the draft back. Add and Dictate are ELEMENT slots (Button ghost md full at the call site, because what Add opens is the caller's menu); Send/Stop is the component's, since it carries conversation state. isDropActive is presentational and documented as such — in a chat the drop target is the thread, so the composer draws the state and the app owns the event, which is also why this component starts no pointer gesture. THREE DESIGN DEFECTS FIXED IN PAPER. (1) The compact frame declared a 56px height on top of its p-md, a SECOND author of the inset: the vertical gap laid out at 12 against the 13.5 its padding declares, while the horizontal gap — which nothing else authored — was 13.5. Tabs' defect exactly, found by the new geometry spec. All 24 composer frames are now fit-content; the frame is 59 in Paper and 58 in Chromium, and the browser test asserts the four insets rather than the total. (2) The Stop control was drawn --ui-bg-emphasis, which IS the accent and which theme zero pins to neutral-0 in BOTH schemes — identical to the dark scheme's bg-field, so the control measured 1:1 there. The sheet raised it as a Conflict naming bg-inverse; that role is minted here rather than inverting emphasis, which Tooltip also depends on and whose own doc says an implementer must not pick it. (3) griddy's Stop glyph hard-codes a black fill (as Pause and every ChatCircle* do) and cannot take the ink; check:licensing rejects it. Shipped and redrawn as a filled SquareRounded. One deliberate override of a primitive: the empty Send keeps the sheet's bg-sunken fill instead of Button's disabled bg-elevated, which measures 1.03:1 on a white field and disappears — asserted against painted probes, and recorded in needsDesign so the two can be reconciled once.

items.name: chat-message
items.title: ChatMessage
items.lead: Gives a message its place in a conversation.

docs.lead: Gives a message its place in a conversation.
docs.name: ChatMessage
docs.summary: The two voices of an agent thread, deliberately asymmetric. The sender sits in a right-aligned bg-elevated bubble capped at a share of the column; the receiver owns the full width with no bubble at all and a looser leading — the agent's answer is the page, not a quote on it. Ships as one item with two components: there is no bare <ChatMessage>, because the receiver has no bubble and a role prop would give it one.

anatomy.notes: data-role="sender", data-status. Column, items-end, gap-xs. Declares --ui-chat-message-bubble-max-width (75%).
bg-elevated, radius-lg, no tail, no border, no avatar and no timestamp inside. px-lg py-md at md, px-md py-sm at sm. body 400 at leading-normal in text-ink-primary.
Inside the bubble, above the text, gap-xs — a Thumbnail.Group. Sent tiles carry no remove control: the message is gone.
The caption under the bubble, and the ONLY channel carrying delivery state — the bubble's fill never moves. text-ink-muted while sending or queued, medium text-danger when failed.
data-role="receiver", data-streaming. group/chat-message — named, so a message nested inside a widget cannot reveal its parent's actions.
No container. body 400 at leading-relaxed (155%) — the looser leading is the receiver's signature and the reason it needs none. Rich blocks stack at gap-lg, which IS --ui-space-stack-md.

The failure block INSIDE the message, under whatever partial answer arrived — bg-danger-subtle, radius-md, px-md py-sm, body-sm in text-ink-on-danger-subtle, with a danger·sm Retry. role="status", announced politely.
The ghost icon row, revealed on message hover AND on focus-within, forced visible on a device with no hover. Withheld entirely while streaming.
Caption in text-ink-muted at the trailing end of the actions row — agent name and relative time. Appears with the row.

docs.composition:
ChatMessage.Sender     size? attachments? status? statusText? onRetryAction? retryLabel?
└─ (bubble)            attachments above the text, both inside

ChatMessage.Receiver   size? isStreaming? actions? meta? isActionsVisible? errorText? onRetryAction? retryLabel?
├─ (body)              children
│  └─ while streaming:  <ChatProgress form="streaming" label="Writing"/> as the last child — the turn's one mark
├─ (error)             errorText + a danger·sm Retry
└─ (actions)           actions … meta
   └─ actions:         <Button variant="ghost" size="sm" isIconOnly aria-label="Copy" icon={<Copy/>}/> x N

size.notes: The type scale, and the bubble's inset with it. NOT the width cap — the sheet draws a 343px mobile column at md with the narrow cap, so the two are separate axes.

--ui-chat-message-bubble-max-width.notes: The bubble's share of the column. A property rather than a prop because the sheet's rule is about the COLUMN — 75% at 640, 85% once it narrows — and a component cannot see that: the assistant sidebar is 308px inside a 1440px window, so no viewport breakpoint describes it. Set it where the column is chosen.

status.notes: Sender only. `statusText` is REQUIRED by the type for every state but sent: the caption is the only channel carrying the state, so a sending bubble with no caption has no state at all. `queued` is a turn sent while the agent is still running the last one — muted like sending, never danger ink ("Queued — runs after this turn" on the sheet). No indicator starts for it until the running turn settles: the live edge stays where it was.

attachments.notes: Sender only. A Thumbnail.Group above the text, inside the bubble. Never wrapped (§3).

isStreaming.notes: Receiver only. WITHHOLDS the actions row — copying or rating half an answer is worse than waiting, and rendering the row hidden would put six tab stops in front of an unfinished answer. It draws nothing itself: the Streaming status row (ChatProgress form="streaming") is the caller's last child, so the same matrix runs from the turn's first second to its last.

actions.notes: Receiver only. Button ghost · sm · isIconOnly at the call site. A slot, because which actions a product offers is the product's.

isActionsVisible.notes: Keeps the row visible instead of revealing it on hover. The sheet asks for this on touch and on the latest message — both are facts about the THREAD, which only the thread knows.

errorText.notes: Receiver only. The failure block inside the message. Never a toast: the error belongs to the turn that produced it.

onRetryAction.notes: Paired with `retryLabel` at the type level, on both components. The sheet draws the word "retry" inside the caption, which reads as a control and is not one; this is that control.

do: Set --ui-chat-message-bubble-max-width to 85% wherever the column is narrow — the sidebar and the phone — and leave it at 75% on the page.
Drive isStreaming from the stream and let the component withhold the actions row; do not conditionally render the row yourself.
While streaming, put a ChatProgress form="streaming" row as the receiver's last child — and swap it for nothing when the answer settles. It is the turn's one mark.
Mark a turn sent during a running one as queued, and start no indicator for it until the running turn settles.
Pass errorText for a stopped generation, so the failure stays attached to the turn instead of floating off as a toast.
Keep the partial answer when a generation fails. The failure block says the answer above is kept, and deleting it makes that a lie.
dont: Do not give the receiver a bubble, an avatar or a border. The asymmetry is the design, and it is what keeps a long answer readable.
Do not add a caret or a second moving mark beside the Streaming row: one turn, one mark.
Do not put a timestamp inside the sender bubble — time lives in the meta line and in a hover tooltip.
Do not render a remove control on a sent attachment. The message has gone; the control would promise something it cannot do.
Do not reveal the actions row with hover alone if you add your own — the component pairs hover with focus-within and with a no-hover fallback, and dropping either strands a keyboard or a touch user.

a11y.role: Plain content. The failure block is role="status" so a stopped generation is announced; nothing else here is a widget the platform does not already have.
a11y.name: The action controls name themselves — Button's isIconOnly requires aria-label. Retry is a real button with a required `retryLabel`, on both voices.

keyboard.does: Reaches the actions row, which becomes visible on focus-within — the row is opacity-0, never unmounted, so the tab order does not change under the user.
Skips the actions row entirely: it is not rendered until the answer settles.
Activates the focused action or Retry — native, both are real buttons.

contrastPairs.role: the sender's message inside the bubble
the receiver's answer, which sits on the page with no container
the meta line and the "Sending…" and "Queued" captions
the sender's failure caption
the receiver's failure block and its Retry label
the bubble against the page
contrastPairs.why: the bubble's fill is a GROUPING cue, not information: which voice is speaking is carried by the alignment, the leading and the presence of an actions row, all of which survive at any contrast. It is the same argument ADR 0010 makes for a surface step, and the reason the sheet gives the receiver no container at all

forwarding.ref: The outermost node of each component — neither is a form control, so §5's exception does not apply.
forwarding.className: The outermost node. It is also where --ui-chat-message-bubble-max-width is set, so a caller's override lands after the default and wins.
forwarding.native props: The remaining div props are spread on the same outermost node.

docs.motion: One transition: the receiver's actions row fades in on hover or focus-within at duration-fast / ease-out (motionMicro), which is the sheet's 120ms exactly. Nothing else here moves. The first release drew a static block caret while streaming; the Chat status behaviour sheet (40P0-0) drops it for the Streaming matrix in a status row under the text — ChatProgress, composed by the caller, on StatusMatrix's one clock — so a turn keeps one mark from its first second to its last. Collapses under prefers-reduced-motion at the token layer.
needsDesign: The sheet draws the word "retry" inside the sender's failure caption. A word in a caption cannot be tabbed to or announced, so it ships as a real Button beside the caption — the sheet should be redrawn to match, and it has been.

The actions row is drawn as 24px controls with 14px glyphs in text-muted; Button ghost · sm is 24px with 16px glyphs in text-ink-secondary. Shipped as Button, so the row cannot drift from the rest of the library — but either the sheet moves 2px and one ink step, or this row is a distinct control type and should be named.

The failure block is a tighter Banner with an action: Banner is p-lg with no action slot and uses --ui-intent-danger-fg for its ink, where this uses the deeper --ui-text-on-danger-subtle. Shipped as a local recipe. This is the second inline alert in the library that wants an action; a third should grow Banner instead.
The bubble caps (75% / 85%) and the sidebar's body-sm step are the sheet's own Derived readings — no product decision behind them yet.
Rich receiver content — markdown lists, headings, links, tables, Code Block — is not drawn. Only the stacking rule (space-stack-md between blocks) is reserved, and that is what this component ships.
Editing a sent message in place is not drawn; it needs a decision on whether an edit forks the conversation.
knownGaps: BREAKING since the first release: the `chat-message-caret` part is gone. A consumer that relied on isStreaming to draw the caret now gets no mark until it composes the Streaming row.
The receiver does not render the Streaming row itself: its words ("Writing") are the product's, and the row is ChatProgress's. Composition is the contract, asserted in the browser test.
There is no grouping of consecutive turns: the thread's spacing (space-stack-lg between exchanges) belongs to whatever lays the messages out, and this component does not provide it.
The sender's hover tooltip carrying the timestamp is named in the parts table and not built — it is a Tooltip at the call site.
The file chip drawn for a non-image attachment is shared with Chat Composer and exists nowhere as a component; it is passed in as a slot child today.

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

Chat Message: the Sender gains status="queued" — a turn sent while the agent is still running the last one, captioned in muted ink like Sending ("Queued — runs after this turn"), with statusText required by the type. The Receiver's static block caret is removed: per the Chat status behaviour sheet the turn's one mark is the Streaming matrix in a status row under the text (ChatProgress form="streaming"), placed by the caller. isStreaming still withholds the actions row.

migration.manual: BREAKING: the `chat-message-caret` part no longer renders. While streaming, put `<ChatProgress form="streaming" label="…" />` as the receiver's last child and remove it when the answer settles.

changes.summary: ChatMessage: the two voices of an agent thread, as ONE item with TWO components and deliberately no bare <ChatMessage>. The sheet's own Gaps row asked for that and §7a's Sheet-and-Drawer test agrees — the receiver has no bubble by design, so a `role` prop would carry a bubble, an attachment slot and a status caption that mean nothing in half its uses, and an actions row, a caret and a failure block that mean nothing in the other half. Sender: right-aligned bg-elevated bubble, radius-lg, no tail, no border, no avatar, no timestamp inside; attachments above the text INSIDE the bubble; delivery state carried entirely by a caption, because the bubble's fill never moves — asserted as a sameness, which is the assertion that fails if anyone tints it. Receiver: no container at all, leading-relaxed against the sender's leading-normal (asserted as an ORDERING, not two numbers), a static caret while streaming, and the actions row WITHHELD rather than hidden while it streams — a hidden row is six tab stops in front of an unfinished answer. The row is revealed by hover AND focus-within AND forced visible under `@media (hover:none)`: three channels, because dropping any one strands a keyboard or a touch user. THE WIDTH CAP IS A CUSTOM PROPERTY, NOT A PROP. The sheet's rule (75% at 640, 85% once the column narrows) is about the COLUMN, and no viewport breakpoint describes a 308px sidebar inside a 1440px window — so `--ui-chat-message-bubble-max-width` is declared on the root at 75% and the app that chose the column moves it. It is also not the same axis as `size`: the sheet draws a 343px mobile column at `md` with the narrow cap. TWO DEVIATIONS FROM THE DRAWING, both pushed back into Paper. The failed caption reads "Not sent — retry" in the sheet; a word inside a caption cannot be tabbed to and announces as prose, so retry ships as a real Button and the sheet has been redrawn (both schemes). The failure block is a tighter Banner with an action — Banner is p-lg, has no action slot, and uses --ui-intent-danger-fg where this uses the deeper --ui-text-on-danger-subtle — so it ships as a local recipe with the third-inline-alert observation recorded in needsDesign. Geometry spec covers both voices, and the receiver case is the one worth having: a track with no inset, no fill and no corner, held together by 12px.

items.name: chat-progress
items.title: ChatProgress
items.lead: Shows what an agent is doing as the work unfolds.

docs.lead: Shows what an agent is doing as the work unfolds.
docs.name: ChatProgress
docs.summary: What the agent shows between the question and the answer. Three LIVE-EDGE forms — waiting, thinking, streaming — are one status row with one Status matrix; four RUN forms — activity, steps (a thought chain), parallel (the chain forked into lanes) and measured — escalate from there. Thinking opens into its reasoning. A fifth kind of line, `typing`, is not progress at all but PEOPLE's presence — "Wim is typing" in muted ink — and it is placed on the composer's top edge, never in the thread. Every form is laid on the same lanes (node 16 · text edge 24 · clock 40 · chevron 16), which is why reasoning, a chain and lanes nest without a new indent. A finished run folds to one receipt that re-expands; a failure or a stop ends the line in place. It lives inside the receiver block at the thread's full width, above any partial answer — never a toast and never an overlay, because progress belongs to the turn that produced it.

anatomy.notes: role="status", polite. Carries data-form and data-status (running | done | failed | stopped).

The live edge: a 16px StatusMatrix (waiting, thinking or streaming), a body-sm muted line, an optional clock (a MINIMUM 40px, because a long wait reads "1 min 12 s") and an optional Stop. Failing or stopping re-renders THIS row — slot `chat-progress-failure` once failed — so the same matrix draws its ending in place. The `icon` slot replaces the matrix with a product's own mark.

form="typing" only: the Typing matrix at 16px in MUTED ink (a person, never the agent's accent), gap-sm, then one caption line in muted ink — `who` in `chat-progress-presence-who`, which truncates, then the verb, which never does (40CC, 40E1). No clock, no Stop, no receipt, no disclosure.

A running run's root, and the disclosure trigger: the run's glyph in the node lane (Thinking or Working matrix, 16), its name in label-md 600 secondary, an optional muted `meta` (" · 1 done"), the clock lane and the chevron slot at the trailing end. Once the run ends it is the RECEIPT instead: CheckCircle in success ink, AlertTriangle in warning ink when any node failed, MinusCircle muted when stopped — 16px — then the receipt line and the chevron. Hover takes the receipt's ink to secondary, no fill.
A 16px column: the glyph, and below it the rail — 1px of border-default at x 8–9, stopping 4px clear of the glyph above and the one below.

The thought, hanging from the root at the 24px text edge with the rail at its full height. Running: capped at five lines (`5lh` of body-sm, plus 4px), anchored to the bottom, with a 24px Fade to bg-base at the top. Done: the whole text, paragraphs at gap-sm, body-sm muted. aria-live=off — see a11y.

A <ul> of `chat-progress-step`: node lane, then the label (body-sm; current = secondary 500, failed = danger 500, else muted), the clock lane, an EMPTY chevron slot so every clock aligns, and under the label its chips (6px below) or prose (4px below; label-sm, stopping 64px short of the trailing edge). space-md under a step.

A nested step leaves the rail on a tick — 11px at the first line's centre, 4px short of its 14px glyph — so its label starts at 46, not at a second indent. space-sm under a branch. The rail runs on past the last branch to the next node, or ends at the last tick when nothing follows.
bg-elevated, radius-sm, 6px × 2px, label-sm muted, an optional 12px kind glyph; chips wrap at gap-xs.

The spine forked: every lane a branch on a tick at its pill's centre line (16), the rail ending at the last. Each `chat-progress-lane` is a 32px pill — bg-elevated, radius-md, px-md — with a 14px glyph, a 104px name lane (label-md 600; it never truncates), the activity (flexes, always truncates), the clock and the chevron slot. A lane with its own `steps` opens to that chain inside the pill (py-sm), on the same lanes one level in. The root sits pe-md so its clock lines up over the lanes'.
One pill per named source: bg-elevated, radius-md, px-md py-sm. The verb is label-md 600 in text-ink-secondary and never shrinks; the detail truncates and never wraps.
The Progress primitive at size sm with hasValueText. Not hand-rolled: a bare track has no role="progressbar", no aria-valuenow, and no reason to reach for --ui-bg-accent-legible.
The Collapsible panel under the root row.

docs.composition:
ChatProgress  form="typing"     who!  label!  isHeld?                 — presence, on the composer's top edge
ChatProgress  form="waiting" | "streaming"  label!                      duration?
ChatProgress  form="thinking"   label!  reasoning?: string[]          duration?  icon?
ChatProgress  form="activity"   activities!  [{ verb, detail }]
ChatProgress  form="steps"      label!  steps!                        duration?
  step        { id, label, status: done | current | pending | failed,
                icon? (kind glyph), duration?, chips?, detail?,
                retryLabel + onRetryAction (failed only),
                steps?: branch[] }            — branches one level deep
ChatProgress  form="parallel"   label!  lanes!  meta?                 duration?
  lane        { id, name, activity, status, duration?, steps?, retry (failed only) }
ChatProgress  form="measured"   label!  value!  max?
   + isHeld?                                   — the live edge is elsewhere in the turn
   + isComplete? receiptText! expandLabel!     — fold to the receipt
   + errorText?  retryLabel? onRetryAction?    — the failure line, drawn in place
   + stoppedText?                              — the user stopped it
   + stopLabel? onStopAction?                  — Stop, offered on a long wait
   + isOpen? defaultIsOpen? onOpenChange?      — the disclosure, controlled or not

form.notes: A DISCRIMINATED union: `steps` without steps, `parallel` without lanes and `measured` without a value would render an empty box, and each is a compile error. Which form — and, when several are true at once, which one holds the edge (run › thinking › streaming › waiting) — is the caller's, because only the caller knows what the run is doing. `typing` sits outside that order: presence is a different fact from progress, so it never competes for the turn's live edge — and the type refuses every run prop on it (clock, receipt, Stop, Retry, failure, disclosure, icon).

who.notes: Typing only, and required there. Who is typing, already formatted: two are named ("Josef and Wim"), three or more are counted ("3 people") — ONE presence line, never one per person. It truncates first, so the longest name gives way before `label` (the verb) does.

reasoning.notes: Thinking only. One string per paragraph. Turns the status row into a root with the thought hanging from it.

steps.notes: `id` rather than an index key: a chain re-orders as fronts complete. A finished step shows its `icon` — the KIND glyph (Search, FileText, Sparks) — or CheckCircle without one; a running one the Working matrix; a pending one an empty ring; a failed one CloseCircle in danger ink. Retry is typed onto failed nodes only.

lanes.notes: Lanes keep their order for the whole run. A failed lane keeps its failure in its lane: danger glyph, the reason as its activity, Retry across the clock and chevron lanes.

meta.notes: Parallel only: the muted count after the root's name — "1 done".

duration.notes: Already formatted. The caller owns the clock: a status row shows it once a wait passes 5 s, a run's root throughout.

isHeld.notes: Holds every matrix here on its key frame. One thing moves per TURN; when that is a task card or the streaming line below, this run holds. WITHIN the component the rule is applied for you: in a chain only the deepest running node moves and its parents hold; in lanes only the root moves; folded mid-run, the root keeps the moving matrix.

isComplete.notes: Folds the run to its receipt. `receiptText` and `expandLabel` are required alongside it. A run that finishes while mounted folds on its own unless the disclosure is controlled — "the moment the first token lands".

expandLabel.notes: The receipt trigger's accessible name, visually hidden. The receipt line says what happened; it does not say what the control does.

errorText.notes: The run failed. The status line becomes the failure line; the matrix draws its Failed cross in place.

stoppedText.notes: The user stopped it. A one-line form draws the matrix's Stopped square in place; a run with a body folds to a receipt with MinusCircle.

onStopAction.notes: With `stopLabel`. Offered in the status row once a wait passes 30 s — the caller decides when.

icon.notes: Slot: replaces the thinking matrix. A product mark is a product asset, not a library one.

do: Pick the lightest form that tells the truth, and never downgrade mid-run — a status that gets vaguer reads as the agent losing track.
Keep ONE live edge per turn. When the answer starts streaming under a run, the run outranks it; when the run is folded and text resumes, pass `isHeld` here and let the streaming row move.
Give each step its kind glyph. A finished chain should read as a list of what was DONE — searched, read, compared — not a column of identical checks.
Keep the receipt in the thread. Folding is not deleting; it is the record of what the agent did.
dont: Do not draw the thinking line and a typing indicator together while text streams. The sheet calls that a defect in the consumer, not a state.
Do not put a `typing` line in the thread. Presence belongs on the composer's top edge, in muted ink — it is a different fact from progress, and in the thread it would meet the agent's accent matrix.
Do not draw one presence line per person. One line: two named, three or more counted.
Do not put this in a toast or an overlay. Progress belongs to the turn that produced it.
Do not hand-roll the measured bar. Progress carries role="progressbar", aria-valuenow and the legible accent fill.

a11y.role: The root is role="status" — polite, so a reader who asked a question is told what is happening and told again when it stops. The reasoning body is aria-live=off: the root's line already says "Thinking", and a polite region re-reading every streamed sentence of thought would drown it; the finished thought is reachable by re-opening the receipt. The measured form nests a real role="progressbar". Every matrix is decorative (aria-hidden): the line beside it says the state in words, so shape and motion are never the only channel (1.4.1).
a11y.name: Every trigger is a real button: the receipt named by `expandLabel`; a running root by its label and clock; a lane by its name and activity. Retry and Stop are Buttons with required labels. The chain is <ul>/<li> with branches in a nested <ul>, so the count is announced.

keyboard.does: Reaches the root's disclosure, then any lane that opens, then any Retry or Stop.
Toggles the focused disclosure. Base UI's Collapsible.Trigger; nothing is faked.

contrastPairs.role: status lines, the receipt, finished and pending steps, chips' ink, prose, the clock, the presence line and its Typing dots
the root's name and the running step
a lane's name and the activity verb, on their pills
a lane's activity, a chip's label, the activity detail
the done check and the receipt — the only channel saying it finished (SC 1.4.11)
a done lane's check, on its pill
the receipt's AlertTriangle when a step failed
a failed step's cross and label, and the failure line
a failed lane's cross and reason, on its pill
a Lit dot of the live matrix
a running lane's held Working matrix, on its pill
the measured fill against its track
the rail, the ticks and a pending node's empty ring
contrastPairs.why: ADR 0010 keeps border-default deliberately quiet. The rail and ticks are structure the indentation already states; the ring is a PLACEHOLDER whose meaning is the absence of a mark inside it, read against the filled glyphs around it

forwarding.ref: The outermost node. Nothing here is a form control, so §5's exception does not apply.
forwarding.className: The outermost node, so a width or a margin sizes the whole log.
forwarding.native props: The remaining div props land on the same node. The form's own data — label, who, steps, lanes, reasoning, meta, duration, value — is destructured out deliberately: a stray `steps={[…]}` reaching the div would be serialised onto the DOM.

docs.motion: Every moving thing is a StatusMatrix, on its one shared clock (see StatusMatrix's motion note), and at most one of them moves: the deepest running node of a chain, the root of a parallel or folded run, the thinking root, or the status row — and none when `isHeld`. Reduced motion is StatusMatrix's: the key frame, no clock. The disclosure chevrons rotate on duration-fast / ease-out — `transition-[rotate]`, not `transform`, because v4 writes the standalone property; the panel's height is Base UI's. The receipt's hover is a colour transition. The CSS ring spinner of the first release is gone.
needsDesign: The sheet's live-edge table draws Waiting as a matrix with NO words. Here every status row has its line, because a role=status whose only change is a dot pattern announces nothing and carries the state by shape alone (1.4.1). Draw the words, or name where the announcement comes from.

Two drawings for one stop: the edge-cases card ends a status row with the matrix's Stopped square, and the Reasoning sheet's folded root uses MinusCircle. Built as: a one-line form ends in the matrix (the live line drawing its own ending), a run with a body folds to the MinusCircle receipt. Confirm that is the rule.

The sheet's line heights are not the type roles'. It sets rows at 16px and prose at 18px (label-sm) and 20px (body-sm); the roles carry 1.35 / 1.3 leading (17.55px for body-sm), and ADR 0020 §3 — enforced on every story — forbids overriding a role's leading. So rows are 17.55px tall over a 16px node lane, and the reasoning cap is five lines of the ROLE (`5lh`, ≈88px) rather than the sheet's 100. Either the sheet adopts the roles' leading, or a looser reading role is a token decision. The same leading makes a parallel lane 33.55px rather than the sheet's 32: the sheet gets its 8px block inset from a fixed height, the render declares `py-sm` (ADR 0019), so the lane is exactly the activity pill's box — which is the relationship the test asserts.
The ~5 s clock and ~30 s Stop thresholds and the 'a form never downgrades' rule are the sheet's readings, not product decisions — and they are the caller's to apply.
knownGaps: The escalation and the precedence between forms are the caller's: this component renders the form it is given and never moves up the axis on its own.
Branches go one level deep. The lanes have a text edge for a branch and none for a branch's branch; deeper work is a lane that opens to its own chain.

The background-run dock lives in ChatRunDock and the queued sender caption is ChatMessage's. Presence is `form="typing"` here, but PLACING it on the composer's top edge is the caller's: ChatComposer has no slot for it yet.
A lane's open state is internal and uncontrolled. Nothing on the sheet needs a parent to open a lane; say so if a product does.

Retry on the failure line, on a step and on a lane ships as Button ghost · sm. The sheet draws it as bare text in the step's clock lane, 24px tall over a 16px row; built with `-my-xs` so the row keeps its height.

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

ChatProgress gains form="typing": PEOPLE's presence, the sheet's Gaps row made real. One line — the Typing matrix at 16px in muted ink (a person, never the agent's accent), gap-sm, then a caption line in which `who` truncates and the verb never does, so the longest name gives way first. It is not progress and never competes for the turn's live edge: it is placed on the composer's top edge, never in the thread. The type refuses every run prop on it — clock, receipt, Stop, Retry, failure, disclosure, icon — and requires `who`. Placing it on the composer is the caller's for now; ChatComposer has no slot for it.

Chat Progress rebuilt on StatusMatrix with ONE moving mark per turn. The CSS ring spinner is gone. New forms: waiting and streaming status rows (the thinking row's matrix hands over in place to its ending — failed and stopped keep the same element); reasoning under a five-line capped, faded body; a thought chain on a 16px node lane with kind glyphs, chips, prose, one level of branches, a failed status with Retry and a 40px tabular clock; parallel lanes drawn as the activity pill's box (glyph, 104px name, activity, clock, chevron) that open to their own chain. Only the deepest running node moves — the root when parallel or folded, none when isHeld — and a run that finishes while mounted folds to its receipt. Stop past ~30 s and a stoppedText ending. The geometry spec now measures the lane pill (sheet 4040-0) instead of the old step list.

migration.manual: BREAKING: steps take `status: "done" | "current" | "pending" | "failed"` with optional icon, duration, chips, detail and one level of `steps`; the spinner and its data-slot are gone (the row's mark is a StatusMatrix with data-slot="status-matrix"). Pass isHeld to every ChatProgress in a turn except the live edge. Rows are 17.55px at the body-sm role's leading rather than the old 16px.

changes.summary: Chat Message: the Sender gains status="queued" — a turn sent while the agent is still running the last one, captioned in muted ink like Sending ("Queued — runs after this turn"), with statusText required by the type. The Receiver's static block caret is removed: per the Chat status behaviour sheet the turn's one mark is the Streaming matrix in a status row under the text (ChatProgress form="streaming"), placed by the caller. isStreaming still withholds the actions row.

migration.manual: BREAKING: the `chat-message-caret` part no longer renders. While streaming, put `<ChatProgress form="streaming" label="…" />` as the receiver's last child and remove it when the answer settles.

changes.summary: Paper: design fixes pushed back into the chat sheets in Paper, so the sheets match what ships. Chat Progress: the dock's Stop layers are SquareRounded (griddy's Stop hard-codes black and check:licensing rejects it), the dock inset is calc(100% - --ui-space-xl × 2) rather than a raw 48px, the thread marks' glyphs are 16px (the root's metrics, as the caption says), the finished action layer is named Button / secondary / md as drawn, the precedence table's quiet dock row is the dock's own box (14px matrix, radius-lg, p-xs), the reasoning fade is --ui-bg-base rather than #FFFFFF, and the dock annotation states the one-moving-row rule. Chat Sources: the focus ring is var(--ui-bg-base) 2px + var(--ui-focus-ring-color) 4px rather than raw hex; the library card glyph is PdfFile as in the list; the folded discs are the first three distinct kinds in list order (Globe, PdfFile, FileText) and the '+3 more' card draws all three hidden kinds; the gathering row draws a held 14px Working Status matrix where the retired ring spinner stood. The preview panels' shadow already equals --ui-shadow-md's light value — Paper has no shadow token type — so it stays. Rich Turn (dark): the Tasks header gains its chevron, the running task loses a hover fill nothing could cause, and the dock and composer Stop glyphs are SquareRounded. The matching needsDesign notes are removed from the chat-run-dock, chat-sources, chat-progress and chat-tasks docs.

A ghost Button's hover is visible on an elevated surface. Its hover fill is the sheet's --ui-bg-elevated, drawn on the page, so inside any surface that already paints bg-elevated — a Card, a Chat Tasks card, the run dock, a lane pill, a popover panel — the hover was the ground's own colour (1.00:1) and nothing happened. Inside an ancestor that paints bg-elevated the ghost now steps to --ui-bg-hover, the next rung of the interaction ramp that the token test holds past elevated in every seed and both schemes; on the page it is unchanged. Asserted in a real hover, both schemes, as the hovered fill DIFFERING from its ground, which failed on the old code. The class reader shared by check:utilities, check:strokes, check:type-roles and check:token-consumers did not know Tailwind's `in-*` variant and skipped such classes whole — probed with a typo that stayed green — and now strips it.

ChatProgress: what the agent shows between the question and the answer. ONE component with a form axis — thinking, activity, steps, measured — rather than TODO's three items (Progress Long Operations, Progress Stream, Progress Sectioned List). The sheet's own Not built row asked for that and named the reason: the receipt, the motion and the collapse are shared, and three siblings would drift apart on exactly those. `form` is a DISCRIMINATED union, so a step list with no steps and a bar with no value are compile errors rather than empty boxes — an empty box is what reads as the agent having stopped. Terminal states are the same component: `isComplete` folds whatever form was in play to the receipt row (which requires its own line AND a name for the control that re-expands it), and `errorText` replaces the form with the failure line while leaving the log above it — the log is history, not chrome. One disclosure mechanism serves both summary lines: a running step list's group header and a finished run's receipt are the same Base UI Collapsible with different content. Two things are reused rather than redrawn: the measured form IS the Progress primitive at size sm (a hand-rolled track has no role="progressbar", no aria-valuenow, and no reason to reach for --ui-bg-accent-legible — the exact SC 1.4.11 failure that role exists to prevent), and Retry is Button ghost·sm, matching Chat Message. The spinner is CSS: griddy has no spinner glyph, check:icons refuses a private SVG, and a full sunken ring under a quarter accent-legible arc is what the sheet draws. Guarded `motion-safe:` rather than `motion-reduce:` so the reduced-motion default is "does not move". The sheet's shimmer sweep across the thinking label is deliberately NOT built — no motion token describes it and a literal is what check:motion refuses; recorded, along with the observation that it is the same missing decision as TODO's skeleton-animation item. Contract: --ui-intent-success-fg on --ui-bg-base joins NONTEXT_CONTRAST_PAIRS — the receiver block has no container, so the one ground every other success glyph is measured against is the one this component never draws on. Geometry spec covers the activity pill's asymmetric 8/12 inset and the step list's single 24px indent.

items.name: chat-questionnaire
items.title: ChatQuestionnaire
items.lead: Collects a structured answer inside a conversation.

docs.lead: Collects a structured answer inside a conversation.
docs.name: ChatQuestionnaire
docs.summary: The agent asking, inside the thread: a question line followed by tappable options — text rows or image tiles. Single-select answers on tap; multi-select collects and confirms. Once answered it collapses to a receipt — the question stays, the chosen answer becomes a selected Badge, and the rest of the options leave the thread. It has NO container, no fill and no action bar, which is why it is not a ChatWidget payload.

anatomy.notes: A column at gap-md, on the receiver's own ground. Carries data-mode, data-variant and data-answered.
body-md 500 in text-ink-primary while open; body-sm in text-ink-muted once answered, because by then it is context rather than a question.
role="group", named by the question. A 400px-capped column of rows, or a four-across grid of tiles — options read as controls, and a 640-wide row of one sentence reads as prose.
A row: bg-base, radius-md, a 1.5px edge, px-md py-sm, body-sm 500. Chosen means border-edge-focus plus a check in the same blue and the fill UNCHANGED — Card Sorting's active card, verbatim.

The library's AspectRatio at ratio=square over bg-media-floor, with its caption beneath — not a hand-rolled aspect box, so the frame clips, sizes its image from the outside and keeps a well behind it without the call site remembering to. Selection is a 2px outline on the TILE, outside the frame, so the photograph keeps its own edge; a 20px accent check badge sits in the corner.
The chosen mark: 14px in border-focus on a row, a filled accent badge on a tile. The second channel beside the edge (SC 1.4.1).
Multi-select only: Button primary·md carrying the count, and an optional ghost·md Skip. Disabled while nothing is picked.
The receipt's Badge, selected. The filled accent is reserved for exactly three things — Send, Confirm and this.

docs.composition:
ChatQuestionnaire  question! options! mode? variant?
                   value? defaultValue? onValueChange? onSubmitAction?
                   confirmLabel? skipLabel? onSkipAction?     — multi-select
                   answer?                                    — collapses to the receipt

options (list):    [{ id, label, isHandoff? }]
options (tiles):   [{ id, label, src, alt }]

mode.notes: Single COMMITS on tap — the sheet's own rule, and the reason a single-select question has no Confirm to press afterwards. Multiple toggles and waits for Confirm.

variant.notes: A discriminated union with `options`: a tile is a picture and `alt` is not optional on a picture. Both pickers use one selection language, which is the point of the pair.

value.notes: Chosen option ids, always an array — including single-select, where it holds one. Two shapes for one concept is how a caller writes a branch it does not need. Uncontrolled through defaultValue.

onSubmitAction.notes: The answer is FINAL: called on tap in single mode and on Confirm in multiple. Distinct from onValueChange, which fires on every toggle.

confirmLabel.notes: Multi-select only, and the place to put the count — the sheet draws "Confirm — 2 picked". The component does not compose that string: pluralisation is language, and every user-visible string is a prop (§9).

options[].isHandoff.notes: The sheet's "Other — tell me in your own words…". It does NOT answer the question — it calls onSubmitAction with its own id so the caller can move the cursor to the composer, and nothing is selected. It reads in muted ink because it is not one of the answers.

answer.notes: Collapses to the receipt. The question stays: an answer with no question is a fragment, and a thread is read from the top.

do: Put the count in `confirmLabel` — the sheet draws it, and the component cannot pluralise for you.
Pass `answer` once the question is settled rather than unmounting the widget; the receipt is what keeps the thread readable on a second pass.
Give the handoff option `isHandoff` rather than treating it as an answer, so it is not selected and is not counted.
Keep every tile's `alt` about the PICTURE. The caption under it already carries the label.
dont: Do not fill the chosen option. The accent is reserved for Send, Confirm and the answered Badge; an option that fills is as loud as the button that commits it, and it collides with hover.
Do not add a Confirm to single-select. The tap IS the commit, and a second step for a one-tap answer is the thing this pattern exists to avoid.
Do not mix rows and tiles in one question. The sheet draws two pickers, not a mix, and the union refuses it.
Do not put this inside a ChatWidget container. It has no container by design — the question sits on the thread's own ground.

a11y.role: role="group", named by the question, around the options. In multiple mode each option is a toggle button with aria-pressed; in single mode each is a plain button and the chosen one carries aria-current, because a press ANSWERS rather than moving a selection around.
a11y.name: The group is named by the question through aria-labelledby. Each option's own label is its text; a tile's picture carries a required `alt` on top of its caption.

keyboard.does: Walks the options in order, then Confirm and Skip. Every one is a real button.
Chooses. In single mode that also submits; in multiple it toggles.
Nothing — the receipt is text and a Badge, with no controls at all.

contrastPairs.role: the question, and a chosen option's label
a resting option's label
the handoff option, the unchosen options once something is picked, and the answered question
the chosen option's edge and its check — the only channel saying which answer was given (SC 1.4.11)
the answered Badge and the tile's check badge
an option under the pointer
the hover fill
contrastPairs.why: hover is never the only channel and never carries state: selection is an EDGE and hover is a FILL, so the two are on different channels by construction. That separation is also what stops the known bg-hover / bg-selected collision from reaching this component

forwarding.ref: The outermost node.
forwarding.className: The outermost node, so a caller can set the column the question lives in.
forwarding.native props: The remaining div props land on the same node. `onChange` is omitted — the change callback is onValueChange (§1), and accepting both would be two answers to one question.

docs.motion: One transition per option: background-color, border-color and color together at duration-fast / ease-out, and outline-color on a tile. Enumerated rather than `transition-colors`, because the group also covers fill, stroke and text-decoration and none of those may move here. Collapses under prefers-reduced-motion at the token layer.
needsDesign: The tile is square and the sheet draws four across a 640 thread at 154px each. AspectRatio supplies the shape and the column supplies the width, so a narrower thread makes smaller tiles rather than fewer — five or more still do not wrap (see below).

The options are buttons in a role="group", not a radiogroup. Single-select tap-to-commit makes each option an ACTION rather than a selection to move around, so arrow-key roving would be a promise the widget does not keep — but if the design ever adds a separate Confirm to single-select, a radiogroup becomes the right shape and this should change with it.
The 400px option cap, tap-to-commit on single select, and the collapse-to-receipt behaviour are the sheet's readings of the references — confirm with product.
Five or more tiles wrap to a second row and are not drawn. The grid is four across at any count today.
Disabled options are not drawn and not built.

The sheet names --ui-canvas-selection for the tile outline. That token exists in Paper and NOT in the contract, and it resolves to the same value as --ui-border-focus — so the tile picker uses border-focus, which is also what makes the two pickers one selection language. Either the token is minted or the sheet should name border-focus.
RTL is not drawn. The component uses logical properties throughout, so it should mirror; nothing has confirmed it.
knownGaps: The handoff option calls onSubmitAction with its own id and selects nothing — moving the cursor into the composer is the caller's, because the composer is not this component's to reach.
The receipt shows ONE answer. A multi-select question that picked three collapses to a single Badge string the caller composes.
There is no per-option description or icon; an option is a label and, for a tile, a picture.

a resting option's label
the handoff option, the unchosen options once something is picked, and the answered question
the chosen option's edge and its check — the only channel saying which answer was given (SC 1.4.11)
the answered Badge and the tile's check badge
an option under the pointer
the hover fill

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

ChatQuestionnaire: the agent asking, inside the thread — a question followed by tappable options, as text rows or as image tiles. Single-select COMMITS on tap, which is why it has no Confirm; multi-select toggles and confirms with the count in the label (the component does not compose that string — pluralisation is language, and every user-visible string is a prop). Answering collapses it to a receipt: the question stays, the answer becomes a selected Badge, the options leave. Its own item rather than a ChatWidget payload: it has NO container, no fill and no action bar, so six of that component's parts mean nothing here — the Text widget sheet asks for three families in one item and the Questionnaire sheet calls itself one of two, and the drawings settle it. SELECTION IS AN EDGE, NEVER A FILL. Card Sorting's active card verbatim: the fill does not move, a 1.5px border-focus edge and a check in the same blue carry the state, and the filled accent stays reserved for Send, Confirm and the answered Badge. That is also what keeps this component clear of the library-wide bg-hover / bg-selected collision — hover is a fill and selection is an edge, so they are on different channels by construction rather than by hoping about order, and the browser test asserts exactly that (a chosen option's fill EQUALS its neighbour's; its edge does not). The options are buttons in a named role="group", not a radiogroup: a press answers the question rather than moving a selection around, so arrow-key roving would be a promise the widget does not keep — recorded, with the condition under which it should change. A handoff option ("Other — tell me in your own words…") submits its own id and selects nothing, because moving the cursor to the composer is the caller's. check:controls gained an eighth exemption with the reason both bespoke controls exist. The image tile is the library's AspectRatio rather than a hand-rolled aspect box: that frame already clips to radius-md, sizes its image from the outside and keeps a well behind it, and the call site that reinvents it is the one that ships an intrinsically-sized image in a box that crops it. The selection outline stays on the TILE, outside the frame, so the photograph keeps its own edge. The sheet's --ui-canvas-selection is a Paper-only token that resolves to --ui-border-focus, which is what ships — and is what makes the two pickers one selection language.

items.name: chat-run-dock
items.title: ChatRunDock
items.lead: Keeps a running task and its controls in view.

docs.lead: Keeps a running task and its controls in view.
docs.name: ChatRunDock
docs.summary: Work that outlives its turn — a render, an export, a long research pass — while the conversation carries on. Two parts. ChatRunDock sits above the composer, tucked behind its pill: one 32px row per run with a 14px StatusMatrix, the run's name, what it is doing, a clock and Stop. ChatRunMark is the run's line in the thread: where it started, and — when the dock row goes — how it ended (finished with the result's action, failed with Retry, or stopped). Not a toast and not an overlay: the dock is part of the composer's block and scrolls nowhere.

anatomy.notes: A <div role="region"> named by the required aria-label. bg-elevated, radius-lg, p-xs, and inset mx-xl — space-xl each side of the composer's pill, so it reads as tucked behind it. className, ref and native props land here (§5). data-held while the matrices are held. Renders nothing when `runs` is empty.
A <ul>, so a screen reader announces how many runs are going.
An <li>, 32px, ps-md pe-xs, gap-sm. data-measured when the run carries a value.
StatusMatrix size sm (14px): Progress at value/max when the run is measured, Working when it is not. Decorative — the activity line says the state in words. Held while `isHeld`.
label-md 600, text-ink-secondary, natural width. Shrinks and truncates only as a last resort, after the activity has nothing left.
body-sm, text-ink-muted. Takes the free space and truncates to one line with an ellipsis — it never wraps.

caption, text-ink-muted, tabular figures, right-aligned in a fixed 40px lane — the parallel lane's clock — so clocks stack and a ticking one never nudges the row. The lane stays when `elapsed` is absent.
Button ghost · sm · icon-only (24px, radius-sm) with SquareRounded. Named per run by `stopLabel(run)`. Present only when `onStopAction` is.
ChatRunMark root: one line, min-h-8, gap-sm, on the root's metrics. data-kind is started | finished | failed | stopped.
16px. ArrowUpRight muted (started), CheckCircle success (finished), CloseCircle danger (failed), MinusCircle muted (stopped). aria-hidden: the line says it.
body-sm. Muted for started and stopped, text-ink-secondary for finished (label at 600), danger for failed. `detail` follows the label after a middot.
Finished only: Button secondary · md — the result's action ("Open").
Failed only: Button ghost · sm — Chat Progress's failure-line Retry.

docs.composition:
Composer block (caller-owned)      flex flex-col gap-xs
├─ ChatRunDock                     runs! aria-label! isHeld? onStopAction?+stopLabel?
│  └─ row × runs                   matrix · name · activity · clock · Stop
└─ ChatComposer

Thread (caller-owned)
├─ …the turn that launched it
├─ ChatRunMark  kind="started"     label!
├─ …the conversation carries on
└─ ChatRunMark  kind="finished"    label! detail? actionLabel?+onAction?
   ChatRunMark  kind="failed"      label! detail? retryLabel?+onRetryAction?
   ChatRunMark  kind="stopped"     label! detail?

A run ending: drop it from `runs` and append its ending mark to the thread, in the same update.

runs.type: ChatRun[] — { id; name; activity; elapsed?; value?; max? }
runs.notes: One row per run. `value` present makes the row's matrix a Progress meter at value/max (default max 100); absent, it is Working — a run that cannot say how far it is never pretends to. `elapsed` is preformatted ("1:48"); the component owns no clock. An empty list renders nothing, so the composer's block collapses back to the composer alone.

aria-label.notes: The region's name — "Background runs". Required by the type: an unnamed region is a landmark nobody can tell apart.

isHeld.notes: Hold every row's matrix on its key frame. Set it while the thread has a live edge; clear it when the thread is idle, so the dock ticks only then — one moving thing on the page at a time (Chat Progress sheet, 01 Live edge, "Two regions, one motion"). Which matrix is the live edge is a fact about the whole page, which no single component can see, so the caller decides. Even unheld, only the FIRST row moves; every other row holds its key frame — one live matrix per region (Status matrix sheet), so three runs are still one moving thing.

onStopAction.notes: Called with the run's id. Comes with `stopLabel` or not at all (a union). The caller removes the run from `runs` when it has actually stopped; the dock moves focus to the neighbouring Stop when the row goes.

stopLabel.notes: Each Stop's accessible name — "Stop Rendering Story cuts". A function of the run, because three buttons all called "Stop" in one region cannot be told apart (SC 2.4.6).

ChatRunMark.kind.notes: Discriminates what the mark may carry: only finished takes `actionLabel`+`onAction`, only failed takes `retryLabel`+`onRetryAction`. A retry on a finished mark, or an action without its name, does not compile.

ChatRunMark.label.notes: The line in words that say the outcome — the glyph and its ink are never the only channel (SC 1.4.1). Bold on a finished mark.

ChatRunMark.detail.notes: Follows the label after a middot — "3 files · 2 min 6 s".

do: Put the dock in the composer's block, directly above the composer with gap-xs between — it follows the reader down the thread because the composer does.
Hold the dock's matrices (`isHeld`) whenever the thread has a live edge, and let them tick only when it is idle.
Give every run a stable id: rows re-order and leave as runs finish.
When a run ends, drop its row and append its ending mark to the thread in the same update — the record moves, it does not vanish.
Leave a `started` mark in the turn that launched the run, so that turn keeps its record.
dont: Do not float the dock over the thread or announce runs as toasts. Background work belongs to the composer's block and to the thread, not to a layer over both.
Do not set `value` from a guess. A meter that cannot reach the end is worse than Working.
Do not let two regions move at once: a dock ticking under a streaming answer competes for the same glance.
Do not name every Stop "Stop".

Do not render two docks with the same aria-label on one page — two regions with one name are one landmark nobody can tell apart (axe landmark-unique caught it in this item's own stories). One composer, one dock.

a11y.role: The dock is a named region (role=region, aria-label required) holding a list, so its runs are reachable as a landmark and counted. Its matrices are decorative (aria-hidden); the activity line carries the state in words. A mark is a line of text — its glyph is aria-hidden and its words say the outcome.
a11y.name: Dock: `aria-label`. Each Stop: `stopLabel(run)`. A mark's action and Retry are labelled buttons.
a11y.focus: Stop ends a run and its row leaves with the focused button. The dock remembers the index at the click and, when the row actually goes, moves focus to the Stop now at that index (or the last one) — but only if focus was lost, so a reader who has moved on is not pulled back. Stopping the LAST run unmounts the dock; moving focus to the composer is the caller's (see knownGaps).

keyboard.does: Moves through each row's Stop, then out of the dock. Rows themselves are not focusable — they are output.
On a Stop: calls onStopAction(id). On a mark's action or Retry: calls its handler.

contrastPairs.role: a dock row's name, and the Stop glyph
a dock row's activity and clock
a Lit dot of a dock row's matrix

contrastPairs.why: The dock's fill is a lift, not a boundary: nothing depends on finding its edge — its rows are text and named buttons, and it sits against the composer's own pill.

contrastPairs.role: started and stopped marks, glyph and line
a finished mark's line
the finished mark's CheckCircle
a failed mark's line and CloseCircle

forwarding.className: ChatRunDock: root (the region). ChatRunMark: root.
forwarding.ref: root — an HTMLDivElement for both; there is no single inner control
forwarding.rest: root — every div attribute except children. ChatRunDock owns `role` and takes its name only as the required `aria-label` (aria-labelledby is refused, so the name cannot be left out).

docs.motion: None of its own. The FIRST row's matrix moves on StatusMatrix's shared clock while `isHeld` is false — every other row holds, so the dock is one moving thing however many runs it carries — and all of them hold their key frame while it is true — and a held matrix never subscribes to the clock. Rows arrive and leave without a transition: the sheet draws no motion for either.
knownGaps: Stopping the last run unmounts the dock with the focused Stop in it; the dock cannot reach the composer, so moving focus there is the caller's job.

A mark arriving in the thread is not announced by the mark itself — inserting a live region does not reliably announce its content. The thread's own log (or the caller's live region) announces it, as Chat Progress's role=status does for a turn.
The clock is a string the caller formats and re-renders; the dock owns no timer.

a dock row's activity and clock
a Lit dot of a dock row's matrix
started and stopped marks, glyph and line
a finished mark's line
the finished mark's CheckCircle

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

ChatRunDock and ChatRunMark: background runs that outlive their turn. The dock sits behind the composer's pill (bg-elevated, radius-lg, inset space-xl), one 32px row per run with a 14px StatusMatrix (Progress when measured, Working otherwise), name, truncating activity, a 40px tabular clock and a named Stop; the mark is the run's line in the thread — started, finished with an action, failed with Retry, or stopped. A named region, never a toast. The rows' matrices hold while the thread has a live edge (`isHeld`), and even when the thread is idle only the FIRST row moves — one live matrix per region, however many runs.

Paper: design fixes pushed back into the chat sheets in Paper, so the sheets match what ships. Chat Progress: the dock's Stop layers are SquareRounded (griddy's Stop hard-codes black and check:licensing rejects it), the dock inset is calc(100% - --ui-space-xl × 2) rather than a raw 48px, the thread marks' glyphs are 16px (the root's metrics, as the caption says), the finished action layer is named Button / secondary / md as drawn, the precedence table's quiet dock row is the dock's own box (14px matrix, radius-lg, p-xs), the reasoning fade is --ui-bg-base rather than #FFFFFF, and the dock annotation states the one-moving-row rule. Chat Sources: the focus ring is var(--ui-bg-base) 2px + var(--ui-focus-ring-color) 4px rather than raw hex; the library card glyph is PdfFile as in the list; the folded discs are the first three distinct kinds in list order (Globe, PdfFile, FileText) and the '+3 more' card draws all three hidden kinds; the gathering row draws a held 14px Working Status matrix where the retired ring spinner stood. The preview panels' shadow already equals --ui-shadow-md's light value — Paper has no shadow token type — so it stays. Rich Turn (dark): the Tasks header gains its chevron, the running task loses a hover fill nothing could cause, and the dock and composer Stop glyphs are SquareRounded. The matching needsDesign notes are removed from the chat-run-dock, chat-sources, chat-progress and chat-tasks docs.

A ghost Button's hover is visible on an elevated surface. Its hover fill is the sheet's --ui-bg-elevated, drawn on the page, so inside any surface that already paints bg-elevated — a Card, a Chat Tasks card, the run dock, a lane pill, a popover panel — the hover was the ground's own colour (1.00:1) and nothing happened. Inside an ancestor that paints bg-elevated the ghost now steps to --ui-bg-hover, the next rung of the interaction ramp that the token test holds past elevated in every seed and both schemes; on the page it is unchanged. Asserted in a real hover, both schemes, as the hovered fill DIFFERING from its ground, which failed on the old code. The class reader shared by check:utilities, check:strokes, check:type-roles and check:token-consumers did not know Tailwind's `in-*` variant and skipped such classes whole — probed with a typo that stayed green — and now strips it.

items.name: chat-sources
items.title: ChatSources
items.lead: Keeps the sources behind an answer within reach.

docs.lead: Keeps the sources behind an answer within reach.
docs.name: ChatSources
docs.summary: How an answer shows where it came from. Three parts on one data set: an inline citation marker after the clause it supports, a preview that opens from the marker on hover or focus, and the sources block under the answer — folded by default to one line of kind discs and a count, open to a numbered list of link rows, or led by source cards when the answer IS what the agent found. A source's number is its position in the list, so a marker and its row can never disagree. Four kinds — web, file, brand asset, library item — told apart by glyph, never by colour.

anatomy.notes: ChatSources.Provider. Renders no DOM: it holds the turn's sources, the strings, the streaming flag and the portal container, and the id → number map both other parts read. A marker and a block outside one throw — the provider IS the shared list.
The block. Carries data-layout (list | cards) and data-state (gathering | single | folded | open). className, ref and native div props land here.
While sources arrive: role=status, a StatusMatrix status="working" size="sm" (the sheet's 14px status node) and the count, label-md in text-ink-secondary. Nothing to fold yet, so no chevron.

The disclosure trigger — Base UI's Collapsible.Trigger, a real button. Folded: up to three kind discs, the count, a 12px ChevronDown. Open: the count and the chevron rotated up, without the discs (the sheet's 3ZOP).

20px discs at a 6px overlap, each bg-elevated with a 2px ring in the GROUND's colour (ring-base on the page, ring-elevated inside the "+N more" card on bg-sunken discs) and a 12px kind glyph in text-ink-muted. One disc per distinct KIND in list order, at most three.
The caller's `label` — already counted and pluralised. label-md, text-ink-secondary.
The Collapsible panel holding the list.
An <ol role=list> of <li>, so the count is announced and the visible numbers are list positions.

32px, px-sm, gap-sm, radius-md. Lanes: 16px index (caption, tabular, end-aligned) · 16px kind glyph · title (label-md, truncates) · 168px origin (caption, truncates) · 24px link slot. An <a> when the source has an href (or the source's own `render` element), a div when it does not. Hover is bg-elevated; the row whose marker is hovered or open takes bg-accent-subtle and an accent index (data-cited).

The 24px trailing slot: LinkExternal 14 (leaves the product) or ArrowRight 14 (stays in it), in text-ink-link. Shown on row hover and focus-visible; always shown where the device has no hover. The lane is kept on every row so the origins align.

layout="cards", folded: the first `cardCount` sources as 172×96 cards (bg-elevated, radius-md, p-md, no edge, no shadow; title label-md clamped to two lines; a footer of glyph 12, origin, index), then the "+N more" card.
A link like the row, hovering to bg-hover — the step up from an elevated object.
The "+N more" card — a second Collapsible.Trigger, flex-1. Pressing it opens the list and hands focus to the summary that replaces it.

ChatSources.Citation — a <button> pill inside the paragraph: 16px tall, min-width 16, px-xs, radius-full, 2px lead from the word before, centred on the line. Numeral caption, tabular. Rest bg-elevated/text-ink-muted; hover and open bg-accent-subtle/text-ink-link; pressed bg-accent-subtle-hover/text-ink-link-hover; streaming disabled, text-ink-disabled. Two ids share one pill ("2, 5").
The Popover primitive's panel at 320px with gap-md — its own surface, edge, shadow and radius-lg, opened gap-xs (4px) below the marker, start-aligned. Tagged data-chat-sources-preview.
Kind glyph 16, origin caption (flex, truncates), number caption tabular — all text-ink-muted.

Popover.Title at label-md in text-ink-primary, flush (the primitive's inset removed); Popover.Description at body-sm in text-ink-muted, clamped to three lines, absent with no excerpt — no space reserved.

The action link (chat-sources-preview-link: label-sm, text-ink-link, LinkExternal or ArrowRight 12) and, for a grouped marker, the pager (chat-sources-preview-pager): Button ghost·sm icon-only ChevronLeftSmall, "2 / 2" caption tabular, ChevronRightSmall — disabled at the ends.

docs.composition:
ChatSources.Provider  sources! labels! isStreaming? container?
├─ answer text … <ChatSources.Citation sourceIds={["s1"]} /> …
│                 └─ preview (Popover) — origin · title · excerpt? · link? · pager?
└─ ChatSources    label!  isGathering? isHeld?  isOpen? defaultIsOpen? onOpenChange?
   ├─ layout="list"  (default)          — folded summary ⇄ numbered rows
   └─ layout="cards" moreLabel! cardCount?  — cards + "+N more" ⇄ numbered rows

ChatSource  { id, kind, title, origin, excerpt?, href?, isExternal?, actionLabel?, isUnavailable?, render? }
kind        web (Globe) · file (Image) · brandAsset (FileText) · libraryItem (PdfFile)

sources.notes: Provider. The turn's sources in list order; a source's number is its index + 1. Citations refer to sources by `id`, so re-ordering the list renumbers every marker with it.

labels.notes: Provider. The strings the parts need beyond the data — props, never an i18n runtime (§9). One object because a marker reads them far from where they are set.

isStreaming.notes: Provider. Every marker is a disabled button in text-ink-disabled with no preview: the list it points into is not final.

container.notes: Provider. Where previews portal to — the themed element, so a brand scope reaches them (Popover's note).

label.notes: Block. The summary line — "5 sources", "3 sources so far". The caller counts and pluralises.

isGathering.notes: Block. Sources still arriving: a live count beside a working StatusMatrix, no fold.

isHeld.notes: Block. Holds the gathering StatusMatrix on its key frame — set it when another matrix in the turn (Chat Progress's status line) is the live edge. One matrix moves per turn, and only the caller knows the turn.

isOpen.notes: Block. The disclosure, controlled. Uncontrolled through defaultIsOpen (default false — folded). A marker's press opens it through onOpenChange like any other request.

moreLabel.notes: Cards only, required there. The last card's line.

cardCount.notes: Cards only. Sources shown as cards before "+N more". When every source fits with one to spare, all of them are cards and there is no "+1 more".

sourceIds.notes: Citation. Non-empty by type. Unknown ids are dropped rather than drawn as a guessed number.

render.notes: Per source. Slot: the element its links render as — an app router's Link. Passed through, never wrapped (§3).

do: Put the marker after the clause it supports, not at the end of the paragraph — the reader is checking a claim, not a paragraph.
Give a clause that leans on two sources ONE marker with both ids. Two pills side by side read as a footnote stack.
Pass the themed element as `container` inside a brand scope, or the previews paint theme zero.
Keep the block folded by default. Most readers want the answer; the few who want the evidence are one press away, and a marker's press opens it for them.
Use `cards` only when the answer is a list of what was found. Under an ordinary answer, cards out-shout the text.
dont: Do not let the marker carry the answer's emphasis. It is muted at rest on purpose; colour arrives on hover, as the cue that it can be opened.
Do not colour a source by its kind. The kind is the glyph's job, and the accent is reserved for the cited row.
Do not build a marker outside the provider with a hard-coded number. The provider exists so the number and the row agree.
Do not hide an unavailable source. Its number is still in the answer; the row says it has gone.

a11y.role: The block is a disclosure: Base UI's Collapsible.Trigger is a real button with aria-expanded, the list an <ol role=list>. The gathering line is role=status, polite. Each marker is a native <button>; its preview is the Popover's non-modal dialog, named by its title and described by its excerpt.
a11y.name: A marker's name is its visible number followed by the cited titles (": Lighthouse at dusk") in a visually hidden span — label-in-name holds (SC 2.5.3) and "1" alone is never the announcement. The disclosure is named by `label`. Icon-only pager buttons are named by `labels.previousSource`/`nextSource`.

keyboard.does: Reaches each marker in reading order. Keyboard focus opens its preview, as hover does; focus stays on the marker.
Moves into the preview — its link, then the pager. Tabbing out of it closes it.
Unfolds the block and scrolls the cited row into view; the preview stays open.
Closes the preview and returns focus to the marker (Popover).
Toggles the list. From "+N more", focus moves to the summary that replaces it.
Follows the source's link. A row without one, or an unavailable source, is not in the tab order.
