contrastPairs.why: Deliberately inert while the answer streams (the sheet's 40H0 note, 1.94:1): the marker is a disabled native button, which SC 1.4.3 exempts as an inactive control, and the number it carries is not final until the turn settles.

contrastPairs.role: an unavailable source's row
contrastPairs.why: The row is aria-disabled: the source can no longer be opened, and LinkBroken in place of the kind glyph plus the "No longer available" origin say so in shape and words, not only in the faded ink. Inactive content under SC 1.4.3's exemption.

contrastPairs.role: a resting marker's pill, the kind discs and the source cards
contrastPairs.why: A grouping fill, never the boundary (1.11:1 light, 1.24 dark — the sheet's token map). The marker is identified by its numeral and its position after a clause, a card by its text; nothing depends on seeing the fill's edge (SC 1.4.11).

forwarding.className: Block: the root div. Citation: the button. Provider renders nothing to forward to.
forwarding.ref: Block: the root div. Citation: the <button> — the one control, so a caller can focus or measure it.
forwarding.rest: Block: native div props on the root; the block's own props (label, layout, moreLabel, cardCount, isGathering, isHeld, the disclosure trio) are destructured out so none reaches the DOM as an attribute. Citation: native button props on the button, with its own pointer, key, click and focus handlers composed after the caller's (composeEventHandlers) — a caller that calls preventDefault() opts out. `type` and `disabled` are the component's.

docs.motion: Four transitions, all on motionMicro (duration-fast, ease-out): the marker's background-color and color between rest, hover·open and pressed; a row's and a card's background-color as it takes the hover fill or the cited wash; the row's link slot fading in; and the disclosure chevron's `rotate` (Accordion's recipe — `transition-[rotate]`, never `transform`). The preview's own fade-and-scale is the Popover's. Hover intent reuses Tooltip's constants: the preview opens after HOVER_INTENT_DELAY_MS, and because it holds a link it lingers for HOVER_INTENT_SKIP_MS after the pointer leaves the marker so the pointer can cross into it — entering the panel cancels the close. A marker's press scrolls the cited row into view smoothly, or instantly under prefers-reduced-motion (scrollIntoView is JavaScript, outside the token layer's duration collapse, so the component asks the media query itself). The gathering StatusMatrix is the only loop, and it carries its own reduced-motion handling.
needsDesign: No linger constant: the preview's close-after-leave reuses HOVER_INTENT_SKIP_MS, which motion.ts defines for the skip window between tooltips, not for crossing a gap into a panel. A hover-card linger should be named in the motion layer.
The `file` kind is drawn with Image, which reads as image-specific. A generic attachment glyph (File, Paperclip) may be meant.
The brand row's hover slot draws LinkExternal while the brand preview's action draws ArrowRight (in-app). Here both follow `isExternal`: external → LinkExternal, in-app → ArrowRight.

Origins differ between surfaces for the same source: "moma.example · Web" in the preview against "moma.example" in the row, "Brand guidelines · Chapter 4" against "Guidelines · Chapter 4". One `origin` string serves both.
Origin captions are drawn at weight 400; the caption role is 600 and the type-role gate measures it, so they ship at 600. Either the sheet moves or the role table gains an origin exception.

The single-source and unavailable rows are drawn with no px-sm, no index and no link slot. Here the single row drops only the index (there is nothing to number) and both keep the padding and the slot lane so they align with every other row.

Not drawn: the unavailable source's preview; the size-sm / 343px column; dark for each marker state; the preview's touch sheet; focus-visible on rows and cards; how many cards precede "+N more" (2 here, as drawn); what the unavailable row's ink should be if it must stay readable — text-ink-disabled measures below AA as text.
knownGaps: Opening the preview without moving focus into it passes `initialFocus: false` to Base UI's popup through the Popover panel's rest spread, which Popover's own props do not name. If Popover grows an `initialFocus` prop, this should use it.
On touch the preview opens from a tap; there is no bottom-sheet form for narrow screens.
Markers are not announced as sources arrive while streaming; they become operable when `isStreaming` turns off.
A source's `render` element replaces every link that source draws (row, card, preview action). A per-surface slot is not modelled.

items.name: chat-tasks
items.title: ChatTasks
items.lead: Brings proposed tasks into a conversation for review.

docs.lead: Brings proposed tasks into a conversation for review.
docs.name: ChatTasks
docs.summary: The plan the agent is working to — a list it writes, ticks off and revises across turns. Not Chat Progress: progress is the log of one turn and folds to a receipt; a task list is an object in the thread with a title, which the reader can read, approve and change, so it gets a container — the chat-widget card (bg-elevated, radius-lg, p-sm), reused rather than restyled. One list per thread is live, and a revision updates it in place: rows never reorder, a dropped task stays where it stood as Skipped, an added one says New. Four list statuses — proposed (numbered, with an approval footer and no disclosure), running, complete and stopped (each folding to a header whose glyph becomes the list's status). Six row statuses — done, current, pending, needs-you, failed, skipped. The plan never moves: the current task holds Working's key frame, because the turn's live edge is elsewhere.

anatomy.notes: ChatWidget's own root — bg-elevated, radius-lg, p-sm, no border, no shadow — with gap-xs between header and rows where the widget's payloads sit at gap-sm. Carries data-status (proposed | running | complete | stopped). Running, complete and stopped render it AS the Collapsible root, so the card is the disclosure rather than containing one.

32px, px-md, gap-sm, radius-md. Base UI's Collapsible.Trigger while the plan runs; a plain div while proposed. Hover is bg-hover — one step up from the card in both schemes — never bg-elevated, which is the card.

The 16px lane. ListBulleted (text-muted) while open or proposed. Folded it becomes the list's status: the held Working matrix (running), CheckCircle in success (complete), MinusCircle in muted (stopped). data-glyph says which.
label-md 600 in text-primary, truncating. Folded and running, it gives way to the current task's label; the plan's name stays in the trigger's accessible name, visually hidden.
caption in text-muted, tabular-nums, never shrinks. Caller-worded: "2 of 5", "5 of 5 · 3 min", "Stopped at 2 of 5", "2 of 5 · revised", "5 steps · about 3 min".
ChevronDown 12, text-muted, rotating 180° while open — Accordion's and Chat Progress's recipe, and the direction the sheet draws. Absent while proposed.
The Collapsible panel holding the list. Unmounted while folded.
An <ol> — a plan is ordered, and a screen reader is given the count and each position. Flush: no fill, no divider.

An <li>: a 16px glyph lane, the label, an optional trailing lane. 32px minimum, px-md, gap-sm. data-task-status names the row's status (or "proposed"); data-new marks an added task; the current row carries aria-current="step".

The row's lane. done: CheckCircle, success. current: StatusMatrix status="working" size="md" isHeld. pending: a 16px border-default ring. needs-you: the same ring in the warning ink. failed: CloseCircle, danger. skipped: MinusCircle, muted.
The empty status: a 16px circle at the hairline stroke. border-default for pending, border-warning for needs-you.

body-sm. Ink follows the reader's interest: still-to-do is text-secondary, done and skipped recede to text-muted, current is text-primary. Needs-you is label-md (13px at 600) in text-primary. Failed shows the REASON here, in danger ink, on one line. No strikethrough anywhere — the glyph says done. Done, current and pending prefix a visually hidden status word from statusLabels.
The current task's second line — caption in text-muted. The row aligns to its top and takes py-sm when it is present.
Badge, not a lookalike: warning·sm with needsYouLabel on a needs-you row, info·sm with newLabel on a task added in a revision.
A skipped row's trailing caption in text-muted — "Skipped", or "Skipped — you asked for feed only".
Button ghost·sm in a failed row's trailing lane. The row gives back pe-xs for it, as the sheet draws.
Proposed only: the 1-based position in the glyph lane — caption, tabular, right-aligned in 16px. aria-hidden, because the <ol> already announces each position.

Proposed only, when onDropAction is passed: Button ghost·sm isIconOnly with Close, named per row by getDropLabel. Revealed on row hover AND on focus-within, and always shown on a device with no hover. The row takes a bg-hover fill under the pointer only when it can be dropped.
Proposed only: px-sm pt-sm pb-xs, gap-sm. Button primary·md (runLabel), Button secondary·md (changeLabel, optional), and a muted caption pushed to the trailing edge (footnote, optional).

docs.composition:
ChatTasks  status="proposed"                    label! count! tasks! [{ id, label }]
   runLabel! onRunAction!                       — the footer's one filled action
   + changeLabel? onChangeAction?               — together or not at all
   + getDropLabel? onDropAction?                — hover-revealed Close per row, together or not at all
   + footnote?

ChatTasks  status="running" | "complete" | "stopped"
   label! count! statusLabels! { done, current, pending }
   tasks! [{ id, label, status, …words the status needs, isNew? newLabel? }]
     status="done"
     status="current"   activity?
     status="pending"
     status="needsYou"  needsYouLabel!
     status="failed"    reason!   + retryLabel? onRetryAction?
     status="skipped"   skippedLabel!
   + isOpen? defaultIsOpen? onOpenChange?       — the disclosure, controlled or not

status.notes: Behavioural, so required (§2). A DISCRIMINATED union: proposed takes ChatProposedTask[] and the approval props and has no disclosure; the other three take ChatTask[] and statusLabels. A plan that FINISHES while mounted asks to fold — uncontrolled it folds, controlled the parent is told through onOpenChange(false) and decides. Nothing else folds it.

label.notes: The plan's name. `label` rather than `title`, which a div already has as a tooltip, and the word ChatProgress uses for a step group's name.

count.notes: Already worded, because the words change by status and by locale. It counts the tasks that still count — a dropped task is Skipped where it stood and leaves the total: 2 of 5, not 2 of 6.

tasks.notes: Rendered in the order given, and the caller keeps that order stable across revisions — rows never reorder under the reader. Each task's `id` is the React key: a revised plan re-uses rows by id, and an index key would hand one task's state to another.

ChatTask (failed).type: { reason: string; retryLabel?: string; onRetryAction?: () => void }
ChatTask (failed).notes: `reason` REPLACES the label on screen, in danger ink, on one line — write it so it names the task. The label is still read out first, visually hidden. A retry is a handler and a name together, never one of the two.

ChatTask (needsYou | skipped).notes: The words those rows show. Required by the type — a warning badge or a trailing note with nothing in it is a status nobody has said.

ChatTask.isNew.notes: With `newLabel`, required alongside it. Whether a task is still new is the thread's fact (the sheet: until the next turn), so the caller sets and clears it.

statusLabels.type: { done: string; current: string; pending: string }
statusLabels.notes: Required once the plan runs. Done, current and pending are told apart by glyph and ink only, and neither reaches a screen reader (SC 1.3.1); each row prefixes its visually hidden word. The other three statuses already carry visible words.

getDropLabel.notes: One accessible name PER ROW for the icon-only Close. A single string would give eight buttons the same name, indistinguishable in a screen reader's list of controls; only the caller can word "Drop 'Cut a 9:16 Story version'".

isOpen.notes: The disclosure, controlled. Uncontrolled through defaultIsOpen, which defaults to open — except complete, which mounts folded.

do: Keep ONE live list per thread, and update it in place when the plan changes. Re-posting it lower down leaves two plans in the thread that disagree.
Leave a dropped task where it stood as Skipped, and mark an added one New until the next turn. Rows never reorder under the reader.
Count only the tasks that still count in the header — 2 of 5 after a drop, not 2 of 6.
Write a failed task's reason so it names the task — it is the row's only visible line.
Let the turn's live edge be the only moving StatusMatrix. This component holds its own; never pass it a moving one.
dont: Do not use this for one turn's log. That is ChatProgress, which folds to a receipt; a plan is an object that outlives the turn.
Do not strike through a done task. The glyph says done; a strikethrough makes the record of what happened harder to read.
Do not fold a proposed plan. It has no disclosure on purpose: the person who has to approve it must see it.
Do not restyle the card. It is ChatWidget's surface; a second elevated card drifts from the first.

a11y.role: Plain content in a card. The plan is an <ol> of <li>, so a screen reader is given the count and each position; the current row carries aria-current="step". No live region: re-announcing a whole list on every tick is noise, so what a change should say aloud is the caller's (see knownGaps).
a11y.name: The disclosure trigger is named by its visible text — the title (or, folded and running, the current task with the plan's name before it, visually hidden) and the count — and states aria-expanded. Retry, Run, Change and each Close are real Buttons; Close is named per row by getDropLabel.

keyboard.does: Reaches the header while the plan runs, then any Retry in the open list. While proposed: each row's Close (when dropping is offered — revealed as it takes focus), then Run and Change.
Toggles the disclosure on the header — Base UI's Collapsible.Trigger, a real button. Activates any other control.

contrastPairs.role: the title, the current task, a needs-you task
tasks still to do, and every proposed task
done and skipped tasks, the count, the activity line, the skipped note, the proposed index, the footnote, the list and chevron glyphs
a failed task's reason — text in the danger ink, and the CloseCircle beside it
the done glyph and the folded complete header's glyph — the only channel saying a task finished besides the hidden status word (SC 1.4.11)
a needs-you task's ring
a Lit dot of the held Working matrix on the current task and the folded running header
the title under a hovered header
a proposed task under a hovered row
the count and index under a hover
the held matrix in a hovered folded running header
the CheckCircle in a hovered folded complete header
the Needs you badge (Badge warning)
the New badge (Badge info)
a pending task's empty ring
contrastPairs.why: the ring is a PLACEHOLDER for a glyph rather than a boundary anything depends on identifying — what says the task is pending is the absence of a mark inside it, read against the filled glyphs around it, and the visually hidden status word says it in words. Chat Progress's pending ring makes the same argument on the page

contrastPairs.role: the card against the page
contrastPairs.why: ChatWidget's own grouping fill. What makes the plan an object is its title, its count and its list, none of which needs the step to be measurable — the argument ChatWidget and the sender bubble already make

contrastPairs.role: the hover fill on the header and on a droppable proposed row
contrastPairs.why: a hover state is pointer feedback, not information: the cursor change and, on a row, the revealed Close are what it announces, and focus has its own outline

forwarding.ref: The outermost node — the card. Nothing here is a form control, so §5's exception does not apply.
forwarding.className: The outermost node, merged after the card's own gap-xs, so a width or a margin sizes the whole card.
forwarding.native props: The remaining div props land on the same node. The plan's own data — label, count, tasks, statusLabels and the handlers — is destructured out deliberately: a stray `tasks={[…]}` reaching the div would be serialised onto the DOM as an attribute. `title` is omitted from the accepted props because `label` is the plan's name.

docs.motion: Almost none, deliberately — the plan never moves. The current task and the folded running header hold StatusMatrix's Working key frame (`isHeld`), because only the turn's live edge animates and that edge is elsewhere; a held matrix subscribes to no clock. The header's hover fill transitions background-color on duration-fast / ease-out (motionMicro). The chevron rotates on the same timing — `transition-[rotate]`, not `transform`, because v4 writes the standalone property. A droppable proposed row fades its hover fill and its Close in on motionMicro too, opacity rather than mounting so the tab order never changes. The panel opens and closes without a height animation, as Chat Progress's does. All of it collapses under prefers-reduced-motion at the token layer.
needsDesign: A failed row's line: the sheet draws one string, "the reason, in one line", and no task label. Shipped as the reason REPLACING the label on screen, with the label read out first for a screen reader. If the label should stay visible with the reason beside or under it (as Chat Progress's failed step does), the row needs a second line or a separator the sheet does not draw.

Type weights follow the role table, not the sheet: done, pending and skipped labels render at body-sm's 500 (the sheet sets no weight), and the count and activity at caption's 600 (the sheet draws 400). The needs-you label is label-md — the role that is 13px at 600 — instead of body-sm with a weight override, so no type-role exception is needed.

Off-scale: the sheet puts 2px between the current task's label and its activity line. There is no 2px space token; the role leadings (17.55 + 16.2 inside py-sm) land the row at 49.75px against the sheet's 50, so the gap is dropped rather than invented.

The trailing lane has no width rule. A long skipped note ("Skipped — you asked for feed only") never shrinks and squeezes the label; the sheet draws it at 548px where it fits. Truncation, a cap, or wrapping under the label is undecided.
"New" lasting until the next turn and "one live list per thread" are the sheet's own readings (Gaps · thresholds), not product decisions.
knownGaps: Not a live region. A tick, a failure or a needs-you is not announced; a caller that needs one says it in its own polite region — Chat Progress's role=status is the model.
The header count and its words are the caller's: the component does not count tasks, because "2 of 5 · revised" and "Stopped at 2 of 5" are sentences, not arithmetic.
Folded and running, the title gives way to the FIRST task whose status is current; a plan with none (waiting on a needs-you, say) keeps its own title.

Nothing below 343px is drawn; the sheet's Gaps row lists size sm, a list longer than the viewport and focus-visible on task rows as not drawn. Rows are not focusable here, so the last is moot until a row gains an action.
Reordering a proposed plan is not built — the sheet offers drop and "Change it", not drag.

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

ChatTasks: the plan the agent works to, written, ticked off and revised in place. A chat-widget card with a disclosure header; proposed plans show numbered rows with Run / Change it and a per-row drop; running, complete and stopped plans show six row statuses (done, current, pending, needsYou, failed, skipped) and fold to a header whose glyph is the plan's status. The current task holds StatusMatrix Working's key frame — the plan never moves.

Paper: design fixes pushed back into the chat sheets in Paper, so the sheets match what ships. Chat Progress: the dock's Stop layers are SquareRounded (griddy's Stop hard-codes black and check:licensing rejects it), the dock inset is calc(100% - --ui-space-xl × 2) rather than a raw 48px, the thread marks' glyphs are 16px (the root's metrics, as the caption says), the finished action layer is named Button / secondary / md as drawn, the precedence table's quiet dock row is the dock's own box (14px matrix, radius-lg, p-xs), the reasoning fade is --ui-bg-base rather than #FFFFFF, and the dock annotation states the one-moving-row rule. Chat Sources: the focus ring is var(--ui-bg-base) 2px + var(--ui-focus-ring-color) 4px rather than raw hex; the library card glyph is PdfFile as in the list; the folded discs are the first three distinct kinds in list order (Globe, PdfFile, FileText) and the '+3 more' card draws all three hidden kinds; the gathering row draws a held 14px Working Status matrix where the retired ring spinner stood. The preview panels' shadow already equals --ui-shadow-md's light value — Paper has no shadow token type — so it stays. Rich Turn (dark): the Tasks header gains its chevron, the running task loses a hover fill nothing could cause, and the dock and composer Stop glyphs are SquareRounded. The matching needsDesign notes are removed from the chat-run-dock, chat-sources, chat-progress and chat-tasks docs.

A ghost Button's hover is visible on an elevated surface. Its hover fill is the sheet's --ui-bg-elevated, drawn on the page, so inside any surface that already paints bg-elevated — a Card, a Chat Tasks card, the run dock, a lane pill, a popover panel — the hover was the ground's own colour (1.00:1) and nothing happened. Inside an ancestor that paints bg-elevated the ghost now steps to --ui-bg-hover, the next rung of the interaction ramp that the token test holds past elevated in every seed and both schemes; on the page it is unchanged. Asserted in a real hover, both schemes, as the hovered fill DIFFERING from its ground, which failed on the old code. The class reader shared by check:utilities, check:strokes, check:type-roles and check:token-consumers did not know Tailwind's `in-*` variant and skipped such classes whole — probed with a typo that stayed green — and now strips it.

items.name: chat-widget
items.title: ChatWidget
items.lead: Keeps a conversation’s output in a form you can use.

docs.lead: Keeps a conversation’s output in a form you can use.
docs.name: ChatWidget
docs.summary: The artifact container — the thing the agent hands you to take away. One shell with two payload families: TEXT (a header naming the artifact, prose capped and faded, a Copy/Edit bar) and MEDIA (a stage at a fixed ratio, an optional frame rail and caption, an Edit/Download bar). It is one component because the container, the action bar and the dark treatment are identical across both, which is exactly what the sheet's own Not built row asks for. bg-elevated, radius-lg, an 8px inset and no border — the fill alone separates the artifact from the receiver's prose.

anatomy.notes: bg-elevated, radius-lg, p-sm on all four sides, gap-sm. No border and no shadow: the fill is the whole boundary, the same lift the sender bubble uses.

Text family only. px-md pt-xs — which puts the name 20px from the container edge, the same 20px an action-bar label starts at, since those buttons sit at the inset plus their own px-md. Type aligns to type.
label-md 600 in text-ink-primary, truncating. The only part of the header row that may shrink; the icon and the chip are fixed slots.

The receiver block's typography unchanged — body-md 400 at leading-relaxed, paragraphs stacked at gap-md, px-md. Capped at 320px; past that it scrolls, becomes a named region and enters the tab order.

A 48px gradient from the container's own fill to transparent, drawn ONLY while the body scrolls. `from-elevated to-transparent` — two stops the theme already has, which is the answer to the sheet's Conflict: it is not a colour, so no token can express it.

The stage: radius-md inside the container's radius-lg, which is concentric by construction (16 outer − 8 inset = 8 inner). bg-media-floor while empty, overflow-clip, a fixed ratio from AspectRatio's own six.
Slot: controls floating in the stage's trailing bottom corner — the sheet's paging arrows and frame counter.
The carousel's frame strip, a <ul> of Thumbnails so a screen reader is given the count. Named by a required `label`.
The provenance line between media and bar — caption size in text-ink-muted.

The bar, in both families with the verbs swapped. Leading verbs are Button secondary·md; the `end` slot takes the trailing Button ghost·md icon buttons. Pushed apart by a spacer, not by justify-between, so a bar with one verb still puts its icons on the trailing edge.

docs.composition:
ChatWidget                                    — the shared container
├─ ChatWidget.Header   name! icon? chip?      — text family
├─ ChatWidget.Body     scrollLabel!           — text family
├─ ChatWidget.Media    ratio? overlay?        — media family
├─ ChatWidget.Rail     label!                 — media family, carousel
├─ ChatWidget.Caption                         — media family
└─ ChatWidget.Actions  end?
   children: <Button variant="secondary" size="md" icon={<Copy/>}>Copy</Button>
   end:      <Button variant="ghost" size="md" isIconOnly aria-label="Save" icon={<Bookmark/>}/>

Header.name.notes: What the artifact IS. Truncates — a filename is identification, and a wrapped one turns a one-line header into two.

Header.chip.notes: Slot: a Badge, unselected, naming the kind. A fixed slot that never shrinks, so the name gives way first.

Body.scrollLabel.notes: REQUIRED, and applied only while the body actually overflows its 320px cap. A capped body that scrolls is a scrollable region (SC 2.1.1) and needs a keyboard path; a region reachable by keyboard with no name is as useless as a named one nobody can reach. When the content fits, no role, no name and no tab stop — an unconditional tab stop in front of every short draft is the other half of that failure.

Media.ratio.notes: All frames in one widget share it. Mixing ratios is what splits an answer into separate widgets, so this is per-widget rather than per-frame.

Media.overlay.notes: Slot: floats in the stage's trailing bottom corner. Paging arrows and the frame counter live here.

Rail.label.notes: Required. Names the frame list — an unnamed list of thumbnails announces as a list of images and says nothing about what they are.

Actions.end.notes: Slot: the trailing icon buttons. Separate from children so the bar can push them apart without the caller writing a spacer.

do: Reach for this only when the agent is handing over an ARTIFACT — something to copy, edit, download or keep.
Give the media stage its final size from the first byte, so generating, loading and failure happen inside the same frame and the thread never reflows when the image lands.
Put Copy first in a text widget's bar. Copying is what the artifact is for.
Pass a Badge as the header chip rather than styling your own — the sheet's kind chip IS Badge unselected.
dont: Do not put conversation in this container. An explanation, a question, a summary of what the agent just did — those are the receiver block, uncontained. Once everything is a card, the container stops meaning "take this with you" and the thread turns into a stack of boxes.
Do not give the container a border or a shadow. The fill alone is the boundary, and an edge on top of it makes the artifact heavier than the answer around it.
Do not change the container's inset without changing the media's radius. 16 outer minus an 8px inset is what makes the two curves concentric, and it is the rule that breaks visibly.
Do not use this for a questionnaire. That family has no container at all — it is ChatQuestionnaire.

a11y.role: Plain content, with one exception: the body becomes a named, focusable region WHILE it scrolls and is a plain div when it does not. The rail is a real <ul>.
a11y.name: The body's region is named by `scrollLabel`; the rail by `label`. Both are required at the type level. Action controls name themselves — Button's isIconOnly requires aria-label.

keyboard.does: Reaches the body only while it scrolls, then the action bar's controls in order.
Scrolls it, once it holds focus — which is the whole reason the tab stop exists.
Activates the focused action. Every control in the bar is a real Button.

contrastPairs.role: the artifact's name and its body copy
the header glyph, the caption, and every action-bar label
the container against the page
contrastPairs.why: the fill is a GROUPING cue: what makes the artifact an artifact is that it has a name, a bar and a boundary at all, none of which needs the step to be measurable. It is the same argument the sender bubble makes, and the reason neither carries a border

contrastPairs.role: the media stage before a picture lands
contrastPairs.why: it is the GROUND a photograph is judged against, deliberately invariant to both the scheme and the brand — see the contract. Nothing is read on it: what sits there is either a picture or a caller-composed placeholder that carries its own ink

forwarding.ref: Each part forwards to its own outermost node. Body forwards to the SCROLLER rather than to its positioning frame, because scrollTop is what a caller takes a ref for here.
forwarding.className: The outermost node of each part.
forwarding.native props: Spread on the same node. Body's land on the scroller, alongside the conditional region attributes.

docs.motion: NONE, deliberately. The fade over a scrolling body is a static gradient rather than an animation, and the media stage does not animate its arrival because the frame was already reserved from the first byte — an artifact that fades in is one the thread reflowed for. An earlier draft carried `transition-[opacity]` on the action bar; nothing here ever changes its opacity, which makes it the motion version of a prop that does nothing, and it was removed.
needsDesign: The carousel is drawn on the sheet and only half built here: Media takes an `overlay` slot and Rail lays out the frames, but which frame is current and what pressing one does is state the thread owns. A real Carousel is its own item, and the sheet's own structure agrees — its Anatomy section is a single image and the carousel is a separate section.
The action bar's wrap behaviour under 308px is not drawn. The bar never wraps today, which means it overflows in the sidebar.

Button secondary·md carries a 16px glyph and gap-sm; the sheet draws 14px and gap-xs, and the ghost icon buttons at radius-sm where Button md is radius-md. Shipped as Button so the bar cannot drift from the rest of the library — but the sheet and Button should agree on one set of numbers.

The media states (generating, loading, failed) are compositions rather than props: the caller puts a Progress, a DotPattern or a failure well inside the stage. The sheet draws all three; whether they should be a prop is the open question.

Rich body content — headings, lists, links, inline emphasis, code — is drawn as plain paragraphs only, and the vertical rhythm inside the container is undecided. Shares its answer with Chat Message's markdown gap and TODO's Code Block item.
knownGaps: The 320px body cap and the 48px fade are the sheet's own Derived readings, not product decisions.

The fade is drawn unconditionally while the body scrolls, so the last line stays faded when the reader reaches the bottom. Fixing it needs a scroll listener; the mask alternative fades content rather than painting over it and has the same flaw.
Inline editing inside the container, and version history when the agent rewrites the same artifact, are not drawn and not built.
The media stage's 624x480 caps come from the 640 thread; the component takes its width from its container instead, so a wider thread makes a wider stage.

contrast.role: the artifact's name and its body copy
the header glyph, the caption, and every action-bar label
the container against the page
the media stage before a picture lands

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

ChatTasks: the plan the agent works to, written, ticked off and revised in place. A chat-widget card with a disclosure header; proposed plans show numbered rows with Run / Change it and a per-row drop; running, complete and stopped plans show six row statuses (done, current, pending, needsYou, failed, skipped) and fold to a header whose glyph is the plan's status. The current task holds StatusMatrix Working's key frame — the plan never moves.

Two fades that showed their edges. Header's affix fade variant painted its ramp in the page's solid ground under a bar that is the page at 90%, so the strip just below the bar was MORE opaque than the bar — a bright seam exactly where the variant is meant to be seamless; it now paints in ground="affix" and starts at the bar's alpha. ChatWidget's body hand-rolled a 48px two-stop ramp shown whenever the body could scroll, so it kept covering the last message after the reader had scrolled to it; it is now a Fade bound to the scroller (data-slot chat-widget-fade kept).

Fade's two-stop linear ramp is replaced by a perceptual one (new lib item fade-ramp): a Gaussian penumbra sampled at seventeen stops, so there is no corner at either end to read as a stripe or a start line, plus a dark-scheme table that leaves the same perceptual fraction of ink visible as light does (light ink under a dark veil kept 53% of its lightness at 0.5 alpha against 46% in light, so dark trails lingered). Depths move one step to 24/48/96 (sm/md/lg) because the eased ramp's first quarter is under 9% alpha — md 48 covers about what linear 32 did, and dissolves where that one ghosted a single line. fadeMask uses the same profile as the paint's complement. Chosen by rendering six curves at four depths over the shipped copy in both schemes (fade.doc.ts, knownGaps 'Ramp research').

migration.manual: Callers that sized a layout around the band's depth (an action slot placed relative to a 32px ramp, a sticky region offset by -32px) re-check against 48px for md, 24px for sm and 96px for lg. To keep an old depth, set --ui-fade-band-depth on the band's style.

changes.summary: Fade gains scrollContainer and ground="affix". Bound to a scroller, the band's strength follows how much content runs past its edge, easing out over the last band-depth of scroll instead of popping off at the last pixel; it insets itself off a classic scrollbar (right, left in RTL, or bottom) instead of veiling the track; and it renders hidden until measured, server-side too. The strength is written to the band's own style, so scrolling re-renders nothing. ground="affix" paints in the translucent pinned-bar role, so the ramp starts at the bar's own alpha. useScrollEdges exports the measurement under it as scrollDistances(). Card.Body, Combobox and ChatWidget now bind their fades this way.

ChatWidget: the artifact container, as one shell with two payload families. The Text sheet's Not built row asked for one item covering three families; it ships covering TWO, and the third — questionnaire — is `chat-questionnaire`, because the questionnaire sheet draws no container at all: no fill, no header, no action bar, so six of this component's parts mean nothing to it (§7a's Sheet-and-Drawer test). The disagreement is between the two sheets, is recorded in both docs, and the drawings settle it. Compound parts: Root, Header, Body, Media, Rail, Caption, Actions. THREE THINGS WORTH READING. (1) The concentric rule the media sheet says breaks visibly — radius-lg outer, an 8px inset, radius-md inner — is asserted as ARITHMETIC (outer === inner + padding) in the browser test and declared as the repo's only `concentric-radius` geometry case; the media's radius sits on the slot node as well as on its sizer, because a radius living only on an inner sizer is one the laws cannot reach. (2) The body's 320px cap makes it a SCROLLABLE REGION, and the role, the name and the tab stop are applied together and only WHILE it actually overflows — measured with a ResizeObserver over the box and its children, since the content is streamed in. `scrollLabel` is required by the type: an unconditional tab stop in front of every short draft and a nameless reachable region are the same defect wearing different clothes. (3) The sheet raised the bottom fade as a Conflict — a gradient from bg-elevated to its own transparent, which no colour token can express, so either a gradient token pair is minted or the implementation derives it. It is derived: `from-elevated to-transparent`, two stops the theme already has, which resolves the Conflict without a token. Also found by the story-a11y run and recorded rather than papered over: the sheet's generating media state puts a Progress on the dark media ground, where Progress's --ui-text-muted label measures under AA.

items.title: Checkbox
items.lead: Selects independent options, on their own or as part of a group.

docs.lead: Selects independent options, on their own or as part of a group.
docs.name: Checkbox
docs.summary: A binary choice with its label as one control. Supports the mixed state for a parent whose children are partly selected. Controlled or uncontrolled through the shared useControllableState hook.

anatomy.notes: The <label>. Carries data-state (checked | unchecked | mixed) and data-disabled, and IS the click target — padded to 24px tall so the 18px box is not the target on its own.
The real <input type="checkbox">, visually clipped with sr-only but focusable, tabbable and in the form. The forwarded ref lands here (CONVENTIONS §5).
The 18px painted box. aria-hidden — the input carries all semantics.
children. The accessible name, natively.

docs.composition:
Checkbox
├─ children           ReactNode (required) — the label AND the accessible name
├─ isChecked?         controlled
├─ defaultIsChecked?  uncontrolled
└─ isIndeterminate?   always controlled — only the caller knows the children

children.notes: Required. The whole row is one <label>, so the name comes from the DOM rather than an aria-label that can drift from what is on screen.

isChecked.notes: Controlled. Omit and the component owns its state.

isIndeterminate.notes: The mixed state. Deliberately has no `default*` counterpart: mixed is a statement about OTHER checkboxes, so a component that owned it would be guessing. Clicking a mixed box reports true and leaves resolving the children to the caller — which is what browsers do natively.

isDisabled.notes: Sets the `disabled` attribute — never pointer-events-none, which would kill an explaining tooltip.

labelPlacement.notes: Which side of the control the label sits on. end is the shipped inline row. start is the SETTINGS ROW: full width, label first, the control pinned to the end in a fixed lane, so a stack of rows forms one column of controls (#9 Proposals sheet, 03). Visual order only (flex-row-reverse): the input stays first in the DOM, so the peer styling and the reading order hold, and in RTL the sides mirror with the text.

description.notes: A line under the label: body-sm in --ui-text-muted (5.93:1 light, 4.94:1 dark), gap-xs below, --ui-text-disabled when disabled. Inside the <label>, so it is part of the hit target; announced as the input's DESCRIPTION (aria-describedby), with the name pinned to the label text (aria-labelledby) so a long description is never read as the name. A caller's own aria-describedby is kept beside it. With a description the row aligns to the top and the control sits on the label's first line.

onCheckedChange.notes: Fires on every change in both modes. The raw onChange is still forwarded and runs after ours (CONVENTIONS §5).

do: Pass the visible label as children — it becomes the accessible name for free.
Use isIndeterminate on a 'select all' whose children are partly selected, and drive it from the children's state.
Prefer uncontrolled (defaultIsChecked) inside a plain form; the input participates natively.
dont: Do not render a checkbox without children. There is no nameless form — the type requires it.
Do not pass both isChecked and defaultIsChecked and expect the second to matter; the hook warns in development if a component switches modes.
Do not set indeterminate through a ref yourself — it is a DOM property with no attribute, and the component already writes it in an effect.
Do not rely on the box alone as the target. The label is the target; keeping it short does not shrink the 24px floor.

a11y.role: checkbox (native). Mixed state comes from the `indeterminate` DOM property, which maps to aria-checked="mixed" without an ARIA attribute.
a11y.name: The children, via the wrapping <label>. No aria-label is used or needed.

keyboard.does: Moves focus to the input, which is clipped but never hidden from the tab order.
Toggles. Native implicit activation — no JS key handler exists, and none should.
Nothing, per the platform. Enter submits the form; a checkbox that toggled on Enter would be the odd one out.

a11y.target: The sheet's row is 19px tall — under the 24px floor of WCAG 2.5.8. The <label> is padded to min-h-6 so the whole row, box and text together, is one 24px target. The painted box stays 18px, as designed.

contrastPairs.role: the tick on a checked box
the dash on a mixed box
the unchecked box edge
the label

a11y.forcedColors: The tick and dash are real glyphs in currentColor, not a background image, so they survive forced-colors mode where the box's fill does not. Checked reads as a tick, mixed as a dash, unchecked as an empty box.

knownGaps: One size. The sheet draws a single 18px box; no sm/lg is designed.
No isInvalid / errorText. A required checkbox (terms acceptance) has no designed error treatment yet — the field-level error pattern lives on Input.

No CheckboxGroup. The sheet's nested list uses a 26px indent (18px box + 8px gap), which is a composition concern; grouping, the parent's mixed derivation and group labelling are not componentised yet.
Forced-colors behaviour is reasoned from the markup, not asserted in CI — Playwright can force it, and no test does yet.

Mixed hover is CLOSED (2026-11-03, Audit #9 "Missing"), DERIVED like every Checkbox hover: the edge firms from --ui-border-strong to --ui-text-primary, the dash's own ink — the same one-step firming unchecked gets. The sheet's obvious candidate, a --ui-bg-hover fill, measured 1.00:1 against the mixed --ui-bg-sunken fill in light (the two are the same value) and stepped DOWN in dark, where sunken is a fill above every hover and active fill.
labelPlacement and description are CLOSED (2026-11-02, #9): drawn on the #9 Proposals sheet, light and dark, and approved on the Audit #9 sheet.

The row centres its content (`items-center`), matching the sheet. (A row WITH a description aligns to the label's first line instead — that is the description variant's own drawing.) A label wrapping to several lines therefore centres against the box rather than aligning to its first line; the sheet draws only single-line labels.
docs.motion: The box transitions `background-color`, `border-color` and `box-shadow` at --ui-duration-fast with --ui-ease-out. The tick is not separately animated — it is present or it is not, so the checked state is readable the instant it changes rather than a frame later.

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

A mixed (indeterminate) Checkbox now has a hover: its edge firms from --ui-border-strong to --ui-text-primary, the dash's own ink — the same one-step firming an unchecked box gets (control → strong). Closes the Audit #9 "Missing" row (Paper, Components - Handoff). DERIVED, like every Checkbox hover. The sheet's suggested --ui-bg-hover fill was measured and rejected: it equals --ui-bg-sunken in light (1.00:1) and sits below it in dark, so the box would have receded on hover in one scheme only. Browser test added.

Checkbox, Radio and Switch draw their checked/selected look from the native input's :checked (peer-checked:) rather than from React state, so they work as plain form controls on a statically rendered page and before hydration (#34). The check glyph and radio dot are always in the DOM and revealed by the same selector. Checkbox's indeterminate state is still render-time (it has no HTML attribute).

Checkbox and Switch gain labelPlacement ("end" default, "start" = the settings row: full width, label first, control pinned to the end) and description (body-sm muted under the label, inside the <label> so it is part of the hit target). The description is announced as the input's description: the name is pinned to the label text with aria-labelledby so a long description is never read as the name, and a caller's own aria-describedby is kept. With a description the row aligns to the top and the control sits on the label's first line; placement is visual only (flex-row-reverse), so the input stays before the control for every peer-* selector and RTL mirrors with the text (#9; approved on the Audit #9 sheet).

check:motion joins the gate list, and every animating component now documents its motion. The gate rejects a literal duration or easing in registry/ (a discipline that was already perfect — zero hard-coded durations across 26 files — and had nothing keeping it that way), transition-all (CONVENTIONS section 6 has said this since the beginning and nothing enforced it), a keyframe with no reduced-motion guard, and an animating component with no top-level motion: note in its doc. It reads lib recipes alongside components as check:overlays does, so Header's motion is found in @/lib/chrome-control where it actually lives rather than reported as absent. 27 doc files gain a motion: note describing what moves, what drives it and what reduced motion does to it; Sheet's and ImageUpload's existing notes are PROMOTED out of a11y to the top level, where Button already had its, because motion is a description of what a component does rather than solely an accessibility concern and a field meaning one thing at two depths stops being findable. ImageUpload's note is corrected while being promoted: it credited the token layer with stopping its spinner, and what actually stops it is the motion-safe: variant. Two findings are recorded in the notes rather than fixed: Sidebar's collapsible section snaps via the hidden attribute where Accordion animates the identical interaction against Base UI's published height, and Banner reaches for transition-colors where the rest of the library enumerates properties. No component's rendered motion changes; no .tsx is touched.

migration.manual: Documentation only — every change is inside a *.doc.ts, and no component's classes or rendered motion moved. If you consume the doc files and read `a11y.motion`, it has moved to the top-level `motion` key on Sheet and ImageUpload; Button was already there and the other 27 are new.

changes.summary: A real <table> with fixed lanes and one flexing column, three densities (row 36/44/56, inline 12/16/24, body 13/14/16), sortable headers that report rather than sort, row selection whose labels the type requires, and loading and empty bodies that keep the header and the lane widths. The frame carries three corner values, all as drawn: radius-lg outside, the concentric calc(radius-lg - space-xs) on the body's clip — the sheet's 12px, which is not a step on the radius scale — and radius-md on the body's top edge. The row fill, the dividers and the first row's corners all sit on the CELLS — border-radius does not apply in the collapsing border model and a <tr> renders none in either, so the sheet's rounded first row forces the separate model. The dividers are border-b-elevated — the mat itself showing between rows that float on it, rather than a border role free to drift from the surface it imitates. Rows are not tab stops: everything a row does is reachable from the checkbox inside it, and the sheet's focus row is drawn with has-[:focus-visible] on the row. The design corrections are recorded in the doc's needsDesign, the two largest being hover and press painted the same value (shipped per the sheet's own annotation as bg-hover and bg-active, so a press has feedback at all) and the disabled row's text-disabled ink, which measures 2.09:1 in light — a row's data is content, not an inactive control's label, so it ships at text-muted. The gutter's annotated 3px selection edge is NOT shipped: selection is only reachable through the select lane, so a selected row always carries a checked box.

migration.manual: New item — nothing to migrate. `npx shadcn add @bydiorama/table`; it pulls in `cn`, `checkbox` and `use-controllable-state`, and expects react and griddy-icons as peers. Table sorts nothing: hold the sort state and order the rows yourself, and give getRowId a stable id rather than an index or selection follows the wrong rows the first time a column is sorted.

changes.summary: Protect checkbox state contracts

Checkbox, plus the first registry hook. The whole row is one <label>, so the visible text is the accessible name natively and is part of the target: the sheet's 19px row is padded to the 24px floor of WCAG 2.5.8 while the painted box stays 18px. The native input is present and only visually clipped, which keeps Space activation, form participation and the indeterminate -> aria-checked="mixed" mapping — none of which survive a div with role=checkbox. Mixed is deliberately controlled-only: it is a statement about OTHER checkboxes, so a component that owned it would be guessing. State runs through the new use-controllable-state hook (CONVENTIONS §4), the first item under registry/hooks and therefore the first to need the @/hooks alias in all four resolvers (root tsconfig, storybook tsconfig, vitest, storybook main). Four design defects fixed in Paper first: a white tick on the pale-blue accent measuring 1.51:1 and a disabled-ink dash on the sunken well at 1.76:1 (both far under SC 1.4.11's 3:1, now 11.35:1 and 14.11:1 on the correct roles), the unchecked edge moved from border-default (2.14:1) to border-control (3.11:1), and raw radius/gap/tracking values swapped for tokens. Three tooling defects found and fixed while building: the utilities gate had no mt-/ms-/size-/inset- namespaces so a directional-margin typo emitted no CSS unreported (80 -> 193 utilities checked, probed by breaking it); the rem emitter rounded to 3 places, turning the designed 13px label into 13.008px (now 4, which is exact for whole px on a 16px base); and test:browser never regenerated tokens, so the browser suite could assert against a stale stylesheet.

migration.manual: --ui-border-strong changes value in DERIVED dark schemes only (theme zero's light scheme authors it and is unchanged). It was an alpha hairline compositing to 1.78:1 against the dark page — weaker than --ui-border-control at 3.09:1, inverting ADR 0010's own subtle -> default -> control -> strong ordering — and is now built the same way control is, one step nearer the ink at a 4.5:1 floor. Any dark-scheme surface using border-strong will read more defined. Type sizes shift by up to 0.008px where a role is not a multiple of 4.

items.name: combobox
items.title: Combobox
items.lead: Finds and chooses an option by typing or browsing.

docs.lead: Finds and chooses an option by typing or browsing.
docs.name: Combobox
docs.summary: An editable text field with a filtered listbox: one committed value, free text allowed, options in labelled groups, rows that can be links, and an action row that is always present. Focus never leaves the input — the highlighted row is an aria-activedescendant, not a focused element, which is why neither Popover (moves focus) nor Menu (actions, not a listbox) fits. Nothing in it is new surface: the field is Input's control and the panel and rows are Select's. The ARIA 1.2 combobox pattern comes from Base UI's Combobox (ADR 0012), as Multiselect's does. Resolves #17.

anatomy.notes: The field column: label, control, then error and helper text. The panel portals INTO this node, so a brand scope around the field reaches the panel.
A real <label for> naming the input. label-md, text-secondary, Select's px-sm inset — the listbox-picker family, not the bare Input. sr-only when isLabelHidden, never removed.

Input's control, unchanged: h-field-lg/md/sm, px-field-inset-*, the 1.5px border-subtle hairline, bg-field, the two-stop focus ring via focus-within. Open is focused, so the open field always carries the ring.
Optional leading slot, never wrapped (§3). Sized to 16px and muted ink by the control.
The <input role="combobox">. Keeps focus the whole time. Value at the field's type step, weight 500; the ref lands here (§5).

Only while the input has TEXT (not only while a value is committed). A 24px square — the SC 2.5.8 floor — radius-sm (radius-full on a pill), Close 16 in text-muted, bg-hover on hover. Out of the tab order; Escape twice is its keyboard path. Named by clearLabel.
ChevronDown, ChevronUp while open, 16px in text-muted with a 24px hit area. Opens the full list without typing. Out of the tab order; named by triggerLabel. Omit with hasTrigger={false}.

Select's panel: bg-surface, 1px border-subtle, radius-md over a 4px inset (concentric with radius-sm rows), shadow-md, 8px below the field, min-width the field's, capped at --available-height/width, z --ui-z-dropdown.

The ONE live region (role=status, polite). A visible status row on the option recipe for loading (Button's spinner), empty and list error (AlertCircle in intent-danger-fg); otherwise a visually hidden result count. Outside the listbox, whose children may only be options and groups.
role=listbox, and the scroller. aria-busy while isLoading.
role=group named by its heading. Groups are separated by 8px of SPACE, no rule — menuSeparator as shipped.
menuGroupLabel: px-md pt-md pb-sm, label-sm, text-muted. Never highlightable.
Select's row: p-md, radius-sm, gap-sm, body-md, text-primary; rows stack flush. Highlight is bg-hover; selection is weight 600 plus a tick — two channels, never a fill.
Carries the selected row's weight, so the row itself renders exactly its type role (ADR 0020 §3).
A fixed 16px trailing lane on EVERY row — the tick, the link arrow, or nothing — so labels align.

The same row as an <a role="option"> (or linkRender), ArrowUpRight in text-muted in the lane. Enter or a press follows the href and commits nothing; never drawn selected. tabIndex -1: a link is otherwise a tab stop, and Tab would walk into the panel.
"Try again" under a list error: a real option row with a leading RefreshCw, so the keyboard reaches it. Runs onRetry; commits nothing; keeps the list open.

Pinned below the rows (sticky to the bottom of the scrolling list, on the panel's fill), 8px of space above, no rule. While the list scrolls, a Fade (bottom, md, ground surface) sits just above it; hidden at the scroll end and when the list fits.
ComboboxAction: the option recipe with a leading icon slot. role=option, last in arrow order, Enter runs it with the query and closes. Never a value.
caption, px-sm. Error first, both in aria-describedby.

docs.composition:
Combobox   label (required) / isLabelHidden?
           items (required)   ComboboxItem[] | ComboboxItemGroup[]
                              ComboboxItem      { value, label, href?, isDisabled? }
                              ComboboxItemGroup { label, items: ComboboxItem[] }
           value? / defaultValue? / onValueChange?          committed value, by item value
           inputValue? / defaultInputValue? / onInputValueChange?   the text (async hook)
           onSubmitText?                                    Enter with nothing highlighted
           filter?   (item, query) => boolean | null        null = items already filtered
           isLoading? / loadingMessage?
           emptyMessage?   string | (query) => string
           listError? / onRetry? / retryLabel?               the LIST failed, not the field
           resultsMessage?   (count) => string
           action?   <ComboboxAction icon? onAction={(query) => …}>
                       string | (query) => ReactNode
                     </ComboboxAction>
           size? / shape? / surface? / icon? / hasTrigger?
           placeholder? / isDisabled? / isRequired? / helperText? / errorText?
           triggerLabel? / clearLabel? / linkRender? / container? / className?

label.notes: Required — a placeholder is not a label (§10).

items.notes: A flat list or labelled groups. `value` must be unique across groups. `href` makes a row a link; `isDisabled` keeps it visible, unhighlightable and skipped by the arrow keys.

value.notes: The committed value, by item value — not the item, so re-fetched results keep it. Separate from the text: free text can sit in the field while a value stays committed, and the field does not distinguish the two visually (the sheet's rule).

onValueChange.notes: Fires on a commit (Enter or a press on an option), and with null when the text is cleared (clear control, Escape twice, or deleting every character). Never for a link, the action or Try again.

inputValue.notes: Controlled text. A blur never rewrites it — Base UI resyncs the text to the committed label when the list closes, and that resync is refused here because it would throw away free text.

onInputValueChange.notes: Every change to the text. The async hook: debounce and abort in the caller (the component holds no timers and no fetch), pass results back as items, set filter={null}.

onSubmitText.notes: Enter with nothing highlighted — the free text, as typed. The list closes; a surrounding form still submits natively. Named onSubmitText, not onSubmit, because a form's onSubmit receives an event and this receives a string.

filter.default: case- and accent-insensitive contains on the label
filter.notes: Only TYPING narrows the list: reopening after a commit shows everything with the committed row highlighted, not a list of one.

isLoading.notes: aria-busy on the listbox. With no rows to show, a loading status row stands in. Stale rows stay while a refresh is in flight.

emptyMessage.notes: A status row, then the action — an empty result is never a dead end.

listError.notes: The LIST failed. A status row with AlertCircle; the field stays valid (no aria-invalid). Field validation is errorText.

onRetry.notes: Adds Try again as an option under listError.

resultsMessage.notes: Announced politely as results change. A function so the plural is the caller's, in the caller's language (§9).

action.notes: Slot (§3): the row pinned below the list, in every state, last in arrow order. ComboboxAction's children may be a function of the query; onAction receives the query.

size.notes: Input's ladder: 48 / 40 / 32, value body-md / body-md / caption. The panel's rows do not change with it (Select's rule — see needsDesign).

shape.notes: Input's two shapes. full insets one space step wider and rounds the clear square; the panel stays radius-md.

surface.notes: Input's ground pair (ADR 0017): enabled and disabled fills chosen together.

hasTrigger.notes: The chevron. A search field may omit it; the list still opens on typing and ArrowDown.

linkRender.notes: Your router's Link (§9: no framework imports). Receives href, the option role and the row classes.

errorText.notes: Field invalid: danger edge, aria-invalid, the message first in aria-describedby.

container.notes: Where the panel portals. The default keeps it inside any brand scope; pass one only to escape a clipping ancestor.

do: Give every Combobox a label; use isLabelHidden when the design shows none.
Use it where free text matters — search, a person picker that can also search. For one value from a short, known list, use Select.
Pass results by VALUE-stable items, so the highlight and the committed value survive a refresh.
Keep the action row's label in terms of the query: "Search everything for “Jo”".
For async results set filter={null}, debounce in the caller, and drive isLoading / listError from the request.
dont: Do not use listError for a validation problem, or errorText for a failed request — one is the list, the other the field.
Do not put focusable controls inside a row — the row IS the option, and focus never leaves the input.
Do not bold matched substrings: bold is already the selection channel (see knownGaps).
Do not import Base UI types into your own props — check:boundaries fails the build (ADR 0012).

a11y.role: The ARIA 1.2 combobox: an <input role="combobox" aria-autocomplete="list"> controlling a role=listbox, with role=group sections named by their headings and role=option rows (links included). From Base UI.
a11y.name: label via <label for>. errorText and helperText join aria-describedby, error first. The clear control and chevron carry clearLabel and triggerLabel.

keyboard.does: Opens the list and filters it (or fires onInputValueChange for async). Nothing is highlighted until the user moves — free text is never silently replaced by the first match.

Open the list if closed (ArrowDown highlights the first row). Move through rows in order across groups, skipping disabled rows and group labels, ending on the action. No wrap. From nothing highlighted, ArrowUp lands on the last row.
While open: the first row / the action. While closed: move the caret, as in any text field.

On an option: commit and close. On a link: follow it, commit nothing. On the action: run it with the query and close. On Try again: retry, keep the list open. With nothing highlighted: onSubmitText(text), close.
First press closes and keeps the text. Second press (list closed) clears the text and the committed value — the clear control's keyboard path.
Closes without committing the highlight; the free text stays. The clear control, chevron and link rows are out of the tab order, so Tab leaves the field.

a11y.focus: Focus never leaves the input: rows prevent the pointer-down that would blur it, and so does the panel's own inset. The highlight is aria-activedescendant. While open, Base UI's focus manager marks the rest of the page aria-hidden (the input is outside the popup, which makes the manager modal).
a11y.liveRegion: One polite role=status in the panel: the loading / empty / error line, or the result count (resultsMessage) when there are rows. When results replace a status, the highlight follows the row's VALUE: kept if it survived, dropped if not — never left on whatever took its index.

the label

the field's error message

contrastPairs.why: Measured on the sheet at 1.19:1 light / 1.21:1 dark. It is Select's and Menu's value, so not a new defect, and the highlighted row is ALSO announced (aria-activedescendant) and outlined under forced colours. Declared as decorative rather than left unlisted so the number stays measured — and recorded in needsDesign, because a combobox is keyboard-driven far more than a select and this fill is the only visible indicator of where the user is.

forwarding.ref: Goes to the <input> — the form-control exception in CONVENTIONS §5. The wrapper stays reachable through data-slot.
forwarding.className: Lands on the outermost field column (data-slot="combobox"), so className="w-64" sizes the whole field and the panel's min-width follows the control.
forwarding.rest: No native props are spread: every attribute the input carries is owned by the combobox contract (role, aria-*, value). Reach parts with data-slot.

needsDesign: OPEN — highlight contrast. The highlighted row is bg-hover at 1.19:1 (light) / 1.21:1 (dark) against the panel — Select's and Menu's value. Acceptable for a select; a combobox is driven by the keyboard far more, and the fill is the only visible indicator of position. Decide whether the family's highlight should get stronger.
OPEN — panel row size per field size. Rows are body-md / p-md at every field size, as Select's are, so an sm field (32px) opens 46px rows. Confirm, or size the panel with the field.

OPEN — one inset rule for the field family. Label, error and helper take Select's px-sm inset; Input's label sits flush (card.doc.ts already records the alignment gap). Combobox follows Select because it is the same family; choose one rule for all four fields.

OPEN — the pill inset. shape="full" insets one space step wider (16 / 12 / 12) and rounds the clear square, derived from Input's own pill (#18). Whatever #18 lands for Input wins; the popup stays radius-md under a pill field.
OPEN — one empty treatment. Combobox's empty state is a status row on the option recipe (body-md, p-md, text-muted); Multiselect's is button-sm at px-lg. Reconcile.

OPEN — matched-substring emphasis, option descriptions, leading option icons and virtualised long lists are not drawn. Bold is already the selection channel, so a bolded match would collide with it — a different channel is needed if emphasis is wanted.

DERIVED — the clear control (24px, out of the tab order, Escape twice) and the optional chevron trigger are drawn by no other sheet. Confirm they belong to the field family rather than to Combobox alone.

DERIVED — loading, empty and error are single status rows on the option recipe; the spinner is Button's; Try again is an option row with RefreshCw. Confirm the error text colour (text-primary beside a danger AlertCircle) for the family.

INTERPRETED — the sheet places the bottom Fade at the top of the action region (top: -32px, the pre-2026-11 depth; the eased ramp is 48px). Shipped the same way, so it exists only when there is an action row; a list with no action scrolls to the panel edge with no fade. The band is bound to the list (scrollContainer), so it eases out over the last rows rather than switching off at the end.

INTERPRETED — ArrowDown on a CLOSED field opens it AND highlights the first row (Base UI's open-on-arrow, and the APG pattern); typing opens with nothing highlighted. The behaviour table says ArrowDown "opens the list if closed" without saying which.
INTERPRETED — Escape twice clears the committed value as well as the text (Base UI's semantics, and consistent with deleting every character). The table says it "clears the text".
knownGaps: Home/End while open, skipping disabled rows, and the highlight following a row's value across results are reached by stepping Base UI's own arrow-key handling (synthetic ArrowUp/ArrowDown on the input): Base UI exposes no imperative highlight API, disables Home/End for a typeable input, and lets the arrow keys land on disabled combobox rows. Contained to combobox.tsx and asserted in the browser test; worth replacing if Base UI grows the API.

While the list is open, Base UI's focus manager marks everything outside the field and its panel aria-hidden. A second focusable field beside an open combobox is therefore aria-hidden-but-focusable for as long as the list is open (Tab closes the list first). It is Base UI's modal-focus-manager behaviour for an input outside its popup, not something this file opts into.

The glyphs on the field — leading icon, clear, chevron — are text-muted on bg-field, a pair the token contract does not audit (check:contrast refuses to accept it as declared for that reason). Select's chevron and Input's icons sit on the same unaudited pair today. The sheet measures it at the placeholder's 5.93:1 in theme zero; adding [--ui-text-muted, --ui-bg-field] to the contract's pairs is a tokens change for the whole field family, left to that change rather than made here.
No form participation by name (no `name` prop) — the committed value is reported through onValueChange only.
The panel portals into the field's own root by default (as Multiselect's does) so it re-skins under a brand scope; an ancestor with overflow: hidden will clip it. Pass `container` to escape.
No virtualisation: every row is in the DOM. Long async lists should be capped by the caller.
Matched text is not emphasised (see needsDesign).
docs.motion: The control transitions border-color, box-shadow and background-color; rows and the clear square transition background-color; the panel fades and scales from 98% through data-[starting-style]/data-[ending-style] — all at --ui-duration-fast with --ui-ease-out (motionMicro). The Fade's visibility is an opacity transition (Fade's own). The loading spinner is Button's animate-spin, stopped under prefers-reduced-motion.
