changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

design/paper/specs/combobox.geometry.json is back in the tree. geometry.browser.test.tsx and the combobox-option-row case were committed without it, so type-check failed (TS2307) and the browser suite's Vite overlay cascaded into ~170 unrelated failures. The spec is the one extracted from Component --- Combobox on 2026-11-02 (it had ended up in a local stash with unrelated demo exports); its values were re-checked against the sheet's option row (padding 12, gap 8, radius-sm, 16px lane). check:design-spec now covers 13 specs.

Fade's two-stop linear ramp is replaced by a perceptual one (new lib item fade-ramp): a Gaussian penumbra sampled at seventeen stops, so there is no corner at either end to read as a stripe or a start line, plus a dark-scheme table that leaves the same perceptual fraction of ink visible as light does (light ink under a dark veil kept 53% of its lightness at 0.5 alpha against 46% in light, so dark trails lingered). Depths move one step to 24/48/96 (sm/md/lg) because the eased ramp's first quarter is under 9% alpha — md 48 covers about what linear 32 did, and dissolves where that one ghosted a single line. fadeMask uses the same profile as the paint's complement. Chosen by rendering six curves at four depths over the shipped copy in both schemes (fade.doc.ts, knownGaps 'Ramp research').

migration.manual: Callers that sized a layout around the band's depth (an action slot placed relative to a 32px ramp, a sticky region offset by -32px) re-check against 48px for md, 24px for sm and 96px for lg. To keep an old depth, set --ui-fade-band-depth on the band's style.

changes.summary: Fade gains scrollContainer and ground="affix". Bound to a scroller, the band's strength follows how much content runs past its edge, easing out over the last band-depth of scroll instead of popping off at the last pixel; it insets itself off a classic scrollbar (right, left in RTL, or bottom) instead of veiling the track; and it renders hidden until measured, server-side too. The strength is written to the band's own style, so scrolling re-renders nothing. ground="affix" paints in the translucent pinned-bar role, so the ramp starts at the bar's own alpha. useScrollEdges exports the measurement under it as scrollDistances(). Card.Body, Combobox and ChatWidget now bind their fades this way.

Combobox: an editable text field with a filtered listbox — free text, labelled groups, link rows, async loading/empty/error states and an always-present action row, on Input's control and Select's panel (resolves #17). New exports: `Combobox`, `ComboboxAction`, and the types `ComboboxProps`, `ComboboxItem`, `ComboboxItemGroup`, `ComboboxFilter`, `ComboboxSize`, `ComboboxShape`, `ComboboxSurface`, `ComboboxActionProps`. Focus never leaves the input (aria-activedescendant); the ARIA 1.2 pattern is Base UI's Combobox, as Multiselect's is. Three behaviours the sheet asks for and Base UI does not offer are reached by stepping Base UI's own arrow-key handling, contained to combobox.tsx: Home/End while open, skipping disabled rows (Base UI's combobox lets the arrows land on them), and the highlight following a row's VALUE when results change (Base UI keeps the index, so the highlight slid onto whatever replaced the row). Base UI's resync of the text to the committed label on close is refused, so free text survives a blur. Link rows carry tabIndex -1 — an <a href> in a panel portalled into the field's root was a tab stop, and Tab walked into the list instead of closing it. The listbox is itself the scroller, because axe accepts a non-focusable scrolling region only for a combobox's own popup. Status: experimental. Apps that built the pattern locally (patterns/brand-search) can move onto it.

items.name: context-menu
items.title: ContextMenu
items.lead: Offers actions for the item under the pointer.

docs.lead: Offers actions for the item under the pointer.
docs.name: ContextMenu
docs.summary: The same menu, opened by a right-click on a region rather than by a button. Only three parts live here — Root, Trigger and Panel — because Base UI's ContextMenu re-exports Menu's Item, Group, Separator and Submenu verbatim: they are the same rows in the same popup, and duplicating them would create two drawings of one surface. The keyboard path matters more here than anywhere else in this library, because a surface that only opens on right-click is unreachable without a pointer — and it depends on the region being FOCUSABLE, which is the caller's job.

anatomy.notes: The region a right-click opens the menu over. Renders a div rather than wrapping in one, so the area the user aims at is the element the caller already has.
role=menu, from the SHARED menu surface — the same recipe Menu.Panel uses. Anchored to the POINTER, not to an element, so it takes no side or align.
Menu's own parts, used inside this root. Not re-exported here: one surface, one set of parts.

docs.composition:
ContextMenu                  isOpen? / defaultIsOpen? / onOpenChange?
├─ ContextMenu.Trigger       render? — the region that responds to a right-click
└─ ContextMenu.Panel         container?
   ├─ Menu.Item              icon? / trailing? / isDisabled? / onSelect?
   ├─ Menu.Separator
   └─ Menu.Group label="…"

isOpen.notes: Controlled open state. Omit and the menu owns it.

onOpenChange.notes: Fires for the right-click, the context-menu key, Escape, an outside press and a chosen item.

Trigger.render.notes: Slot: the region itself. Never wrapped (§3) — the hit area is the caller's own element.

Panel.container.notes: Where to portal. Theme tokens are INHERITED custom properties, so a panel on document.body leaves a brand scope behind and paints theme zero.

do: Give every context menu action a second route — a toolbar button, a Menu, a keyboard shortcut. A right-click is a shortcut, never the only way to do something.
Keep the trigger region visibly bounded, or nobody discovers it is there.
Use Menu.Item and Menu.Separator inside it. They are the same parts by construction.
dont: Do not make a context menu the only path to an action. Touch has no right-click.
Do not nest a ContextMenu inside another ContextMenu's trigger — the inner one wins and the outer becomes unreachable.
Do not suppress the browser's own context menu on a region where the user might want it — a text selection, an image, a link.

a11y.role: menu, with menuitem rows — Base UI's, identical to Menu's.
a11y.name: The panel has no trigger label to inherit, so the ROWS carry all the meaning. Give the trigger region an accessible name of its own if the menu's actions depend on which region was clicked.

keyboard.does: Opens the menu on the focused region — via the BROWSER, not via this library. Chrome and Firefox fire a native `contextmenu` event on the focused element for this chord, and Base UI listens for that event and nothing else. It therefore works only if the region is focusable, and it cannot be proved with a synthetic key press: Playwright dispatches keys through CDP, which never produces the native contextmenu, so such a test fails on working code.
The same, on keyboards that have the dedicated key — and the same caveat.
Moves the highlight through every row, disabled ones included — they are announced as disabled rather than hidden. See Menu's note.
Chooses the highlighted row and closes.
Closes and returns focus to the trigger region.

a11y.focus: The trigger region must be focusable for the keyboard path to exist — pass a focusable element through `render`, or give the region a tabIndex. A div with no tab stop can only ever be right-clicked, and nothing in this library will warn you. Escape restores focus to wherever it was when the menu opened, which is the region only if the region had it.

contrastPairs.role: a resting row — the shared menu surface
the highlighted row
the panel edge
contrastPairs.why: ADR 0010: the panel is identified by its fill and shadow against the page, not by its hairline.

needsDesign: The Context Menu artboard draws the panel with no trigger at all, so nothing says what the right-clickable region looks like — whether it takes a hover, a focus ring, or any affordance announcing that a menu exists there. A surface with no discoverability is one most users never find.
The same inline-versus-flyout question as Menu: the second variant draws a second level expanded inside the panel. See menu.doc.ts, where it is recorded in full.
The panel is drawn identically to Menu's, which is why they share one recipe — confirm that is intentional and not a copy that will be revised on one artboard only.
knownGaps: The keyboard path is the browser's, not ours. Base UI's trigger has no keydown handler at all; it listens for `contextmenu` and nothing else. That is the right layering — the platform already does the job (§9) — but it means the path is untestable here and silently absent on any region the caller forgets to make focusable. A `tabIndex` default on the trigger was considered and rejected: it would put every right-clickable region into the tab order, which is worse.
No long-press support for touch. Base UI does not provide it, and a touch user reaches these actions only through whatever second route the caller supplies.
No checkbox or radio items, though Base UI provides both. The sheet draws neither.
docs.motion: All of it comes from `@/lib/menu-surface`, so it is identical to Menu by construction: the panel fades on `opacity` through `data-[starting-style]`/`data-[ending-style]`, and rows transition `background-color` and `color`, everything at --ui-duration-fast with --ui-ease-out. The panel deliberately does not scale — Base UI points `--transform-origin` at the anchor, which for a menu sits inside the panel, so scaling about it slid the panel's edge while it grew.

contrast.role: a resting row — the shared menu surface
the highlighted row
the panel edge

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

Menu and ContextMenu rows are set in text-body-md, Select's option role, instead of text-body-lg. Closes #22. A design review of a members table, with a role Select and a row Menu on every line, found the menu a size above the dropdown beside it: 16px/500 against 14px/400, in what is the same kind of popup, list and gesture. Matched by ROLE rather than by copying numbers, because since ADR 0020 a role carries its own weight and leading, so naming Select's role is what keeps the two from drifting. Menu.Item, Menu.SubTrigger and every ContextMenu row change together, since they are one recipe. Separately, the consumer className is now merged INSIDE the recipe, through the same cn() as the base classes. The call sites used to run `menuItem(cn(className))`, which merged the caller's classes only with each other and then appended them, so `className="text-body-md"` worked only because Tailwind happened to emit it after `.text-body-lg`. The stylesheet order decided, which is the failure cn() exists to prevent. All four recipes (panel, row, separator, group label) now merge, so a conflicting utility replaces the base one in the rendered class list. The browser test compares a Menu row and sub trigger to a real Select option on size, weight, leading, tracking and family, and asserts the class list holds exactly one type role after `className="text-caption"`. Both fail against the old recipe.

migration.manual: Remove any local override that shrank menu rows (for example an unlayered rule on [data-slot="menu-item"] / [data-slot="menu-sub-trigger"]); the rows now render at body-md on their own. A caller who wants the old 16px row passes className="text-body-lg", which now actually replaces the base role. Local copies of lib/menu-surface.ts need lib/cn.ts beside them; the manifest now declares that dependency.

changes.summary: check:motion joins the gate list, and every animating component now documents its motion. The gate rejects a literal duration or easing in registry/ (a discipline that was already perfect — zero hard-coded durations across 26 files — and had nothing keeping it that way), transition-all (CONVENTIONS section 6 has said this since the beginning and nothing enforced it), a keyframe with no reduced-motion guard, and an animating component with no top-level motion: note in its doc. It reads lib recipes alongside components as check:overlays does, so Header's motion is found in @/lib/chrome-control where it actually lives rather than reported as absent. 27 doc files gain a motion: note describing what moves, what drives it and what reduced motion does to it; Sheet's and ImageUpload's existing notes are PROMOTED out of a11y to the top level, where Button already had its, because motion is a description of what a component does rather than solely an accessibility concern and a field meaning one thing at two depths stops being findable. ImageUpload's note is corrected while being promoted: it credited the token layer with stopping its spinner, and what actually stops it is the motion-safe: variant. Two findings are recorded in the notes rather than fixed: Sidebar's collapsible section snaps via the hidden attribute where Accordion animates the identical interaction against Base UI's published height, and Banner reaches for transition-colors where the rest of the library enumerates properties. No component's rendered motion changes; no .tsx is touched.

migration.manual: Documentation only — every change is inside a *.doc.ts, and no component's classes or rendered motion moved. If you consume the doc files and read `a11y.motion`, it has moved to the top-level `motion` key on Sheet and ImageUpload; Button was already there and the other 27 are new.

changes.summary: Three reported issues on the menu surface. The panel WIGGLED as it opened: Base UI's `--transform-origin` points at the anchor, which for a menu sits inside the panel rather than at a corner — measured at `44.6px -8px` on a 224px panel — so `scale-98` grew the box about a point 45px in from its left edge and slid that edge while it grew, and the origin itself shifted between the first two frames. It only appeared on a CONTROLLED menu, because open state routed through React makes the panel mount with `data-starting-style` and actually run the transition, where the uncontrolled path measured a constant box from frame 0. The scale is gone; the entrance is opacity only, and the test now asserts the rect does not move across the whole entrance rather than that a class is absent. The SEPARATOR is space with no rule, as the sheet draws it and as design confirmed — it keeps `role="separator"`, so the grouping is announced whether or not anything is painted. And the STORIES no longer open themselves: a docs page renders every story at once, so a `defaultIsOpen` anywhere meant menus flew open on load. One Menu story opens itself and its name says so; every ContextMenu story is closed, because a context menu is anchored to the POINTER and opening one without a pointer lands it over its own trigger region.

Menu and ContextMenu, both on Base UI (ADR 0012), sharing ONE surface. They are not cousins that look alike: Base UI's ContextMenu re-exports Menu's Item, Group, Separator and Submenu verbatim, so ContextMenu ships only Root, Trigger and Panel and its rows ARE Menu's. The panel and row recipes live in `lib/menu-surface`, and the browser test renders a Menu row beside a ContextMenu row and compares their computed styles — a lib recipe has no doc for check:contrast to see, so the relationship is what gets asserted. Item.onSelect is named for the verb rather than the pointer, and the type test proves onClick does not compile. Two claims in the first draft of the docs were wrong and the browser found both: that the arrows SKIP disabled rows (they reach them, which is right — a row a screen-reader user cannot reach is one they cannot be told the reason for), and that Shift+F10 is something this library implements (it is not; Base UI's trigger has no keydown handler at all, the BROWSER turns the chord into a native contextmenu event, and that only works if the caller made the region focusable).

items.name: date-picker
items.title: DatePicker
items.lead: Chooses a date with a field and a calendar.

docs.lead: Chooses a date with a field and a calendar.
docs.name: DatePicker
docs.summary: A date field that opens a Calendar. Two things this system already owns, composed: the field is Input's control surface — a field is a field — and the panel is the Calendar card itself rather than a second surface wrapped around one. Anchoring, dismissal and focus restoration come from Base UI (ADR 0012); the grid, its ARIA and its keyboard contract are ours.

anatomy.notes: Label, field, panel and messages as one accessible unit. flex column, gap-sm.
Required. px-sm — bare text inside a rounded surface takes the inset (§6). isLabelHidden renders it sr-only rather than omitting it.
Input's lg control, character for character: h-12, px-md, radius-md, 1.5px border-subtle on bg-field. The browser test compares it to a live Select rather than to a number.
The formatted date, or the placeholder in ink-placeholder. Truncates rather than wrapping — the control has one line.
Chevron down closed, up open. A second channel beside aria-expanded.
Positioning only — no fill, no edge, no radius. The Calendar card IS the panel; wrapping one surface in another would draw two boundaries where the sheet draws one.
Rendered before the helper, so a correction is read first.
Persistent guidance. Stays visible alongside an error.

docs.composition:
DatePicker   label (required)
             value? / defaultValue? / onValueChange?
             isOpen? / defaultIsOpen? / onOpenChange?
             placeholder? / formatValue?
             helperText? / errorText? / isDisabled? / isLabelHidden?
             month? / defaultMonth? / onMonthChange?
             isDateDisabled? / weekStartsOn? / today?
             container?

label.notes: Required — a placeholder is not a label. It disappears the moment a date is chosen, taking the field's name with it.

isLabelHidden.notes: Visually hidden, never omitted. A field with no name is a field a screen reader cannot describe.

value.notes: Controlled selection. null means nothing is chosen.

onValueChange.notes: One callback for choose and clear (§1).

isOpen.notes: Controlled open state. Runs through useControllableState rather than being left to the behaviour layer, because choosing a date has to CLOSE the panel and Base UI offers no imperative close.

onOpenChange.notes: Fires for the trigger, Escape, an outside press and a chosen date.

placeholder.notes: What the empty box shows. NOT the accessible name.

formatValue.notes: The sheet draws 'August 3rd, 2026'. No Intl option produces an English ordinal, and hand-rolling one would be correct in exactly one language — so the default is the platform's and the ordinal is a call-site decision.

isDisabled.notes: The native attribute, never pointer-events: none — a disabled control still has to be hoverable to explain itself.

helperText.notes: Persistent guidance, announced through aria-describedby alongside any error.

errorText.notes: Its presence sets aria-invalid and the danger border, so the two cannot drift apart.

month.notes: Controlled visible month, forwarded to Calendar. Any date within it will do.

defaultMonth.notes: Which month opens first. Omit and the Calendar starts at the selection, or today.

onMonthChange.notes: Fires for the arrows, the month and year selects, and an arrow key that walks off the edge.

isDateDisabled.notes: Marks a date unselectable. It stays FOCUSABLE, so a screen-reader user can still be told why.

weekStartsOn.notes: 0 = Sunday, as the sheet draws it.

today.notes: Which day is marked as today. The clock is an untestable input; see the fuller note on Calendar.

container.notes: Where to portal the panel. Theme tokens are INHERITED custom properties, so a panel on document.body leaves a brand scope behind and paints theme zero. Pass the themed element to bring it back inside.

do: Give the field a label describing what the date is for — 'Deadline', not 'Date'.
Pass `today` in a test or a server render; the real clock makes any baseline a scheduled failure.
Use `isDateDisabled` for unavailable ranges rather than filtering days out — a missing cell breaks the grid's geometry and the arrow keys with it.
Pass `container` when the field sits inside a brand-themed scope and the panel must inherit it.
dont: Do not use the placeholder as the label. It is gone the moment a date is chosen.
Do not reach for a date library to format the value — `formatValue` takes a function, and Intl already knows every locale this component would otherwise have to ship a table for.
Do not wrap the panel in a card of your own. The Calendar already is one.

a11y.role: A button that owns a dialog-less popover: aria-expanded and aria-controls come from the behaviour layer. Inside it, the Calendar is an ARIA grid with its own contract.
a11y.name: The `label` prop, wired with aria-labelledby. Helper and error text are both joined into aria-describedby — an error rarely makes the guidance irrelevant, and dropping it mid-correction is exactly when it is needed.

keyboard.does: Opens the panel. Native — the trigger is a real button.
Closes the panel and returns focus to the trigger.
Enters the open panel at one day, not thirty-one. The Calendar's roving tabindex owns the rest.
Focus lands on the DAY the grid is resting on, not on the previous-month arrow — Base UI's default first-focusable would put the keyboard three Tabs from the thing the field exists to choose.
Move within the Calendar — see its own keyboard table.

a11y.focus: Choosing a date closes the panel and Base UI restores focus to the trigger. CLEARING — clicking the selected day again — deliberately leaves it open, because the next thing that user wants is another date.

contrastPairs.role: the chosen date in the field
the placeholder
the label
the helper text
the error message
a disabled field's remaining ink
the field's resting edge
contrastPairs.why: ADR 0010: the field is identified by its fill, label and padding, not by its hairline. `border-control` is the conformant boundary for engagements that require one.

needsDesign: The sheet draws the trigger at px-lg (16) where Input's control is px-md (12) — the same divergence Select records. Shipped as Input's, because the whole claim is that a field is a field.
One size only. The sheet draws the 48px field and nothing else, so there is no sm/md geometry to follow even though Input, Select and Multiselect all have one.

The field draws 'August 3rd, 2026' — an English ordinal no Intl option produces. Shipped as dateStyle: 'long' ('3 August 2026' / 'August 3, 2026' by locale), with formatValue as the call-site escape hatch.
No disabled, error or busy state is drawn for the field; all three are derived from Input's.
No clear affordance is drawn. Clearing is 'click the selected day again', which is discoverable only by accident — a trailing clear control would need designing.
knownGaps: One date only. No range and no time-of-day; the sheet draws neither.
The panel is a popover, not a dialog: it does not trap focus, because a date field is not a decision that must be acknowledged (§7a).
No min/max props. `isDateDisabled` covers the same ground and is the more general of the two.
The trigger is not a text input — a date cannot be typed. That is the sheet's design, and it costs keyboard users the fastest path to a distant date; the year select is the mitigation.
docs.motion: The field transitions `border-color` and `box-shadow` on focus at --ui-duration-fast with --ui-ease-out; the calendar panel fades and scales from 98% through `data-[starting-style]`/`data-[ending-style]` over the same timing. `scale` is named in the transition list — Tailwind v4 writes `scale-*` standalone, so a list naming `transform` animates nothing.

contrast.role: the chosen date in the field
the placeholder
the label
the helper text
the error message
a disabled field's remaining ink
the field's resting edge

changes.summary: check:dependencies now resolves every `@/` import in a distributed file against the manifest's INSTALL TARGETS, and it found two shipped items importing paths their consumers do not have: multiselect imported '@/ui/badge/badge.tsx' and card-sorting '@/ui/button/button.tsx' — this repo's folder layout, while the CLI installs those files as 'ui/badge.tsx' and 'ui/button.tsx'. Both declared the right registryDependencies, so the CLI delivered the right FILES under the wrong NAMES; nothing compared the two because the gate skipped `@/` with a comment saying 'the alias ones are what registryDependencies is for'. Fixed to '@/ui/badge' and '@/ui/button', with the alias registered in all four resolvers (root tsconfig, storybook tsconfig, .storybook/main.ts, vitest.config.ts) so the path we ship is the path we type-check. Two keys per item in the Vite configs, longer first: Vite matches a string alias as a prefix, so a lone '@/ui/badge' would turn the folder form tests use into '.../badge.tsx/badge.tsx'. The gate checks both halves — an import that matches no target, and a target imported without its registryDependency — and both were probed failing-first.

DatePicker: a date field that opens a Calendar. The field is Input's lg control character for character — the browser test renders one beside a live Select and compares their computed height, radius, border, fill and padding, because asserting 48px on each would pass while the two drifted apart. The panel is positioning only: no fill, no edge, no radius, because the Calendar card IS the panel and wrapping one surface in another draws two boundaries where the sheet draws one. Choosing a date closes it; CLEARING (clicking the selected day again) deliberately does not, since the next thing that user wants is another date. Open state runs through useControllableState rather than being left to Base UI as Popover's is — the component has to close itself and there is no imperative close. The value is formatted with Intl at dateStyle 'long' and formatValue is the call-site escape hatch, so no date library ships with it; the sheet's 'August 3rd, 2026' is an English ordinal no Intl option produces. Two defects found by gates rather than by review: the Base UI popup carries role=dialog and had no accessible name (caught by the story-a11y project, fixed with aria-label), and sr-only composed on top of px-sm leaves a 'hidden' label 16px wide because the later padding undoes the reset — the two are alternatives here, not layers.

items.name: diagram
items.title: Diagram
items.lead: A read-only node-link viewer — pipelines, lineage, org charts, dependency and state graphs — where every node is real UI.

docs.lead: A read-only node-link viewer — pipelines, lineage, org charts, dependency and state graphs — where every node is real UI.
docs.name: Diagram
docs.summary: A read-only node-link viewer — pipelines, lineage, org charts, dependency and state graphs — where every node is real UI. Nodes are an HTML layer and edges an SVG layer under one pan-and-zoom transform, on DotPattern over bg-base. The figure carries a title, a takeaway, an adjacency-list view and a polite announcer; the drawing is one tab stop with a spatial keyboard model, and the view follows focus.

anatomy.notes: A <figure> named by the title and described by the takeaway. bg-surface, border-subtle, radius-md, 24px inset — Chart's frame. className and the rest land here.
label-md, primary. The `label` prop.
body-sm, muted. The takeaway a person wrote.
Button secondary md, icon-only (ListBulleted), aria-pressed. Swaps the drawing for the adjacency list.
`height` px tall (default 480), bg-base under DotPattern, border-subtle, radius-md, clipped. A drag on the ground pans; pinch or Ctrl/⌘ + wheel zooms. A plain wheel scrolls the page.
The one tab stop: role=group, aria-roledescription "diagram", named by the title, described by the keyboard hint.
One transform (translate, scale) for every layer below, at --ui-duration-base with --ui-ease-out except while a drag is panning.

160px wide, at least 56 tall (72 with a two-line description), bg-surface, a 1.5px border-strong ring, radius-md, 12px inline. The label in label-md primary, one line; the description in label-sm 400 muted, clamped at two lines. `renderNode` replaces the content, never the frame.

Each node with its description and group, then its relations as ghost Buttons ("informs Layout", "Brief informs it") that move focus to that node's entry.

docs.composition:
Diagram                       label · description · nodes · edges · layout? · direction? · route?
├─ Diagram.Group              id · label · defaultIsCollapsed? — config; members name it in parentId
├─ Diagram.Controls           zoom in, zoom out, fit (bottom right)
├─ Diagram.Minimap            the whole drawing, the visible part framed (bottom left)
└─ Diagram.Legend             items? · labels? (top right)

label.notes: The visible title, the figure's name and the keyboard region's name.

description.notes: The takeaway. A screen-reader user hears it before anything else.

nodes.notes: Our own shape (lib/graph): id, label (the accessible name), description, position, parentId, data.

edges.notes: source, target, label (the predicate), isDirected (default true), isInferred.

layout.notes: Layered for flows and DAGs; tree for hierarchies (each node's first parent); radial for a tree round its root; none takes every position as given. A node's own `position` wins in every layout.

direction.notes: The flow, for layered and tree.

route.notes: A back edge or two nodes on one rank fall back to straight, rather than doubling back through the source.

nodeSize.notes: The size the layout uses BEFORE the nodes are measured: on the server, and on the first client frame. Measured sizes replace it after mount; a node's width is this width.

selected.notes: Controlled selection, with onSelect. defaultSelected for uncontrolled.

onSelect.notes: Enter or a click; Escape clears.

highlight.notes: A path of node ids (lib/graph's shortestPath answers one): its edges turn active, everything off it dims.

renderNode.notes: The node's content. The frame, its states and its size stay Diagram's.

isLoading.notes: Three bg-sunken node blocks, aria-busy, and no tab stop.

inferredLabel.notes: The word an inferred edge carries. Every user-visible string is a prop.

keyboardHint.notes: The viewport's description: the keys, once.

do: Write the description as the point of the drawing ("Proofs gate the press run"), not as "A diagram of…".
Give saved positions when you have them: the diagram is then a pure server render, and a reload never moves a node.
Name every edge whose meaning is not obvious from its ends; the label is what the keyboard reads.
Use Diagram.Group for a subflow a reader may want to fold away.
dont: Do not use it as an editor: nodes cannot be dragged or connected (plan §8.6). That is a separate decision with its own behaviour layer.
Do not draw a dense network with it — every node is a DOM element. Network is the component for glyph nodes and force layouts.
Do not put interactive controls inside renderNode: the drawing is one tab stop, and its nodes are not focusable.

a11y.role: A <figure> named by the title and described by the takeaway. The drawing is a role=group with aria-roledescription "diagram"; nodes and edges are aria-hidden pictures of what the announcer and the list say.
a11y.name: `label` via aria-labelledby on the figure and the viewport; `description` via aria-describedby on the figure; `keyboardHint` on the viewport.

keyboard.does: Into the drawing, on the selected node or the first in reading order. Inside: walks the focused node's relations, then leaves — never a trap.
Back through the relations to the node, then leaves.
To the nearest node in that direction (straight ahead beats closer but off to the side).
The first and last node in reading order.
Selects the focused node (again clears it); on a relation, goes to its far node; on a collapsed group, expands it.
Opens a collapsed group, or closes the group the focused node is in.
From a relation back to its node; on a node, clears the selection.
Zoom in and out about the centre.
Fit the drawing to the frame.
Pan 64px.

A group's box is drawn round wherever its members land; an automatic layout does not keep outsiders out of it. Give positions for a drawing where that matters.

Edges to collapsed groups are de-duplicated per pair of ends, so two members' edges to one outsider draw once; the list still shows both.
Trees are not a role=tree in the list view; every layout gets the same adjacency list.
The DotPattern ground does not pan with the drawing.

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Diagram (V3): a viewer for flows and hierarchies on lib/graph. HTML nodes over SVG edges under one transform on a DotPattern ground; layered, tree and radial layouts or your own positions, with a size hint so server markup lays out; Diagram.Group draws round its members and collapses to one node that carries their edges; Diagram.Controls, Minimap and Legend. Keyboard: arrows move to the nearest node in that direction, Tab walks a node's relations, Enter selects or follows, Space opens and closes a group, Escape clears; a visually hidden adjacency list names every relation.
