No component's rendered motion changes; no .tsx is touched.

migration.manual: Documentation only — every change is inside a *.doc.ts, and no component's classes or rendered motion moved. If you consume the doc files and read `a11y.motion`, it has moved to the top-level `motion` key on Sheet and ImageUpload; Button was already there and the other 27 are new.

changes.summary: Progress gains an `xs` size — the 6px track the Image Upload sheet draws inside a file row. Additive: md and sm are unchanged. It exists so that row does not hand-roll a track, because a hand-drawn bar has no role=progressbar, no aria-valuenow, and no reason to reach for --ui-bg-accent-legible — the upload sheet fills its own track with --ui-bg-accent, 1.24:1 against the well in light. Reusing Progress makes that failure unrepeatable rather than merely discouraged.

migration.manual: Additive — no existing size changed. `size="xs"` is available on Progress.

changes.summary: A form field whose control is a drop target, in the sheet's four caller-settable states plus a drag-over state the component owns. It is built on a real <input type="file"> with a real <label>, so the keyboard path is the native picker rather than a re-implementation — which is also why it is allowlisted in check:gestures rather than carrying an onKeyDown that does nothing. Five design fixes, each measured: the file row's progress fill was --ui-bg-accent at 1.24:1 against its own track and is now a real Progress at 3.07:1; the Replace pill was outlined in --ui-border-default at 2.14:1 and is now Button variant=outline at 3.11:1; the busy label was --ui-text-disabled at 1.94:1 and is now --ui-text-secondary; the rejection prose was --ui-text-muted on the danger well at 4.00:1 in dark and is now --ui-text-on-danger-subtle at 5.93:1; and 'browse' was styled text with no control behind it, so the component was pointer-only (SC 2.1.1) — it is now a real underlined button. errorText is what puts the field in `rejected`, as on Input, so the message and the state cannot disagree.

migration.manual: New item — nothing to migrate. `npx shadcn add @bydiorama/image-upload`; it pulls in `cn` and `progress`, and expects react and griddy-icons as peers.

items.name: input
items.title: Input
items.lead: Takes a line of text, with room for a label, a hint and a useful error.

docs.lead: Takes a line of text, with room for a label, a hint and a useful error.
docs.name: Input
docs.summary: Single-line text field with its label, helper text and error message as one accessible unit. Three sizes, two shapes, leading and trailing slots.

anatomy.notes: The wrapper. Owns the vertical rhythm between label, control and messages.
Always rendered. isLabelHidden makes it visually hidden, never absent.
The bordered surface. Carries the border, background, focus ring and data-size/data-shape/data-invalid/data-disabled.
The native <input>. Transparent and borderless — the control draws the chrome.
Rendered before helper so the correction is read first.
Persistent guidance; stays visible alongside an error.

docs.composition:
Input   size? lg|md|sm · shape? soft|full
├─ label        string (required) — visually hidden via isLabelHidden
├─ control
│  ├─ icon?     ReactElement — griddy-icons only
│  ├─ input     native <input>
│  └─ iconEnd?  ReactElement — reveal toggle, unit, clear button,
│                or a round submit: <Button isIconOnly shape="full"> on a full field
├─ errorText?   string — presence marks the field invalid
└─ helperText?  string

label.notes: Required by the type system, not by review. A placeholder is not a label — it vanishes the moment the user types, taking the field's name with it.

isLabelHidden.notes: Visually hidden, still in the accessibility tree and still a click target.

size.notes: 48 / 40 / 32px with a 14 / 14 / 12px value (body-md, body-md, caption). All clear the 24px target floor; lg is the touch size for primary forms. md moved from caption to body-md (#16): the owner's frames draw every 40px field value at 14px, and a row mixing Input and Select at md read as two type styles. sm stays caption — the field tokens carry no type step (ADR 0020 §4 keeps type out of density), and a 14px value's 21.7px line in a compact 28px field would leave 3px of block padding.

shape.notes: Omitted follows the brand controlShape (soft in theme zero); explicit soft/full wins. Theme-shaped fields carry data-shape=theme. soft is the form field (radius-md). full is the capsule a search field draws: rounded-full, with the inline padding one spacing step wider (16 / 12 / 12px at default density, a calc on the density token so it still moves with data-ui-density) because a capsule's ends curve in on the text. A round submit goes in iconEnd: on a full field the end padding collapses to the block padding minus the edge whenever the last child is a <button>, so a circle sized lg field + md Button, md + sm, sm + sm sits CONCENTRIC — 8 / 8 / 4px from the edge on every side. Asserted in the browser test.

isDisabled.notes: Native disabled: blocked and out of the tab order.

isRequired.notes: Sets the native required attribute and appends an aria-hidden asterisk to the visible label.

isInvalid.notes: Only needed when the error is reported elsewhere (a form-level summary); errorText implies it.

helperText.notes: Announced via aria-describedby. Kept alongside an error rather than replaced.

errorText.notes: Presence sets aria-invalid and the danger border. Announced first when both messages exist.

icon.notes: Slot. Leading adornment. The component sizes the slot at 16px, the size the sheet draws at every control size. Without that the glyph arrives at whatever the icon library defaults to — griddy hard-codes width/height="24" as attributes — which rendered every icon 50% oversize.

iconEnd.notes: Slot. Trailing adornment — reveal toggle, unit, clear, or a round submit on a full field (see shape). A Button placed here keeps its own accessible name and its own focus outline; the field's focus-within ring also lights, because focus is inside the field.

do: Always pass a real label, even when the design shows none — use isLabelHidden.
Put the error in errorText rather than styling the field yourself; it wires aria-invalid and aria-describedby together.
Use iconEnd for a password reveal or clear button, and give that button its own accessible name.

For a pill search field, use shape="full" with an icon-only Button shape="full" in iconEnd, one Button size under the field (lg field + md Button, md + sm, sm + sm) — that is the pairing the end padding is concentric for.
Control the value with value + onChange, or leave it uncontrolled with defaultValue.
dont: Do not use a placeholder as the label — it disappears on input and is announced inconsistently.
Do not set aria-invalid by hand alongside errorText; the component derives it and the two drift apart.
Do not rely on the red border alone to convey an error — errorText is the non-colour channel WCAG 1.4.1 requires.
Do not add outline-none to the control; the focus ring lives there and suppressing it removes the indicator entirely.

a11y.role: textbox (native input)

keyboard.does: Moves in and out. isDisabled removes it from the sequence.
Native. The component adds no key handling.

a11y.labelling: label is a real <label htmlFor>, so clicking it focuses the field. The id is generated with useId when not supplied, which keeps multiple instances on a page distinct.
a11y.describedBy: helperText and errorText each get an id and both are joined into aria-describedby, error first, so a screen reader reads the correction before the guidance.
a11y.focus: Drawn on the control via focus-within: border moves to --ui-border-focus AND the --ui-focus-ring halo renders. Focus-within rather than focus-visible is deliberate for a text field — a pointer click must show where typing will land.

contrastPairs.role: the value
the placeholder
the value, on a chrome ground (surface="chrome")
the placeholder, on a chrome ground
a disabled field's value on a chrome ground
contrastPairs.why: WCAG 1.4.3 exempts disabled controls, and a disabled field has to READ as unavailable — holding its ink to 4.5:1 would make it indistinguishable from an available one, which is the real failure. Declared rather than omitted because ADR 0017 added a second ground and an unlisted pair is an unchecked pair: this is the exact ink-on-fill combination the new pair exists to keep distinct.

contrastPairs.role: the label
the focus ring
the resting hairline
contrastPairs.why: ADR 0010 § 'Which token an edge takes': the field is identified by its fill, its persistent visible label and its padding, so the hairline is a hint and not the boundary anything depends on. That is a KNOWING trade against SC 1.4.11 on a resting form control, and it is declared here — as a measured decorative pair — rather than left as an absence, because an unlisted pair is an unchecked pair and this is the one edge in the library that is deliberately under the non-text floor. `border-control` is the one-token switch for an engagement that needs the other answer; Checkbox already takes it, because a checkbox's box IS its boundary.

forwarding.ref: Goes to the <input>, not the outermost node — the documented form-control exception in CONVENTIONS §5. A ref to the wrapper cannot focus the field or be handed to a form library.
forwarding.className: Lands on the outermost field wrapper, so `className="w-64"` sizes the whole field and the control follows. Target an inner part with data-slot.
forwarding.rest: Native props (type, placeholder, value, maxLength…) go to the <input> that owns them.

knownGaps: Errors are announced via aria-describedby, which a screen reader reads on focus. An error appearing while focus is elsewhere (after a submit) is NOT announced — that belongs to a form-level error summary with focus management, not to this component. Do not add role="alert" per field: a form failing with five errors would interrupt five times.
No hover state was drawn in the design sheet. The implemented hover (subtle → default border) is DERIVED from Button's secondary variant so controls behave alike — confirm with design.

Multi-line is a separate component (Textarea), not a prop here. Enter submits in an Input and inserts a newline in a textarea, and the height comes from `rows` rather than a size step — one component would have to branch on both. Textarea reuses this control surface and asserts the match against a real Input; what did NOT carry over is the height, which in a textarea is rows line boxes rather than a size step.
No read-only visual state; native readOnly renders as default today.

A round submit at sm (Button sm in a 32px field) sits 4px from the edge, and the control clips its overflow — so the outermost pixel of that Button's 2px focus outline (offset 2px) is clipped. The field's own focus-within ring still shows. At lg and md the 8px gap holds the whole outline.
docs.motion: The field transitions `border-color`, `box-shadow` and `background-color` at --ui-duration-fast with --ui-ease-out, so focus and a validity change arrive as a settle rather than a flash. Nothing else moves; the label and helper text are static.

contrast.role: the value
the placeholder
the value, on a chrome ground (surface="chrome")
the placeholder, on a chrome ground
a disabled field's value on a chrome ground
the label
the focus ring
the resting hairline

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.
Omitted Input shape follows the brand control shape with matching capsule and trailing-control insets; explicit shapes still override it.

Input's danger edge is drawn from the inner input's aria-invalid (has-aria-invalid:) rather than only from props, so a validation script that sets aria-invalid without a React render paints it too (#34). Focus still wins over the danger edge.

Closes #18. Input takes `shape?: "soft" | "full"`, Button's and Avatar's words for the same two shapes (§2), default soft, so nothing that exists changes. full is a capsule: rounded-full, with the inline padding one spacing step wider (16 / 12 / 12px at default density) because a capsule's ends curve in on the text. It is written as a calc on the density token (`--ui-field-*-inset` + `--ui-space-xs`), so it still moves with data-ui-density. The control carries `data-shape`. The trailing round submit uses the existing `iconEnd` slot rather than a new one: on a full field, when the last child is a <button>, the end padding collapses to the block padding minus the edge, so an icon-only Button shape="full" one size under the field (lg field + md Button, md + sm, sm + sm) sits concentric with the capsule, 8 / 8 / 4px from the edge on every side. That is what service-portal's Brand Home search re-implemented as a native input inside a frame recipe, losing Input's label, helper, error wiring, sizes and focus. New Shapes and PillSearch stories; the browser test asserts the capsule radius, the wider inset, the inset following density, and the circle's end gap equal to its top gap within the 0.5px dPR-1 border floor (the last fails 9/5/9px off without the collapse, probed). Known: at sm the 4px gap clips the outermost pixel of the Button's focus outline; the field's own focus-within ring still shows.

Closes #16. A field's value at md is now body-md (14px) in Input, Textarea, Select and Multiselect, where it was caption (12px); lg stays body-md and sm stays caption. Two defects, one decision. First, Select's trigger, and Multiselect's, ignored their size map for text: `SIZE[size]` carried the caption step, then a hard-coded `text-body-md` on the next line won the merge, so every Select rendered 14px at every size while the Input beside it rendered 12 at md and sm. The boxes matched (40px at md), so the geometry relationship test passed for the bug's whole life; only the text inside differed. The hard-coded class is gone and the map is the only thing on either trigger that names a type role. Second, the direction: the maintainer decided md settles at 14px, not 12, because the owner's Paper frames draw every 40px field value at body-md, and service-portal had to patch `[data-slot="control"][data-size="md"]` to get there. sm stays caption because the field tokens carry no type step at all (ADR 0020 §4 keeps type out of density), so the map is the only authority, and a 14px value's 21.7px line in a compact 28px field leaves 3px of block padding. Textarea's md box is now lg's box (127px at 6 rows) with the narrower inline inset. DatePicker draws lg only and does not change. Select's and Multiselect's browser tests now compare the VALUE's font-size and line-height to a real Input's at every size; both fail against the old trigger (probed). Deliberate visual change: the `select` matrix baseline moves (its md and sm rows) and the `textarea` baseline moves (its md row), light and dark, darwin and linux. The input, multiselect and date-picker cases draw lg only and do not move for this. Weight is NOT yet one relationship: Input's value is font-medium (500) at every size, while Select, Multiselect, DatePicker and Textarea take their role's weight (body-md 400, caption 600), so a Select at sm now renders 600 where it rendered 400. Recorded for a maintainer decision rather than changed here.

migration.manual: Remove any local override that forced field text to one size (for example a rule on [data-slot="control"][data-size="md"] setting body-md); md renders body-md on its own now. A form that relied on Select rendering 14px at sm will see 12px there, matching Input; pass size="md" if you meant the larger value.

changes.summary: check:motion joins the gate list, and every animating component now documents its motion. The gate rejects a literal duration or easing in registry/ (a discipline that was already perfect — zero hard-coded durations across 26 files — and had nothing keeping it that way), transition-all (CONVENTIONS section 6 has said this since the beginning and nothing enforced it), a keyframe with no reduced-motion guard, and an animating component with no top-level motion: note in its doc. It reads lib recipes alongside components as check:overlays does, so Header's motion is found in @/lib/chrome-control where it actually lives rather than reported as absent. 27 doc files gain a motion: note describing what moves, what drives it and what reduced motion does to it; Sheet's and ImageUpload's existing notes are PROMOTED out of a11y to the top level, where Button already had its, because motion is a description of what a component does rather than solely an accessibility concern and a field meaning one thing at two depths stops being findable. ImageUpload's note is corrected while being promoted: it credited the token layer with stopping its spinner, and what actually stops it is the motion-safe: variant. Two findings are recorded in the notes rather than fixed: Sidebar's collapsible section snaps via the hidden attribute where Accordion animates the identical interaction against Base UI's published height, and Banner reaches for transition-colors where the rest of the library enumerates properties. No component's rendered motion changes; no .tsx is touched.

migration.manual: Documentation only — every change is inside a *.doc.ts, and no component's classes or rendered motion moved. If you consume the doc files and read `a11y.motion`, it has moved to the top-level `motion` key on Sheet and ImageUpload; Button was already there and the other 27 are new.

changes.summary: Input and Textarea gain `surface: "page" | "chrome"`, and the field fill becomes a GROUND x STATE matrix (ADR 0017). A review flagged the editor inspector for drawing its fields on `bg-sunken` — the value a DISABLED field is filled with. The reading was half right: the drawing was correct and the library was incomplete. Those fields sit on a `bg-elevated` panel, not on the page, and a field is a well cut from whatever contains it, so the same fill means different things on different floors. `resolve.ts` already said so — the comment above `--ui-bg-field` reads 'a field is RECESSED from whatever contains it' — while the derivation reads the page, so the role only held when the page was the container and there was no name for the other case. Four roles now: `--ui-bg-field` / `--ui-bg-field-disabled` on the page, `--ui-bg-field-chrome` / `--ui-bg-field-chrome-disabled` on chrome. `--ui-bg-field-disabled` and `--ui-bg-field-chrome` resolve to the SAME VALUE in theme zero and that is the finding rather than a slip: neutral-90 under a white page reads as unavailable, the identical neutral-90 inside a neutral-95 inspector reads as a well you can type into. So the assertion is not that the four differ — it is that each PAIR separates on its own ground, in both schemes across every stress seed, plus the chrome field reading as a well against the panel. The mechanism of the original collision was a state pointing at a surface role (`isDisabled && "bg-sunken"`); both components now take the enabled and disabled fills TOGETHER from one map, so they cannot be picked apart. The ground is a prop rather than inference because a panel knows it is a panel and an input does not — and the tempting alternative, having chrome surfaces re-point `--ui-bg-field` for their subtree, breaks on exactly the components that need it most, since a Popover, Menu or Select panel is portalled to document.body and inherits nothing. Every value is floored by measurement rather than authored as a step, so a brand whose surfaces sit close together cannot collapse a pair. Light is unchanged; two dark baselines moved, and the dark disabled fill now separates from its field at 1.237 where it used to manage 1.127.

migration.manual: Nothing to change at a call site: `surface` defaults to "page" and every light value is byte-identical. Pass surface="chrome" for a field inside an inspector, island, drawer or bottom sheet — anything floored with bg-elevated — and both its enabled and disabled fills move together. In dark, a DISABLED field's fill changes from #282522 to #2F2C29; if you pinned that value in a test or an override, it moves. Two dark visual baselines were regenerated. Select, Multiselect and Combobox still fill from bg-field directly and want the same prop.

changes.summary: The consumer lockfile now RECORDS a local fork instead of only warning about one, and ADR 0010 stops contradicting Input. Two pieces of contract hygiene from the same consumer review. (1) `lock` already detected a file whose installed content diverged from the registry and printed '⚠ diverges from registry', but the warning went to a terminal while `files` recorded the fork's OWN hash — so from the next command onward a fork was indistinguishable from a clean install, and `sync` reported it as `stale`, the same word a clean install gets when upstream moves. One reads as 'run the update', the other as 'you will lose work'; they printed the same, and a consumer's Badge fork was overwritten across two syncs with every check green. LockedItem gains `forked`: the target mapped to the hash the REGISTRY shipped for it at lock time. The upstream hash is the second half and not decoration — `files[target]` is the fork, so 'has the thing I forked changed underneath me?' has no baseline without it, and that is the question deciding whether a fork still needs carrying. `sync` gains `forked` and `forked-and-stale` statuses and names the affected files ('re-installing this item OVERWRITES: ...'). A fork the registry has since adopted reads as `current`: the flag is a claim about divergence, not a permanent label. (2) ADR 0010 point 3 said --ui-border-control 'currently has no consumer — that is its job, not a defect', which outlived its truth: it ships in Button's outline ring, Checkbox's unchecked box, Multiselect's option box and Switch's hovered off-track, none of them a form-conformance engagement. Read against Input shipping border-subtle, the two descriptions appeared to contradict each other. The ADR gains a § 'Which token an edge takes' stating the actual rule — is this boundary the only thing identifying the control? — and it is now the ONLY place that rule is written; contract.ts defers to it instead of half-restating it, and Input declares its resting hairline as a measured decorative pair so the knowing trade against SC 1.4.11 is a number in check:contrast rather than an absence.

migration.manual: An existing ui.lock.json stays valid — `forked` is optional and absent means 'no forks recorded'. To pick up the flag for a fork you already carry, re-run `lock <item> --revision <sha>`: it re-detects the divergence and writes it down. Nothing changes for a component; the Input change is documentation of an existing decision, not a new value.

changes.summary: Protect input description wiring

Six defects found in the Input design sheet during spec extraction and fixed in Paper rather than transcribed. Two were accessibility failures: the focus state used --ui-border-default (a near-invisible grey shift, failing WCAG 2.4.7/1.4.11) and now uses --ui-border-focus plus the --ui-focus-ring halo; the error state's field border was identical to default, leaving the error conveyed by message colour alone, and now uses --ui-intent-danger-fg at 4.8:1. Four were token-discipline defects: raw 8px radii on every field (now --ui-radius-md), the label ink as raw palette step --ui-neutral-20 (now --ui-text-secondary), the error text as raw --ui-red-40 (now --ui-intent-danger-fg), and raw 8px stack gaps (now --ui-space-sm). The icon variant was additionally a stale pre-redesign node carrying a raw #999999 border, 1px width and the wrong surface — rebased onto the current field spec.

migration.manual: Design-side only; the implementation was built from the corrected values.

changes.summary: CONVENTIONS §5 refined by the first compound component. Two rules that were unambiguous for Button (a single element) diverged for Input. (1) ref: form controls forward to the interactive element rather than the outermost node — a ref to a wrapper cannot focus the field, read a value, or be handed to a form library, which is every reason a caller takes one. (2) className: always lands on the OUTERMOST node so sizing behaves predictably, while native props go to the element that owns them; Input initially put className on the control while spreading rest onto the input, which was inconsistent in a way no gate could see. Both now have browser regression tests asserting computed width and attribute placement.

migration.manual: Components authored before this: check that className reaches the outermost node and that a form control's ref reaches its interactive element.

changes.summary: Second component, first built entirely through the add-component skill. Single-line text field composing label, control, helper and error as one accessible unit: label is a required prop (a placeholder is not a label), errorText derives aria-invalid and joins aria-describedby error-first, ids come from useId so instances never collide. Three sizes 48/40/32, all clearing the 24px target floor. Leading/trailing slots; the trailing action carries its own accessible name. Needed NO new tokens — the contract covered every role, which is the first evidence it has stabilised. Six design bugs were pushed back into Paper rather than transcribed (see the design-fixes entry). Hover is DERIVED from Button's secondary variant, not drawn — recorded as a known gap in the doc.

migration.manual: New item. `npx shadcn add @bydiorama/input`; pulls in the `cn` lib item, expects react and griddy-icons as peers.

items.name: knowledge-graph-explorer
items.title: KnowledgeGraphExplorer
items.lead: Brings connected knowledge into a view you can search and explore.

docs.lead: Brings connected knowledge into a view you can search and explore.
docs.name: KnowledgeGraphExplorer
docs.summary: Explore a knowledge graph a neighbourhood at a time: search for an entity, filter by type, read and walk its relations in a detail panel, ask for more of the graph, and retrace the way you came. A block — Combobox, Checkbox, Network, Button — not a bigger component: it owns the composition and the history, and nothing else. A jump that lands more than one hop from where you were highlights the path between them.

anatomy.notes: bg-surface, border-subtle, radius-md, 24px inset, 16px between rows. className, ref and the rest land here.

24px apart: the search (Combobox md, 320 wide, a Search glyph, no trigger, label visually hidden), the type filter, then at the end "7 of 1,284 shown" (label-sm 400 muted) and the table toggle (Button secondary md, icon-only, ChartTable).

A fieldset of Checkboxes 20px apart, named by `filterLabel`. Each: a 10px round swatch in the type's data-cat-N-solid, the type's name, and its count in 400 muted. Unchecking hides the type's nodes and their edges; the selection survives.

A <nav> named "History, <label>" — the explorer's own label keeps two explorers' landmarks apart: the steps so far, ChevronRightSmall between them, 4px apart. Earlier steps are buttons (label-sm 400 muted, primary on hover) that go back and drop what came after; the current one is 600 primary, aria-current="location".
Network with its head kept for assistive tech only, `height` tall (456 by default, the sheet's), filling the row beside the panel. Network.Controls bottom right.

A role=group named by the entity (by detailsLabel while nothing is selected), not a landmark — two explorers would otherwise announce two regions with one name. 320 wide and as tall as the canvas, bg-surface, border-subtle, radius-md, 16px inset and gap. Scrolls when the relations outgrow it.
A 24px chip — the type's wash with a 1.5px ring in its solid and its glyph — the type's name in label-sm muted, and a ghost icon-only Close (sm).
The name in title-sm primary, the description under it in body-sm muted.

Under a border-subtle rule, 12px down: "Relations 4" and, when there are any, "Linked from 1". Rows 2px apart, 8px inset, radius-sm, bg-hover on hover: the verb in a 96px lane (400 muted), an 8px swatch, the name (label-md primary), "inferred" when it is, and ChevronRightSmall. A row selects that neighbour.
Button secondary sm, full width, Plus, at the foot: "Expand neighbours (12)". Disabled when there is nothing more to load.

docs.composition:
KnowledgeGraphExplorer        label · description · nodes · edges · types · onExpandRequest?
├─ Combobox                   search over the loaded entities, grouped by type
├─ Checkbox × types           the type filter, with counts
├─ nav (history)              the steps so far; earlier ones go back
├─ Network                    head hidden; selection, highlight and table view driven from here
│  └─ Network.Controls
└─ group (detail)             type chip, name, description, relations, Expand neighbours

label.notes: Names the drawing (Network's figure).

description.notes: The takeaway, read before the drawing.

nodes.notes: What is loaded so far — the neighbourhoods explored, not the store.

types.notes: Every type's name, pinned slot and glyph. The filter lists them in this order.

total.notes: How many entities the store holds, for "7 of 1,284 shown". Default: nodes.length.

hiddenNeighbours.notes: Relations per node that exist but are not loaded: the canvas chip, the panel's count, and the announcement.

onExpandRequest.notes: Load the node's neighbourhood and append it. The nodes already drawn stay where they are.

selected.notes: Controlled selection, with onSelect; defaultSelected for uncontrolled. The history starts from defaultSelected.

renderer.notes: Passed to Network: NetworkCanvas for a store that can load past 2,000 elements.

…labels.notes: searchLabel, searchPlaceholder, filterLabel, historyLabel, relationsLabel, linkedFromLabel, expandLabel, closeLabel, detailsLabel, tableLabel, inferredLabel, emptyDetailText, shownText: every user-visible string is a prop.

do: Load a neighbourhood at a time and report what is left in hiddenNeighbours; it is what makes the graph explorable rather than a hairball.
Pin each type's slot in `types`, so filtering never repaints the survivors.
Count a relation as hidden until it is loaded, even when both its ends already are.
dont: Do not hand it the whole store. A 5,000-node first paint is a picture, not an exploration.
Do not rebuild it for a different panel — compose Network yourself; this block is one arrangement of it.

a11y.role: A plain container. The search is a combobox, the filter a fieldset of checkboxes, the history a nav with aria-current, the drawing Network's figure, and the panel a group named by the entity it shows.
a11y.name: The drawing: `label` and `description`, kept for assistive tech while the head is hidden. The panel: the entity's name.

keyboard.does: Search, each type, the table toggle, the history's earlier steps, the drawing (Network's keyboard), then the panel: Close, each relation, Expand neighbours.
With nothing selected, back to the search field.

contrastPairs.role: names, current history step, relation names
counts, verbs, earlier history steps, "shown"
a type swatch
contrastPairs.why: The type is named beside every swatch, in the filter and in each relation row; the swatch only ties the row to the canvas.

forwarding.className: root

forwarding.rest: root — every HTML attribute except children and onSelect

docs.motion: Its own motion is the chrome control's: the relation rows' and the history steps' hover fill and ink ease at the shared control timing. Everything else that moves is a part's — Network's world transform as focus follows and the view fits, the Combobox panel, the Checkbox mark — and each part documents its own. Nothing in the block runs a keyframe; under prefers-reduced-motion the duration tokens collapse.
needsDesign: "Linked from": the sheet draws only outgoing relations; incoming ones are listed apart, read from the other end — the library's reading.
The empty panel (nothing selected) is not drawn.
The table toggle in the toolbar is not drawn; the sheet's toolbar ends at "7 of 1,284 shown".
knownGaps: Search covers what is loaded, not the store. A server search is the Combobox's async mode (filter={null}, onInputValueChange); the block does not wire it.
A controlled `selected` does not feed the history; the history records what this block selected.
The panel and the canvas sit side by side at every width: below ~900px the canvas gets narrow. A stacked arrangement is not built.
Path highlight shows only for the last jump, and only when it is longer than one hop.

items.name: media-toggle
items.title: MediaToggle
items.lead: Pauses and resumes media with a clear state and a named action.

docs.lead: Pauses and resumes media with a clear state and a named action.
docs.name: MediaToggle
docs.summary: The pause/play control WCAG 2.2.2 requires for video that starts on its own — an ambient hero, a background loop. A round chrome control on the media family, driving the media element it is given.

anatomy.notes: A <button>. The chrome-control recipe made round: --ui-bg-media fill, --ui-text-on-media glyph, no edge. Hover and press lift to --ui-bg-media-floor. data-state is playing | paused.
griddy PauseCircle while playing, PlayCircle while paused, 16px at both sizes — the glyph shows the ACTION. Not the bare Pause: it hard-codes fill="black" in griddy-icons 0.2 and cannot take the ink.

docs.composition:
<div class="relative">            the caller owns placement — bottom-end, inset space-lg
├─ <video ref={video} autoPlay muted loop playsInline />
└─ MediaToggle  target={video} pauseLabel playLabel size?

target.notes: The element to drive. The toggle calls play()/pause() and follows the element's own play/pause events, so it never disagrees with the video. Omit it to handle onPausedChange yourself.

defaultIsPaused.notes: Uncontrolled start. Omitted: playing, unless prefers-reduced-motion is set — then it pauses the target on mount and starts paused.

pauseLabel.notes: The accessible name while playing. Name the thing: "Pause background video", not "Pause".

size.notes: md 32, lg 44 (the touch target). Both move with density like every control size.

do: Give every autoplaying video longer than five seconds one of these (WCAG 2.2.2).
Pass target so the button follows the element; autoplay can be refused, and the button must not say "Pause" over a still frame.
Place it inside the media frame, bottom-end, inset space-lg.
dont: Do not use the inverse Button variant over video: inverse flips light in the dark scheme, media does not.
Do not add aria-pressed — the name already changes with the state, and "Pause, pressed" contradicts itself.

a11y.role: button
a11y.name: pauseLabel while playing, playLabel while paused — always the action pressing performs.

keyboard.does: Toggles playback.

contrastPairs.role: the glyph on its disc
the glyph on the hovered disc
the focus ring's outer stop

knownGaps: The disc's own boundary against an arbitrary video frame is not guaranteed — a frame the colour of --ui-bg-media hides the disc, though never the glyph. A ring was not drawn.
No Button for media grounds: inverse flips with the scheme and media does not, so an onMedia variant waits for a call site.
docs.motion: The disc's fill eases between --ui-bg-media and --ui-bg-media-floor over --ui-duration-fast (chromeControl's transition). The glyph swaps without animation. Reduced motion collapses the duration at the token layer — and, separately, starts the controlled VIDEO paused.

items.name: menu
items.title: Menu
items.lead: Offers a set of actions from a trigger.

docs.lead: Offers a set of actions from a trigger.
docs.name: Menu
docs.summary: A list of commands, opened from a trigger. The whole ARIA menu contract — role=menu and menuitem, roving focus, typeahead, Escape and outside-press dismissal, submenu timing and the aria-haspopup/aria-expanded wiring — comes from the Base UI behaviour layer (ADR 0012), wrapped so no third-party type reaches a public prop signature. Its panel and rows are the shared menu surface, which ContextMenu draws from the same recipe.

anatomy.notes: A render slot. Pass a Button; it keeps its own type, ref and accessible name and gains only the ARIA wiring.
role=menu. radius-md over a 4px inset around radius-sm rows — 4 + 4 = 8, concentric (§6). Capped to --available-height/width, so it shrinks rather than running off a short window.

role=menuitem. p-md, radius-sm, text-body-md in primary ink — Select's option role, matched BY ROLE so the size, weight and leading cannot drift apart: two panels on one page should be one panel. Carries data-highlighted from the behaviour layer, which is what the arrow keys move.
Truncates. The icon and trailing slots sit outside it, so a long label never pushes them out of the row.
role=separator. SPACE, not a rule — 8px above and below, and nothing painted. Announced either way, which is the half that matters.
role=group, named by its label so a screen reader announces the grouping the eye gets from the spacing.
A heading, never interactive. label-sm in muted ink.
A row that opens a nested panel beside itself, drawn from the same row recipe as menu-item. Chevron RIGHT — see needsDesign.

docs.composition:
Menu                       isOpen? / defaultIsOpen? / onOpenChange? / isModal?
├─ Menu.Trigger render={<Button/>}
└─ Menu.Panel              side? / align? / sideOffset? / container?
   ├─ Menu.Item            icon? / trailing? / isDisabled? / onSelect? / render?
   ├─ Menu.Separator
   ├─ Menu.Group label="…"
   │  └─ Menu.Item
   └─ Menu.Sub
      ├─ Menu.SubTrigger
      └─ Menu.Panel

isOpen.notes: Controlled open state. Omit and the menu owns it — the behaviour layer already implements the controlled/uncontrolled contract, so running useControllableState over it as well would be two implementations of one thing.

onOpenChange.notes: Fires for the trigger, Escape, an outside press and a chosen item.

isModal.notes: Traps focus and blocks the page behind. A menu is not modal by default; a menu that must be answered is a Modal (§7a).

Panel.side.notes: Preferred side. Base UI flips it when it would collide.

Panel.container.notes: Where to portal. Theme tokens are INHERITED custom properties, so a panel on document.body leaves a brand scope behind and paints theme zero.

Item.onSelect.notes: Named for the verb (§1). NOT onClick: a menu row is chosen by keyboard as often as by pointer, and a handler named for one input is how the other gets forgotten.

Item.icon.notes: Leading glyph. The component sizes it to 16 (§7) — an unsized slot ships griddy's 24.

Item.trailing.notes: A shortcut hint, a check, a count.

Item.render.notes: Renders the row as something else — an <a> for a link. Note that the row's own data-slot loses to the rendered element's, which is true of every render slot here.

Item.isDisabled.notes: Sets aria-disabled and refuses activation by pointer and by Enter, but stays REACHABLE by the arrow keys so it can be announced. This doc originally claimed the arrows skipped it; the browser test disagreed, and the behaviour layer was right.

Item.className.notes: Merged through cn() TOGETHER with the row's own classes, so a conflicting utility REPLACES the base one rather than racing it in the stylesheet — `className="text-caption"` removes `text-body-md` from the row's class list. Same on SubTrigger, Panel and Separator.

Group.label.notes: Names the group AND draws its heading. Without it the grouping is visual only.

do: Use Menu for actions. A list of links is navigation, and role=menu full of links announces them as commands — the Sidebar is the shape for that.
Give a destructive item its own trailing confirmation, or open a Modal from it; a menu row cannot be undone.
Pass `container` when the trigger sits inside a brand-themed scope.
Keep labels short enough not to truncate — the label is the only thing announced.
dont: Do not put a form inside a menu. Typeahead swallows the keystrokes; that is a Popover.
Do not nest more than one level of Menu.Sub. Base UI supports it and a pointer user cannot reliably hold the path.
Do not use onClick on Menu.Item — there is no such prop, deliberately.

a11y.role: menu, with menuitem rows, group and separator. All from Base UI, including the trigger's aria-haspopup and aria-expanded.
a11y.name: The trigger names the menu. Each row is named by its own label text; an icon-only row would announce nothing, so the label is required.

keyboard.does: Opens the menu and focuses its first item.

Moves the highlight through EVERY row, disabled ones included, wrapping at the ends. Reaching a disabled row is deliberate — it is announced as disabled rather than hidden, for the same reason Calendar keeps unavailable dates focusable: a row a screen-reader user cannot reach is one they cannot be told the reason for.
Opens the nested panel; Arrow Left closes it and returns.
Jumps to the row whose label starts with what was typed.
Chooses it and closes the menu.
Closes and returns focus to the trigger.

a11y.focus: The panel takes focus on open and returns it to the trigger on close, both from the behaviour layer. Highlight is `data-highlighted`, which moves with the arrows and with the pointer alike — and it carries a forced-colors outline, because forced colours flattens the author background that otherwise carries it.

contrastPairs.role: a resting menu row
the highlighted row
a group heading
the panel edge
contrastPairs.why: ADR 0010: the panel is identified by its fill and shadow against the page, not by its hairline. The separator paints nothing at all — it is space plus a role.

needsDesign: The sheet draws a chevron-DOWN on 'Admin Settings' and 'Team Settings', and the second variant shows a second level expanded INLINE beneath its parent, in the same panel, in muted nav ink. That is a disclosure, not a submenu. Shipped as a Base UI submenu with a chevron-RIGHT, because an inline disclosure inside role=menu breaks the roving-focus model that makes a menu a menu — and because the Sidebar already ships exactly the inline pattern, with the same layer names the sheet uses here ('Primary Level 1 Item', 'Second Level 2 Item'). If the drawing is the intent, this surface is a Sidebar inside a Popover and not a Menu at all. This is the one question worth answering first. Confirmed by the designer (Paper comment, 2026-11-02 review): the inline second-level rows carry EXTRA inline padding — 16px (space-lg) against the first level's 12px (space-md), with the label at 16/500 in --ui-nav-ink-muted — deliberately; whichever component ends up owning the inline disclosure takes that 4px step. The Sidebar sheet itself still draws both levels at one inset, so the step belongs to the in-panel variant only.

The sheet paints the panel --ui-bg-surface and its rows --ui-nav-ink, which mixes two role families: the nav inks are derived against --ui-nav-bg, the rail they belong to. Declaring --ui-nav-ink-muted on --ui-bg-surface made the resolver's own audit fail at 1.03:1 in dark for the saturated-accent seed, because no single ink can serve two surfaces a brand has pulled that far apart. Shipped with --ui-text-primary on --ui-bg-surface and --ui-bg-hover for the highlight, which is what Select's list already uses. The artboard's layer names say where the mix came from — the rows are Sidebar frames, copied.

The sheet draws rows at 16px/600. Shipped at text-body-md, Select's option role, after a design review of a members table — a role Select and a row Menu on every line — found the menu a size above the dropdowns beside it, in what is the same kind of popup (#22). The sheet wants redrawing at body-md so the two drawings agree.

The panel's inset is drawn at 8px, which does not close §6's arithmetic — 4 + 8 wants a 12px outer radius and the scale has no 12px step. Shipped at 4px, exactly as Select's panel resolved the identical problem.
No disabled row is drawn; its ink is derived from --ui-nav-ink-disabled.
No icons are drawn on any row, though the slot exists.
The trigger is drawn as a medium Button with a chevron; nothing says whether the chevron should flip when the menu opens, as the Date Picker's does.
knownGaps: No checkbox or radio items, though Base UI provides both. The sheet draws neither.
No keyboard-shortcut column. `trailing` will hold one, but there is no styled part for it.
The panel has one width, driven by min-w-56 and its content. The sheet draws a panel that fills its column.
docs.motion: All of it comes from `@/lib/menu-surface`, so it is identical to ContextMenu by construction: the panel fades on `opacity` through `data-[starting-style]`/`data-[ending-style]`, and rows transition `background-color` and `color`, everything at --ui-duration-fast with --ui-ease-out. The fade only actually runs on a CONTROLLED menu — routing open state through React is what makes the panel mount carrying `data-starting-style`, where the uncontrolled path measured a constant box from frame 0.

contrast.role: a resting menu row
the highlighted row
a group heading
the panel edge

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

Menu and ContextMenu rows are set in text-body-md, Select's option role, instead of text-body-lg. Closes #22. A design review of a members table, with a role Select and a row Menu on every line, found the menu a size above the dropdown beside it: 16px/500 against 14px/400, in what is the same kind of popup, list and gesture. Matched by ROLE rather than by copying numbers, because since ADR 0020 a role carries its own weight and leading, so naming Select's role is what keeps the two from drifting. Menu.Item, Menu.SubTrigger and every ContextMenu row change together, since they are one recipe. Separately, the consumer className is now merged INSIDE the recipe, through the same cn() as the base classes. The call sites used to run `menuItem(cn(className))`, which merged the caller's classes only with each other and then appended them, so `className="text-body-md"` worked only because Tailwind happened to emit it after `.text-body-lg`. The stylesheet order decided, which is the failure cn() exists to prevent. All four recipes (panel, row, separator, group label) now merge, so a conflicting utility replaces the base one in the rendered class list. The browser test compares a Menu row and sub trigger to a real Select option on size, weight, leading, tracking and family, and asserts the class list holds exactly one type role after `className="text-caption"`. Both fail against the old recipe.

migration.manual: Remove any local override that shrank menu rows (for example an unlayered rule on [data-slot="menu-item"] / [data-slot="menu-sub-trigger"]); the rows now render at body-md on their own. A caller who wants the old 16px row passes className="text-body-lg", which now actually replaces the base role. Local copies of lib/menu-surface.ts need lib/cn.ts beside them; the manifest now declares that dependency.

changes.summary: check:motion joins the gate list, and every animating component now documents its motion. The gate rejects a literal duration or easing in registry/ (a discipline that was already perfect — zero hard-coded durations across 26 files — and had nothing keeping it that way), transition-all (CONVENTIONS section 6 has said this since the beginning and nothing enforced it), a keyframe with no reduced-motion guard, and an animating component with no top-level motion: note in its doc. It reads lib recipes alongside components as check:overlays does, so Header's motion is found in @/lib/chrome-control where it actually lives rather than reported as absent. 27 doc files gain a motion: note describing what moves, what drives it and what reduced motion does to it; Sheet's and ImageUpload's existing notes are PROMOTED out of a11y to the top level, where Button already had its, because motion is a description of what a component does rather than solely an accessibility concern and a field meaning one thing at two depths stops being findable. ImageUpload's note is corrected while being promoted: it credited the token layer with stopping its spinner, and what actually stops it is the motion-safe: variant. Two findings are recorded in the notes rather than fixed: Sidebar's collapsible section snaps via the hidden attribute where Accordion animates the identical interaction against Base UI's published height, and Banner reaches for transition-colors where the rest of the library enumerates properties. No component's rendered motion changes; no .tsx is touched.

migration.manual: Documentation only — every change is inside a *.doc.ts, and no component's classes or rendered motion moved. If you consume the doc files and read `a11y.motion`, it has moved to the top-level `motion` key on Sheet and ImageUpload; Button was already there and the other 27 are new.

changes.summary: Three reported issues on the menu surface. The panel WIGGLED as it opened: Base UI's `--transform-origin` points at the anchor, which for a menu sits inside the panel rather than at a corner — measured at `44.6px -8px` on a 224px panel — so `scale-98` grew the box about a point 45px in from its left edge and slid that edge while it grew, and the origin itself shifted between the first two frames. It only appeared on a CONTROLLED menu, because open state routed through React makes the panel mount with `data-starting-style` and actually run the transition, where the uncontrolled path measured a constant box from frame 0. The scale is gone; the entrance is opacity only, and the test now asserts the rect does not move across the whole entrance rather than that a class is absent. The SEPARATOR is space with no rule, as the sheet draws it and as design confirmed — it keeps `role="separator"`, so the grouping is announced whether or not anything is painted. And the STORIES no longer open themselves: a docs page renders every story at once, so a `defaultIsOpen` anywhere meant menus flew open on load. One Menu story opens itself and its name says so; every ContextMenu story is closed, because a context menu is anchored to the POINTER and opening one without a pointer lands it over its own trigger region.

Menu and ContextMenu, both on Base UI (ADR 0012), sharing ONE surface. They are not cousins that look alike: Base UI's ContextMenu re-exports Menu's Item, Group, Separator and Submenu verbatim, so ContextMenu ships only Root, Trigger and Panel and its rows ARE Menu's. The panel and row recipes live in `lib/menu-surface`, and the browser test renders a Menu row beside a ContextMenu row and compares their computed styles — a lib recipe has no doc for check:contrast to see, so the relationship is what gets asserted. Item.onSelect is named for the verb rather than the pointer, and the type test proves onClick does not compile. Two claims in the first draft of the docs were wrong and the browser found both: that the arrows SKIP disabled rows (they reach them, which is right — a row a screen-reader user cannot reach is one they cannot be told the reason for), and that Shift+F10 is something this library implements (it is not; Base UI's trigger has no keydown handler at all, the BROWSER turns the chord into a native contextmenu event, and that only works if the caller made the region focusable).

items.name: meter
items.title: Meter
items.lead: Places a measurement within a known range.

docs.lead: Places a measurement within a known range.
docs.name: Meter
docs.summary: One value against a range — a gauge, not a task. A labelled 8px bar (or an 80px ring) with role=meter, an optional target rule, and warning/danger states that must carry their own words. Use Progress for something that finishes; use Meter for something that is measured.

anatomy.notes: className lands here (§5). Carries data-shape and data-status; aria-busy while loading.
label-sm, muted. Names the meter via aria-labelledby. sr-only with isLabelHidden, and always on the radial shape.
label-sm 600, primary, tabular-nums. The printed reading, status words included. aria-hidden: aria-valuetext announces the same string.
role=meter with aria-valuenow/-min/-max/-valuetext. 8px tall, or 16px when a target rule crosses it.
bg-sunken pill (space-sm high). On the radial shape, an r=34 ring stroked at the same thickness.
accent-legible, or the warning / danger ink. Pill ends; absent at zero. On radial, an arc from 12 o'clock, clockwise.
A solid 2px rule (stroke-thick) in border-strong, the full 16px height.
label-sm muted, under the rule: starts at it in the first half of the range, ends at it in the second.
Radial only: the status words under the ring, where the linear meter prints them after the value.
value=null: the emptyText in place of the reading, above an empty track.

docs.composition:
Meter
├─ label            string (required)
├─ value            number | null (required) — null requires emptyText
├─ min? / max?      default 0 / 100
├─ valueText?       default: rounded percentage of the range
├─ status?          warning | danger — requires statusText
├─ shape?           linear | radial
├─ target?          number — linear only, requires targetText
└─ isLoading? / isLabelHidden?

label.notes: Required — a meter with no name announces only a number.

value.notes: Clamped into min…max, and the clamped value is what aria-valuenow reports. null means no reading yet and requires emptyText, because an empty bar with no words reads as zero.

valueText.notes: What the reading reads as, printed AND announced. Pass it for units ('412 of 600 sheets'); the default percentage uses no locale, so a server and a client cannot disagree about it.

status.notes: Recolours the fill with the intent ink and REQUIRES statusText ('near limit'), appended to the value. The type enforces it: a state carried by colour alone fails SC 1.4.1.

shape.notes: radial is the sheet's 80px ring beside a stat. It takes no target — none is drawn on it — and the type refuses one rather than ignoring it.

target.notes: A goal on the same scale, drawn as a solid rule (never a dashed one, ADR 0023 §6). Requires targetText.

isLoading.notes: Empty track, no reading, aria-busy. The height is reserved, so a row of meters never jumps.

do: Use Meter for a level that can rise and fall: stock, quota, capacity, a score.
Write statusText as the consequence, not the colour: 'near limit', 'over budget'.
Pass valueText when the unit is not a percentage.
dont: Do not use Meter for something that completes — that is Progress.
Do not encode warning or danger by colour alone; the type will not let you omit statusText.
Do not put two meters' values on one scale with different maxima side by side without saying so in valueText.

a11y.role: meter (ARIA 1.2) on the bar or ring, with aria-valuenow, -valuemin, -valuemax and aria-valuetext. With no reading the track is aria-hidden and the emptyText carries the state — aria-valuenow is never invented.
a11y.name: `label` via aria-labelledby; sr-only when hidden, never removed.

keyboard.does: Not focusable. A meter is output, not a control.

contrastPairs.role: the fill against its track
the warning fill against its track
the danger fill against its track
the target rule on a card
the value
the label, target label and empty text

forwarding.className: root
forwarding.ref: root (an HTMLDivElement) — a meter is not a form control, so there is no inner element to prefer
forwarding.rest: root — every HTML attribute except role, children and value, which the component owns

needsDesign: The radial shape's status words: the sheet draws the ring only in its resting state, so 'near limit' is placed under the ring here without a drawing.
The radial shape's visible label: the sheet pairs the ring with a stat and draws no label, so the label is screen-reader only.
knownGaps: No tabular figures: Aspekta ships no `tnum` feature and its digits are proportional (367–602 units), so `tabular-nums` is a no-op in this face — figures right-align on their last digit but do not line up digit by digit, and a figure that changes in place changes width. Filed against the face (ADR 0011 item 5); pinned by registry/fonts/aspekta/aspekta.test.ts.

The target rule is border-strong, where the sheet draws text-primary: an ink role used as a fill is the wrong-category signal (add-component §2), and border-strong is the line role already audited at 3:1 on the page and the card.
Meter vs Progress Indicator Circular (TODO.md) is not settled; the sheet's Gaps row records it as a Conflict.
On the stress brand the track is 1.12:1 on white, so the end of the range is near invisible; the printed reading has to stay (sheet, Measured).
No intent thresholds (low/high/optimum as on native <meter>): the consumer decides the status, so the words are always theirs.
docs.motion: None. A new value redraws; a gauge that animates on every update draws the eye to a change that may not matter.

the warning fill against its track
the danger fill against its track
the target rule on a card
the value

ADR 0011 item 5 checked: Aspekta ships no `tnum` feature and its default digits are proportional (367–602 units), so `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` is a no-op wherever the library uses it. No code or visual change.
