items.name: modal
items.title: Modal
items.lead: Pauses the current task for a decision.

docs.lead: Pauses the current task for a decision.
docs.name: Modal
docs.summary: A dialog that takes over the page: scrim behind, focus trapped inside, focus restored to the trigger on close. Second component on the Base UI behaviour layer, deliberately the same shape as Popover. Its surface is deliberately Card's — same 24px corner, border-subtle hairline, shadow-md and title-sm header — so a dialog raised over cards reads as the same object as them (#23, the owner's redraw of the portal's 'Remove member' confirm). Only the ground (bg-surface: the scrim already separates it from the page) and the gap (gap-2xl) differ.

anatomy.notes: The control that opens it. Pass your own element via `render` — never wrapped.
The backdrop. Uses --ui-scrim, a scheme-only role: a warm 16% veil in light, a heavier black in dark.

The dialog. Card's surface class for class — radius-lg (issue #40), a 1px border-subtle hairline and shadow-md — on bg-surface, with p-lg and gap-2xl. Centred, width-capped by size, and scrolls internally.
Card.Header's title: title-sm at the role's own 600, inset by Card's unboxed px-sm. Becomes the dialog's accessible name automatically.
body-md in secondary ink, inset px-sm with the title so the two share a left edge (CONVENTIONS §6). Wired to aria-describedby automatically.
The action row, `justify-between` per the sheet.
Any control that dismisses. Takes an element via `render`.

docs.composition:
Modal                     isOpen? / defaultIsOpen? / onOpenChange? / isDismissable?
├─ Modal.Trigger          render={<Button>…</Button>}
└─ Modal.Surface          size? / initialFocus? / finalFocus?
   ├─ Modal.Title
   ├─ Modal.Description?
   ├─ <your content>      Inputs, a form, anything
   └─ Modal.Footer
      ├─ Modal.Close      render={<Button variant="secondary">Cancel</Button>}
      └─ <primary action>

Surface.initialFocus.notes: Where focus lands when the dialog opens. The default is the first tabbable element inside it; a confirmation whose first control is destructive should pass Cancel's ref instead. A function is called at open time; returning null, or a ref that is still empty, keeps the default rather than dropping focus. Restated as ModalFocusTarget, the same shape as Sheet's SheetFocusTarget, and deliberately not Base UI's, whose `false` would leave focus behind the scrim.

Surface.finalFocus.notes: Where focus goes when the dialog closes. The default is the trigger, or whatever was focused before it opened. Set it when that element will be gone, for example the row a delete confirmation removes, so focus lands somewhere real rather than on <body>. Same fallback rule as initialFocus.

isOpen.notes: Controlled. Omit and the modal owns it.

onOpenChange.notes: One callback for both directions (§1). Narrowed from Base UI's signature so no third-party type reaches ours.

isDismissable.notes: Escape and scrim-click dismiss. On by default — trapping someone in a dialog is a last resort. Turn it off only when losing their work would be worse than the friction.

size.notes: A width cap, not a height: the dialog grows with its content and scrolls internally past the viewport. 416px (the drawn width) and 640px. These were max-w-md/max-w-xl, which resolve against this system's SPACING scale rather than Tailwind's container scale — 12px and 24px caps that min-w-80 overrode, so both sizes rendered identically until it was measured.

container.notes: Where the dialog is portalled. Theme tokens are INHERITED custom properties, so a surface in the body leaves any brand scope on a wrapper and paints theme zero. Pass the themed element to bring it back; see sheet.doc.ts for why it is a prop rather than automatic.

render.notes: On Trigger and Close. Passed through, not wrapped (§3), so the element keeps its tag, ref and accessible name and gains only the ARIA wiring.

do: Give every modal a Modal.Title — it is the accessible name, with no aria-label to keep in sync.
Put the dismissing action in Modal.Close and the committing one beside it; the footer separates them deliberately.
Use isDismissable={false} only for genuinely destructive or unsaved-work cases, and always leave an explicit Cancel.
Let long content scroll inside the surface — it is capped to the viewport already.
dont: Do not use a Modal for a message that does not need acknowledgement; that is a Banner, or a Popover.
Do not nest modals. If a modal needs a second decision, it needs a second step.
Do not import Base UI types into your own props — `check:boundaries` fails the build (ADR 0002).
Do not pass isModal; a Modal is always modal, and a non-modal dialog with a scrim is a Popover wearing a costume.

Do not restyle the surface or title away from Card's at the call site. The browser test compares Modal's computed radius, border, shadow and title to a rendered Card's, so the two move together; a local override (the portal shipped one on modal-surface and modal-title before #23) is a fork of both. ADR 0016's table listed Modal under shadow-sm; it now takes md with Card, recorded as an amendment there.

a11y.role: dialog, modal (from Base UI). The page behind is inert while open.
a11y.name: Modal.Title via aria-labelledby, automatically. Modal.Description wires aria-describedby the same way.

keyboard.does: Opens from the trigger — native, since the trigger is a real button.
Closes when isDismissable, and RESTORES FOCUS to the trigger. Asserted in Chromium.
Cycles within the dialog only; focus cannot reach the page behind.

a11y.focus: Focus moves into the surface on open and returns to the trigger on close. Both asserted in a real browser — focus falling to <body> is the classic hand-rolled-dialog failure. `initialFocus` and `finalFocus` on the Surface move either end deliberately; both are asserted too, against the default they replace.

contrastPairs.role: the title on the surface
the description
the surface hairline
contrastPairs.why: the dialog's boundary is the scrim plus shadow-md; the hairline says where the surface ends, as on Card (ADR 0010 point 2, ADR 0016 point 6)

knownGaps: No close (×) button in the corner — the sheet draws none, and dismissal is the footer's Cancel plus Escape/scrim. Add one when design draws it.
The sheet draws its body as two inline fields; those are Input components at the call site, not part of Modal.
Sizes: the sheet draws one width. md is that width; lg is DERIVED for content-heavy dialogs — confirm with design.
No dark-scheme drawing of the surface or scrim; the resolver derives both.

ALIGNMENT GAP, shared with Card: Title and Description take the unboxed px-sm, but an Input's own label does not, so a field placed directly in the dialog has its label 8px left of the title. Card records the same gap; whichever fix lands there (an inset-aware Input or a field wrapper) applies here too.

The redraw annotates the title inset as py-xs px-sm. Card.Header carries px-sm only, and this matches Card literally, so the title has no vertical inset of its own. If the drawing's py-xs is wanted, it belongs on Card.Header too, or the two headers stop matching.
docs.motion: The scrim fades and the panel fades and scales from 98%, both at --ui-duration-fast with --ui-ease-out, driven by `data-[starting-style]` and `data-[ending-style]`. `scale` is named explicitly in the transition list: Tailwind v4 writes `scale-*` as the standalone `scale` property, so the original list naming `transform` animated nothing and the modal snapped open at full size. Measured with getAnimations() in Chromium, which is how that became a fact rather than a theory.

contrast.role: the title on the surface
the description
the surface hairline

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

Card, Popover's panel and Modal's surface draw at --ui-radius-lg (16px), not radius-xl (24) — the 2026-10-27/29 owner decision, platform-wide (#40). Modal's radius half of #23 is reversed; its hairline, shadow and title are unchanged. A radius-md boxed child at p-lg is no longer concentric; accepted in review.

migration.manual: Remove any consumer patch that forced [data-slot=card|popover-panel|modal-surface] to --ui-radius-lg (e.g. service-portal's `Registry patch (TEMPORARY)` block).

changes.summary: Modal wears Card's surface, adopting the owner's redraw of the confirm dialog (portal Brand Profile › Members, 'Remove member'). Closes #23. Surface: rounded-lg (16px) becomes rounded-xl (24px), it gains Card's 1px border-subtle hairline (`border border-edge-subtle`, ADR 0010), and shadow-sm becomes Card's shadow-md (ADR 0016, amended). Title: text-title-lg becomes text-title-sm — the role's own weight is the 600 the drawing asks for, so no type-role exception is declared — inset by Card's unboxed px-sm. The description takes the same px-sm so title and description keep one left edge (CONVENTIONS §6 for bare text inside a large radius); the drawing did not say, and that alignment is this change's call. Gap (gap-2xl), padding (p-lg) and the bg-surface ground are unchanged. Why: a dialog raised over cards now reads as the same object as them, and title-lg was the loudest thing on screen for a one-line question in a 416px dialog. The browser test asserts the RELATIONSHIP to a rendered Card — radius, all four border sides, the whole box-shadow list, and the title's size, weight, leading, tracking and text inset — so the two cannot drift; it failed on all three points against the old classes. Not adopted: the drawing's py-xs on the title, because Card.Header has none and matching Card literally was the brief. --ui-text-title-lg lost its last component consumer and is now listed in check:token-consumers as a page-heading role. Visual baselines that change: modal (light and dark, darwin and linux), not regenerated here.

migration.manual: If you applied the portal's temporary rule on [data-slot="modal-surface"] and [data-slot="modal-title"]:not(.sr-only), delete it: the component ships those values now, and the override would fight the description's new px-sm inset. A Modal.Title you styled larger on purpose keeps working through className, but it now diverges from Card's header type by design.

changes.summary: Modal.Surface and Drawer.Panel declare `initialFocus` and `finalFocus`, the same props #28 gave Sheet.Panel, with the same semantics. Both forwarded `rest` to Base UI's Dialog.Popup untyped, so the props already reached the behaviour layer by accident. They were undeclared, and a rename upstream would have broken them silently. Each takes a ref or a function returning the element. A function returning null, or a ref still empty, keeps the default instead of dropping focus. Base UI's boolean and interaction-type forms are not offered, because `false` would leave focus behind the scrim. The types are restated locally as `ModalFocusTarget` and `DrawerFocusTarget` rather than shared from a lib item, because the components ship as independent source and every other behaviour-layer shape in these files (DismissDetails, the forBaseUI shim) is restated per file. check:boundaries stays green. For a Drawer the default matters more than it looks: the first tabbable element is the drag handle, which is also a close button. The browser tests put two buttons ahead of the target and assert focus lands on it and returns to a named element on Escape, in both forms, against a control case proving the defaults. Removing the mapping fails all eight.

migration.manual: A caller passing `initialFocus`/`finalFocus` through the untyped spread keeps working with a ref or a function returning an element. A boolean, or a function taking Base UI's interaction type, no longer type-checks; pass a ref or `() => element` instead.

changes.summary: check:motion joins the gate list, and every animating component now documents its motion. The gate rejects a literal duration or easing in registry/ (a discipline that was already perfect — zero hard-coded durations across 26 files — and had nothing keeping it that way), transition-all (CONVENTIONS section 6 has said this since the beginning and nothing enforced it), a keyframe with no reduced-motion guard, and an animating component with no top-level motion: note in its doc. It reads lib recipes alongside components as check:overlays does, so Header's motion is found in @/lib/chrome-control where it actually lives rather than reported as absent. 27 doc files gain a motion: note describing what moves, what drives it and what reduced motion does to it; Sheet's and ImageUpload's existing notes are PROMOTED out of a11y to the top level, where Button already had its, because motion is a description of what a component does rather than solely an accessibility concern and a field meaning one thing at two depths stops being findable. ImageUpload's note is corrected while being promoted: it credited the token layer with stopping its spinner, and what actually stops it is the motion-safe: variant. Two findings are recorded in the notes rather than fixed: Sidebar's collapsible section snaps via the hidden attribute where Accordion animates the identical interaction against Base UI's published height, and Banner reaches for transition-colors where the rest of the library enumerates properties. No component's rendered motion changes; no .tsx is touched.

migration.manual: Documentation only — every change is inside a *.doc.ts, and no component's classes or rendered motion moved. If you consume the doc files and read `a11y.motion`, it has moved to the top-level `motion` key on Sheet and ImageUpload; Button was already there and the other 27 are new.

changes.summary: Modal — the second component on the Base UI behaviour layer, and the evidence that ADR 0012's wrapper pattern generalises rather than being something that worked once. Deliberately the same shape as Popover: Root/Trigger/Surface/Title/Description/Footer/Close, our own props outside, no Base UI type in any exported signature, the same one-line exactOptionalPropertyTypes shim contained to the one file check:boundaries isolates. It is ALWAYS modal and takes no isModal prop, because a non-modal dialog with a scrim is a Popover wearing a costume. The footer is justify-between per the sheet, separating the dismissing action from the committing one. A real defect found by the browser suite: `dismissible` is NOT a prop on Base UI's DialogRoot, so passing it was silently ignored and Escape closed a modal that had explicitly opted out — isDismissable is now implemented by cancelling the escape-key and outside-press reasons in onOpenChange, with a second test proving an explicit Modal.Close still works, since cancelling close-press too would have made the dialog unclosable. Tooling: --ui-scrim is a scheme-only role that was emitted as CSS with no Tailwind utility, so any component wanting it had to use the arbitrary bg-(--ui-scrim) form, which check:utilities skips by design. The emitter now mints --color-scrim, so `bg-scrim` exists and is verified.

migration.manual: New peer dependency on @base-ui-components/react, the same range Popover declares. `bg-scrim` is a new utility; nothing previously used the scrim, so nothing changes visually.

items.name: multiselect
items.title: Multiselect
items.lead: Chooses several values from a searchable list.

docs.lead: Chooses several values from a searchable list.
docs.name: Multiselect
docs.summary: A filterable list of options where more than one can be chosen, with the selection shown as removable chips. The hardest ARIA pattern in the library — none of it is written here; it comes from the Base UI behaviour layer (ADR 0012).

anatomy.notes: The field wrapper. className lands here (§5).
Names the trigger via aria-labelledby. Takes the unboxed inset.

48px, radius-md — the SAME control surface as Input size lg, asserted as a relationship rather than as numbers. Its value takes Input's type step at every size (14 / 14 / 12px) from the size map alone; a hard-coded text-body-md after the map used to win the merge (#16).
The selection, as Badge components with real remove buttons. Hidden when empty.
The portalled list surface. radius-lg, bg-surface, hairline and shadow-md.
Filters the list. Carries its own accessible name ("Search <label>").
A row. IS the control — it carries role=option, which is why it holds a checkbox VISUAL rather than a Checkbox component.

docs.composition:
Multiselect
├─ label            string (required) — the accessible name
├─ items            { value, label, isDisabled? }[]
├─ value? / defaultValue?   string[] — by item value
├─ onValueChange?   (value: string[]) => void
└─ placeholder? / searchPlaceholder? / emptyMessage?

label.notes: Required — a control has a name (§10). Use isLabelHidden when the design shows none; a placeholder is not a label.

items.notes: The full option set. Filtering happens inside; do not filter this yourself.

value.notes: Controlled selection, by item value — not by object identity, so a re-fetched list does not lose the selection.

onValueChange.notes: Fires with the new selection as values. Narrowed from Base UI's item objects so no third-party shape reaches the signature.

emptyMessage.notes: Shown when the search matches nothing — never leave a filtered list silently blank.

do: Give it a real label; it becomes the trigger's accessible name.
Key the selection by value, so a re-fetched item list keeps it.
Let the search do the filtering — pass the whole item set.
Write item labels that read on their own; the chip's remove button is named from them.
dont: Do not filter `items` yourself in response to the search; the component and its ARIA already do.
Do not nest a Checkbox component in a row — the row IS the option, and a real input inside role=option is a second control inside the first.
Do not use this for a single choice; that is a Select.
Do not import Base UI types into your own props — check:boundaries fails the build (ADR 0002).

a11y.role: combobox trigger + listbox with aria-multiselectable, from Base UI. Options carry aria-selected.
a11y.name: The `label` prop via aria-labelledby. The search input has its own name; each chip's remove button is named "Remove <label>".

keyboard.does: Opens the list from the trigger.
Filters. Active-descendant management stays with the behaviour layer.
Move through options without moving DOM focus off the input.
Toggles the active option and KEEPS the list open — choosing three things should not cost three round trips.
Closes and restores focus to the trigger. Asserted in Chromium.

contrastPairs.role: the trigger value
the tick on a selected row
option ink on the panel

knownGaps: Nine design defects were corrected rather than transcribed — see the ledger entry. Most consequential: an 11px chip label (below the 12px floor), a 1.51:1 tick, and four palette steps where intent/accent roles exist.

Chips are Badge components rather than Base UI's Chip parts, so the arrow-key navigation BETWEEN chips that Base UI offers is not adopted. Removal is still fully keyboard operable via each chip's button.
The option row reuses Checkbox's visual language but not the component; the two could drift. A shared visual primitive would fix it and does not exist yet.
No grouping, no async loading, no create-on-the-fly. None are drawn.

The panel is radius-md over a 4px inset around radius-sm children — the search field and every row — so §6 closes at 4 + 4 = 8. The sheet draws an 8px inset (J3M-0), which does not close on any radius the scale has; see the same note in select.doc.ts.
docs.motion: The trigger transitions `border-color` and `box-shadow` at --ui-duration-fast with --ui-ease-out; the list fades on `opacity` through `data-[starting-style]`/`data-[ending-style]` over the same timing. Chips have no enter or exit animation — a selection appears and disappears immediately, which keeps a fast multi-select from queueing motion behind itself.

contrast.role: the trigger value
the tick on a selected row
option ink on the panel

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

useControllableState no longer reads or writes refs during render, so it passes eslint-plugin-react-hooks@7 `recommended` (react-hooks/refs) in consumer apps (#35). onChange is synced in an insertion effect; the controlled/uncontrolled switch warning moved to an effect; the setter depends on isControlled instead of a ref, so it is stable for every caller that does not switch modes (which already warns). The library now lints its own registry/ with the same preset, which also moved Calendar's focused-date correction from an effect to render-time derivation, useIsStuck's reset to its cleanup, and three ref-through-helper call sites (DatePicker, MultiSelect, CardSorting) to direct attributes.

Closes #16. A field's value at md is now body-md (14px) in Input, Textarea, Select and Multiselect, where it was caption (12px); lg stays body-md and sm stays caption. Two defects, one decision. First, Select's trigger, and Multiselect's, ignored their size map for text: `SIZE[size]` carried the caption step, then a hard-coded `text-body-md` on the next line won the merge, so every Select rendered 14px at every size while the Input beside it rendered 12 at md and sm. The boxes matched (40px at md), so the geometry relationship test passed for the bug's whole life; only the text inside differed. The hard-coded class is gone and the map is the only thing on either trigger that names a type role. Second, the direction: the maintainer decided md settles at 14px, not 12, because the owner's Paper frames draw every 40px field value at body-md, and service-portal had to patch `[data-slot="control"][data-size="md"]` to get there. sm stays caption because the field tokens carry no type step at all (ADR 0020 §4 keeps type out of density), so the map is the only authority, and a 14px value's 21.7px line in a compact 28px field leaves 3px of block padding. Textarea's md box is now lg's box (127px at 6 rows) with the narrower inline inset. DatePicker draws lg only and does not change. Select's and Multiselect's browser tests now compare the VALUE's font-size and line-height to a real Input's at every size; both fail against the old trigger (probed). Deliberate visual change: the `select` matrix baseline moves (its md and sm rows) and the `textarea` baseline moves (its md row), light and dark, darwin and linux. The input, multiselect and date-picker cases draw lg only and do not move for this. Weight is NOT yet one relationship: Input's value is font-medium (500) at every size, while Select, Multiselect, DatePicker and Textarea take their role's weight (body-md 400, caption 600), so a Select at sm now renders 600 where it rendered 400. Recorded for a maintainer decision rather than changed here.

migration.manual: Remove any local override that forced field text to one size (for example a rule on [data-slot="control"][data-size="md"] setting body-md); md renders body-md on its own now. A form that relied on Select rendering 14px at sm will see 12px there, matching Input; pass size="md" if you meant the larger value.

changes.summary: --ui-bg-elevated is corrected in two ways, and both were only visible by measuring a running browser. (1) IN DARK IT OVERSHOT THE INTERACTION RAMP. Elevation raised 0.06 while --ui-bg-hover raises 0.05, so the raised SURFACE landed between hover and active: measured against --ui-bg-surface in theme zero's dark scheme, elevated 1.247 and hover 1.210. Every neutral ramp in the library is drawn as elevated → hover → active, so all of them inverted at their first rung, 1.031 apart — invisible AND backwards. Header.Item's four-step item ramp (the page you were on read quieter than the one under the pointer), the chrome control's rest → hover (hovering made it very slightly darker), and Multiselect's selected-vs-highlighted rows. Light was 1.079 / 1.188 / 1.434 throughout and never showed it, because theme zero AUTHORS light elevation and the derivation moves light elevation the opposite way from hover. Dark now raises 0.03 → 1.121, inside bg-hover in both schemes. (2) IT COULD COLLAPSE ONTO WHAT IT FLOATS OVER. A surface already at the top of the lightness range cannot be raised, so a brand seeded with surface #ffffff got elevated == surface. For a modal that is survivable — its border and shadow carry the separation — but the chrome control and a Header item's hover are a FILL WITH NO EDGE, so it meant no control and no hover feedback at all. When the raise measures as nothing the derivation now steps down instead. Two resolver tests enforce it across every stress brand and both schemes: the neutral fill stack must be ordered by MEASURED contrast (elevated < hover < active, with a real margin), and elevated must measure at least 1.02 against surface. Found by a consumer measuring computed styles in a real browser, not by reading code.

migration.manual: Dark-scheme cards, menu panels, chrome controls, dropzones and table mats are one step less raised than before (1.247 → 1.121 against bg-surface); their ink contrast improves accordingly. Nothing to change at a call site. If you pinned a dark bg-elevated hex in a test or a screenshot baseline, re-take it. A brand theme whose `surface` is pure white now gets a recessed bg-elevated rather than one identical to the surface — if you compensated for the collapse with a local override, remove it.

changes.summary: check:dependencies now resolves every `@/` import in a distributed file against the manifest's INSTALL TARGETS, and it found two shipped items importing paths their consumers do not have: multiselect imported '@/ui/badge/badge.tsx' and card-sorting '@/ui/button/button.tsx' — this repo's folder layout, while the CLI installs those files as 'ui/badge.tsx' and 'ui/button.tsx'. Both declared the right registryDependencies, so the CLI delivered the right FILES under the wrong NAMES; nothing compared the two because the gate skipped `@/` with a comment saying 'the alias ones are what registryDependencies is for'. Fixed to '@/ui/badge' and '@/ui/button', with the alias registered in all four resolvers (root tsconfig, storybook tsconfig, .storybook/main.ts, vitest.config.ts) so the path we ship is the path we type-check. Two keys per item in the Vite configs, longer first: Vite matches a string alias as a prefix, so a lone '@/ui/badge' would turn the folder form tests use into '.../badge.tsx/badge.tsx'. The gate checks both halves — an import that matches no target, and a target imported without its registryDependency — and both were probed failing-first.

Multiselect — blocked since the behaviour-layer question was opened, and the first component assembled from our own primitives: Input's control surface for the trigger, Badge for the chips, Checkbox's visual language for the rows, all over Base UI's Combobox. None of the hard ARIA is written here — listbox roles, aria-multiselectable, active-descendant management, typeahead, filtering and dismissal come from the behaviour layer (ADR 0012), narrowed so no third-party type reaches a public signature: selection is keyed by VALUE rather than by item object, so a re-fetched list keeps it. The option rows deliberately reuse Checkbox's visuals but NOT the Checkbox component, because the row itself carries role=option and a real input nested inside it would be a second control inside the first. Chips nest a Badge inside Base UI's Chip, which supplies the context ChipRemove requires. Nine design defects were corrected rather than transcribed, the worst being an 11px chip label (under the 12px floor ADR 0009 set), a --ui-neutral-100 tick on --ui-blue-80 measuring 1.51:1 against SC 1.4.11's 3:1, and four palette steps where accent and elevated roles already exist. The trigger's agreement with Input is asserted as a RELATIONSHIP rather than as numbers, so the two cannot silently drift apart.

migration.manual: New peer dependencies: @base-ui-components/react (same range as Popover and Modal) and griddy-icons. Registry dependency on badge.

items.name: nav-rail
items.title: NavRail
items.lead: Keeps the main destinations in a compact column.

docs.lead: Keeps the main destinations in a compact column.
docs.name: NavRail
docs.summary: The navigation rail at its narrow width: 48px, one icon per row. A SIBLING of Sidebar rather than a mode of it, because six of Sidebar's ten parts change what they MEAN at this width rather than what they measure — CONVENTIONS §7a already splits Sheet from Drawer on that test. The one-line difference: at full width a row is a slot, at rail width a row is a control. Shares the --ui-nav-* family and the row lane with Sidebar, so a layout can swap one for the other without the navigation changing colour.

anatomy.notes: A <nav>, named by its label. w-nav-rail (--ui-nav-rail-width, 3rem), bg-nav, radius-lg, overflow-clip. The width is MEASURED, not chosen: the artboard declares none, it is fit-content around space-sm padding on the shared 32px chrome control.
Names the landmark, and can never be shown — there is no room for a heading at 48px, so unlike Sidebar there is no isLabelHidden to get wrong.

p-sm, the same 8px Sidebar's body carries, which is what puts a row on the same lane in both. gap-md between groups against gap-xs within one — that DIFFERENCE is the grouping, and nothing is painted. A gap at all would be wrong in Sidebar, whose rows carry their own 12px padding; a rail row is a bare 32px square, so the gap is the only rhythm there is.

A named <ul>, grouped by SPACE. This is where Sidebar's FIRST LEVEL goes: a primary label with a chevron cannot exist at 48px, so the group keeps its name for assistive tech and its own tighter gap. It shipped with a hairline above it and that was wrong — Menu.Separator had already written the rule down ("SPACE, not a rule"), and a painted line inside a 48px control is clutter.

A 32px square at radius-md with a 16px glyph — the chrome control's geometry and none of its colour, because the page's bg-elevated/ink-primary is exactly what the nav family exists to avoid. An <a> when given href, a <button> otherwise.

A row holding a control the caller supplies — the expand toggle, an Avatar. The row's box and nothing else: no role, no tab stop, no name of its own. A 32px chrome control drops in at exactly the row's size, because that is the size the row was built from.
flex-1, aria-hidden. Pushes what follows to the bottom.

docs.composition:
NavRail                    label (required, always hidden)
├─ NavRail.Slot            <button className={chromeControl()}>  — expand to Sidebar
├─ NavRail.Section         label (required, always hidden)
│  └─ NavRail.Item         icon + label (both required) / href? isCurrent? isDisabled?
├─ NavRail.Section         …a second group, divided by a hairline
├─ NavRail.Spacer
└─ NavRail.Slot            <Avatar …/>  — opens the account menu

NavRail and Sidebar are ALTERNATIVES. Neither knows about the other and
neither owns the state: which one renders is the caller's decision, exactly as
it already was between Sidebar and Header.MenuButton. See ADR 0015.

label.notes: Required — a page may carry several <nav> landmarks and they are indistinguishable without names. Unlike Sidebar's there is no option to show it; 48px has no room for a heading.

Item.icon.notes: REQUIRED, and a type rather than a doc note. The label is invisible at this width, so a row with no glyph is a blank square — there is no text to fall back to. Same precedent as Button's icon-only variant requiring aria-label.

Item.label.notes: The accessible name, and the only name the row has. Rendered as aria-label AND as title, so a pointer user gets the platform's own tooltip. See knownGaps — title is a placeholder for a Tooltip this library does not have.

Item.href.notes: OPTIONAL. With it the row is a real <a> — middle-click, open-in-new-tab and the UA's focus handling come free. Without it the row is a <button>, i.e. an action. It is never a container: nothing Sidebar puts in a slot-row fits in a 32px square.

Item.isCurrent.notes: Sets aria-current="page" and takes the third step of a three-step fill ramp: transparent → --ui-nav-hover-bg → --ui-nav-active-bg. Both, not either — a fill conveys nothing to a screen reader (WCAG 1.4.1). It shipped with hover and current sharing ONE fill and a 2px bar down the leading edge separating them; the family gained a hover step instead, because a rule inside a control is clutter.

Item.isDisabled.notes: Unavailable. The row STAYS in the tab order and keeps its role, announced as disabled — a row a screen-reader user cannot reach is one they cannot be told the reason for. Navigation is prevented on the click, never by dropping the href, and never with pointer-events-none.

Item.render.notes: Slot: swap the row's own <a>/<button> for this element — render={<Link href={href} />} so the app's router owns the transition. Passed through, never wrapped (§3).

Section.label.notes: Required and always invisible. The two-level tree does not survive the width: the second level becomes the only level, and the first becomes a named group.

do: Give every row an icon that reads without its label. The label is the accessible name, not a fallback — nothing renders it.
Group rows with NavRail.Section so the hairlines carry the structure the first level used to.
Put the expand control and the Avatar in NavRail.Slot, and style the expand control with @/lib/chrome-control — it is 32px, which is the row's own size.
Set isCurrent on exactly one row, so the marker and the announcement agree.
Own the rail-or-Sidebar choice in the layout. Neither component has a responsive mode, by design.
dont: Do not treat this as Sidebar collapsed. They are siblings (ADR 0015); a layout renders one or the other, and a transition between them is a cross-fade of two trees rather than one component animating.
Do not put a search field, a Progress bar or anything else Sidebar slots into a row. A rail row is a control, not a container — that is the whole reason this component exists.
Do not convey the current row by fill alone — aria-current is what is announced.

Do not reach for a partial edge — a left bar, a bottom rule, an inset stripe — for ANY state. It reads as clutter at this density. Depth, a full outline or elevation; never a ruler (ui-craft rule 20).
Do not add a second level. There is no room for a disclosure, and a flyout would be a Menu — compose one if you need it.
Do not reach for chromeControl on a row. It carries the PAGE's bg-elevated and ink-primary, so a themed rail would re-skin everything except its own navigation.

a11y.role: navigation landmark. A Section is a named <ul> of rows; rows outside a Section are not list items.
a11y.name: The `label` prop via aria-labelledby, always visually hidden. Each row carries its own name through aria-label, because it renders no text.

keyboard.does: Walks the rows in document order — the platform's own behaviour.
Follows a link row, or activates a button row. Native in both cases.
No arrow-key navigation, for Sidebar's reason: it would mean taking the links out of the tab order. A nav is not a menu.

a11y.target: A row is a 32px square — the shared chrome control's size, comfortably over SC 2.5.8's 24px floor rather than exactly on it, which is where Header's 24px item sits.

contrastPairs.role: a resting row's glyph — non-text, because the row renders no text at all
a hovered row's glyph on the hover fill
the current row's glyph — the ink does not move between states on this rail, so this is the resting ink measured on the current fill

contrastPairs.why: WCAG 1.4.3 exempts disabled controls, and a disabled row has to read as unavailable — holding it to the non-text floor would make it indistinguishable from an available one, which is the actual failure. It is still derived to sit clearly below --ui-nav-ink-muted rather than vanishing.
contrastPairs.role: a disabled row's glyph

needsDesign: No expanded-rail transition is drawn. NavRail and Sidebar are separate trees (ADR 0015), so swapping them is a re-render; if a layout ever wants the width to animate, that is the trigger to revisit the decision.
knownGaps: There is no fourth fill for current AND hovered — pointing at the row you are already on does not deepen it, where Header's bar does. Not laziness: a step past --ui-nav-active-bg is an accent WASH under the `tinted` nav style, landing darker for a dark accent and lighter for a light one, so the two grounds straddle the ink and no single value clears both. Three fills the resolver can always satisfy beat four that break a brand style.

Label discovery by pointer rests on the native `title` attribute, which is slow, unstyleable, invisible on touch and not reachable by keyboard. It ships because the platform's own affordance is strictly better than none, and it is the one line to delete when this library grows a Tooltip. The keyboard and screen-reader paths do NOT depend on it — the name comes from aria-label.
No collapsed-rail toggle of its own. The expand control is a caller-supplied Slot, because the rail does not own which of the two navigations is showing.

check:controls does not see this component's <button>. The gate matches a literal `<button` in JSX and NavRail chooses its tag dynamically, exactly as Header and Sidebar do — the gate documents the limitation, and this is the third component to land in it.
docs.motion: Rows transition `background-color` and `color` at --ui-duration-fast with --ui-ease-out. There is no travelling indicator: the current row is marked by its fill alone (ledger 2026-08-10-nav-current-row-is-fill-only), so nothing moves between rows and the rail never animates position.

contrast.role: a resting row's glyph — non-text, because the row renders no text at all
a hovered row's glyph on the hover fill
the current row's glyph — the ink does not move between states on this rail, so this is the resting ink measured on the current fill
a disabled row's glyph

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

check:motion joins the gate list, and every animating component now documents its motion. The gate rejects a literal duration or easing in registry/ (a discipline that was already perfect — zero hard-coded durations across 26 files — and had nothing keeping it that way), transition-all (CONVENTIONS section 6 has said this since the beginning and nothing enforced it), a keyframe with no reduced-motion guard, and an animating component with no top-level motion: note in its doc. It reads lib recipes alongside components as check:overlays does, so Header's motion is found in @/lib/chrome-control where it actually lives rather than reported as absent. 27 doc files gain a motion: note describing what moves, what drives it and what reduced motion does to it; Sheet's and ImageUpload's existing notes are PROMOTED out of a11y to the top level, where Button already had its, because motion is a description of what a component does rather than solely an accessibility concern and a field meaning one thing at two depths stops being findable. ImageUpload's note is corrected while being promoted: it credited the token layer with stopping its spinner, and what actually stops it is the motion-safe: variant. Two findings are recorded in the notes rather than fixed: Sidebar's collapsible section snaps via the hidden attribute where Accordion animates the identical interaction against Base UI's published height, and Banner reaches for transition-colors where the rest of the library enumerates properties. No component's rendered motion changes; no .tsx is touched.

migration.manual: Documentation only — every change is inside a *.doc.ts, and no component's classes or rendered motion moved. If you consume the doc files and read `a11y.motion`, it has moved to the top-level `motion` key on Sheet and ImageUpload; Button was already there and the other 27 are new.

changes.summary: The current row in Sidebar and NavRail is marked by its FILL and nothing else. Sidebar drops `font-bold` and steps the current row's ink BACK to `--ui-nav-ink-muted` where it used to lift to `--ui-nav-active-ink`; hover no longer lifts ink either, on either component; NavRail's current glyph stays at its resting ink. This is the narrow half of the divergence Header opened when it decided the current page recedes, and it closes the half that was actually wrong rather than the half that was a real difference: a rail still marks position with a fill where a bar does not, because a rail is a persistent map and a bar is a short row you read across — but ink and weight now behave identically across the whole nav family. Weight was the worst of the three channels: bold on the current row reflowed its own label a fraction and made the one row you cannot navigate to the loudest thing in the rail, spending emphasis on the least actionable item exactly as Header's four-step ramp did. Measured: muted on the current fill is 9.64:1 light and 5.42:1 dark, and the fill carries the state at 1.105 / 1.285 against the rail. The pair `--ui-nav-ink-muted` on `--ui-nav-active-bg` is now declared in the token contract so the theme audit covers what these components actually render; `--ui-nav-active-ink` stays in the contract because a re-skin can still reach for it.

migration.manual: The current nav row loses its bold weight and its label goes from full-strength nav ink to muted; its background is unchanged. Hover no longer changes ink on either component. If you styled around the current row's weight or ink — an override, a screenshot baseline, a test asserting the current item is bolder or darker than a resting one — the difference now lives entirely in `background-color`. A top-level Sidebar row shows the ink step clearly (nav-ink to muted); a row inside a section was already muted, so there only the fill changes.

changes.summary: A partial edge is never a state. NavRail shipped a 2px bar down the current row's leading edge to separate it from hover, and separated its groups with hairlines — both wrong, and both against a rule this library had already written: Menu.Separator is "SPACE, not a rule — 8px above and below, and nothing painted". A ruler inside a control reads as clutter and multiplies down a list. The marker was the wrong answer to a REAL problem, which is the part worth keeping: --ui-nav-active-bg was the family's only fill, so hover and current painted the identical square and a rail row has no label to change weight the way Sidebar's does. The fix is a token, not a decoration — --ui-nav-hover-bg joins the contract, and rest/hover/current are now three fills in both rails. Sidebar takes the same step so the two stay interchangeable, and keeps its weight change on top. Grouping in NavRail is now the DIFFERENCE between the body's gap-md and a section's gap-xs, which also removes the `first:` selector the hairline needed and had mis-set. A fourth step for current-AND-hovered was attempted and abandoned on evidence: past --ui-nav-active-bg the value is an accent WASH under the `tinted` nav style, landing darker for a dark accent and lighter for a light one, so the two grounds straddle the ink, legibleOn flips for one of them and no single value clears both — the resolver test caught it at 3.70:1 and then 3.89:1 across two attempts. Three fills the resolver can always satisfy beat four that break a brand style. Codified as ui-craft rules 20–22 and three ratchet entries; the browser test asserts no element paints a border on fewer than four sides, probed against a re-added marker.

migration.manual: --ui-nav-hover-bg is new; a consumer with a hand-written nav theme should give it a value between --ui-nav-bg and --ui-nav-active-bg, or let the resolver derive it. A rail row's hover fill is lighter than before — it used to be the current row's fill, which is the bug.

changes.summary: NavRail — the navigation rail at 48px, and a SIBLING of Sidebar rather than a mode of it (ADR 0015). The test is CONVENTIONS §7a's, the one that already splits Sheet from Drawer: when the CONTRACT differs rather than the appearance, it is a different component. Six of Sidebar's ten parts change what they MEAN at this width rather than what they measure — Search is a 40px field and has to become a control, Profile is an avatar with a name and an address and has to become an avatar, Heading and Slot have nowhere to put 'Select brand' or a Progress bar, and a Section's label-plus-chevron disclosure has room for neither. The one-line version: at full width a row is a slot, at rail width a row is a control, so a row is an <a> when it navigates and a <button> when it acts and never a container. Both `icon` and `label` are REQUIRED types, following Button's icon-only precedent: the label is invisible, so a row with no glyph is a blank square and there is no text to fall back to. Sidebar's first level survives as NavRail.Section — a named <ul> with a hairline — because a group can keep its accessible name at 48px even when its label cannot be drawn. The current row carries a 2px marker in --ui-nav-ink as well as aria-current, since --ui-nav-active-bg is the family's only fill and hover would otherwise paint the identical square; the marker is a painted box rather than an inset shadow because forced-colors forces box-shadow to none and it is the only thing distinguishing current from hover. The pairing with Sidebar is asserted as a RELATIONSHIP rather than as numbers: the browser suite compares the two components' body inset and rail fill to each other, so a change to either that breaks the swap fails rather than drifting. Two design values corrected on the way in: the drawn rail declares no width at all (fit-content around space-sm on the shared 32px chrome control), which settles a 48/50/56 disagreement between the artboard, TODO and sidebarDoc in favour of 48; and the sr-only landmark label moved OUT of the body, because sr-only is position:absolute but a structural pseudo-class still counts DOM position, so `first:border-t-0` matched nothing and every Section drew a divider it should not have.

migration.manual: New component; nothing to migrate. A layout renders NavRail or Sidebar, never both — neither has a responsive mode, by design.

items.name: network
items.title: Network
items.lead: Explores relationships between connected items.

docs.lead: Explores relationships between connected items.
docs.name: Network
docs.summary: A network of typed entities that people explore — a knowledge graph, a social or citation network — where nodes are glyphs, not cards. SVG by default, with a seeded force or radial layout that runs in a worker above 500 nodes and grows incrementally: nodes already drawn are pinned, so appending neighbours never reshuffles them. The keyboard model is the Network sheet's: rings of hops from the selected node, Up and Down round a ring, Right and Left onto a relation and across it, Plus to expand. An adjacency table is one toggle away, and it is the floor for a custom renderer — the Canvas tier — before hydration and in forced colours.

anatomy.notes: A <figure> named by the title and described by the takeaway: Chart's and Diagram's frame (bg-surface, border-subtle, radius-md, 24px inset). data-renderer says which tier drew it. className and the rest land here.
label-md, primary.
body-sm, muted. The takeaway a person wrote.
Button secondary md, icon-only (ChartTable), aria-pressed. Swaps the drawing for the adjacency table.

`height` px tall (default 480), bg-base under DotPattern, border-subtle, radius-md, clipped. A drag pans; pinch or Ctrl/⌘ + wheel zooms. One hit test serves every renderer: the nearest centre within 24px.
The one tab stop: role=group, aria-roledescription "network", named by the title, described by the keyboard hint.

A 20px-radius disc: the canvas (bg-base), the type's data-cat-N-bg wash, and a 1.5px data-cat-N-solid ring at r19.25 so the stroke sits inside the disc. The type's 16px glyph centred in primary ink. A type with no slot — the ninth and later — is Other: no wash, a border-control ring.
No wash: the canvas fill and a 2px text-primary ring at r19. Its relations turn active; everything outside its neighbourhood dims.
Keyboard only: a 2px border-focus ring at r23, clear of the type ring. Highlight in forced colours.
Outside the selected neighbourhood, or off the highlight path: opacity 32%, and its name turns muted at full opacity so it still reads.
label-sm 600 primary on a bg-base pill, 4px inline, centred 26px below the centre in a 180px lane, truncated.
Centre to centre, both ends stopped 26px out; 2px border-control with the sheet's 8×8 arrow head. Active: text-primary. Inferred: text-muted at 1.5px, no head — never dashed.
label-sm 400 muted on a bg-base pill at the midpoint. Active: 600 primary. An inferred edge reads "colleague of · inferred".

"+N" for `hiddenNeighbours`, 4px right of the focus ring: 24px tall, at least 32 wide, 8px inline, 2px gap, rounded-full, bg-elevated, a 1px border-control edge so it reads on the canvas (sheet fix, 2026-11-12). Plus key or a press calls onExpandRequest.
Network.Controls, 16px from the bottom right: Zoom in, Zoom out, Fit — the shared 32px chrome control.
Table sm: Node, Relation, Neighbour, Type — one row per edge, then one per unconnected node.
Three 40px bg-sunken discs, aria-busy, no tab stop: while loading, and while a worker lays out.
A polite live region in the sheet's sentence: "HfG Ulm, Organisation. Otl Aicher co-founded it. 1 of 4 neighbours. 12 more not shown: press Plus to expand."

NetworkCanvas (a separate item): one device-pixel canvas painting the same marks from the same inks, read through the cascade so brand and dark both apply. Node names from half scale up; no glyphs, no edge labels, no name pills.

docs.composition:
Network                       label · description · nodes · edges · types? · layout? · selected?
└─ Network.Controls           zoom in, zoom out, fit (bottom right)
NetworkCanvas                 passed as renderer={NetworkCanvas}; admitted above canvasThreshold

label.notes: The visible title, the figure's name and the keyboard region's name.

description.notes: The takeaway. A screen-reader user hears it first.

nodes.notes: lib/graph's shape: id, label (the accessible name), type, description, position (pinned), data.

edges.notes: source, target, label (the predicate), isDirected (default true), isInferred (muted, thinner, no head, named "inferred").

types.notes: Pin each type's slot, so a filter that removes a type does not repaint the survivors. Default: first appearance on slots 1–8, the rest folded into Other — never a generated ninth hue.

layout.notes: Force: seeded, deterministic, incremental. Radial: rings of hops round `rootId`.

rootId.notes: The radial centre, and where focus starts when nothing is selected.

seed.notes: Same seed, same picture — what keeps the visual gate stable.

selected.notes: Controlled selection, with onSelect. defaultSelected for uncontrolled.

highlight.notes: A path of node ids (shortestPath answers one): its edges turn active, everything off it dims.

hiddenNeighbours.notes: Neighbours that exist but are not drawn yet: the "+N" chip and the announcement's "12 more not shown".

onExpandRequest.notes: Plus, or a press on the chip. Append the neighbours to nodes and edges; the nodes already drawn stay where they are.

onDismiss.notes: Escape on a node with nothing selected — the explorer closes its panel with it.

workerThreshold.notes: Above it the force layout runs in a module worker; below it, on the main thread and on the server.

renderer.notes: A paint surface for big graphs — NetworkCanvas. It paints; Network keeps the keyboard, the announcer, hit-testing and the table.

canvasThreshold.notes: Nodes plus edges above which `renderer` is admitted: the measured SVG ceiling (plan §3.2).

keyboardHint.notes: The viewport's description: the keys, once.

do: Pin every type's slot in `types`, and give each a glyph: the type is then never colour alone.
Grow the graph with onExpandRequest and hiddenNeighbours rather than handing it everything: a person explores a neighbourhood, not 5,000 nodes.
Pass renderer={NetworkCanvas} when a graph can pass 2,000 elements; below that it changes nothing.
Keep the seed stable for a given dataset, so a reload draws the same picture.
dont: Do not use it for a flow with a direction of reading — a pipeline, an org chart. Diagram lays those out in ranks.
Do not put a ninth hue in `types`: fold the long tail into Other, or filter it.
Do not rely on the canvas tier in forced colours or before hydration: Network shows the table there, by design.

a11y.role: A <figure> named by the title and described by the takeaway. The drawing is a role=group with aria-roledescription "network"; nodes and edges are aria-hidden pictures of what the announcer and the table say.
a11y.name: `label` via aria-labelledby on the figure and the viewport; `description` via aria-describedby on the figure; `keyboardHint` on the viewport.

keyboard.does: Into the drawing, on the selected node (or `rootId`, or the first). Inside: walks the focused node's relations clockwise, then leaves — never a trap.
The next or previous node on the same ring — the same number of hops from the selected node — clockwise from twelve o'clock. On a relation: the next or previous relation.
From a node, onto its first relation clockwise from twelve o'clock, read from the far node; from a relation, across it to the far node.
From a node, onto its last relation (the first counter-clockwise); from a relation, back to the near node.
The first and last node of the ring, or relation of the node.
Selects the focused node (again clears it); on a relation, goes to the far node.
Asks to expand the focused node, or a relation's far node, when it has hidden neighbours; otherwise zooms in.
Zoom in and out.
Fit the drawing to the frame.
Pan 64px.
From a relation back to its node; on a node, clears the selection; with nothing selected, calls onDismiss.

docs.motion: The world layer's transform eases at --ui-duration-base with --ui-ease-out, so zoom, fit and follow-focus glide; a drag drops the transition. The layout itself never animates: positions are computed to completion before anything paints, so a new node appears in place rather than flying in. Under prefers-reduced-motion the duration token collapses.
needsDesign: The relation focus state — a 6px border-focus halo under the edge — is Diagram's reading; the Network sheet draws focus on nodes only.
The table view is not drawn; it is the plan's alternative (§3.6), as Table sm.
The Canvas tier has no sheet: it paints the SVG tier's marks, without glyphs.
knownGaps: The force layout is our own (lib/graph), not d3-force: a grid-bounded repulsion and springs, run to completion. Good to a few thousand nodes; it does not detect communities or bundle edges.
Above the worker threshold the first paint is a skeleton until the worker answers; the server sends the skeleton, not the drawing.
Labels are not collision-avoided: in a dense neighbourhood two names can overlap. Zoom, or filter.

The Canvas tier draws no glyphs and no edge labels, and hides node names below half scale; the relation is still in the announcer and the table. It has no forced-colours mode at all — the table stands in.
The table is not filtered by the current view or paginated, so the floor for a 5,000-node graph is a 5,000-row table (plan §8 asks for a filtered one).
Not measured on a mid-range phone: the plan's V4 exit (a 5k-node graph explorable on one) is unverified.

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

Paper: the Network sheet's findings from /review-ui are fixed on the sheet. Dimmed nodes and edges keep their labels in muted ink (they measured 2.8:1 for node names and 1.79:1 for edge labels when the whole mark faded); only fills, rings and strokes recede. The inferred 'colleague of' edge is muted ink at hairline weight with no arrowhead, since the relation is symmetric (plan §3.7). The '+12' expand chip moves clear of the focus ring it overlapped. Arrowheads stop 26px from a node's centre whether it is focused or not, so focus no longer moves them. Network now ships from this sheet and its colour pairs are in network.doc.ts a11y.contrastPairs.

Network (V4): an entity graph on SVG. Seeded force or radial layout, incremental — nodes already placed stay pinned while new ones are appended, and node.position fixes one — with the layout moved to a worker above workerThreshold (500 elements) and identical to the main thread's. Types take data-cat slots 1–8 in order and a ninth folds into Other; each node is a base disc, its wash, a hairline ring in the slot's solid and an optional glyph. Keyboard: Up and Down go round the ring of the focused node's hop distance, Right and Left step onto and along its relations, Plus expands a node with hidden neighbours, Home, End, Tab, Enter and Escape as the sheet says, with every step announced. A '+N' chip asks onExpandRequest for more; a table view shows every relation and replaces the drawing before hydration and in forced colours.

Docs: graph-data-recipes.md maps a Neo4j driver result and RDF (flattened JSON-LD, or any RDF/JS quads) into GraphNode and GraphEdge, with the Cypher and SPARQL that fill hiddenNeighbours for the explorer, and how to mark inferred relations. Dependency-free; each mapping was extracted, type-checked under the repo's settings and run on fixtures, which caught one exactOptionalPropertyTypes slip. The plan's V3 and V4 items are ticked, with the decision to write layered, tree, radial and force layouts in lib/graph instead of admitting dagre, d3-hierarchy or d3-force, and V4's exit recorded as not yet met: nothing tried at 5,000 nodes or on a phone, the layout measured at about 4 s for 5,000 on a desktop CPU.

docs.name: NetworkCanvas
docs.lead: Paints a larger network on a canvas while Network keeps the controls and accessible table.
docs.summary: Pass NetworkCanvas to Network's renderer slot. This optional paint surface is not a standalone graph viewer.

anatomy.notes: Paint-only canvas. Network owns hit testing, focus, announcements and the table.

docs.composition: Network → renderer={NetworkCanvas}

size.notes: The measured drawing surface.

do: Use it through Network's renderer slot.
dont: Do not use the canvas as a standalone interactive surface.

a11y.role: Decorative renderer inside Network; the parent owns semantics.

keyboard.does: Network retains its keyboard controls and adjacency table.

knownGaps: Node glyphs and edge labels are omitted at canvas density; Network's table and announcer retain that information.
docs.motion: The parent supplies viewport changes. The renderer does not animate independently.

NetworkCanvas: Network's Canvas 2D tier for about 2,000 to 20,000 elements, passed as renderer and admitted only above canvasThreshold. It paints the SVG tier's marks at device-pixel resolution from the same path data, resolving every ink through the cascade so brand scopes and dark mode apply, and draws names from half scale up. items.name: popover
items.title: Popover
items.lead: Keeps supporting content close to the control that opens it.

docs.lead: Keeps supporting content close to the control that opens it.
docs.name: Popover
docs.summary: A panel anchored to a trigger, for secondary content that should not take over the page. First component built on the Base UI behaviour layer (ADR 0012): positioning, focus restoration, dismissal and ARIA wiring come from there; the API, anatomy and every pixel are ours.

anatomy.notes: The control that opens it. Pass your own element via `render` — it is never wrapped.

The portalled surface. radius-lg, bg-elevated, a border-subtle hairline and shadow-md — Card's surface (issue #40). Not concentric with a radius-md boxed child at p-lg; accepted by the 2026-10-29 owner review.
Names the panel for assistive tech via aria-labelledby, automatically.

body-md at the relaxed leading in secondary ink at `medium` weight, per the actions sheet. The sheet drew 600 there, but its only description sits in a destructive confirmation and that emphasis does not generalise. Carries the unboxed inset plus py-xs.
Optional dismiss control. Takes an element via `render`.

docs.composition:
Popover                      isOpen? / defaultIsOpen? / onOpenChange? / isModal?
├─ Popover.Trigger           render={<Button>…</Button>}
└─ Popover.Panel             side? align? sideOffset? alignOffset?
   ├─ Popover.Title          inset — bare text
   ├─ Popover.Description    inset — bare text
   ├─ Banner                 flush — the sheet's info well IS the Banner component
   ├─ <any boxed child>      flush — an Input, a card
   └─ Popover.Close          render={<Button>…</Button>}

container.notes: Where the panel is portalled. Theme tokens are INHERITED custom properties, so a panel in the body leaves any brand scope on a wrapper and paints theme zero. Pass the themed element to bring it back; see sheet.doc.ts for why it is a prop rather than automatic.

isOpen.notes: Controlled. Omit and the popover owns it.

onOpenChange.notes: One callback for both directions (§1) — never onOpen + onClose. Narrowed from Base UI's (open, eventDetails) so no third-party type reaches the signature.

isModal.notes: Traps focus and blocks the page behind. A hint is not modal; a short form usually is.

side.notes: Preferred side. Flips automatically on collision.

render.notes: On Trigger and Close. The element is passed through, not wrapped (§3), so it keeps its tag, classes, ref and accessible name and gains only the ARIA wiring.

do: Pass your own control into Trigger's `render` — a Button, usually — so the trigger keeps its own accessible name.
Give every panel a Popover.Title; it becomes the panel's accessible name with no aria-label to keep in sync.
Let boxed children (info wells, inputs) sit flush; use Title/Description for bare text so the inset is applied for you.
Use isModal for a panel containing a form, so focus cannot escape behind it.
dont: Do not import Base UI types into your own props — `check:boundaries` fails the build, and it is what keeps the layer swappable (ADR 0002).
Do not use a Popover for a message that must be acknowledged — that is a Modal.
Do not add padding to bare text yourself; Title and Description already carry the inset, and doubling it breaks the alignment with boxed children.
Do not reach for a Popover as a tooltip. A tooltip is hover-triggered and non-interactive; this is a focusable dialog.

a11y.role: dialog (from Base UI). The trigger carries aria-haspopup="dialog" and aria-expanded, verified in Chromium.
a11y.name: Popover.Title, wired through aria-labelledby automatically. A panel with no Title needs an explicit aria-label.

keyboard.does: Opens from the trigger — native, since the trigger is a real button.
Closes and RESTORES FOCUS to the trigger. Asserted in a real browser: focus falling to <body> is the classic hand-rolled-popover failure.
Moves through the panel's own focusable content; with isModal it is trapped.

contrastPairs.role: the title on the panel
the description
the panel against the page
contrastPairs.why: the boundary is the hairline plus shadow-md, not the fill (ADR 0010)

a11y.dismissal: Outside click, Escape and focus-out all dismiss, without swallowing events the page needs.

knownGaps: Not drawn in the sheet, so DERIVED and marked as such: placement (bottom), 8px offset, collision padding, and the enter/exit transition. Confirm with design.

The panel is capped to --available-height / --available-width (§7c) so a tall popover cannot run off a short window. Neither the cap nor the resulting internal scroll is drawn — the sheet draws one panel short enough that neither applies.
No arrow. Base UI provides Popover.Arrow; the sheet draws none, so none is exposed yet.
No dark-scheme values for the panel are drawn — the resolver derives them, unverified against a design.

The actions row is composed at the call site rather than being a Popover.Actions part — the sheet sits it flush at the panel padding while title and description take the inset, so it is deliberately not wrapped.
docs.motion: The panel fades and scales from 98% at --ui-duration-fast with --ui-ease-out, through `data-[starting-style]`/`data-[ending-style]`. `scale` is named in the transition list for the same reason as Modal's — Tailwind v4 writes it standalone, and a list naming `transform` left this panel snapping open.

contrast.role: the title on the panel
the description
the panel against the page

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

ChatSources: inline citation markers, a hover/focus preview anchored to each, and a sources block under the answer — folded to kind discs and a count, open to numbered link rows, or led by source cards. Numbers are list positions shared through ChatSources.Provider; a working StatusMatrix while sources gather; a disabled marker while the answer streams. The marker is allowlisted in check:controls as an inline pill no Button size describes.

Card, Popover's panel and Modal's surface draw at --ui-radius-lg (16px), not radius-xl (24) — the 2026-10-27/29 owner decision, platform-wide (#40). Modal's radius half of #23 is reversed; its hairline, shadow and title are unchanged. A radius-md boxed child at p-lg is no longer concentric; accepted in review.

migration.manual: Remove any consumer patch that forced [data-slot=card|popover-panel|modal-surface] to --ui-radius-lg (e.g. service-portal's `Registry patch (TEMPORARY)` block).

changes.summary: check:motion joins the gate list, and every animating component now documents its motion. The gate rejects a literal duration or easing in registry/ (a discipline that was already perfect — zero hard-coded durations across 26 files — and had nothing keeping it that way), transition-all (CONVENTIONS section 6 has said this since the beginning and nothing enforced it), a keyframe with no reduced-motion guard, and an animating component with no top-level motion: note in its doc. It reads lib recipes alongside components as check:overlays does, so Header's motion is found in @/lib/chrome-control where it actually lives rather than reported as absent. 27 doc files gain a motion: note describing what moves, what drives it and what reduced motion does to it; Sheet's and ImageUpload's existing notes are PROMOTED out of a11y to the top level, where Button already had its, because motion is a description of what a component does rather than solely an accessibility concern and a field meaning one thing at two depths stops being findable. ImageUpload's note is corrected while being promoted: it credited the token layer with stopping its spinner, and what actually stops it is the motion-safe: variant. Two findings are recorded in the notes rather than fixed: Sidebar's collapsible section snaps via the hidden attribute where Accordion animates the identical interaction against Base UI's published height, and Banner reaches for transition-colors where the rest of the library enumerates properties. No component's rendered motion changes; no .tsx is touched.

migration.manual: Documentation only — every change is inside a *.doc.ts, and no component's classes or rendered motion moved. If you consume the doc files and read `a11y.motion`, it has moved to the top-level `motion` key on Sheet and ImageUpload; Button was already there and the other 27 are new.

changes.summary: Popover — the first component built on the Base UI behaviour layer (ADR 0012), and the proof that the wrapper rule is livable. Positioning, focus restoration, outside-click and Escape dismissal, and the aria-haspopup/aria-expanded/aria-labelledby wiring come from Base UI 1.0.0-rc.0; the API, anatomy and every pixel are ours. No Base UI type reaches an exported signature: placement is our own closed union rather than its Side/Align types, and onOpenChange is narrowed from its (open, eventDetails) to our (isOpen: boolean) per CONVENTIONS §1. check:boundaries ran against a real import for the first time and held. Open state deliberately does NOT go through useControllableState — the behaviour layer already implements the controlled/uncontrolled contract, and running two implementations over one piece of state is how they drift; §4 bans a bespoke implementation, which this is the opposite of. Trigger and Close take an element through `render` and pass it straight through, so a Button keeps its tag, classes, ref and accessible name and gains only the ARIA wiring (§3) — asserted in Chromium. Escape restoring focus to the trigger is asserted too, because focus falling to <body> is the classic hand-rolled-popover failure. Design corrected in Paper first: the panel had NO boundary at all (bg-elevated measures 1.11:1 on a white page) and now carries a border-subtle hairline plus shadow-md; the info glyph was a raw #B1A8A0 at 1.92:1 and is now --ui-text-muted at 4.87:1; radii were inverted (outer 12px inside an inner 16px) and are now concentric at radius-2xl; palette steps, raw gaps and raw type all moved onto roles. Establishes a new craft rule from the updated Card and Popover sheets: inside a radius-2xl panel bare text is inset by --ui-space-sm while boxed children sit flush, encoded structurally in Popover.Title/Description rather than documented.

migration.manual: Adds @base-ui-components/react as a peer dependency — the first behaviour-tier dependency. Every future item that depends on it must declare the SAME range. Separately, FLUID type roles now floor at the scale's own 12px minimum instead of a flat 72% of their maximum: --ui-text-title-sm shrank to 11.52px on narrow viewports, under the floor ADR 0009 set after an 11px label pushed the small button below the WCAG target size. Only title-sm was actually below the floor; other fluid roles are unchanged.

items.name: progress
items.title: Progress
items.lead: Shows how far a task has come and what is still in progress.

docs.lead: Shows how far a task has come and what is still in progress.
docs.name: Progress
docs.summary: A determinate progress bar with an optional label and percentage. Two track heights (20/8px). A div with role=progressbar, because unlike a checkbox or button a progress bar has no native behaviour to inherit.

anatomy.notes: The wrapper. className lands here (§5). Carries data-size.
Names the bar via aria-labelledby. sr-only when isLabelHidden, never removed.
The rounded percentage, shown only with hasValueText.
role=progressbar and the three ARIA value attributes. bg-sunken, pill.
Width-driven, not transform — scaling would squash the rounded ends into ellipses.

docs.composition:
Progress
├─ value          number (required) — clamped into 0…max
├─ max?           default 100
├─ label          string (required) — the accessible name
├─ isLabelHidden? / hasValueText?
└─ size?          lg (20px) | sm (8px)

value.notes: Clamped into 0…max, and the CLAMPED value is what aria-valuenow reports — a bar wider than its track is a layout bug that only appears with real data.

max.notes: Reported as aria-valuemax rather than rescaled away, so '3 of 4' is announced as 3 of 4.

label.notes: Required — a bar with no name announces only a number. Use isLabelHidden when the design shows none.

hasValueText.notes: Shows the rounded percentage beside the label, as the sheet draws it.

size.notes: 16px and 8px tracks, both drawn. RENAMED from lg|sm and the large track resized from 20px: the sheet draws --ui-space-lg (16), and Slider's own scale calls 16px `md`. A `lg` that meant 20px here and 24px there is exactly the shared-vocabulary problem CONVENTIONS §2 exists to prevent.

variant.notes: gradient paints --ui-gradient-brand, the sheet's three-stop spectrum. solid is the default because the fill is a meaningful graphic that must clear 3:1, which the accent role guarantees and a sweep cannot along its whole length. The gradient is BRANDABLE — a client's portal derives its own spectrum from its accent rather than inheriting Diorama's.

do: Give every bar a label, even when hidden; it is the accessible name.
Use max for counts ('3 of 4 files') rather than converting to a percentage yourself.
Use sm inline in dense lists and lg where progress is the point of the screen.
dont: Do not use Progress for an unknown duration — an indeterminate state is not drawn and is not implemented; see knownGaps.
Do not animate the fill with a transform; the rounded ends distort.
Do not put the percentage inside the track — the sheet puts it in the label row, where it stays legible at 8px.

a11y.role: progressbar, with aria-valuenow / -valuemin / -valuemax, all asserted in Chromium.
a11y.name: The `label` prop via aria-labelledby. Hidden labels are sr-only, so they stay in the accessibility tree.

keyboard.does: Not focusable. A progress bar is output, not a control.

contrastPairs.role: the fill against its track
the value text
the label

knownGaps: The gradient's contrast is not audited along its length — only its endpoints are knowable at token time. On a pale brand accent the lightest stop can fall under 3:1 against the track, which is why solid is the default and gradient is opt-in.
No indeterminate state. Not drawn, and the commonest real need after this one.
No intent colouring (a bar that turns danger near its limit) — not drawn.
docs.motion: The bar's `width` transitions at --ui-duration-base with --ui-ease-out. Width rather than a transform on purpose: scaling the fill would squash its rounded ends into ellipses. The transition names `width` alone, so a value arriving in steps reads as a fill advancing rather than as a series of jumps.

contrast.role: the fill against its track
the value text
the label

Chat Progress rebuilt on StatusMatrix with ONE moving mark per turn. The CSS ring spinner is gone. New forms: waiting and streaming status rows (the thinking row's matrix hands over in place to its ending — failed and stopped keep the same element); reasoning under a five-line capped, faded body; a thought chain on a 16px node lane with kind glyphs, chips, prose, one level of branches, a failed status with Retry and a 40px tabular clock; parallel lanes drawn as the activity pill's box (glyph, 104px name, activity, clock, chevron) that open to their own chain. The geometry spec now measures the lane pill (sheet 4040-0) instead of the old step list.

migration.manual: BREAKING: steps take `status: "done" | "current" | "pending" | "failed"` with optional icon, duration, chips, detail and one level of `steps`; the spinner and its data-slot are gone (the row's mark is a StatusMatrix with data-slot="status-matrix").
