changes.summary: Progress gains an `xs` size — the 6px track the Image Upload sheet draws inside a file row. Additive: md and sm are unchanged. It exists so that row does not hand-roll a track, because a hand-drawn bar has no role=progressbar, no aria-valuenow, and no reason to reach for --ui-bg-accent-legible — the upload sheet fills its own track with --ui-bg-accent, 1.24:1 against the well in light. Reusing Progress makes that failure unrepeatable rather than merely discouraged.

migration.manual: Additive — no existing size changed. `size="xs"` is available on Progress.

changes.summary: Progress `size` is now md | sm and the larger track is 16px, where it was lg | sm with a 20px track. Two things were wrong with the old scale and the Slider refactor surfaced both. The 20px never matched the sheet: the Progress artboard draws its tracks at --ui-space-lg (16) and --ui-space-sm (8), so the large bar had been 4px over its own drawing. And `lg` meaning 20px here while Slider's refreshed scale calls 24px `lg` is precisely the shared-vocabulary problem CONVENTIONS §2 exists to prevent — one word, two heights, in two components a consumer stacks in the same panel. Renaming to md aligns the word with Slider's 16px step and leaves no size in this library where `lg` means two different things. The variants, the segmented form and the gradient fill are unchanged; Progress keeps --ui-gradient-brand for its gradient variant, which is the three-stop spectrum its own sheet draws, not the slider's accent ramp.

migration.manual: REQUIRED: replace size="lg" with size="md" — the old value no longer compiles, deliberately, because it would otherwise resolve to a silently different bar. A Progress with no size prop changes from a 20px track to 16px, which matches its own design sheet. If a layout depended on the 20px height, set it explicitly rather than reintroducing the name.

changes.summary: A form field whose control is a drop target, in the sheet's four caller-settable states plus a drag-over state the component owns. It is built on a real <input type="file"> with a real <label>, so the keyboard path is the native picker rather than a re-implementation — which is also why it is allowlisted in check:gestures rather than carrying an onKeyDown that does nothing. Five design fixes, each measured: the file row's progress fill was --ui-bg-accent at 1.24:1 against its own track and is now a real Progress at 3.07:1; the Replace pill was outlined in --ui-border-default at 2.14:1 and is now Button variant=outline at 3.11:1; the busy label was --ui-text-disabled at 1.94:1 and is now --ui-text-secondary; the rejection prose was --ui-text-muted on the danger well at 4.00:1 in dark and is now --ui-text-on-danger-subtle at 5.93:1; and 'browse' was styled text with no control behind it, so the component was pointer-only (SC 2.1.1) — it is now a real underlined button. errorText is what puts the field in `rejected`, as on Input, so the message and the state cannot disagree.

migration.manual: New item — nothing to migrate. `npx shadcn add @bydiorama/image-upload`; it pulls in `cn` and `progress`, and expects react and griddy-icons as peers.

changes.summary: Progress — a determinate bar in two track heights (20/8px), with an optional label row and rounded percentage. Rendered as a div with role=progressbar rather than the native <progress>: unlike a checkbox or a button it has no behaviour to inherit, the native element cannot be styled to this design across browsers, and the ARIA it needs is three attributes, all set here and asserted in Chromium. The value is CLAMPED into 0..max and the clamped value is what aria-valuenow reports, because a fill wider than its track is a layout bug that only appears with real data. max is reported rather than rescaled away, so '3 of 4' announces as 3 of 4. The fill is width-driven, not transform-driven — scaling would squash the pill ends into ellipses. One design defect NOT transcribed: the sheet paints the fill with a three-stop brand gradient (blue-80 to lavender-80 to red-80, in oklab) built from raw palette steps, which do not re-skin with a brand and have no gradient role in the contract. Resolved after review: --ui-gradient-brand is now a BRANDABLE token, derived by rotating the seed's own accent in OKLCH so a client's portal gets its own three-stop sweep rather than inheriting Diorama's, and pinned in theme zero to the exact designed stops. Progress exposes it as variant='gradient'; solid stays the default because the fill is a meaningful graphic that must clear 3:1, which a sweep cannot guarantee along its whole length. The arbitrary bg-(image:--ui-gradient-brand) is skipped by check:utilities by design, so a browser test asserts it paints a real background-image — without the `image:` hint it would set a background COLOUR to a gradient string and paint nothing. REVIEW ALSO FOUND: the fill measures 1.24:1 against its track in light (10.07:1 in dark), failing SC 1.4.11 for a graphic that carries meaning, and the doc had claimed an unverified 3.2:1. The number is corrected and the failure is recorded as open, because the sheet draws the same pale-on-pale pair and fixing it is a design decision.

migration.manual: None — new component.

items.name: radio
items.title: RadioGroup
items.lead: One choice from a set that stays visible.

docs.lead: One choice from a set that stays visible.
docs.name: RadioGroup
docs.summary: One choice from a set that stays visible. The GROUP is the component and the option is its item: the legend, the shared name, the selection and the error all belong to the set, and a Radio on its own is one alternative rather than a control. A real fieldset around real radio inputs, so arrow-key navigation, the single tab stop, form participation and the legend-as-part-of-every-name come from the platform.

anatomy.notes: The <fieldset>. Owns className, the ref and the 12px column. `min-w-0` is not decoration: a fieldset defaults to min-width:min-content, so without it a group of long labels overflows a flex column instead of wrapping.

The <legend>. label-md 13 / 600. It names the question the set answers, which is the one thing no individual option can carry — and the platform prepends it to every option's accessible name for free.
The run of items. 8px apart vertically, stepping to 12 the moment any option carries a description; 24px apart horizontally. The step is a `has-*` pair rather than a prop — see props.orientation.
The <label>. Carries data-state (checked | unchecked) and data-disabled, and IS the target — padded to 24px so the 18px circle is not the target on its own.
The real <input type="radio">, visually clipped with sr-only but focusable, tabbable and in the form. The forwarded ref lands here (CONVENTIONS §5).

The 18px painted circle. aria-hidden — the input carries every semantic. It is a DIRECT sibling of the input and must stay one: the focus ring is a `peer-*` utility, which compiles to a general-sibling combinator, so any wrapper around the circle stops it matching. Nothing fails when that happens — the classes resolve, `check:utilities` passes, and the ring simply never paints.
8px, `bg-current`, so it follows the control's ink through selected and disabled without a second colour rule.

The label-and-description stack, 4px apart. Namespaced rather than called `text`: data-slot is a public selector surface and these live in one document with every other component's, so a generic name is one a consumer's query catches by accident.
children. The accessible name, natively.
The optional second line. Its PRESENCE is also what the group's gap reads.
caption / danger, under the last option. Wired to every input by aria-describedby.
caption / muted. Same wiring.

docs.composition:
RadioGroup
├─ label            string (required) — the legend, and the group's name
├─ isLabelHidden?   keeps it for assistive tech, takes it off the screen
├─ name?            generated if omitted — see props.name
├─ value?           controlled, by option value
├─ defaultValue?    uncontrolled
├─ onValueChange?   (value: string) => void
├─ orientation?     "vertical" (default) | "horizontal"
├─ isDisabled?      disables every option
├─ isInvalid?       errorText implies it
├─ errorText?       string
├─ helperText?      string
└─ children         <Radio> items
   Radio
   ├─ value         string (required)
   ├─ children      ReactNode (required) — the label AND the accessible name
   ├─ description?  string
   └─ isDisabled?   this option only

label.notes: The legend. Required for the same reason every field's label is: a set of options with no question announces each one with no idea what it is an option FOR. Use `isLabelHidden` when the question is already in the surrounding copy — never drop it.

name.notes: Generated from useId when omitted, and the generated one is load-bearing: same-`name` radios are ONE group to the platform, so two groups that both defaulted to a shared literal would share arrow keys and a selection. Pass one only when a form on the server expects a particular field name.

value.notes: Controlled selection, by option value. Omit for uncontrolled; `defaultValue` sets the starting choice. Both run through the shared useControllableState hook (§4).

orientation.notes: Vertical by default. Horizontal is for two or three short options — a row of long labels makes the reader hunt for which circle belongs to which words. Vertical also steps its gap from 8 to 12 when any option carries a description, which is done with a `has-*` pair rather than a prop: the group cannot inspect its children, and a prop whose whole job is to describe the markup underneath it is the prop explosion §3 forbids.

isDisabled.notes: Set on the fieldset, so the platform disables every descendant control — the one place `disabled` cascades. Individual options take their own `isDisabled`.

errorText.notes: What is wrong, and it implies `isInvalid` so the two can never disagree. Rendered under the last option and wired to every INPUT by aria-describedby, not to the fieldset: fieldset descriptions are read inconsistently, and the input is the element that takes focus.

Radio.value.notes: What this option contributes to the group. Compared by identity against the group's value.

Radio.description.notes: A second line for an option whose consequence is not obvious from its name. Adding one switches the row to top alignment and steps the group's gap — both automatic.

do: Give every group a legend, even a hidden one. It is what turns four circles into a question.
Prefer vertical. Horizontal is for two or three short values like Active / Pending / Archived.
Use a Radio group when the options are few and worth reading at a glance; a Select when they are many.
Say what the option COSTS in the description if it is not obvious from the label.
dont: Do not render a <Radio> outside a <RadioGroup> — it throws, because a radio with no group has no name, no selection and nothing to announce.
Do not use a radio group for a yes/no. That is one Checkbox, and it is half the target area and none of the ambiguity.
Do not give two groups on one page the same explicit `name`. The platform will treat them as one set and the arrow keys will jump between them.
Do not build a 'none' option to let the reader undo a choice. A radio group cannot be unset by design; if the choice is optional, say so in the legend and add an explicit option that means it.

a11y.role: A native <fieldset> with a <legend> around native <input type="radio">. No ARIA roles are added, because none are needed — this is the pattern ARIA's radiogroup role exists to imitate.
a11y.name: Each option's name is its own label text, with the legend prepended by the platform. Nothing is set by hand.

keyboard.does: Enters the group at the selected option, or at the first when nothing is selected. One tab stop for the whole set.
Move between options AND select as they go, wrapping at the ends. The platform's behaviour for a same-name set — not re-implemented here.
Selects the focused option. Redundant with the arrows, and expected.
Leaves the group entirely rather than moving to the next option.

a11y.targetSize: The row is the target and is at least 24px tall, clearing SC 2.5.8. The circle alone would be 18 beside a 17px line — a 19px target, which is the arithmetic the min-height exists to fix.
a11y.focus: The clipped input takes focus and the painted circle shows it: --ui-focus-ring outside the edge, plus the edge itself switching to --ui-border-focus. A forced-colors outline runs alongside, because the ring is a box-shadow and forced colours flatten it away.
a11y.liveRegion: None. Selection is announced by the platform as the focused radio changes, and an error added later is picked up through aria-describedby on the input the reader is standing on.

contrastPairs.role: the unselected circle's edge — the only thing drawing the control, so it is held to the graphical floor
the hovered edge, one step further from the ground
the 8px dot on the selected fill
the option label and the legend
the per-option description and the helper text
the group's error message, and the invalid edge

contrastPairs.why: The dot inside a DISABLED selected control. It survives, because a disabled radio still has to say which option is chosen — and it measures 1.76:1 in light and 1.79:1 in dark, so it is under the graphical floor in both schemes: the surface scale puts the two values close in each (dark cleared it at 3.60:1 until the 2026-11-03 warm-ink ramp made sunken a fill above the surface). Declared rather than left out, because an unlisted pair is an unchecked pair and this one is easy to change by accident: WCAG exempts disabled controls, and the moment either token moves for another reason this row is the thing that says what it cost.

forwarding.ref: RadioGroup's ref goes to the <fieldset> — it is not itself a form control. Radio's goes to its <input>, per §5, so it can be focused, read for a value and handed to a form library.
forwarding.className: Lands on the outermost node of each: the fieldset and the option's <label>. Reach anything inside through data-slot.
forwarding.rest: Native fieldset props go to the fieldset; native input props (name excepted — the group owns it) go to the input.

docs.motion: The circle transitions `background-color`, `border-color` and `box-shadow` at --ui-duration-fast with --ui-ease-out — the micro recipe, identical to Checkbox's box. The dot is not separately animated: it is present or it is not, so the selection is readable the instant it changes rather than a frame later.
needsDesign: Hover, focus and disabled are taken from Checkbox rather than drawn on the sheet. They are consistent by construction rather than by decision, and if Checkbox's are ever redrawn these move with them.

No pressed state, on either this or Checkbox. A fill step on an 18px control that flips instantly is not something anybody sees — recorded rather than invented, so the next sheet does not re-derive it.
One size, because Checkbox has one and the pair has to align in a shared column. If a size axis is ever wanted it is Checkbox's to add first, and this follows.

The label-to-description gap is `space-xs` 4, where the sheet drew 2px. 2 is off the 4px scale and the scale has no step below xs; 4 is the nearest legal value and reads the same at 13/12. Confirm, or add a 2px step.
knownGaps: A wrapped label centres against the circle instead of aligning to its first line — unless the option has a description, which switches the row to top alignment and fixes it. Checkbox records the identical defect and has no equivalent escape. Two components asking for one fix.
No indeterminate equivalent, and there should not be one: a set where nothing is chosen is the resting state of every radio group, not a third value.
The group cannot be cleared once a choice is made, which is the platform's behaviour and not a decision made here. An optional question needs an explicit option that means 'none'.

the hovered edge, one step further from the ground
the 8px dot on the selected fill
the option label and the legend
the per-option description and the helper text

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

Checkbox, Radio and Switch draw their checked/selected look from the native input's :checked (peer-checked:) rather than from React state, so they work as plain form controls on a statically rendered page and before hydration (#34). The check glyph and radio dot are always in the DOM and revealed by the same selector. Checkbox's indeterminate state is still render-time (it has no HTML attribute).

The GROUP is the component and the option is its item: RadioGroup owns the legend, the shared name, the selection and the error, and a <Radio> outside one throws rather than rendering something nobody can name. A real fieldset around real radio inputs, so arrow-key navigation, the single tab stop, form participation and the legend-as-part-of-every-name come from the platform and nothing is reached for. Checkbox's geometry with a circle and a dot — 18px control, 1px edge, 8px dot, 24px row — asserted as a RELATIONSHIP against Checkbox in the browser test rather than as numbers on each, so the pair cannot drift apart while both suites stay green. Carries a geometry spec: two cases, the options run and the control, which takes design-spec coverage from one item to two.

items.name: range-slider
items.title: RangeSlider
items.lead: Sets the lower and upper ends of a range.

docs.lead: Sets the lower and upper ends of a range.
docs.name: RangeSlider
docs.summary: Two thumbs on one track; the fill is the span between them. A filter for 'from what, to what' — years, prices, sizes. Everything visible is Slider's — the same track ladder and the same thumb, read from Slider's own geometry table — while three things differ: the value is a pair, each thumb is its own named input, and the thumbs may meet but never cross. Base UI Slider underneath (ADR 0012).

anatomy.notes: The group, and where className lands — named so an effect or a test can reach a part from it (ADR 0022). Before 2026-11-06 this slot named the header row, and the root had none.
The row above the track holding the label and the readout; carries data-size.
Names the GROUP. body-sm, --ui-text-muted.
Both ends with a spaced en dash — "1925 – 1972" — tabular figures, --ui-text-primary. Equal ends collapse to one number. On by default.
Slider's control, character for character: padded to the 24px target at sm/md and inset by half a thumb, so both thumbs' outer edges land on the control's edges at the extremes.
--ui-bg-sunken; Slider's heights and radii by size.

FLAT --ui-bg-accent between the thumbs' centres, square at both ends (they run under the thumbs). Flat because a span has no direction — the gradient says 'more toward the end', which is true of one value and not of an interval. It is the gradient's own first stop.

Two of Slider's thumb, data-end="start" | "end". Each holds its own input[type=range]. The thumb being moved, or hovered, lifts to --ui-shadow-md — only that one — and Base UI paints it above the other.
The label row: label and readout.

docs.composition:
RangeSlider
├─ label                 string (required) — names the group
├─ startThumbLabel       string (required) — names thumb 1
├─ endThumbLabel         string (required) — names thumb 2
├─ value? / defaultValue?   readonly [number, number]
├─ onValueChange?        (value: readonly [number, number]) => void
├─ min? / max? / step?
├─ minStepsBetweenValues? number, default 0
├─ formatValue?          (value: number) => string — per end
├─ hasValueText?         boolean, default true
├─ size?                 sm | md | lg | xl — Slider's ladder
└─ valueControl?         ReactElement — e.g. two Input sm

label.notes: Names the group (aria-labelledby on the root).

startThumbLabel.notes: REQUIRED by the type. Each thumb is its own input and needs its own name — 'Earliest year'. Written as aria-label: an aria-labelledby would outrank it and name both thumbs after the group.

value.notes: Controlled. A tuple, not number[]: there are exactly two thumbs, and the type says so.

defaultValue.notes: Uncontrolled starting pair — the full range unless given.

minStepsBetweenValues.notes: How close the thumbs may get, in steps. They may meet but never cross: a dragged thumb stops at the other rather than pushing it (Base UI's default) or swapping. Pushing moves a value the user was not touching.

formatValue.notes: One END as text, applied to each. The readout joins them with ' – '; each thumb's aria-valuetext is its own end. Without it the ends use the locale's number format — pass String for years, or 1925 reads '1,925'.

hasValueText.notes: On by default, unlike Slider: a range with no readout cannot be read without dragging both ends. Turn it off only when a valueControl shows the ends.

size.notes: Slider's track ladder (8/16/24/32), read from the same table.

valueControl.notes: Slot under the track, never wrapped (§3). The sheet composes two Input sm fields with an en dash between, sharing the slider's state both ways (story: WithFields).

isDisabled.notes: As Slider: --ui-text-disabled, the fill --ui-bg-field-chrome-disabled, both rings --ui-border-subtle with no shadow.

do: Name both thumbs for what they bound — 'Earliest year' / 'Latest year', 'Minimum price' / 'Maximum price'.
Pass formatValue whenever the locale's number format is wrong for the quantity — years, currencies, units.
Format the full range as the filter it is ('Any year') when that is what it means.
dont: Do not use a RangeSlider for one value with a tolerance — that is a Slider and a field.
Do not hide the readout unless a valueControl shows both ends.

a11y.role: A group (the root, aria-labelledby the label) holding TWO sliders — each thumb renders a native input[type=range], so the role is implicit and the keyboard behaviour is the platform's.
a11y.name: Each input is named by its own aria-label (startThumbLabel / endThumbLabel), never by the group's label: Base UI falls back to the group's label only when a thumb has none, and two thumbs named alike announce as 'slider, slider'.
a11y.value: aria-valuenow is each thumb's own end; formatValue becomes that thumb's aria-valuetext. Announced as 'Earliest year, slider, 1925'.
a11y.focus: The ring draws on the focused thumb only, keyed off :has(:focus-visible) because the input inside the thumb is what takes focus.

keyboard.does: Start thumb, then end thumb.
Move the focused thumb by `step`; it stops at the other thumb (plus minStepsBetweenValues). Asserted in Chromium.

keyboard.key: Shift + Arrow / Page Up / Page Down
keyboard.does: Move by ten steps, with the same stop.
The focused thumb's own reachable ends.

a11y.pointer: A press on the bare track moves the NEAREST thumb there; a dragged thumb stops at the other one. Both asserted in Chromium — the drag is the only path that reaches the collision rule, because Base UI clamps key presses whatever the rule is.
a11y.target: As Slider: the control is padded to 24px where the track is thinner.

contrastPairs.role: each thumb's ring against the track — the thumbs identify the control and mark both ends
each thumb's ring against its own white fill

contrastPairs.why: The span fill: 1.24:1 on the track in light — the same pale accent as Slider's ramp start, a secondary cue. The thumbs carry SC 1.4.11 (the pairs above) and the readout states both ends as text.

contrastPairs.role: the readout
the label

needsDesign: Dark: the ring (--ui-bg-accent-legible = #9EDBF3) is the same colour as the span fill, so over the fill the ring disappears and each thumb is read by its body — #171411 on #9EDBF3, 12.1:1 (re-measured on the 2026-11-03 warm-ink dark ramp). Passes; recorded so nobody 'fixes' the ring.
Hover on the control as a whole is not drawn for a range — only the moving thumb lifts. Shipped as the hovered or moving thumb lifting alone.
knownGaps: No tabular figures: Aspekta ships no `tnum` feature and its digits are proportional (367–602 units), so `tabular-nums` is a no-op in this face — figures right-align on their last digit but do not line up digit by digit, and a figure that changes in place changes width. Filed against the face (ADR 0011 item 5); pinned by registry/fonts/aspekta/aspekta.test.ts.
No histogram over the track (the price-filter pattern) and no tick marks. Neither is drawn.
No steppers: two pairs of −/+ beside one track has no drawn layout.
No inline variant — the bar has room for one value.

The sheet draws 'From' / 'To' prefixes INSIDE the two fields. Input has no text-prefix slot (only an icon), so the composed fields are named by visually-hidden labels instead. A prefix slot is Input's gap, not this component's.
docs.motion: Each thumb transitions box-shadow at --ui-duration-fast with --ui-ease-out — the hover/drag lift and the focus ring settling. Positions are never transitioned; the thumbs and the span track the pointer and the keys directly.

contrast.role: each thumb's ring against the track — the thumbs identify the control and mark both ends
each thumb's ring against its own white fill
the readout
the label

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

ADR 0011 item 5 checked: Aspekta ships no `tnum` feature and its default digits are proportional (367–602 units), so `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` is a no-op wherever the library uses it. Figures still right-align on their last digit; they do not line up digit by digit, and a figure that changes in place (tooltip, meter reading, slider readout) changes width. Filed against the face as ADR 0011 directs, not answered with a second family. Chart, ChartCard, StatTiles, Meter, Table and RangeSlider list the gap; registry/fonts/aspekta/aspekta.test.ts pins the measurement and fails when a font update adds the feature. No code or visual change.

RangeSlider's ROOT now carries data-slot="range-slider", matching Slider (ADR 0022); the header row that held that slot name is data-slot="range-slider-header". Kept parallel with Slider so the two controls cannot be targeted differently.

migration.manual: A selector or test that targeted the header row by [data-slot="range-slider"] now targets [data-slot="range-slider-header"]; [data-slot="range-slider"] now matches the whole control.

changes.summary: New item range-slider: two thumbs on one track, the fill the flat --ui-bg-accent span between them. Everything visible is Slider's, read from Slider's own SLIDER_SIZE table and thumb class, and the browser test compares the two per size so they cannot drift. Three things differ: the value is a readonly [number, number] tuple; each thumb is its own input named by a REQUIRED startThumbLabel / endThumbLabel (aria-label — an aria-labelledby would outrank it); and the thumbs may meet but never cross (thumbCollisionBehavior none, minStepsBetweenValues). Only the moving or hovered thumb lifts. The readout (on by default) joins formatValue's ends with a spaced en dash and collapses equal ends. Probed: the drag test fails with Base UI's default `push` (end thumb shoved to 1990); the keyboard path cannot see the collision rule at all. Paper: https://app.paper.design/file/01KZ39A2BC286MT85M658NRR4R/p-Z-0 (Component --- Slider --- Revision / Variants / Dark / API, Behaviour, Tokens, Gaps).

items.name: select
items.title: Select
items.lead: Chooses a value from a list.

docs.lead: Chooses a value from a list.
docs.name: Select
docs.summary: Choose ONE value from a list. The trigger is Input's control surface, exactly as Multiselect's is — a field is a field, and three components inventing three variants of the same box is how a system stops looking like one. Listbox ARIA, typeahead, roving focus and dismissal come from the Base UI behaviour layer (ADR 0012), wrapped so no third-party type reaches a public prop signature.

anatomy.notes: The field column: label, trigger, then error and helper text.
Names the trigger via aria-labelledby. sr-only when isLabelHidden, never removed.

Input's control surface at all three sizes, value type included — asserted as a relationship, not as numbers. The size map is the ONLY thing on the trigger that names a type role; a hard-coded text-body-md after it used to win the merge and render md and sm at 14px (#16).
The chosen label, or the placeholder in placeholder ink.
The chevron. Decorative — the trigger's name comes from the label.
radius-md over a 4px inset around radius-sm rows — concentric exactly, 4 + 4 = 8 (§6). bg-surface, a 1px edge, shadow-md. Capped to --available-height and scrolls internally (§7c).

p-md, radius-sm when highlighted or selected — a touch target as well as a line of text. With a description it is named by its label (aria-labelledby) and described by the second line (aria-describedby).
The label-over-description stack, 4px apart — Radio's.
The optional second line: caption in muted ink (disabled ink on a disabled row). Wraps rather than truncates. Rendered in the popup only, never in the trigger.
The tick on the chosen row.

docs.composition:
Select   label (required) / isLabelHidden?
         items (required)  { value, label, description?, isDisabled? }[]
                           description → a muted second line in the popup row only
         value? / defaultValue? / onValueChange?
         placeholder? / size? / isDisabled?
         helperText? / errorText? / container?

label.notes: Required — a placeholder is not a label. It disappears the moment a value is chosen, taking the field's name with it (§10).

items.notes: { value, label, description?, isDisabled? }. The VALUE is what onValueChange reports; the label is for people. `description` is a second, muted line under the label in the open list — what choosing the option means, for a list where the label does not say (a role, a plan, a permission). It never appears in the trigger, and it is wired as the option's accessible description rather than run into its name.

value.notes: Controlled. null means nothing is chosen.

onValueChange.notes: One callback (§1). Reports the value, never the label — returning the label would make every consumer map it back.

placeholder.notes: What the box shows while empty. NOT the accessible name.

size.notes: 48 / 40 / 32px with a 14 / 14 / 12px value — Input's sizes and Input's type steps, because it is Input's surface. md was 12px in the map and rendered 14 anyway, until #16 put the step in the map alone and moved the whole field family's md to body-md.

errorText.notes: Its presence sets aria-invalid and the danger edge, so the two cannot drift apart.

helperText.notes: Persistent guidance. Announced alongside an error rather than replaced by it.

container.notes: Where the panel is portalled. Theme tokens are INHERITED custom properties, so a panel in the body leaves any brand scope. See sheet.doc.ts.

do: Give every Select a label; the trigger is otherwise anonymous.
Use it for one value out of a known list — reach for Multiselect when more than one can be chosen.
Mark unavailable options with isDisabled rather than filtering them out, so the list stays stable between renders.
Give options a description when the choice is a permission or a plan — say what it grants or costs, in one line.
dont: Do not use a placeholder as the label. It is gone as soon as someone chooses.
Do not convey the chosen row by fill alone — the highlighted row already owns a fill, and colour alone is WCAG 1.4.1. Selection is a tick and a weight.
Do not import Base UI types into your own props — `check:boundaries` fails the build (ADR 0002).
Do not put the description into the label ("Viewer — read only"): it then appears in the trigger and is announced as part of the name.

a11y.role: A button trigger paired with a listbox (from Base UI), with one option per item and the chosen one marked.
a11y.name: The `label` prop via aria-labelledby. errorText and helperText are wired through aria-describedby together. An option with a description is named by its label alone (aria-labelledby on the option) and described by the second line (aria-describedby) — without the labelledby, its name would be computed from the whole row and the description read twice.

keyboard.does: Opens the list from the trigger.
Moves through the options; disabled ones are skipped.
Jumps to the option starting with what you type.
Closes and RESTORES FOCUS to the trigger. Asserted in Chromium.

a11y.focus: Focus returns to the trigger on dismiss — falling to <body> is the classic hand-rolled-listbox failure.

contrastPairs.role: the chosen value in the trigger
the placeholder
an option in the panel
the highlighted option
an option's description
the highlighted option's description

needsDesign: The sheet draws the trigger at px-lg (16) where Input's control is px-md (12). Shipped as Input's, because the whole claim is that a field is a field — confirm which wins.

The panel ships at a 4px inset where the sheet draws 8, so that §6 closes: radius-md (8) over 4px around radius-sm (4) rows is 4 + 4 = 8 exactly. The sheet's own three numbers do not close — 4 + 8 wants a 12px outer radius and the scale has no 12px step. Of the three, the inset carries the least meaning, so it moved and both radii are the sheet's. Bring Paper in line, or say which of the other two should move instead.

The highlighted row is drawn as the palette step --ui-neutral-95 rather than a role. Shipped as bg-hover, the interaction role, because a surface role used as an interaction state is the wrong-category signal the token layer exists to catch. It is one step stronger than drawn.
Row GVO-0 is drawn py-lg px-md where the sheet's other three rows and both of Multiselect's are a uniform p-md. Shipped as p-md, following the majority.
No option GROUPS are drawn, though Base UI supports them.

The option description (#26) is not drawn. Shipped as Radio's description — caption, text-muted, 4px under the label, wrapping — so a second line means one thing across the library. Draw a two-line row on the sheet, at rest, highlighted, selected and disabled.
knownGaps: No search or filtering inside the list — that is Multiselect's combobox, and a searchable single-select would be a third component.

No option groups and no icons in a row. A per-option description is supported (#26) but is DERIVED — the sheet draws a flat list of labels; the second line follows Radio's description (caption, muted, 4px under the label).
The panel does not re-skin under a brand scope without `container` — the portal-theming gap shared with Modal, Popover, Sheet and Drawer.
docs.motion: The trigger transitions `border-color` and `box-shadow`; the list fades and scales from 98% through `data-[starting-style]`/`data-[ending-style]`. Both at --ui-duration-fast with --ui-ease-out. `scale` is named in the transition list — Tailwind v4 writes it standalone.

the placeholder
an option in the panel
the highlighted option
an option's description
the highlighted option's description

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

Closes #26. `SelectItem` takes an optional `description`: a second, muted line under the label in the open list, never in the trigger. A permission picker is the case — service-portal's team-role Select lost what each role grants (Brand Admin: full access…) when it moved onto the registry Select, which drew a flat list of labels. The option is NAMED by its label (aria-labelledby on the option) and DESCRIBED by the second line (aria-describedby). The labelledby is not optional: an option's name is otherwise computed from its whole content, so the description would be read inside the name and then again as the description. The line follows Radio's description — caption, text-muted, 4px under the label, text-disabled on a disabled row — and wraps rather than truncates, since a permission cut off mid-sentence loses the half that matters. Typeahead is pinned to the label through Base UI's `label` prop. New parts `select-option-text` and `select-option-description`; contrast pairs text-muted on bg-surface (5.78 / 6.47) and on bg-hover (4.87 / 5.35) declared. Derived, not drawn: recorded in needsDesign. New WithDescriptions story; browser tests assert the description is in the popup row and absent from the trigger before and after choosing, the option's labelledby and describedby resolve to the label and the description, and an option without one carries neither attribute.

Closes #16. A field's value at md is now body-md (14px) in Input, Textarea, Select and Multiselect, where it was caption (12px); lg stays body-md and sm stays caption. Two defects, one decision. First, Select's trigger, and Multiselect's, ignored their size map for text: `SIZE[size]` carried the caption step, then a hard-coded `text-body-md` on the next line won the merge, so every Select rendered 14px at every size while the Input beside it rendered 12 at md and sm. The boxes matched (40px at md), so the geometry relationship test passed for the bug's whole life; only the text inside differed. The hard-coded class is gone and the map is the only thing on either trigger that names a type role. Second, the direction: the maintainer decided md settles at 14px, not 12, because the owner's Paper frames draw every 40px field value at body-md, and service-portal had to patch `[data-slot="control"][data-size="md"]` to get there. sm stays caption because the field tokens carry no type step at all (ADR 0020 §4 keeps type out of density), so the map is the only authority, and a 14px value's 21.7px line in a compact 28px field leaves 3px of block padding. Textarea's md box is now lg's box (127px at 6 rows) with the narrower inline inset. DatePicker draws lg only and does not change. Select's and Multiselect's browser tests now compare the VALUE's font-size and line-height to a real Input's at every size; both fail against the old trigger (probed). Deliberate visual change: the `select` matrix baseline moves (its md and sm rows) and the `textarea` baseline moves (its md row), light and dark, darwin and linux. The input, multiselect and date-picker cases draw lg only and do not move for this. Weight is NOT yet one relationship: Input's value is font-medium (500) at every size, while Select, Multiselect, DatePicker and Textarea take their role's weight (body-md 400, caption 600), so a Select at sm now renders 600 where it rendered 400. Recorded for a maintainer decision rather than changed here.

migration.manual: Remove any local override that forced field text to one size (for example a rule on [data-slot="control"][data-size="md"] setting body-md); md renders body-md on its own now. A form that relied on Select rendering 14px at sm will see 12px there, matching Input; pass size="md" if you meant the larger value.

changes.summary: Select, Multiselect and DatePicker filled a disabled trigger with `bg-sunken`, a surface role standing in for a state, which ADR 0017 §3 forbids and which Input and Textarea dropped when that ADR landed. It only looked right because the two values happened to be close. When #24 moved the dark field ground, a disabled Select (#282522) and a disabled Input (#3d3a37) beside it stopped matching. All three triggers now take `bg-field-disabled`, Input's page-ground disabled fill. Light is unchanged, because sunken and field-disabled resolve to the same value there (#EDE8E3). Select's browser test asserts the disabled fill equals Input's in both schemes and fails against the old class.

check:motion joins the gate list, and every animating component now documents its motion. The gate rejects a literal duration or easing in registry/ (a discipline that was already perfect — zero hard-coded durations across 26 files — and had nothing keeping it that way), transition-all (CONVENTIONS section 6 has said this since the beginning and nothing enforced it), a keyframe with no reduced-motion guard, and an animating component with no top-level motion: note in its doc. It reads lib recipes alongside components as check:overlays does, so Header's motion is found in @/lib/chrome-control where it actually lives rather than reported as absent. 27 doc files gain a motion: note describing what moves, what drives it and what reduced motion does to it; Sheet's and ImageUpload's existing notes are PROMOTED out of a11y to the top level, where Button already had its, because motion is a description of what a component does rather than solely an accessibility concern and a field meaning one thing at two depths stops being findable. ImageUpload's note is corrected while being promoted: it credited the token layer with stopping its spinner, and what actually stops it is the motion-safe: variant. Two findings are recorded in the notes rather than fixed: Sidebar's collapsible section snaps via the hidden attribute where Accordion animates the identical interaction against Base UI's published height, and Banner reaches for transition-colors where the rest of the library enumerates properties. No component's rendered motion changes; no .tsx is touched.

migration.manual: Documentation only — every change is inside a *.doc.ts, and no component's classes or rendered motion moved. If you consume the doc files and read `a11y.motion`, it has moved to the top-level `motion` key on Sheet and ImageUpload; Button was already there and the other 27 are new.

changes.summary: The residual concentricity gap in Select's and Multiselect's menus is closed. §6 is an equation — outerRadius = innerRadius + padding — and the sheets' own three numbers do not satisfy it: radius-md (8) over an 8px inset around radius-sm (4) rows wants a 12px outer radius, and the scale has no 12px step. Rather than invent a token, the INSET moved from 8 to 4, so 4 + 4 = 8 closes exactly using only steps that already exist. That is the minimal deviation available: of the three numbers two are radii the sheet states deliberately and one is padding, which carries the least meaning, so the padding is what gives. Multiselect's search field takes the same 4px inset, making it concentric on the same arithmetic as the rows. The regression test asserts the EQUATION rather than three pinned numbers — pinning 8/4/4 separately would pass while all three moved consistently-but-wrongly, and would need rewriting by hand every time the design shifts, which is precisely the edit where someone corrects the expectation to match the code and loses the rule. Probed by restoring the 8px inset: 'outer 8 != inner 4 + inset 8: expected 8 to be 12'. Paper still draws the 8px inset and now disagrees with the code by one value; the doc asks design to bring the file in line or to say which of the other two numbers should move instead.

Select ships: choose one value from a list, built on the Base UI behaviour layer (ADR 0012) for listbox ARIA, typeahead, roving focus and dismissal, wrapped so no third-party type reaches a public prop signature. Its trigger is Input's control surface at all three sizes — the browser test renders a Select beside an Input and compares COMPUTED height, radius, border width, edge colour, fill and inset, because asserting 48px on each would pass while the two drifted apart, and drifting apart is the only failure that matters. Selection is shown by a tick AND a weight, never by fill alone: the highlighted row already owns a fill, so a selected fill would be two states competing for one channel, and colour alone is WCAG 1.4.1 regardless. The panel's enter transition is asserted through el.getAnimations() rather than transitionProperty, which reads identically in the working and broken versions — the trap that let Modal and Popover ship a dead entrance. One design gap recorded rather than silently resolved: the sheet draws the trigger at px-lg where Input's control is px-md, and it shipped as Input's, because the whole claim is that a field is a field.

Select's and Multiselect's menus were rebuilt against the sheets (EVQ-0, J2X-0) after both read as un-concentric. Both shipped a radius-lg (16px) panel: Select's over a 4px inset around radius-sm rows, Multiselect's likewise. A 16px corner cannot sit 4px outside a 4px one, and §6 says so — outer = inner + padding. The sheets draw radius-md (8) over an 8px inset, which is what both now use. Select's rows go from px-md py-lg to a uniform p-md, following the three rows in the sheet that agree rather than the one that does not (GVO-0 is the outlier; both of Multiselect's rows are uniform too). Multiselect's search field takes the drawn 40px height, radius-sm and px-lg in place of an invented 32px radius-md. Two things were deliberately NOT transcribed and are recorded as design questions instead: the highlighted row is drawn as the raw palette step --ui-neutral-95 and ships as `bg-hover`, because a surface role used as an interaction state is the wrong-category signal the token layer exists to catch; and the result is still not exactly concentric — 8 over an 8px inset around 4 wants a 12px outer radius, and no 12px radius token exists. Closing that means either radius-lg over a 12px inset, which is exact with the tokens that exist, or a new step. The arithmetic is in the doc so it stays a decision rather than becoming a drift.

items.name: sheet
items.title: Sheet
items.lead: Opens a panel from the side without losing the page behind it.

docs.lead: Opens a panel from the side without losing the page behind it.
docs.name: Sheet
docs.summary: A panel that slides in from the LEFT or RIGHT edge of the screen — the mobile counterpart to a Sidebar, which is what it usually holds. Third component on the Base UI behaviour layer, and deliberately Modal's shape: the focus trap, scroll lock, Escape and focus restoration are the same problem, and only the panel's position differs. Sheet and Drawer are DIFFERENT components here, following shadcn/ui: a Sheet is edge-anchored and dismissed by scrim or Escape; a Drawer comes up from the bottom with a drag handle and is dismissed by dragging. Reaching for one when you want the other is the most common mix-up in this pair.

anatomy.notes: The control that opens it — a hamburger, usually. Pass your own element via `render`; never wrapped.

The backdrop. --ui-scrim, a scheme-only role: a warm 16% veil in light, a heavier black in dark. The design drew this as a raw #98918A29, which is the same value. It is the ONLY thing separating the panel from the page — 1.16:1 in light, 1.61:1 in dark.

The drawer. Full height, 80% of the viewport floored at 256 and capped by `size`, bg-base with --ui-shadow-md — the value the sheet draws, approved 2026-08-25 over Modal's shadow-sm. No padding of its own — every inset belongs to a region inside. Carries data-side, data-size and data-overflow-top/bottom, and is the `group/sheet` the hairlines key off.

The 48px chrome band. p-sm uniform, justify-between — the same 48px as Header's bar, so the band and the bar it covers sit at one height, and 8 plus a 32px chrome control's own 8 puts the glyph on the body's 16px lane. Pinned. Optional, and absent from the navigation composition where Sidebar.Group is already that band.

body-lg / bold / one line, clipped — Drawer.Title's values exactly, from the same drawing. It sits at the TOP OF THE BODY, not in the band: at the band's 8px inset a text node would miss the body's 16px lane by exactly 8. Renders Base UI's Dialog.Title, so it wins the accessible name.

The content region, inset space-lg, and the only part that scrolls — it takes the slack the header and footer leave. A named tab stop with a visible ring WHILE it scrolls and not otherwise (SC 2.1.1); carries data-scrollable.

The action region, inset space-lg. Buttons STACK full width — Drawer's footer, not Modal's justify-between row, because a panel this narrow has no room for two side by side. 104px with two md buttons: 16 + 32 + 8 + 32 + 16. Pinned.
Any control that dismisses. Takes an element via `render`. Never rendered for you.

docs.composition:
Sheet                     isOpen? / defaultIsOpen? / onOpenChange? / isDismissable?
├─ Sheet.Trigger          render={<Button isIconOnly aria-label="Open menu" icon={<Menu />} />}
└─ Sheet.Panel            label (required) / side? / size? / container? / initialFocus? / finalFocus?
   ├─ Sheet.Header        the 48px chrome band — chromeControls, never a Title
   │  └─ Sheet.Close      render={<Button isIconOnly aria-label="Close" icon={<Close />} />}
   ├─ Sheet.Body          the only region that scrolls
   │  └─ Sheet.Title      first child of the Body, not of the band
   └─ Sheet.Footer        actions, stacked full width

Or, for the navigation composition, no regions at all:

Sheet
├─ Sheet.Trigger
└─ Sheet.Panel            label (required) — size defaults to sm, the rail's width
   └─ Sidebar             className="h-full w-full rounded-none"
      └─ Sheet.Close      inside Sidebar.Group, which IS the 48px band

label.notes: On Panel. Required — a dialog with no accessible name is announced as 'dialog' and nothing else. There is no Sheet.Title part IN CODE yet; the design draws one (see knownGaps), and until it lands a visible heading is ordinary content the caller supplies. When Title arrives, `label` stays required as it is on Drawer, and the two must say the same thing: aria-labelledby beats aria-label when both are present.

size.notes: On Panel. The width CAP, not a width: the panel is 80% of the viewport, floored at 256 and capped here. sm is --ui-nav-width (272), md is --ui-dialog-width-md (416) and lg is --ui-dialog-width-lg (640) — three width tokens that already existed, so a Sheet and a Modal holding the same form are the same width. It defaults to sm because that IS the geometry Sheet shipped before the axis existed; reach for md whenever the panel is not holding the navigation rail.

side.notes: Which edge it slides from. Only the two INNER corners are rounded — a fully rounded panel leaves four slivers of scrim in the screen corners, which reads as a modal rather than a drawer. `top` (#33, a site's collapsed menu) is FULL SCREEN: flush on all four edges, no rounding, no width cap (`size` does not apply), sliding down from above. It is not a bottom sheet turned over — that is Drawer, whose contract is the gesture; `top` has no gesture and is dismissed by Close or Escape like the other sides.

initialFocus.notes: On Panel. Where focus lands when the panel opens. The default is the first tabbable element inside it, which in the record-panel composition is Previous, not Close, because the band carries Previous/Next first. Pass Close's ref to land there. A function is called at open time; returning null, or a ref that is still empty, keeps the default instead of dropping focus. Restated in our own type (SheetFocusTarget) rather than Base UI's, which also takes booleans and an interaction type: `false` would leave focus behind the scrim, and that is not a choice this component offers.

finalFocus.notes: On Panel. Where focus goes when the panel closes. The default is the trigger, or whatever was focused before the panel opened. Set it when that element will be gone, for example a row deleted from inside the panel, so focus lands somewhere real rather than on <body>. Same fallback rule as initialFocus.

isOpen.notes: Controlled. Omit and the sheet owns it.

onOpenChange.notes: One callback for both directions (§1). Narrowed from Base UI's signature so no third-party type reaches ours.

isDismissable.notes: Escape and scrim-tap dismiss. On by default: a drawer is a navigation surface, and tapping outside to leave is the gesture every phone user already has. Turning it off cancels those two reasons only — an explicit Sheet.Close still works, or the panel could not be closed at all.

container.notes: Where the panel is portalled. Theme tokens are INHERITED custom properties, so a panel in the body leaves any brand scope on a wrapper and paints theme zero — pass the themed element and it inherits again. A prop rather than something resolved automatically, because the container becomes the panel's containing block: an ancestor with a transform or overflow:hidden would clip a full-height fixed drawer, and only the caller knows whether theirs is safe.

render.notes: On Trigger and Close. Passed through, not wrapped (§3), so the element keeps its tag, ref and accessible name and gains only the ARIA wiring.

do: Open the sheet from the edge its TRIGGER sits on: a menu button in Header.End takes side="right". A drawer that flies in from the opposite edge to the control the user just pressed breaks the connection between them, and `side` defaults to left, so a right-hand trigger has to say so.
Give every Sheet a label; it is the dialog's entire accessible name.
Put a Sidebar inside with className="w-full rounded-none" — the rail's own w-nav and rounded-lg are meant for a docked rail, and the panel already provides both.
Put the close control inside the header band — Sidebar.Group in the navigation composition, Sheet.Header everywhere else. There is no automatic close button, so it is never rendered for you.

Put Sheet.Title at the top of Sheet.Body, never inside Sheet.Header. The band is inset 8 so a 32px chrome control's glyph lands on the body's 16px lane; a text node at that same 8 misses the lane by exactly 8.
Use size="md" for anything that is not the navigation rail. The default is sm because that is what the component already shipped, not because it is the common case.
Use side="right" for a panel that belongs to a trailing action, and left for primary navigation.
dont: Do not use a Sheet on desktop for something a Popover or Modal would do — it covers 80% of the screen for a reason.

Do not add a second header band on top of the navigation's own. Inside the rail composition Sidebar.Group already IS the 48px band at the same p-sm inset, so a Sheet.Header there would compete with it.
Do not put a Button in Sheet.Header where the design draws chrome. A 32px fill with no edge is page chrome, not one of the five button types (§7b) — `chromeControl` is the recipe.
Do not nest a Sheet in a Sheet. A drawer that opens a drawer is a step in a flow, not a layer.
Do not import Base UI types into your own props — `check:boundaries` fails the build (ADR 0002).

a11y.role: dialog, modal (from Base UI). The page behind is inert and does not scroll while open.
a11y.name: The `label` prop as aria-label, and `Sheet.Title` as aria-labelledby when there is one. BOTH are set and aria-labelledby wins, so two that disagree announce the Title and leave `label` silently unused — asserted in the browser suite, in both directions.

keyboard.does: Opens from the trigger — native, since the trigger is a real button.
Closes when isDismissable, and RESTORES FOCUS to the trigger. Asserted in Chromium.
Cycles within the panel only; focus cannot reach the page behind.
Reaches the scroll region — but ONLY while it actually scrolls, so a panel whose content fits has no silent tab stop in it. Arrow keys and Page Up/Down then scroll it (SC 2.1.1).

a11y.focus: Focus moves into the panel on open and returns to the trigger on close. Both asserted in a real browser — focus falling to <body> is the classic hand-rolled-drawer failure. `initialFocus` and `finalFocus` on the Panel move either end deliberately; both are asserted too, against the default they replace.

contrastPairs.role: content on the panel

needsDesign: DARK PANEL EDGE (2026-11-03, the warm-ink ramp). The panel and the page are both --ui-bg-base, and in dark the black-at-55% scrim now leaves only a 1.08:1 step between them (1.61:1 on the old mid-grey page); --ui-shadow-md is inked in the page colour, so it adds little. Drawer and Modal, drawn as the same family, both carry a --ui-border-subtle hairline beside shadow-md and Sheet does not. An inset hairline on the panel's open edge (Header draws its affixed edge the same way, so it costs no geometry) measures 1.45:1 against the dimmed page — but it also adds an edge to the approved LIGHT panel. Decide whether Sheet joins Drawer and Modal.

NOT SHEET'S — it belongs to the interaction ramp and `registry/lib/chrome-control`, which has no doc of its own (the dark half of this note closed 2026-11-03; see knownGaps). --ui-bg-hover and --ui-bg-sunken are the SAME value in light, so a hovered band control and a disabled one paint an identical fill and only the ink separates them, at 15.53:1 and 1.76:1. Tolerable here, since a disabled control cannot enter hover and the two are never adjacent. The number worth acting on is the wider one: SIX --ui-bg-* roles resolve to #EDE8E3 in light — sunken, muted, hover, selected, field-disabled and field-chrome — so any two of them meeting on one surface are indistinguishable, and the hover/selected collision already recorded in the design-component skill is one case of six rather than a pair. Dark separates all six.
knownGaps: CLOSED 2026-11-03 by the warm-ink dark ramp (ADR 0008 amendment): in dark the band control's ramp used to cross the panel it sits on — rest and hover darker than the mid-grey bg-base, pressed lighter. On the new ramp all three step up from the page in order: rest 1.24, hover 1.30, pressed 1.38.

BUILT 2026-08-25 from `Component --- Sheet`: Header, Title, Body, Footer and the sm/md/lg width axis. Two things the drawing had to give up on contact with the browser, both recorded here rather than left to be re-derived. (1) The pinned hairlines are an INSET BOX-SHADOW, not the border the sheet named. `h-12` is a border-box height, so a border-b takes its pixel out of the 32px content lane and `items-center` pays it back as 7.5 above and 8.5 below — the Tabs defect exactly. A box-shadow costs no layout, so the band keeps a true uniform 8px inset, which the geometry spec now proves. Header's principle is kept: always declared, only the colour changes. (2) Sheet.Body needed a keyboard path nothing had drawn — see the next entry.

Sheet.Body is a named tab stop with a visible ring ONLY while it actually scrolls (SC 2.1.1), which is Table's rule in the other axis. Nothing drew it: a body holding static text has no focusable child to scroll it into view, and making it unconditionally focusable puts a silent tab stop in front of every panel whose content fits. The name is the panel's own `label`, which is why that prop lives on the Panel rather than being duplicated.

No top or bottom side, where shadcn's Sheet has all four. §7a splits the pair on the GESTURE: a Drawer carries a handle, follows the finger and closes past a velocity threshold, so a bottom Sheet would be a Drawer that cannot be dragged. This is the one thing a consumer arriving from shadcn will reach for and not find.
No swipe-to-dismiss. It needs a gesture layer the system does not have, and it must never be the only way to close (SC 2.5.7).

No automatic close button, so no showCloseButton prop to turn one off. In the navigation composition the close belongs to Sidebar's own group and a second would compete with it; elsewhere the caller places it in the band. A control the component renders and the caller has to suppress is a control in the wrong place twice.

No Description part, where Modal and shadcn both have one. No drawing shows a paragraph under a sheet's title and Drawer has none either, so Sheet follows its nearer sibling. Add it when a design needs it rather than for symmetry.

DECIDED 2026-08-25: the panel takes --ui-shadow-md, the value the sheet draws and the one Drawer ships from the same drawing, rather than Modal's shadow-sm. It is doing real work rather than decorating — the panel and the page are BOTH --ui-bg-base, so in light the scrim leaves only a 1.16:1 step between them and a single 0.5px blur does not close it. Dark reaches 1.61:1 on its own, because that scrim is black at 55%. No conformance floor applies to a surface boundary, so the number is one to know rather than a failure; if a wider gap is ever wanted it belongs to --ui-scrim, not here.

SHEET AND DRAWER ARE TOLD APART BY GEOMETRY, not only by the gesture. A Sheet is edge-FLUSH: two rounded corners, no border, because an edge on the inner side alone is a rule rather than a boundary. A Drawer FLOATS — inset 4px on its free sides, all four corners at --ui-radius-lg, and a 1px border — which is what makes its own artboard's three panels one component at three sizes, the desktop one included. §7a splits them on the gesture and that still holds; this is the test that settles a STATIC drawing, where no gesture is visible to read.

CORRECTED: the '1px --ui-neutral-90 border' this entry used to claim was a misreading. The drawn panel's edge is --ui-nav-border, a real role, and it is there because that drawing floats the panel inside a window frame on all four sides. This panel is flush with three viewport edges, so it carries no border — an edge on the inner side alone is a rule, not a boundary.

The geometry spec covers the PANEL only. Sheet.Header's uniform 8px inset has no spec case because its two children are a caller-supplied chrome control and a Sheet.Close, which share no single data-slot for the geometry harness to union; it is asserted directly in the browser suite instead.

The RECORD PANEL composition is drawn on the sheet and is not a part: a chrome band carrying Close plus record pagination, an identity block and a completeness hero at the top of the Body, then an Accordion of field groups in its CARD variant — plain has no hover, and six pressable section headers on one surface is the case that needs one. The hero is a composition rather than a component on purpose: Banner is the nearest thing and does not fit, being `items-center` with one text slot where this stacks a label row, a bar, a sentence and two controls. It carries NO fill, which the composition forced rather than chose — bg-elevated was the obvious answer and Accordion's card variant already owns that fill on the same surface, so a filled hero and a field group would have read as the same kind of thing. Every value is a role; if a completeness meter recurs it wants a name rather than being rebuilt per call site.

The identity block SCROLLS rather than pinning, because the band is chrome-only. Checked against the field rather than asserted: of six CRM detail panels surveyed, four pin one compact row and put the identity in the scrolling body, and one scrolls everything. A caller who needs it pinned composes a second band today.

No visual-regression baseline. The matrix renders components inline and a Sheet portals to document.body, so it is excluded for the same reason Modal and Popover are, and the browser contract suite covers it instead — which is now the only thing watching three regions and a three-value width axis.

Brand re-skinning needs `container` — it is not automatic. Without it the panel portals to document.body and leaves the themed subtree; both halves are asserted in the browser suite, and the BrandThemed story passes it. Multiselect's panel still has no equivalent.
docs.motion: Two movements. The pinned regions' hairlines fade their COLOUR in and out as Sheet.Body scrolls — a box-shadow rather than a border, so the 48px band cannot jog by the pixel a border-box border would cost it, and always declared so only the colour animates (Header's rule). The panel translates in from its edge and the scrim fades, both at --ui-duration-base with --ui-ease-out. `translate` is named explicitly in the transition: Tailwind v4's translate-* writes the standalone property, so a list naming `transform` animates nothing — the defect that had Modal and Popover snapping open. Durations come from --ui-duration-*, which collapse to 1ms under prefers-reduced-motion.

contrast.role: content on the panel

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

Sheet.Panel gains side="top": the full-screen variant a site's collapsed menu uses (#33). Flush on all four edges, so no corner is rounded and no width cap applies (size is ignored); it slides down from above on the same motionStandard translate the other sides use. Not a bottom sheet turned over — that is Drawer, whose contract is the gesture.

Sheet.Panel declares `initialFocus` and `finalFocus`, typed as our own `SheetFocusTarget`: a ref, or a function returning the element. Closes #28. A record panel wants Close to take focus on open, but its band carries Previous/Next first, so Base UI's default (the first tabbable element) lands on Previous. That only worked through the panel's untyped `forBaseUI(rest)` spread on Base UI 1.7.0, and would break silently on a rename, because nothing declared it. Restated rather than re-exported (ADR 0012): Base UI's type also takes booleans and passes an interaction type, and `false` would leave focus behind the scrim, which is not a choice a dialog should offer. A function returning null, or a ref still empty, keeps the default rather than dropping focus. check:boundaries stays green. The browser test opens a Previous/Next/Close panel and asserts focus lands on Close and returns to a named element on Escape, in both the ref and function forms, against a control case proving the defaults are Previous and the trigger. Removing the mapping fails all four.

migration.manual: A caller passing `initialFocus`/`finalFocus` through the untyped spread keeps working. A ref or a function returning an element is unchanged; a boolean `initialFocus={false}` or a function taking Base UI's interaction type no longer type-checks, so pass a ref or `() => element` instead.

changes.summary: Sheet has a design sheet, and it names four parts and a width axis the component does not have. Sheet shipped with no artboard of its own: its geometry came from the Sidebar sheet's mobile section, and what that left out is what the component turned out to lack: Header, Title, Body and Footer, a body that scrolls on its own, and any width above the rail's 272px, which is narrower than Modal's SMALLEST dialog. Component --- Sheet now draws all of it in both schemes, with sizes sm/md/lg on --ui-nav-width, --ui-dialog-width-md and --ui-dialog-width-lg — three width tokens that already existed, no new ones — defaulting to sm so nothing that renders today moves. This entry is the DOC half only: sheetDoc.design pointed at 4-0/HE2-0, a node that no longer exists, and now points at the artboard; needsDesign carries four rows a person must settle — the panel's depth (shadow-md drawn against shadow-sm shipped, with the panel-to-page separation measured at 1.16:1 in light and 1.61:1 in dark), and TWO the ramp turned up that are not Sheet's at all: in dark the band control's interaction ramp CROSSES the panel it sits on (rest #373430 and hover #3c3936 darker, pressed --ui-bg-active #494643 lighter), so a resting control reads recessed and a pressed one raised; and SIX --ui-bg-* roles resolve to #EDE8E3 in light (sunken, muted, hover, selected, field-disabled, field-chrome), so hover and disabled paint one fill separated only by ink at 15.53:1 and 1.76:1 — and the hover-against-selected collision already recorded in the design-component skill is one case of six rather than a pair. Both belong to --ui-bg-active/--ui-bg-hover and registry/lib/chrome-control, which has no doc of its own — this is the only surface that reports them, and Header's own note measured REST against the bar in both schemes and stopped there; knownGaps carries the rest as DRAWN, NOT BUILT, and drops the "1px --ui-neutral-90 border" row as a misreading — that edge is --ui-nav-border, and this panel is flush with three viewport edges so it carries none. The implementation plan is design/paper/sheet-implementation-plan.md.

Sheet grows the four regions and the width axis its own design sheet specifies. Header, Title, Body and Footer land, and Sheet stops being the only overlay in the taxonomy with no structural parts — Body and Footer are Drawer's values verbatim, because both came from the same drawing. Only the Body scrolls: with the scroll on the panel, as it shipped, a header scrolled away with the content it labelled. size is a CAP on three width tokens that already existed — sm --ui-nav-width 272, md --ui-dialog-width-md 416, lg --ui-dialog-width-lg 640 — defaulting to sm, which IS the geometry Sheet already shipped, so nothing that renders moved; all three are asserted as computed max-widths that DIFFER, because max-w-md-shaped utilities resolve against this system's spacing scale and that defect had every Modal rendering at one width. Two things the drawing gave up on contact with the browser. The pinned hairlines are an inset box-shadow rather than the border the sheet named: h-12 is border-box, so a border-b takes its pixel out of the 32px content lane and items-center pays it back as 7.5 above and 8.5 below — the Tabs defect, which Header's own bar carries today and has no geometry spec to catch. A box-shadow costs no layout, so the band keeps a uniform 8px inset and the new geometry spec proves it. And Sheet.Body needed a keyboard path nothing had drawn: a named tab stop with a visible inset ring ONLY while it scrolls, Table's rule in the other axis, named from the panel's own label. design/paper/specs/sheet.geometry.json plus its case in the geometry browser test close ADR 0019 for the panel; probed by removing flex-1 from Body, which fails all three declared laws with the arithmetic printed. Two design questions closed the same day. The panel takes --ui-shadow-md rather than Modal's shadow-sm — the value the sheet draws and the one Drawer ships from the same drawing — because the panel and the page are BOTH --ui-bg-base and in light the scrim leaves only a 1.16:1 step between them; the browser suite asserts both layers, having first had to learn that Tailwind emits four fully transparent placeholder layers ahead of the real shadow, so a layer count reads 6 and an equality assertion compares against four things the component never set. And the claim that "Drawer Desktop" is a Sheet is WITHDRAWN: all three panels on the Drawer artboard carry one treatment — radius-lg on all four corners, a 1px border, shadow-md, inset 4px — which is drawer.tsx exactly and which a Sheet never is, being flush to three viewport edges with two corners and no border. Reading identity from an ABSENT feature (no handle) produced the error; the desktop panel has no handle because a pointer has no drag gesture. That gives the pair a GEOMETRIC test to sit beside §7a's gesture test, for settling a static drawing where no gesture is visible to read, and it is recorded in sheetDoc.knownGaps and CONVENTIONS §7a.

A record-panel composition is drawn on the Sheet sheet: the variant that pushed this component past a navigation drawer. A row in a table opened beside it — Sheet.Header carrying Close plus record pagination and an open-the-full-record control, then Sheet.Body holding an identity block, a completeness hero, and an Accordion of field groups at size md. Nothing in it is a new part, which is the point: it exercises the size axis and the scrolling body the same day they shipped. Four decisions are recorded on the sheet with their evidence. The band stays CHROME and the identity scrolls, checked against the field rather than asserted — of six CRM detail panels surveyed on Mobbin, four pin one compact row and put the identity in the scrolling body (Twenty, Apollo, Lightfield, HubSpot) and one scrolls everything (folk); pinning a taller identity block is the minority pattern, and it would also miss the body's 16px lane by the 8 the band is inset. The hero is a COMPOSITION, not a component: Banner is the nearest thing and does not fit, being items-center with one text slot where this stacks a label row, a Progress at size sm, a consequence sentence and two controls. Field rows sit at px-xs inside the panel's px-sm, which is 4 + 8 = 12 and therefore the trigger's p-md exactly, so a group name and its fields share one lane; an empty value is an em dash in --ui-text-placeholder because a missing field and an unexamined one are different things and the meter above counts on the difference. And the chips are two different components that look alike: Disciplines and Tools are Badge neutral md (labels), while the hero's missing-field chips are Button secondary sm shape-full (controls) at 24px, which meets SC 2.5.8 exactly where Badge sm at 22px would not. CORRECTED on review: the field groups were first drawn as Accordion's PLAIN variant with hairline dividers between them, and both halves of that were wrong. A standard accordion has no border and no dividers — grouping is spacing alone, which is CONVENTIONS' own rule that a rule is a spacing problem solved with ink — so the hairlines were an invention. And plain has no hover either: the bg-hover step belongs to CARD, on the whole tile rather than the trigger, exactly as the Accordion sheet's Card States section labels it. Six pressable section headers on one surface is the case that needs it, so the panel is card now, radius-md tiles on bg-elevated at the root's own gap-xs, with Disciplines drawn hovered. That in turn took the fill off the hero: bg-elevated was the obvious answer and the card variant already owns it on the same surface, so the hero sits on the panel ground at the Body's own inset, where its text lane and the tiles' outer edges agree. The needsDesign row filed against Accordion is withdrawn — plain is not missing anything — and the two variants' real difference is recorded in accordion.doc.ts knownGaps instead: plain has no border, no dividers and no hover, card is a tile whose WHOLE surface answers the pointer, and a surface with pressable section headers wants card.

changes.summary: A Sheet opens from the edge its trigger sits on. Header's own story put the menu button in Header.End and let Sheet's `side` default to left, so the drawer flew in from the opposite edge to the control the user had just pressed — reported, and right: the two read as different controls. The composition is corrected to side="right", the rule is stated in both Header's and Sheet's do-lists, and a browser test asserts the RELATIONSHIP rather than coordinates — the button is past the viewport midpoint and the panel shares that edge. Not enforceable in a type, because the Sheet root wraps the Header and cannot see which region its trigger landed in.

Sheet — the mobile drawer, and the third component on the Base UI behaviour layer (ADR 0012). Deliberately Modal's shape rather than a new one: the focus trap, scroll lock, Escape, outside-press and focus restoration are the same problem, and a drawer that solved them again by hand would solve them worse; what differs is only where the panel sits. Full height flush to one edge, 80% width as drawn (256 of 320), floored at that same 256 because a fixed element resolves against the nearest TRANSFORMED ancestor and a percentage silently scopes to a Storybook docs cell, and capped at --ui-nav-width since a Sidebar is what it holds. Only the two INNER corners are rounded — a fully rounded panel leaves four slivers of scrim in the screen corners and reads as a modal, not a drawer — and side flips both the edge and the radius, asserted as a mirror rather than four more numbers. Sheet carries no chrome of its own: the design draws the back and close controls inside the navigation's own header band, so a Sheet-level header would compete with it. `label` is required on the panel because there is no Title part to name it, and a dialog without a name announces as 'dialog' and nothing else. Two design defects pushed back to Paper: the scrim was a raw #98918A29 in all three drawer examples — the exact value of --ui-scrim, which did not exist in the file — and the panel's 1px --ui-neutral-90 border is a raw palette step whose nearest role is a different value, so the panel takes shadow-sm like Modal and the border was dropped rather than transcribed.

items.lead: Organises navigation beside the work.
