docs.name: Sidebar
docs.summary: The primary navigation rail: a named <nav> built from ROWS, not links. A row becomes a link when given an href and is otherwise a plain slot, because the sheet puts a search field in one and a progress bar in another. First consumer of the --ui-nav-* role family, which had existed in the contract since Phase 1 without ever being rendered.

anatomy.notes: The navigation itself. Renders nothing while a layer is showing — so the two-layer swap has exactly two participants and every other part stays ignorant of it.

A secondary screen that REPLACES the navigation: the sheet's 'Profile Settings', with a brand switcher under it. Same shape as Calendar's month and year selects, for the same reason — on a narrow screen a panel over a panel is two surfaces where the drawing has one.
The 32px chrome control in the sheet's 56px band. Named for where it RETURNS to, never just 'Back'.
The layer's heading, at the second-level row's own type and inset.
Avatar, name, address and a trailing chevron; the way into a layer. A real button — it opens a screen — but NOT aria-expanded, because nothing expands.
16px/600 in nav ink, and 12px/500 in MUTED ink. The sheet drew the address in --ui-text-disabled at 2.14:1; an address is content, so WCAG's disabled exemption does not apply.

The rail's own field: 40px at radius-sm with a 1px edge, where Input's is 48px at radius-md with 1.5px. A rail is denser than a form. The WRAPPER draws the focus ring, which is the one place the inner control may carry outline-none.
A row that holds a CONTROL — a Button, an Input, a Progress bar. The row's inset and nothing else: no role, no tab stop, no click target of its own.
A standalone group label — the sheet's 'Select brand'. Drawn in --ui-text-disabled (2.14:1); ships as the rail's own muted step.
A <nav>, named by its label. w-nav (--ui-nav-width, 17rem), bg-nav, radius-lg, and NO padding of its own.
Names the landmark. sr-only by default — the sheet draws no rail heading — never removed.
The scroll column. p-sm and NO gap; the 8 here plus each row's 12 is the sheet's 20px text inset, and the rows stack flush.
The header band (the sheet's `Nav Group`). p-sm. Holds controls — a back button, a close button — not navigation.
A primary-level label with its second-level rows beneath.
A <button> disclosure when isCollapsible, a <span> heading otherwise. 16px at bold weight in --ui-nav-ink.
The section's <ul>. No padding, no gap, no indent: both levels sit at 20px and the hierarchy is carried by type and colour.
A row: p-md, radius-sm, 46px tall as drawn. An <a> when given href, a <div> otherwise. Carries data-current and aria-current="page".
flex-1, aria-hidden. Pushes what follows to the bottom of the rail.

docs.composition:
Sidebar                    label (required) / isLabelHidden?
├─ Sidebar.Group           the header band — children are slots
├─ Sidebar.Item            href? isCurrent? icon? trailing?
├─ Sidebar.Section         label (required) isCollapsible? isOpen? defaultIsOpen? onOpenChange? icon?
│  └─ Sidebar.Item         …second level, rendered as <li>
├─ Sidebar.Spacer
└─ Sidebar.Item            e.g. a Progress, pinned to the bottom

layer.notes: Which secondary layer is showing; null is the navigation. Controlled/uncontrolled through the shared hook (§4) rather than left to each part, because the layer closes from a back button inside it and opens from a row that is not.

onLayerChange.notes: Fires for the profile row and for the back control.

Layer.id.notes: Matched against the Sidebar's `layer` and against Profile's `layer`.

Layer.backLabel.notes: The back control's accessible name. Required and NOT defaulted to 'Back' — a rail may hold more than one layer, and 'Back' alone leaves a screen-reader user to guess what they are returning to.

Profile.email.notes: Rendered in muted ink, not the disabled role. See anatomy.

Profile.avatar.notes: Slot: an Avatar at 32px. Never wrapped (§3).

Profile.layer.notes: The layer this row opens. Without it the row is a plain button and the caller wires onClick.

Search.label.notes: Visually hidden — the sheet draws a placeholder and no label, and a placeholder is not a label (§10).

label.notes: Required — a page may carry several <nav> landmarks and they are indistinguishable without names.

isLabelHidden.notes: Hidden by DEFAULT, unlike every other label in the system: the sheet draws no rail heading, so the label exists to name the landmark rather than to be read.

Item.href.notes: OPTIONAL. With it the row is a real <a> — middle-click, open-in-new-tab and the UA's focus handling all come free. Without it the row is a plain slot and its children fill it, which is how a search field or a progress bar sits in the rail.

Item.isCurrent.notes: Sets aria-current="page". The fill alone conveys nothing to a screen reader (WCAG 1.4.1), and the rail's active fill measures barely over 1:1 against it — so the weight changes too.

Item.isDisabled.notes: Unavailable. The row STAYS in the tab order and keeps its link role — a row a screen-reader user cannot reach is one they cannot be told the reason for. Navigation is prevented on the click rather than by quietly dropping the href, and never with pointer-events-none, which would kill the tooltip explaining why it is off.

Item.icon.notes: Slot: leading glyph, decorative. Never wrapped (§3).

Item.render.notes: Slot: swap the row's own <a>/<div> for this element — pass render={<Link href={href} />} so the app's router owns the transition. Passed through, never wrapped (§3): the row's data-slot, aria-current, the isDisabled invariant and its className merge onto it rather than replacing what it carries.

Section.isCollapsible.notes: OFF by default. The sheet draws a chevron on 'Brand' and none on 'Most recent', so collapsibility is a property of a section rather than the definition of one — and a header that cannot collapse renders as a span, not a button that does nothing.

Section.isOpen / defaultIsOpen / onOpenC.notes: Controlled and uncontrolled, via useControllableState. Ignored unless isCollapsible.

do: Name the sidebar; the landmark is otherwise anonymous.
Set isCurrent on exactly one item, so the announcement matches the fill.
Put non-navigation furniture — a search field, a progress bar, a button — in a Sidebar.Item with no href.
Use Sidebar.Group for the header band's controls, and Sidebar.Spacer to pin a footer row to the bottom.
dont: Do not make items buttons with onClick to fake a link. Navigation is links, and the browser's contract is worth more than arrow keys (ARIA APG: a nav is not a menu).
Do not convey the current page by fill alone — aria-current is what is announced.
Do not indent the second level; the sheet keeps both at 20px, and an indent would be a redundant second signal costing room on a narrow rail.
Do not add a gap between rows. The sheet stacks them flush and the rhythm is each row's own 12px padding — a gap is a second, competing spacing system.
Do not nest a third level; the sheet draws two and deeper trees want a different pattern.
Do not narrow this component to make a rail. NavRail is the rail (ADR 0015) — a Section header cannot disclose at 48px, and Search, Profile, Heading and Slot have nowhere to put what they hold.

a11y.layers: Opening a layer moves focus to its back control; closing returns focus to the row that opened it. The row is UNMOUNTED while the layer shows, so the return is done by finding the row again after the re-render — focusing a remembered node there lands on <body>, which is what the browser test caught.
a11y.role: navigation landmark. A Section is a <ul> of links; rows outside a Section are not list items, because a search field announced as a list item is a lie about the page structure.
a11y.name: The `label` prop via aria-labelledby. Each section's <ul> is reached from its header through aria-controls, so the disclosure and the list it reveals cannot drift apart.

keyboard.does: Walks the links in document order — the platform's own behaviour, asserted in Chromium.
Follows a link, or toggles a collapsible section header. Native in both cases.
Toggles a collapsible section header. It is a real <button>.
No arrow-key navigation: adding it would mean taking the links out of the tab order, which is the wrong trade.

a11y.target: A row measures the sheet's 46px — p-md (12+12) around a 16px line at leading-normal (21.6px). min-h-9 (36px) floors a caller who puts something shorter in the slot; both clear SC 2.5.8's 24px.

contrastPairs.role: section headings and top-level rows on the rail
second-level item ink

the current item — its ink steps BACK to muted rather than up to full, the same two-channel split Header uses: the fill says where you are, and you cannot navigate to it, so it is the one row not worth pointing at. 9.64:1 light, 9.79:1 dark

contrastPairs.why: WCAG 1.4.3 exempts disabled controls from the contrast minimum, and a disabled row has to read as unavailable — holding it to 4.5:1 would make it indistinguishable from an available one, which is the actual accessibility failure. It is still derived to sit clearly below --ui-nav-ink-muted rather than vanishing.
contrastPairs.role: a disabled row

needsDesign: Row focus is derived; the sheet draws rest and current only. Hover is now its own fill (--ui-nav-hover-bg), added when NavRail needed to tell hover from current without a label to change weight.
knownGaps: No collapsed mode, and there will not be one. The narrow rail is NavRail, a sibling component (ADR 0015): six of the ten parts below change what they MEAN at 48px rather than what they measure, which is the same test CONVENTIONS §7a uses to split Sheet from Drawer. A layout renders one or the other, and neither knows about the other. The trigger to revisit is an ANIMATED width transition, which two trees cannot do as cleanly as one component with a mode.
No mobile drawer. The sheet's mobile composition is this Sidebar inside an overlay; the overlay itself is a Sheet, not a Sidebar variant, and is not built yet.

Hover and focus are DERIVED — the sheet draws rest and current only. Hover moved off --ui-nav-active-bg onto its own --ui-nav-hover-bg step, so rest, hover and current are three fills rather than two; the weight change on current stays.
No section dividers. An Avatar and account menu are drawn in the mobile examples but belong to the composition around the rail, not to it.
docs.motion: Rows and the section trigger transition `background-color` and `color`, the section chevron rotates, and the search field transitions `outline-color` and `box-shadow` — all `motionMicro` (--ui-duration-fast, --ui-ease-out). A collapsible SECTION animates its height at `motionStandard` against `--collapsible-panel-height`, the measurement Base UI publishes: `height: auto` cannot be transitioned and a constant would clip a section with more rows than the artboard drew. It used to snap, shown and hidden with the `hidden` attribute, while Accordion animated the identical interaction one component over — the divergence is closed by taking the behaviour layer's answer rather than writing a third. The hard part is not the height but the ORDERING: `hidden` must stay off until the closing animation finishes, or the rows blank before the space closes, and must go back on afterwards, or a collapsed section is flat but still in the tab order. Both halves are asserted. A non-collapsible section has none of this — it is a heading and a list.

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

A collapsible Sidebar.Section now animates its height instead of snapping. It opened and closed with the `hidden` attribute, while Accordion — the identical interaction one component over — animated against the measurement Base UI publishes; two answers to one question is the divergence this library records rather than keeps. The section moves onto Base UI's Collapsible (ADR 0012) and transitions `height` to `--collapsible-panel-height` at motionStandard, exactly as Accordion's panel does: `height: auto` cannot be transitioned and a constant would clip a section with more rows than the artboard drew. The reason to take the behaviour layer's answer rather than write a third is not the height, which is easy — it is the ORDERING. `hidden` must stay off until the closing animation finishes, or the rows blank before the space closes, and must go back on afterwards, or a collapsed section is flat but still in the tab order. `keepMounted` is set because aria-controls must point at something that exists. One regression was introduced and caught while building it: rendering the panel with our own `id` overrode the id Base UI had generated and already pointed aria-controls at, leaving the trigger referencing an element that did not exist — a broken disclosure that looked completely normal, since the attribute was present and the panel still opened. A test asserting that aria-controls RESOLVES, rather than merely exists, is added alongside. A non-collapsible section is untouched and carries none of this machinery.

migration.manual: The expanded and collapsed end states are pixel-identical — the sidebar visual baseline did not move — so nothing static changes. What changes is between them, plus two things worth knowing if you test or style this. The panel's `id` is now generated by the behaviour layer rather than by us, so do not select on it (use `[data-slot="sidebar-sublist"]`); and `hidden` now arrives AFTER the collapse animation rather than with the click, so a test asserting it immediately must await the animation first.

ImageUpload's note is corrected while being promoted: it credited the token layer with stopping its spinner, and what actually stops it is the motion-safe: variant. Two findings are recorded in the notes rather than fixed: Sidebar's collapsible section snaps via the hidden attribute where Accordion animates the identical interaction against Base UI's published height, and Banner reaches for transition-colors where the rest of the library enumerates properties. No component's rendered motion changes; no .tsx is touched.

If you consume the doc files and read `a11y.motion`, it has moved to the top-level `motion` key on Sheet and ImageUpload; Button was already there and the other 27 are new.

changes.summary: The current row in Sidebar and NavRail is marked by its FILL and nothing else. Sidebar drops `font-bold` and steps the current row's ink BACK to `--ui-nav-ink-muted` where it used to lift to `--ui-nav-active-ink`; hover no longer lifts ink either, on either component; NavRail's current glyph stays at its resting ink. This is the narrow half of the divergence Header opened when it decided the current page recedes, and it closes the half that was actually wrong rather than the half that was a real difference: a rail still marks position with a fill where a bar does not, because a rail is a persistent map and a bar is a short row you read across — but ink and weight now behave identically across the whole nav family. Weight was the worst of the three channels: bold on the current row reflowed its own label a fraction and made the one row you cannot navigate to the loudest thing in the rail, spending emphasis on the least actionable item exactly as Header's four-step ramp did. Measured: muted on the current fill is 9.64:1 light and 5.42:1 dark, and the fill carries the state at 1.105 / 1.285 against the rail. The pair `--ui-nav-ink-muted` on `--ui-nav-active-bg` is now declared in the token contract so the theme audit covers what these components actually render; `--ui-nav-active-ink` stays in the contract because a re-skin can still reach for it.

migration.manual: The current nav row loses its bold weight and its label goes from full-strength nav ink to muted; its background is unchanged. Hover no longer changes ink on either component. If you styled around the current row's weight or ink — an override, a screenshot baseline, a test asserting the current item is bolder or darker than a resting one — the difference now lives entirely in `background-color`. A top-level Sidebar row shows the ink step clearly (nav-ink to muted); a row inside a section was already muted, so there only the fill changes.

changes.summary: A partial edge is never a state. NavRail shipped a 2px bar down the current row's leading edge to separate it from hover, and separated its groups with hairlines — both wrong, and both against a rule this library had already written: Menu.Separator is "SPACE, not a rule — 8px above and below, and nothing painted". A ruler inside a control reads as clutter and multiplies down a list. The marker was the wrong answer to a REAL problem, which is the part worth keeping: --ui-nav-active-bg was the family's only fill, so hover and current painted the identical square and a rail row has no label to change weight the way Sidebar's does. The fix is a token, not a decoration — --ui-nav-hover-bg joins the contract, and rest/hover/current are now three fills in both rails. Sidebar takes the same step so the two stay interchangeable, and keeps its weight change on top. Grouping in NavRail is now the DIFFERENCE between the body's gap-md and a section's gap-xs, which also removes the `first:` selector the hairline needed and had mis-set. A fourth step for current-AND-hovered was attempted and abandoned on evidence: past --ui-nav-active-bg the value is an accent WASH under the `tinted` nav style, landing darker for a dark accent and lighter for a light one, so the two grounds straddle the ink, legibleOn flips for one of them and no single value clears both — the resolver test caught it at 3.70:1 and then 3.89:1 across two attempts. Three fills the resolver can always satisfy beat four that break a brand style. Codified as ui-craft rules 20–22 and three ratchet entries; the browser test asserts no element paints a border on fewer than four sides, probed against a re-added marker.

migration.manual: --ui-nav-hover-bg is new; a consumer with a hand-written nav theme should give it a value between --ui-nav-bg and --ui-nav-active-bg, or let the resolver derive it. A rail row's hover fill is lighter than before — it used to be the current row's fill, which is the bug.

changes.summary: Every piece of text in the rail sits on ONE lane, 20px from its edge — measured in the sheet at worldX -813 against a rail at -833, for the row labels, the section heading, the layer title, the profile row's avatar and the search field's placeholder alike. Three new parts missed it: the heading and the layer title carried an extra px-sm and landed at 28, and the search field's text at 24. Reported as 'the indentation of various text classes', which is exactly what three lanes look like from the outside. The search field's edge is now an OUTLINE rather than a border, which is what the sheet draws and for a reason that only appears when measured: a border takes layout space, so the input's text landed 1px inside the lane while every other label sat on it. A browser test now measures every label's left edge against the rail and requires 20 — a relationship, not a coordinate, so it fails on any part that drifts off. Boxed controls (the field, a Slot's Button) share their own lane at 12, 8px inside the text one.

The rail becomes two surfaces and grows its own controls. Sidebar.Main and Sidebar.Layer are the two-layer swap the sheet draws: pressing Sidebar.Profile REPLACES the navigation with a second screen — 'Profile Settings' and a brand switcher — rather than covering it, which is the same choice Calendar's month and year selects make and for the same reason: on the narrow screen this rail lives on, a panel over a panel is two surfaces where the drawing has one. Only those two parts know about the swap, so no row has to ask whether a layer is open. Sidebar.Search is the rail's own field (40px at radius-sm with a 1px edge, where Input's is 48px at radius-md with 1.5px — a rail is denser than a form), Sidebar.Slot is a row that holds a control and adds nothing to it, and Sidebar.Heading is the standalone group label. Layer.backLabel is REQUIRED and deliberately not defaulted to 'Back': a rail may hold more than one layer.

Four uses of --ui-text-disabled in the Sidebar sheet on content that is not disabled, all corrected in Paper. It measures 2.14:1 in light and 2.51:1 in dark, and WCAG exempts disabled CONTROLS, not text that happens to be quiet: the profile row's email address, the 'Select brand' group label, and both search placeholders. Shipped as --ui-text-muted (5.93 / 4.94) for the address, the rail's own --ui-nav-ink-muted (10.66 / 6.97) for the label, and --ui-text-placeholder (5.93 / 4.65) for the placeholders — the role that exists for exactly that. The one remaining --ui-text-disabled in the artboard is a genuinely disabled nav row and is correct. Same defect class as the Calendar weekday headers, which drew the same role for the same reason.
Preserve disabled sidebar safety

Sidebar rows can be disabled — the state the design has drawn since the start (`Second Level Item - Level 2 Disabled`) and the component had no way to express. It needed a role first: the sheet paints it with --ui-text-disabled, which is the PAGE's disabled ink and does not follow a brand that re-skins its nav, so --ui-nav-ink-disabled joins the family, derived 62% of the way from the nav ink toward the rail so it sits clearly below --ui-nav-ink-muted without vanishing. Three deliberate choices in the behaviour. The row keeps its link role, its href and its place in the tab order: a row a screen-reader user cannot reach is one they cannot be told the reason for, and dropping the href would leave something that looks like a link and silently does nothing — navigation is prevented on the click instead. Never pointer-events-none, which removes the row from hit-testing and kills any tooltip explaining why it is off. And hover and current are gated behind the flag, so an unavailable row cannot light up as though it were reachable. The contrast pair is declared DECORATIVE with a reason rather than held to 4.5:1: WCAG 1.4.3 exempts disabled controls, and a disabled row forced to text contrast would be indistinguishable from an available one, which is the actual accessibility failure. It measures 2.63:1 in both schemes.

Design fixes pushed back into Paper for the Sidebar sheet, plus the geometry the code took FROM it. The --ui-nav-* family did not exist in the Paper file at all — six roles that had been in the code contract since Phase 1 with no way for a design to reference them — so the rail was drawn on --ui-bg-surface with raw --ui-neutral-95 fills, which is exactly the drift the family exists to prevent. Created --ui-nav-bg / -ink / -ink-muted / -active-bg / -active-ink / -border in Paper and rebound both rails (the layered spec and the mobile sheet) plus the active row inside the mobile navigation overlay. One real accessibility defect: the CURRENT row was drawn in --ui-text-muted while resting rows sat at --ui-text-primary and --ui-text-secondary — the active item was the weakest ink on the rail, and its fill measures barely over 1:1 against the surface, so the state was carried by almost nothing. It is now --ui-nav-active-ink at 600, matching the shipped component, which changes weight for the same reason. The sheet's Progress fill was a raw --ui-blue-80, the exact value that measured 1.24:1 and caused --ui-bg-accent-legible to be minted; rebound. Going the other way, the code adopted the sheet's geometry, which it had been getting wrong: rows are p-md (12) inside a body of p-sm (8) for a 20px text inset and a 46px row, not px-lg/py-sm for 24 and 37; the row radius is radius-sm, not radius-md; and rows stack FLUSH — the sheet's six-row section measures exactly 6x46 — so the gap-xs between them was a second spacing system competing with the row's own padding. The 8px block padding on the body is ours and stays: the sheet lets the first and last rows touch the rail's edges, which left a collapsed final section jammed against the bottom.

Sidebar — the primary navigation rail, and the first consumer of the --ui-nav-* role family, which had sat in the contract since Phase 1 without ever being rendered. Built as a plain <nav> rather than a behaviour-layer component: navigation is links, and Tab order, Enter activation, middle-click and open-in-new-tab are worth more than the arrow keys a roving-tabindex menu would buy at their expense (ARIA APG — a nav is not a menu). Composed as SLOTS, not links: the design's own layer names (Nav Group, Primary Level Item, Second Level Item, Spacer) describe rows, and one of those rows holds a search field while another holds a whole Progress bar — so Sidebar.Item takes an OPTIONAL href and renders an <a> only when given one. An anchor wrapping a form control is invalid, and a row that cannot hold one cannot draw the sheet. Sidebar.Section carries the second level with isCollapsible OFF by default, because the sheet draws a chevron on 'Brand' and none on 'Most recent'; a header that cannot collapse renders as a span rather than a button that does nothing. Rows inside a Section are <li>, rows outside one are not, since announcing a search field as a list item misdescribes the page. Both levels sit at the same 24px inset (8 on the body plus 16 on the row) and are told apart by weight and ink — an indent would be a redundant second signal costing room on a narrow rail. The current page is ANNOUNCED via aria-current and changes weight too, because the active fill measures barely over 1:1 against the rail. Four tooling and token defects the component exposed, all first-of-its-kind: --ui-nav-width and --ui-nav-rail-width had NO Tailwind utility at all, the same gap --ui-scrim had before Modal, and now emit into the spacing namespace as w-nav / w-nav-rail; the nav colour family was the only one the emitter never remapped, so it minted the stuttering bg-nav-bg and text-nav-ink, now bg-nav, text-ink-nav, bg-nav-active, text-ink-nav-active and border-edge-nav; --ui-nav-ink-muted on --ui-nav-bg was rendered by every second-level item while absent from CONTRAST_PAIRS, caught by the contrast gate added hours earlier; and the rail's 16px type was first written as text-title-sm, which is a FLUID role — it computed to 12.17px in Chromium and would be smallest on a phone, the one viewport where the sheet actually draws this rail. A fixed-width surface takes fixed type roles, so both levels are text-body-lg. axe also caught the BrandThemed story rendering two <nav> landmarks with the same name — a landmark-unique violation, and exactly what the required `label` prop exists to prevent. Design defects corrected: a raw 16px rail radius and a run of raw 4/8/16px paddings became scale tokens, and the active item used --ui-bg-elevated rather than --ui-nav-active-bg, which is the whole reason the nav family exists.

migration.manual: The nav utilities are RENAMED: bg-nav-bg becomes bg-nav, text-nav-ink becomes text-ink-nav, bg-nav-active-bg becomes bg-nav-active, text-nav-active-ink becomes text-ink-nav-active, and border-nav-border becomes border-edge-nav. Nothing consumed them before Sidebar, so no shipped component changes.

items.name: site-header
items.title: SiteHeader
items.lead: Connects a site’s pages with navigation that adapts to a small screen.

docs.lead: Connects a site’s pages with navigation that adapts to a small screen.
docs.name: SiteHeader
docs.summary: The SITE header (#33): a wordmark, a short row of quiet links and one call to action, composed from Header — which stays app chrome. Data-driven rather than compound, because every marketing site here is Astro and an .astro file cannot compose Header's parts across the island boundary. Below the caller's collapse point the bar keeps two words, the wordmark and Menu; the menu is a full-screen Sheet from the top.

anatomy.notes: Header, at its own 48px (h-12), px-xl wide and px-lg collapsed. `affix` is ON by default — a site's bar stays reachable — and is Header's own prop, so the affix ground, blur and hairline are Header's. Carries `data-site-header` (the scope of its media query) and, while it sits on the hero, `data-over-media`.

One link to brand.href (default "/"). Type-only by default: brand.label at title-sm 16/600 in the bar's ink. With brand.wordmark the artwork is shown, hidden from assistive tech, and brand.label names the link — the organisation, never "Home" or "Logo". No brand-mark TILE: on a site the mark is the favicon's job (#33, revision 2).

Header.Nav, named by navLabel, holding Header.Item variant="quiet" links: label-md 13/600, px-sm, 32px tall, no fill in ANY state. Ink is the only channel — --ui-text-muted at rest, --ui-text-primary on hover and on the current page (2.90:1 apart), aria-current="page" on the current one. Hidden below collapseBelow.
Button primary md (32px) rendered as an <a>. The bar's only filled shape. Below collapseBelow it leaves the bar and reappears, full width at lg, at the menu's foot.

Header.MenuButton in its TEXT form: the word menuText at label-md, a 44px target, no surface. Its name is menuLabel, which must START with the visible word (SC 2.5.3) — "Menu, site navigation", not "Open navigation". Present only below collapseBelow: the bar renders the nav OR the menu button, never both.

A Sheet, side="top" — full screen, sliding down. Its first row is the bar again (wordmark, and closeText exactly where menuText was). Then the items at title-lg 24/500 in 44px rows, muted with the current one in primary, then the CTA full-width where a thumb reaches it and an optional menuFooter line in body-sm muted. Focus is trapped, Escape and Close dismiss, the page behind does not scroll — all Sheet's. Following a link closes it.

Only with isOverMedia and scrim (default on): --ui-bg-media at 72% (MEDIA_SCRIM_ALPHA) held for the bar's 48px, then ramped to 0 over 32px more on the perceptual dark ramp. Behind the bar's content, pointer-events none, aria-hidden; fades out as the bar affixes.

docs.composition:
<SiteHeader
  brand={{ label: "Diorama" }}
  items={[
    { label: "Work", href: "/work" },
    { label: "Studio", href: "/studio", isCurrent: true },
    { label: "Journal", href: "/journal" },
    { label: "Careers", href: "/careers" },
  ]}
  cta={{ label: "Book a call", href: "/contact" }}
  collapseBelow="62rem"
  menuFooter="studio@diorama.example"
/>

// On a hero: put it directly before the first section. The bar pulls that
// section up under itself and paints the media inks until it affixes.
<SiteHeader isOverMedia brand={brand} items={items} cta={cta} />
<section className="relative min-h-[70vh] bg-media">…</section>

// Astro: the desktop bar is plain HTML. Only the collapsed menu needs React,
// so hydrate it on narrow screens only.
<SiteHeader client:media="(width < 62rem)" {...props} />

brand.type: { label: string; href?: string; wordmark?: ReactNode }
brand.notes: label is the link's accessible name and, without wordmark, the visible type-only wordmark. href defaults to "/". wordmark is decorative artwork (an SVG sized 20px tall).

items.type: { label: string; href: string; isCurrent?: boolean }[]
items.notes: The quiet links. Exactly one isCurrent, or none. Rendered twice — in the bar and in the menu — and only one copy is ever displayed, so assistive tech never meets both.

cta.notes: The one call to action. A link styled as Button primary — it goes somewhere, so it is an <a> (Patterns — Navigation).

collapseBelow.notes: The collapse point, a px/rem/em length. There is no breakpoint token (#32 is deferred), so it is the caller's — bydiorama.com's 991px is 62rem. Emitted as a range media query in a scoped <style>, so the switch exists in server-rendered HTML before hydration. Anything that is not a plain length is refused (it lands in CSS) and falls back to 62rem with a dev error.

isOverMedia.notes: The bar sits ON the first section: no fill, the media inks (on-media-muted rest, on-media for hover, current, wordmark and Menu) and the scrim, until the page scrolls under it — then affix takes over and it is the ordinary pinned bar. It pulls the next section up by its own 48px (-mb-12), so place it immediately before the hero.

scrim.notes: The over-media scrim. Off only for a hero that is guaranteed dark: without it the inks are measured against nothing.

affix.notes: Header's affix, on by default here. { fade: true } is Header's fade variant.

navLabel.notes: Names the navigation landmark (in the bar and in the menu) and the menu dialog.

menuText.notes: The visible word on the collapsed bar's control.

menuLabel.notes: The control's accessible name. Must start with menuText (SC 2.5.3, label in name) — a dev error says so if it does not.

closeText.notes: The visible word on the same control inside the open menu.

closeLabel.notes: Its accessible name; must start with closeText.

menuFooter.notes: A line under the CTA in the open menu — a contact address. body-sm, muted.

do: Use it for a marketing or editorial site. An app's top bar is Header, composed — it has an account menu, a brand switcher and a Sidebar the menu opens; this has none of those.
Give exactly one item isCurrent on pages that are in the nav, and none on pages that are not.
Set collapseBelow to the width at which the row of items and the CTA stops fitting beside the wordmark with room to spare — measure the longest locale.
Place an over-media header directly before the hero, and give the hero its own height: the bar overlaps the top 48px of it.
dont: Do not add a second filled button. The CTA is the bar's only shape; a second one makes neither the call to action.
Do not pass a brand-mark tile as the wordmark. A site's mark belongs in the favicon; the bar carries the name.
Do not rename the menu control to an icon. The text control is the design: a glyph on a chrome square is the app bar's, and would be the only boxed shape besides the CTA.
Do not turn the scrim off over photography you do not control. It is what the over-media contrast is measured against.

Do not reach for Header.Item variant="quiet" in an app bar to make it 'calmer'. The quiet item's rest ink is muted, which is the app bar's CURRENT-page ink — mixing the two variants in one bar inverts what current means.

a11y.role: banner (Header's <header>), containing a navigation landmark named navLabel. Below the collapse point the menu is a modal dialog (Sheet) named navLabel, holding a second navigation landmark with the same name — only one of the two is ever displayed.
a11y.name: The wordmark link from brand.label; the nav and the dialog from navLabel; the menu control from menuLabel/closeLabel, each starting with its visible word.

keyboard.does: Wordmark, then the items, then the CTA — or, collapsed, wordmark then Menu.
On Menu, opens the menu with focus inside it (Sheet). Enter follows a link.
Closes the menu and returns focus to Menu (Sheet).

a11y.target: Quiet items are 32px tall, the CTA 32px, the menu control and the menu rows 44px — every target clears SC 2.5.8's 24px, and the two touch-only controls clear 2.5.5's 44px.

contrastPairs.role: a quiet item at REST on the page ground, and the menu's rows. 5.93:1 light, 7.02:1 dark
the wordmark, Menu/Close, and a quiet item hovered or current — 2.90:1 above the rest ink, which is what makes the current page legible as current

a quiet item at rest while the bar is AFFIXED — muted, as at rest: 4.75:1 light / 5.38:1 dark. It stepped up to secondary while the old mid-grey dark ramp put muted at 3.66:1 here (closed 2026-11-03, with Header's current item)
the wordmark, Menu and the current item while affixed
a quiet item at rest OVER MEDIA, measured against the scrim over a white photograph — the bar's worst case, and why the scrim is 72% rather than the sheet's 64%
the wordmark, Menu and a hovered or current item over media
the CTA's label, in the bar and in the menu — the accent fill does not depend on the ground under it

needsDesign: Current page over media: on-media is only 1.33:1 from the on-media-muted rest ink (2.90:1 on the page). aria-current carries it for assistive tech; visually it is the sheet's open choice — accept it, or add a 1.5px on-media underline to the current item over media only. Shipped as accepted (no underline) until decided.
knownGaps: The collapse point is a prop, not a token: there is no breakpoint scale yet (#32 is deferred). When #32 adds one, collapseBelow should accept its names.

Shipped under registry/ui as a ui item, not registry/blocks as the #33 sheet drew it: every gate (utilities, contrast, motion, controls, visual coverage) scans registry/ui, and a block outside it would ship ungated. It is still a separate item from Header, which was the decision that mattered.
Items are flat. A site nav with a dropdown (Header.Item's trailing chevron + Menu) is not designed for the site bar.

The scrim is 72% (MEDIA_SCRIM_ALPHA), not the sheet's 64%: 64% was the lowest alpha that passed for the full on-media ink, and the system has one measured media scrim. A darker hero shows no difference; a white one gains contrast.
docs.motion: Quiet items transition `color` at --ui-duration-fast (Header.Item's own motionMicro); the affix change is Header's (background and shadow at motionStandard); the scrim fades its opacity with the same token as the bar affixes, so the two cross over rather than snap. The menu slides down from the top with Sheet's motionStandard translate and fades; reduced motion removes the travel (Sheet's).

contrast.role: a quiet item at REST on the page ground, and the menu's rows. 5.93:1 light, 7.02:1 dark
the wordmark, Menu/Close, and a quiet item hovered or current — 2.90:1 above the rest ink, which is what makes the current page legible as current

a quiet item at rest while the bar is AFFIXED — muted, as at rest: 4.75:1 light / 5.38:1 dark. It stepped up to secondary while the old mid-grey dark ramp put muted at 3.66:1 here (closed 2026-11-03, with Header's current item)
the wordmark, Menu and the current item while affixed
a quiet item at rest OVER MEDIA, measured against the scrim over a white photograph — the bar's worst case, and why the scrim is 72% rather than the sheet's 64%
the wordmark, Menu and a hovered or current item over media
the CTA's label, in the bar and in the menu — the accent fill does not depend on the ground under it

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

New item SiteHeader (#33, minimal revision): a marketing site's bar composed from Header — a type-only wordmark link, Header.Item variant="quiet" links, and one CTA (Button primary md as an <a>). Data-driven (brand, items, cta) because an Astro page cannot compose Header's parts across the island boundary. Below collapseBelow (a caller length, default 62rem — there is no breakpoint token while #32 is deferred) the bar keeps the wordmark and a text Menu control; the menu is a full-screen Sheet from the top with title-lg rows and the CTA at its foot. The switch is a scoped range media query in a <style>, so the desktop bar is static-safe HTML. isOverMedia: no fill, the media inks and a --ui-bg-media scrim held for 48px then ramped out over 32px on the perceptual dark ramp, until the bar affixes. The scrim is 72% (MEDIA_SCRIM_ALPHA), not the sheet's 64%: --ui-bg-media-floor is defined at 72%, so check:contrast measures the bar's worst case (rest ink 4.62:1, full ink 6.14:1). Shipped in registry/ui rather than registry/blocks so every gate applies.

items.name: skeleton
items.title: Skeleton
items.lead: A placeholder standing in for content that has not arrived.

docs.lead: A placeholder standing in for content that has not arrived.
docs.name: Skeleton
docs.summary: A placeholder standing in for content that has not arrived. One element, no variants, sized entirely from the outside with className — the same shape as shadcn/ui's Skeleton, so a consumer's intuition transfers. Defaults to a full-width bar at body height, pulses under motion-safe, and is aria-hidden: the announcement belongs on the region that is loading, as aria-busy, which only the caller can place.

anatomy.notes: The only node. Owns the fill, the radius, the pulse, className and the ref. Its SIZE is the caller's — `h-4 w-full` is a default to be displaced, not a specification.

docs.composition:
Skeleton └─ (no props of its own — className sizes it, native div props pass through)
{isLoading ? :

{title}

}
// A shape is composed at the call site rather than configured:

className.notes: The whole API. Merges last, so every default is displaceable: `size-10 rounded-full` is an avatar, `h-2.5 w-3/5` is Table's own bar, `h-48` is a media block. This is deliberate rather than minimal-for-its-own-sake — a `variant` or `lines` prop would re-describe the layout the skeleton is standing in for, and the layout is already written next to it.

do: Size it with className at the call site — it should be the shape of the thing that is loading.
Put aria-busy on the REGION being replaced, so assistive tech is told once rather than per placeholder.
Match the real content's height, so nothing jumps when the data arrives.
Compose several to make a shape; that is what the component is for.
dont: Do not render one for every field of a large form — a few bars standing for the shape read better than a faithful wireframe, and 40 pulsing boxes is noise.
Do not put text or controls inside it. It is a rectangle; anything real inside it is hidden from assistive tech by the aria-hidden it carries.
Do not use it as an empty state — that is EmptyState, and the two must not look alike. A skeleton says 'coming'; an empty slot says 'nothing here'.

Do not re-invent it for a dense surface — pass a height. Table's loading body composes this at h-2.5 rather than drawing its own bar, which is what stopped the library having two placeholder treatments.

a11y.role: none — aria-hidden div. It carries no semantics on purpose: a screen reader announcing a dozen empty boxes says nothing anyone can act on.
a11y.name: None, and it must not have one. The loading state is announced by aria-busy on the region the skeletons replace, which is the only place that knows what is loading and when it stops.
a11y.focus: Never focusable, and never replacing a focused element without the caller moving focus deliberately (§10). A skeleton swapped in under the user's focus point is how focus falls to <body>.

contrastPairs.why: The bar against the page — the same pair AspectRatio declares for the same fill. Decorative rather than a boundary: nothing depends on identifying a skeleton's edge, and it is replaced by real content within a second or so. Declared rather than omitted so the number stays visible, because a placeholder too quiet to see is a page that looks broken rather than busy, and that is a design question rather than a code one.

forwarding.ref: Goes to the bar — the only node, and not a form control, so the §5 default applies.
forwarding.className: Lands on the bar and merges last, which is the whole API.
forwarding.rest: Native div props go to the bar. `aria-hidden` is set BEFORE the spread rather than after — the one deliberate exception to §5's contract-props-win rule, so a caller with a single skeleton standing for a single named thing can label it instead. Everything else follows §5.

docs.motion: A `motion-safe:animate-pulse` keyframe, and the only thing the component animates. The guard is required rather than stylistic: a keyframe carries its own timing, so the token layer's duration collapse cannot reach it (ADR 0018) — without `motion-safe:` this would pulse straight through prefers-reduced-motion. It settles to a plain recessed rectangle there, and the shape carries the meaning on its own. The TIMING is taken back off Tailwind: `animate-pulse` bakes 2s and its own curve into the class NAME, which is a hard-coded duration in the one place check:motion cannot look and no brand can reach, so `[animation-duration:var(--ui-duration-loop)]` and `[animation-timing-function:var(--ui-ease-default)]` override it while the keyframes stay Tailwind's. --ui-duration-loop exists for this: it is the only duration token describing a REPEAT rather than a journey, which is why it sits an order of magnitude above the rest. motion.browser.test.tsx asserts the override actually wins the cascade — an arbitrary property losing to the shorthand would leave the token decorative and every gate still green.
needsDesign: THERE IS NO SHEET. design/paper/README.md lists Skeleton among the components still to be drawn, so every value below is derived rather than transcribed. Everything in this list is a question, not a defect.

RESOLVED as a token rather than an exception: --ui-duration-loop (2000ms) now carries the pulse period, and --ui-ease-default its curve, both applied over animate-pulse so the keyframes stay Tailwind's and the timing becomes ours. 2000ms is Tailwind's number kept deliberately — it is a reasonable loading rhythm and nothing had measured an alternative — so the VALUE is still a question for the sheet even though its home is no longer. What changed is that it is now reachable: check:motion can see it, a brand can move it, and motion.browser.test.tsx asserts the pulse runs at it.

The pulse animates OPACITY, so the bar fades toward the page rather than brightening toward the ink. On a dark scheme that reads as the bar receding rather than shimmering. A left-to-right sheen is the common alternative and is a different decision, not a tweak.

The default height (h-4, 16px) and radius (rounded-sm) are derived from Table's internal skeleton bar, which is drawn at h-2.5 (10px) inside a dense row. Two heights for one idea is exactly the kind of divergence the library records rather than hides; which is the system's placeholder height is a question for the sheet.

No contrast floor is drawn for a placeholder. --ui-bg-sunken on --ui-bg-base measures 1.22:1 light and 1.50:1 dark (in dark a fill above the page on the 2026-11-03 warm-ink ramp, not a recess), which is quiet enough that a page of skeletons can read as blank rather than loading. Whether a placeholder should be louder than a well is a design decision this component inherited by reusing the well.
knownGaps: Table composes this component for its loading body, passing h-2.5 for its denser row. It did not at first: it drew its own static bars, and the reason recorded was that a pulsing bar cannot have a reproducible visual baseline. That reason no longer holds — the visual harness pauses infinite animations at their first keyframe rather than banning them — so the two placeholder treatments are now one. The remaining difference is height, which is a real difference: a table row is not a line of body text.

There is no `lines` or `variant` prop, so a paragraph of three bars is three elements at the call site. That is the intended trade — see props.className — but it does mean a repeated pattern has no name yet. If one earns a name it belongs in blocks/, composed from this, not as a prop on it.
aria-hidden is a default rather than an invariant, so a caller can remove it. Nothing stops them announcing a wall of placeholders; the doc is the only thing saying not to.

The pulse is not synchronised across instances. Several skeletons mounted at different times breathe out of phase, which is visible in a list that streams in. CSS animations start on element creation and there is no shared clock without JavaScript.

The default width is `w-full`, so it needs a parent with a resolved width. Inside a shrink-to-fit parent — a bare flex item, an inline-block, a Storybook Docs cell — `w-full` is circular and an empty div collapses to nothing, which is the same 0px box the default height exists to prevent, arriving down the other axis. The browser test mounts into a fixed 200px container for exactly this reason. If a skeleton renders at zero width, look at its parent before looking at the component; `w-32` or a sized parent both fix it.

The visual baseline captures the pulse PAUSED at its first keyframe. That is deliberate and is what let Skeleton have a baseline at all — `stable()` in the visual harness used to await `animation.finished`, which never resolves for a loop, so any looping frame hung the suite. What a baseline can therefore prove about this component is its fill, radius and rhythm, never its motion; `skeleton.browser.test.tsx` covers that instead.

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

Table's loading body composes the Skeleton component instead of drawing its own bar. It drew a static `block h-2.5 rounded-sm bg-sunken` span, and the recorded reason for it being static rather than pulsing was that a visual baseline has to be reproducible. That reason no longer holds: the visual harness pauses infinite animations at their first keyframe rather than banning them, so a pulsing bar is now as reproducible as a still one — and the proof is that Table's baseline did not move by a single pixel, because frame zero of the pulse is full opacity, which is exactly what the static bar was. The library therefore stops having two placeholder treatments for one idea. The remaining difference is height, which is a real one and is passed at the call site: h-2.5 for a dense table row rather than Skeleton's 16px body-text default. Widths still ripple deterministically by row and column.

migration.manual: Table now requires the `skeleton` item — `npx @bydiorama/ui add table` pulls it in. Nothing renders differently at rest; the bars breathe while loading where they previously sat still.

changes.summary: --ui-duration-loop (2000ms) joins the contract — the only duration token describing a REPEAT rather than a journey, which is why it sits an order of magnitude above the rest, whose longest is 400ms for an entrance. It exists because Skeleton was pulsing at Tailwind's built-in 2s: a hard-coded duration hiding inside a utility NAME, where check:motion cannot see it and no brand can reach it. Skeleton keeps `animate-pulse` for its keyframes and takes the timing back with `[animation-duration:var(--ui-duration-loop)]` and `[animation-timing-function:var(--ui-ease-default)]`. The override is only worth anything if it wins the cascade — an arbitrary property losing to the `animation` shorthand would leave the token decorative and every gate still green — so motion.browser.test.tsx asserts the computed animation-duration EQUALS the resolved token. The reduced-motion override deliberately leaves this at 2000ms rather than collapsing it to 1ms like the others: 1ms would make a loop spin a thousand times a second rather than stop it, and a keyframe is stopped by the `motion-safe:` guard ADR 0018 requires, not by its duration. The VALUE is still a question for the sheet — 2000ms is Tailwind's number, kept because it is a reasonable loading rhythm and nothing had measured an alternative — but its home is no longer.

migration.manual: New token, additive. Re-emit your token CSS (`pnpm tokens`) before updating Skeleton, or its pulse resolves against an undefined variable and does not animate at all.

changes.summary: Skeleton — a placeholder standing in for content that has not arrived. The smallest component in the library on purpose: one div, no props of its own, sized entirely from the outside with className, which keeps it shape-compatible with shadcn/ui's Skeleton so a consumer's intuition transfers. A `lines` or `variant` vocabulary was considered and rejected: every version of it re-describes the layout the skeleton is standing in for, and that layout is already written beside it, so a shape is composed at the call site instead. Three things it does that shadcn's does not, each closing a real failure. It defaults to h-4 w-full, because a className-sized placeholder rendered without one is a 0px box and a component that draws nothing reads as broken rather than as loading. It fills with --ui-bg-sunken, the same recessed well Table's internal loading bars, AspectRatio, Thumbnail and Avatar already use, rather than inventing a placeholder role. And it is aria-hidden by default, because a screen reader announcing a dozen empty boxes says nothing anyone can act on — the announcement belongs on the region as aria-busy, which only the caller can place. That attribute is set BEFORE the prop spread rather than after, the one deliberate exception to the CONVENTIONS section 5 contract-props-win rule, so a caller standing one skeleton in for one named thing can label it; the browser test asserts the escape hatch so a tidy-up cannot silently remove it. The pulse is motion-safe:animate-pulse — required rather than stylistic, since a keyframe carries its own timing and the token layer's duration collapse cannot reach it (ADR 0018). BUILT WITHOUT A DESIGN SPEC: design/paper/README.md lists Skeleton among the sheets still to be drawn, so all five needsDesign entries are open questions rather than defects, including the one the library cannot answer for itself — Table's bars are 10px and static where this is 16px and pulsing, which is two placeholder treatments for one idea, recorded rather than hidden.

migration.manual: New item; nothing to migrate. `npx @bydiorama/ui add skeleton` installs ui/skeleton.tsx and its doc. Note it does NOT replace Table's loading body, which draws its own bars on the lane widths its header defines.

items.name: slider
items.title: Slider
items.lead: Adjusts a value along a track.

docs.lead: Adjusts a value along a track.
docs.name: Slider
docs.summary: A single-value slider in three shapes: a TRACK in four heights (8/16/24/32px) with a gradient fill, optional steppers and a value-control slot; an INLINE bar (32/40/48px) with the label and value inside it, for dense panels; and a BALANCE slider whose fill grows from an origin toward the thumb, between two named poles. Pointer capture, keyboard stepping, RTL and touch come from the Base UI behaviour layer (ADR 0012). Two thumbs are RangeSlider.

anatomy.notes: The group, and where className lands. Named so an effect can reach a part from it (ADR 0022): fx("aurora") on a track Slider paints its fill. Before 2026-11-06 this slot named the header row, and the root had none.
Track only. The row above the track holding the label and, with hasValueText, the value; carries data-size.

Names the control. Wired to the INPUT, not just the group — see a11y. Track: body-sm, --ui-text-muted, above the track. Inline: inside the bar at the start, --ui-text-secondary (muted measures 4.1:1 on the hover wash), truncating with an ellipsis.
The current value — formatValue's text when given. Tabular figures, so it does not shimmer under a drag. Track: shown with hasValueText. Inline: always shown, at the bar's end; it never truncates.

The pointer target and the hover group: anywhere on it lifts the thumb, because a press anywhere moves it. Track: padded ONLY at sm and md, each to exactly 24px; inset by half a thumb. Inline: IS the bar — --ui-bg-elevated, radius-md, overflow clip, and it carries the focus ring.
Track only. Holds the steppers, the track and the value control. Present whether or not the steppers are, so the track does not change shape when they appear.
Track: --ui-bg-sunken, a pill at sm/md/lg and radius-md at xl, so it matches the 32px controls it shares a row with. Inline: the bar's whole box, unpainted.

Track: --ui-gradient-accent from the start to the value, rounded on its LEADING edge only — a trailing radius would curve away from the thumb and leave a crescent of bare track. With an origin: from the origin to the value, square at both ends, the ramp mirrored below the origin so it deepens toward the thumb. Inline: the flat --ui-bg-accent-subtle wash (a gradient behind text puts it on two grounds), stepping to --ui-bg-accent-subtle-hover on hover and drag.

Only with `origin`. Track: a 2px --ui-border-default tick, the track's height plus space-xs above and below, above the fill and below the thumb — so at the origin its ends show above and below the thumb. Inline: two 2x6 notches on the bar's top and bottom edges, so it never reads as a second handle or crosses the label.

Contains the native input[type=range] that IS the control. Track: 16/16/24px circles and a 16x32 pill at xl; --ui-bg-base with a 2px --ui-bg-accent-legible ring and --ui-shadow-sm, lifting to --ui-shadow-md on hover and drag. Inline: a 2px handle, the bar minus 8 above and below, --ui-border-strong stepping to --ui-text-primary.

Track only, with startLabel / endLabel: caption under the track's ends, aligned to the control's edges. --ui-text-muted; the pole the value leans toward (relative to the origin) turns --ui-text-primary. Parts: slider-pole-start, slider-pole-end, each with data-leaning.
Optional, track only. The shared 32px chrome control; steps down by one `step`.
Optional, track only. Steps up by one `step`.
Inline only. The row holding label and value, laid over the bar with pointer-events: none so every press reaches the bar. Inset 8 / 12 / 16 by size.

docs.composition:
Slider
├─ label            string (required) — the accessible name
├─ value? / defaultValue?   number — one thumb, so a number, never an array
├─ onValueChange?   (value: number) => void
├─ min? / max? / step?
├─ formatValue?     (value: number) => string — shown AND announced
├─ getAriaValueText? (value: number) => string — overrides the announcement only
├─ origin?          number — the fill grows from here; makes it bipolar
├─ variant?         "track" (default)
│  ├─ size?         sm (8) | md (16) | lg (24) | xl (32, squared)
│  ├─ startLabel? / endLabel?  string — the poles, under the track
│  ├─ hasSteppers?  boolean — requires decrementLabel AND incrementLabel
│  └─ valueControl? ReactElement
└─ variant="inline"
   └─ size?         sm (32) | md (40) | lg (48) — no steppers, poles or value control

label.notes: Required — a slider with no name announces only a number.

value.notes: Controlled. A NUMBER, not an array: Base UI models one and many thumbs with the same type, and a one-thumb control should never make a caller destructure. Uncontrolled works too — the value is held internally either way, which is what lets the steppers, the origin fill and the leaning pole follow the thumb.

onValueChange.notes: Narrowed from Base UI's number | number[]. Also fires when the origin detent snaps a released value onto the origin.

step.notes: Keyboard stepping, pointer snapping and the origin's detent radius all honour it.

variant.notes: inline puts the label and value inside a field-height bar with a 2px handle, for panels of many settings. It takes sm/md/lg on the field ladder (32/40/48); xl, steppers, poles and the value control are track-only, and the type refuses them on inline.

size.notes: Track: 8/16/24/32px. xl is the control-row height and squares off to radius-md, because the sheet draws it beside a 32px Select. Inline: sm | md | lg only.

origin.notes: Where the fill starts; defaults to min. Inside the range it makes the slider bipolar — a sentiment slider between two poles: the origin mark is drawn, the fill runs from it toward the thumb (mirrored below it), and a POINTER released within one step of it lands on it. Keyboard steps are never snapped, or the step beside the origin could not be reached. Clamped to min/max.

startLabel.notes: Track only. The start pole — 'Casual'. Drawn under the track's start in caption, --ui-text-muted, turning --ui-text-primary when the value leans that way. Usable without an origin as plain endpoint labels.

formatValue.notes: The value as words or with its unit — 'Mostly formal', '12 px', '45°'. Shown in the value slot AND written to aria-valuetext, so what is seen and what is heard cannot drift. A balance slider should always pass one: 70 means nothing between Casual and Formal.

getAriaValueText.notes: Overrides formatValue for the ANNOUNCEMENT only, when what is heard should differ from what is shown ('12 px' shown, '12 pixels' heard). Without either, a screen reader announces the bare number. Restated as (value) => string rather than Base UI's (formattedValue, value, index): one thumb has no index.

hasValueText.notes: Track only — inline always shows its value, because with no thumb the number is the readout.

hasSteppers.notes: Track only. Renders the -/+ pair from the shared chrome control. They step by one `step` from where the thumb is and clamp to min/max — the same arithmetic the keyboard performs. Each is disabled at its end of the range.

decrementLabel.notes: REQUIRED with hasSteppers, by the type. Two icon-only buttons with no name announce as 'button, button', and the component cannot write the words: it has no i18n runtime (§9) and does not know what is being stepped.

valueControl.notes: Track only. Slot, never wrapped (§3). The sheet puts a Select showing the value here. It is a slot rather than a built-in because the options and their formatting are the caller's data.

isDisabled.notes: Every text --ui-text-disabled, the fill --ui-bg-field-chrome-disabled, the thumb ring --ui-border-subtle with no shadow; inline's bar --ui-bg-field-disabled. cursor: not-allowed.

do: Give every slider a label; it becomes the accessible name.
Set a step that matches the quantity — a slider that reports 62.4718 is worse than one that reports 62.
Use hasValueText whenever the value is not visible elsewhere; a track alone does not say where it is.
Use variant="inline" for a panel of many numeric settings, stacked 4px apart (space-xs).
Give a balance slider an origin, both poles and a formatValue — the poles name the axis, the words say where on it the value sits.
dont: Do not use this for a range — that is RangeSlider.
Do not use a balance slider for a quantity. If the middle means 'half done' rather than 'neither', it is a plain track.
Do not shrink the control to the painted track — the 8px size keeps a 24px target on purpose (SC 2.5.8).
Do not remove the thumb's ring; white on the sheet's pale blue-80 measures 1.51:1 without it.
Do not pass a Select's data to the Slider — compose it into valueControl instead.

a11y.role: slider, IMPLICIT: Base UI renders a native input[type=range] inside the thumb rather than a div with role=slider. Querying [role="slider"] finds nothing, which is the point — the implicit role and its keyboard behaviour come from the platform.
a11y.name: The `label` prop, via aria-labelledby on BOTH the group and the thumb. Naming only the group leaves the input itself unnamed — found in review, because the group's name does not name the control inside it.
a11y.value: aria-valuenow is the number. formatValue (or getAriaValueText, which wins for the announcement) adds aria-valuetext on the same input, which screen readers announce in its place — so a balance slider says "Mostly formal" instead of "70". The poles are visible text only; the descriptor is what carries the position.
a11y.focus: The ring is drawn on the THUMB for the track variant and on the BAR for inline. Base UI focuses the native input inside the thumb, never the thumb div, so the ring keys off `:has(:focus-visible)` — a `focus-visible:` utility on the div never matched, and the ring was declared and never painted until 2026-11-03. The focused thumb keeps --ui-shadow-sm under the ring; the hover lift is suppressed while focused.

keyboard.does: Step by `step`. Asserted in Chromium.

keyboard.key: Shift + Arrow / Page Up / Page Down
keyboard.does: Step by ten.
Jump to min and max — the part a hand-rolled slider usually omits. On a balance slider these are the two poles.
Focuses the thumb's input; the ring draws on the thumb (track) or the bar (inline).

a11y.target: Track: padded only where the track needs it — sm (8px) gains py-sm and md (16px) gains py-xs, both reaching exactly 24px; lg (24) and xl (32) already clear the floor. Inline: the whole 32/40/48px bar is the target, label and value included.

contrastPairs.role: the THUMB's ring against the track — the thumb is what identifies the control and marks the value, so this is the pair SC 1.4.11 turns on
the thumb's ring against the thumb's own white fill — a ring that vanishes into the thumb identifies nothing either

contrastPairs.why: Stands in for the --ui-gradient-accent fill, which check:contrast cannot measure because a gradient is not a pair of roles. The ramp is the sheet's own blue-80 into blue-70 and is deliberately pale: measured 1.24:1 and 1.80:1 against the track in light. It is a SECONDARY cue, not the one the control is identified by — the thumb ring above carries conformance, and packages/tokens/src/resolve.test.ts asserts it for every stress brand.

contrastPairs.role: the INLINE handle on the filled side of the bar — with no thumb, it is the mark that shows the value
the inline handle on the empty side of the bar (and flush against it at 0)
the inline handle on hover and drag, against the hover wash

contrastPairs.why: The inline wash against the empty bar: 1.12:1 in light, the same quiet step the reference draws. The handle carries the value (the two pairs above), and the value is also printed as text.
The origin mark. It says where 'neither' is; the descriptor (aria-valuetext and the visible value) and the leaning pole say which way the value leans, so the mark identifies no state on its own.

contrastPairs.role: the inline label over the filled part of the bar
the inline label over the hover wash — why it is secondary and not muted
the inline label over the empty part of the bar
the inline value over the wash (at high values)
the inline value over the empty bar
the value text, and the leaning pole
the label, and the pole the value does not lean toward

needsDesign: The fill's ramp measures 1.24:1 and 1.80:1 against the track in light. Shipped AS DRAWN, on the designer's instruction to preserve the gradients: the thumb identifies the control and its ring is floored at 3:1. Still wants a recorded yes — the sheet's Gaps row is 'Derived', not 'Decided'.
Balance has no key back to the origin — Home and End go to the poles. The sheet leaves it open (none, or Delete resets).

Inline departs from the Blueprint reference twice, on purpose: a handle at rest (the bar has no other drag affordance) and the accent wash instead of grey (no neutral role pair reaches a visible step on --ui-bg-elevated without a new role). The sheet asks whether a neutral version is wanted.
knownGaps: CLOSED 2026-11-03 by the warm-ink dark ramp (ADR 0008 amendment): the empty track (--ui-bg-sunken) measured 1.10:1 on --ui-bg-surface in dark and all but vanished. In dark sunken is now a fill above the surface, #383531 on #1E1B18 at 1.41:1 — past the at-least-1.3 the gap asked for. Light is unchanged at 1.19:1.

CLOSED 2026-11-03 by the warm-ink dark ramp (ADR 0008 amendment): the disabled thumb body (--ui-bg-base #171411) and the disabled fill (--ui-bg-field-chrome-disabled #2A2724) were both #423E3A on the old mid-grey page, and read as no thumb. They now measure 1.24:1 apart.
No tick marks, named steps or vertical orientation. None is drawn.
No typed entry on the inline bar (double-click to edit). Compose a field into valueControl on a track slider instead.

The steppers are plain buttons rather than a NumberField: they change the slider's own value, so the slider stays the single source of it. A caller wanting a typable number field should compose one into valueControl and drive both from the same state.
RTL: positions use inline-start, but the gradient fill and its mirroring are drawn left-to-right; nothing has been checked in an RTL layout.
docs.motion: Transitions only, at --ui-duration-fast with --ui-ease-out: the thumb's box-shadow (the hover/drag lift and the focus ring settling), the inline handle's border-color and the inline wash's background-color. POSITIONS are never transitioned — the thumb, handle and fill track the pointer and the arrow keys directly, because interpolating there would put the control behind the input driving it. The leaning pole is a colour swap with no transition: a static cue, not motion.
