changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

Slider's ROOT now carries data-slot="slider", like every other control's, so an effect applied through className can reach its parts (ADR 0022: `fx("aurora")` paints the track fill). The header row above the track, which held that slot name without being documented, is now data-slot="slider-header". Both are in slider.doc.ts's anatomy.

migration.manual: A selector or test that targeted the header row by [data-slot="slider"] — the label and value line above a track Slider — now targets [data-slot="slider-header"]. [data-slot="slider"] now matches the whole control. Copies of slider.tsx: add "data-slot": "slider" to BaseSlider.Root's props and rename the header row's slot.

changes.summary: Slider's keyboard focus ring was declared and never painted. Base UI focuses the native input[type=range] INSIDE the thumb, never the thumb div, so `focus-visible:shadow-(--ui-focus-ring)` on the div matched nothing — every gate was green because the class resolved and the token existed, and no test had ever focused a slider and looked. The thumb now keys off `has-focus-visible:` (and so does the forced-colors outline), keeping --ui-shadow-sm beneath the ring as the sheet draws it. The same mistake hid the disabled ring: `disabled:` on a div never matches, so it now keys off Base UI's data-disabled. The group also carries aria-disabled when disabled, so its label and value read as parts of a disabled control rather than as low-contrast text. Probed: the browser test fails against the shipped class with no focus colour in the computed shadow. Paper: https://app.paper.design/file/01KZ39A2BC286MT85M658NRR4R/p-Z-0 (Component --- Slider --- Revision / Variants / Dark / API, Behaviour, Tokens, Gaps). Consumers with a copied slider.tsx should take the thumb class.

Slider grows to the redrawn sheet. variant="inline" puts the label and value inside a field-height bar (32/40/48, sm/md/lg) with a 2px --ui-border-strong handle, the flat --ui-bg-accent-subtle wash as the fill and the focus ring on the bar — xl, steppers, poles and the value control are typed `never` on it. origin makes a slider bipolar: the fill runs from an origin mark toward the thumb (the gradient mirrored below it), a POINTER released within one step lands on the origin (keyboard never snaps), and startLabel / endLabel draw the poles, the leaning one in --ui-text-primary. formatValue is shown in the value slot AND written to aria-valuetext; getAriaValueText still overrides the announcement only. The thumb lifts to --ui-shadow-md on hover and drag (exclusive with the focus ring by construction), the value uses tabular figures, and disabled text takes --ui-text-disabled. The value is now held internally (useControllableState), which closes the knownGap where steppers stopped after one step on an uncontrolled slider. SLIDER_SIZE and sliderThumbClass are exported for RangeSlider. --ui-border-strong on --ui-bg-accent-subtle and on --ui-bg-elevated join NONTEXT_CONTRAST_PAIRS (4.79 / 5.36 light, 3.37 / 5.67 dark). Geometry: design/paper/specs/slider.geometry.json (inline bar). No API removed; Image Edit unchanged. Paper: https://app.paper.design/file/01KZ39A2BC286MT85M658NRR4R/p-Z-0 (Component --- Slider --- Revision / Variants / Dark / API, Behaviour, Tokens, Gaps).

cn's tailwind-merge config registered the stroke widths (hairline, thick) for the physical sides only. `border-s-thick` was read as a side COLOUR and deleted by the next border colour in the same list — Slider's inline handle rendered 0px wide with every gate green, found by its browser test. border-w-s and border-w-e are now registered; cn.test pins both. Probed: the cn test fails with the line removed.

New item range-slider: two thumbs on one track, the fill the flat --ui-bg-accent span between them. Everything visible is Slider's, read from Slider's own SLIDER_SIZE table and thumb class, and the browser test compares the two per size so they cannot drift. Three things differ: the value is a readonly [number, number] tuple; each thumb is its own input named by a REQUIRED startThumbLabel / endThumbLabel (aria-label — an aria-labelledby would outrank it); and the thumbs may meet but never cross (thumbCollisionBehavior none, minStepsBetweenValues). Only the moving or hovered thumb lifts. The readout (on by default) joins formatValue's ends with a spaced en dash and collapses equal ends. Probed: the drag test fails with Base UI's default `push` (end thumb shoved to 1990); the keyboard path cannot see the collision rule at all. Paper: https://app.paper.design/file/01KZ39A2BC286MT85M658NRR4R/p-Z-0 (Component --- Slider --- Revision / Variants / Dark / API, Behaviour, Tokens, Gaps).

Slider takes `getAriaValueText?: (value: number) => string`, written to aria-valuetext on the thumb's native input. Closes #25. Five 0-100 brand-voice sliders with named poles (Casual to Formal) announced "Formality, 70", which means nothing without the poles; folding the poles into the label named the control but still read the value as a bare number. The text goes on the INPUT because that is the element carrying the slider role, so a valuetext anywhere else would be announced by nothing. Restated in our own shape rather than Base UI's `(formattedValue, value, index)`: one thumb has no index, and the pre-formatted string is the locale formatting a caller writing this function is replacing. check:boundaries stays green. The doc's knownGaps entry for valuetext is removed. The browser test reads aria-valuetext off the input at the default, after Home and after End, and asserts the function is called with one numeric argument.

check:motion joins the gate list, and every animating component now documents its motion. The gate rejects a literal duration or easing in registry/ (a discipline that was already perfect — zero hard-coded durations across 26 files — and had nothing keeping it that way), transition-all (CONVENTIONS section 6 has said this since the beginning and nothing enforced it), a keyframe with no reduced-motion guard, and an animating component with no top-level motion: note in its doc. It reads lib recipes alongside components as check:overlays does, so Header's motion is found in @/lib/chrome-control where it actually lives rather than reported as absent. 27 doc files gain a motion: note describing what moves, what drives it and what reduced motion does to it; Sheet's and ImageUpload's existing notes are PROMOTED out of a11y to the top level, where Button already had its, because motion is a description of what a component does rather than solely an accessibility concern and a field meaning one thing at two depths stops being findable. ImageUpload's note is corrected while being promoted: it credited the token layer with stopping its spinner, and what actually stops it is the motion-safe: variant. Two findings are recorded in the notes rather than fixed: Sidebar's collapsible section snaps via the hidden attribute where Accordion animates the identical interaction against Base UI's published height, and Banner reaches for transition-colors where the rest of the library enumerates properties. No component's rendered motion changes; no .tsx is touched.

migration.manual: Documentation only — every change is inside a *.doc.ts, and no component's classes or rendered motion moved. If you consume the doc files and read `a11y.motion`, it has moved to the top-level `motion` key on Sheet and ImageUpload; Button was already there and the other 27 are new.

changes.summary: Slider's steppers take optional `decrementIcon` / `incrementIcon` slots, defaulting to the existing −/+. A stepper's MARK depends on what is being stepped, not only its label: Image Edit steps a rotation, where the two ends are counter-clockwise and clockwise rather than less and more, and the sheet draws curved arrows there. The labels already varied for exactly that reason; this is the visual half of the same fact. Additive — every existing Slider renders unchanged.

migration.manual: Additive. Pass `decrementIcon`/`incrementIcon` alongside `hasSteppers` to replace the −/+ glyphs; omit them and nothing changes.

changes.summary: Slider refactored against the redrawn sheet, which grew from one section to six. BREAKING, twice over. `size` is now sm | md | lg | xl (8/16/24/32px tracks) where it was lg | sm (20/8px): `lg` still exists but now means 24px rather than 20, and the DEFAULT moved from lg to md, so a slider with no size prop goes from a 20px track to a 16px one. Both changes come from the sheet, which draws 8/16/24 and no 20 anywhere. `xl` is the fourth thing it draws and behaves differently on purpose: a 32px bar squared off to radius-md rather than a pill, because the sheet only uses it in a row with 32px steppers and a Select, and a pill beside a soft-cornered control reads as a different family — the same argument Button's per-size radius makes. NEW: the fill is a gradient (--ui-gradient-accent) rather than a flat --ui-bg-accent-legible, which is the sheet's clearest new idea, and it ships with the sheet's own stops — see the token entry for the SC 1.4.11 argument that rests on the thumb rather than the fill. NEW: hasSteppers renders the -/+ pair from the shared chrome control, stepping by one `step` and clamping to min/max — the same arithmetic the keyboard already performs, so the two cannot disagree, and each button disables at its end of the range. decrementLabel and incrementLabel are REQUIRED with it by the type, the isIconOnly/aria-label shape: two icon-only buttons with no name announce as 'button, button' and the component cannot write the words. NEW: valueControl is a SLOT for the Select the sheet puts beside the track. A slot rather than a built-in because the options and their formatting are the caller's data — a Slider that owned an `items` prop would be two components in one (§3). The thumb keeps --ui-bg-accent-legible for its ring: the sheet's raw blue-80 puts the white thumb at 1.51:1 against its own ring, which is the value this component already moved away from once. The thumb is also four SHAPES rather than one scaled four ways — a 16px circle at sm and md, 24px at lg, and at xl a 32x16 VERTICAL PILL spanning the bar, which is what makes that row read as a bar with a grip instead of a track with a dot. It shipped as a 20px circle first, from reading the sheet's placeholder frame instead of the handle, and is now asserted per size. The control is padded only where the track is under 24px (sm gains py-sm, md py-xs, both reaching exactly 24); a flat pad on all four made three rows 16px taller than the sheet draws them, invisibly, because the 32px steppers centre inside whatever height the row has.

migration.manual: REQUIRED: audit every <Slider>. A slider with no `size` changes from a 20px track to 16px — pass size="lg" for the nearest larger track (24px) or accept the new default. A slider passing size="lg" keeps compiling and grows from 20px to 24px, which is the one change that will NOT announce itself, so grep for it. The fill changes from a flat colour to a gradient; anything asserting `backgroundColor` on [data-slot="slider-fill"] now reads rgba(0, 0, 0, 0) and must read backgroundImage instead. Steppers require a controlled slider: they read `value ?? defaultValue` and call onValueChange, so an uncontrolled slider steps once from its default and then stops — recorded in the doc's knownGaps.

changes.summary: Three defects found by looking at the built Storybook. (1) ImageEdit drew the picture TWICE — dimmed across the stage and again inside the crop — and the two could never align: each was object-contain inside a different box (384x260 against 240x168), so they resolved to different scales and offsets, and rotating showed both quads at once. Now one image, with the crop dimming everything outside it via a box-shadow whose spread exceeds the stage; that also follows border-radius, so the circular mask gets a circular hole for free. (2) Slider's thumb overhung the track at both extremes, because Base UI centres it on the value — at the minimum half of it sat outside the track and inside the 8px gap to the stepper button. The control is now inset by half a thumb, so the thumb's OUTER edge lands on the control's edge and the track it travels is the track it paints. Reported against Image Edit; it was every slider at 0 and at 100. (3) Thumbnail gains isLoading — a centred CSS spinner on the well, with the withheld, announced as role=status named after the file. Thumbnail.Group's stacked spread now eases out over --ui-duration-slow to a ZERO gap rather than snapping to +4px on the standard curve: half the travel, and all the interaction needs, since what the overlap hides is the next tile's top-right corner where the remove control sits.

migration.manual: Slider renders slightly differently at every size: the track is inset by half a thumb (8px each side; 12px at lg), so a track measures 16-24px narrower than before and the thumb no longer overhangs. No API change. Thumbnail's `isLoading` is additive and defaults to false.

changes.summary: A crop stage with zoom and optional rotation, in the sheet's two shapes. The crop WINDOW is fixed and the image moves behind it, which is what the sheet actually draws — the corner marks are decoration, and the circular avatar row has none because a round crop cannot deliver the rectangle a corner handle promises. It is the body of a dialog rather than the dialog: Modal supplies the surface, title, close and footer. Four fixes: the stage is --ui-bg-media rather than --ui-bg-emphasis, which IS the accent and resolves to #ffe066 under a pale-yellow brand seed; both adjustments are the Slider component rather than the sheet's hand-drawn track, whose fill measured 1.24:1 and whose knob edge measured 1.76:1 against the track; Cancel is Button variant=outline (3.11:1) rather than the drawn --ui-border-default (2.14:1); and the sheet draws NO keyboard path for the crop at all, so arrow keys pan the image with Shift for a coarse step, announced through an sr-only hint on the stage. That last one is an invention and is recorded as mine under needsDesign.

migration.manual: New item — nothing to migrate. `npx shadcn add @bydiorama/image-edit`; it pulls in `cn`, `slider` and `use-controllable-state`, and expects react and griddy-icons as peers.

changes.summary: Slider — a single-value control in two track heights (20/8px), on the Base UI behaviour layer. Pointer capture, keyboard stepping, Home/End, RTL and touch are each individually easy to get almost right and their near-misses only surface for someone on a keyboard or a screen reader, which is precisely what ADR 0012 exists for. The value is narrowed to a NUMBER: Base UI models one and many thumbs with the same number | number[] type, and a one-thumb control should never make a caller destructure an array. Two defects found by the browser suite rather than by reading. First, the accessible name was not wired: Base UI renders a native input[type=range] INSIDE the thumb, and naming the surrounding group does not name that input — aria-labelledby now goes on both. Second, the 24px target assertion failed at the small size, because py-xs around an 8px track yields 16px; the control is padded to py-sm so the affordance stays thin while the target stays legal (SC 2.5.8). Also worth recording: querying [role="slider"] finds nothing, because the role is IMPLICIT on the native input — which is the point of using one. Design defects corrected: the fill used --ui-blue-80 and the thumb --ui-neutral-100, both palette steps, and the thumb shadow was a raw hex.

migration.manual: New peer dependency on @base-ui-components/react, the same range Popover, Modal and Multiselect declare.

docs.name: Sparkline
docs.summary: An inline, axis-free trend in one of the eight categorical data slots: a line, an area or columns, at 160×40 or 120×32. One image to assistive technology, named by `label` and described by a required, person-written `description` — the one chart allowed to ship without a data table (ADR 0023 §4).

anatomy.notes: role=img, aria-label from `label`, aria-describedby the description. className lands here (§5). Carries data-variant, data-size and data-series.
An sr-only span holding `description`. Inside the root so it travels with it; referenced, not rendered.
The SVG. aria-hidden: its paths say nothing the description does not.
variant=area only. The slot's own -bg wash, closed to the bottom edge.
2px (--ui-stroke-thick), round caps and joins, the slot's -solid ink.
A 6px disc in bg-surface under the end dot, so the dot separates from the line it ends.
The latest value: a 4px dot in the slot's -solid ink. Alone and centred for a one-point series.
variant=column. 8px wide at most, 2px surface gap, 4px radius at the data end, standing on zero.
isLoading. bg-sunken, radius-sm, the full box — height is reserved so a row of tiles never jumps.

docs.composition:
Sparkline
├─ data           number[] (required) — oldest first; NaN and ±Infinity dropped
├─ label          string (required) — the accessible name: what is measured
├─ description    string (required) — the takeaway, in words
├─ variant?       line | area | column
├─ series?        1…8 — the categorical slot
├─ size?          md (160×40) | sm (120×32) | xs (64×20)
├─ domain?        [min, max] — share one across a column of sparklines
├─ hasEndMarker?  default true (line, area)
└─ isLoading?

data.notes: Oldest first, evenly spaced. Non-finite values are DROPPED rather than drawn at zero — plotting NaN at the baseline states a value nobody measured.

label.notes: Names what is measured. Not shown: a sparkline sits beside a label the layout already draws, and drawing it twice is noise.

description.notes: Required by the type, because it is what replaces the data table every other chart must ship. Write the takeaway a reader should leave with ('Rose 12% since January, peaking in October'), not 'a sparkline'.

variant.notes: All three are on the sheet. Columns stand on ZERO, never on the minimum: a column's length is its value.

series.notes: The ordinal data slot (--ui-data-cat-N). Use the slot this series has in the full chart it summarises, so colour keeps meaning one thing across a screen. Not `slot`: that is a global HTML attribute.

size.notes: 160×40 and 120×32, the two sizes the sheet draws, and xs 64×20 for a table row's trend (the library's own reading; see needsDesign). Fixed, not fluid: a stretched sparkline exaggerates its own slope.

hasEndMarker.notes: The ringed dot on the latest value. On by default because a trend that does not mark where it ends does not say where it is now. Ignored for columns.

domain.notes: Line and area: the value range the height spans. Default is the series' own min–max, which stretches any wobble to full height — right alone, wrong in a column of sparklines, where a flat 12 ↔ 13 draws like a crash beside a real one. Pass ONE domain to every sparkline in the column — only when the rows share a unit (an index, a share); raw volumes of very different sizes would flatten every small row, and those want their own range. Widened to hold every value, so it never clips. Columns ignore it: they stand on zero.

isLoading.notes: Reserves the box with a sunken skeleton and sets aria-busy. The name and description stay, so a screen reader is not handed a nameless busy image.

do: Put the number the sparkline supports next to it in text; the line shows shape, not value.
Give the sparkline the same series slot its series has in the full chart.
Write the description as the sentence you would say aloud about the trend.
dont: Do not use a sparkline where the reader needs to read values — use a chart with axes and a table.
Do not stretch it to fill a column; pick the size that fits.
Do not reuse a slot for a different series elsewhere on the same screen.
Do not put two series in one sparkline. It has no legend, so the second series would be told apart by colour alone.

a11y.role: img on the root, named by aria-label and described by aria-describedby; the SVG is aria-hidden.
a11y.name: `label`. The description is `description`, required by the type.

keyboard.does: Not focusable. A sparkline is output, not a control, and it ships no handlers.

contrastPairs.role: the line, dot and columns on a card (every slot 1–8 is audited on base and surface in NONTEXT_CONTRAST_PAIRS)
the same marks on the page

forwarding.className: root
forwarding.ref: root (an HTMLDivElement)
forwarding.rest: root — every HTML attribute except role and children, which the component owns

needsDesign: The xs size (64×20) for a trend inside a table row: the library's reading of the stand-in screen's keyword column. The sheet draws 160×40 and 120×32 only; at 20px the end marker's 6px ring leaves an 8px band for the line, which may want a smaller marker. Drawn from code on the Rules, shares, dots and bins sheet (Gaps: Derived).
knownGaps: The marker ring is painted bg-surface, as drawn. On bg-base (the page) it shows as a faint disc in light; a ground-following ring needs a token or a mask, and the sheet never drew the page case.

The area wash uses the slot's -bg role (14%) where the sheet types opacity 0.1 on the shape. The sheet's own Gaps row asks for --ui-data-area-opacity; until that exists the -bg role is the nearest contract value.
No hover or focus value readout. Inline sparklines in the sheet are static; an interactive one belongs to the Chart primitives.
No forced-colours treatment beyond the browser's: lines and dots stay visible as system colours, which is enough for one series and is why a sparkline is limited to one.
The gradient, sheen, glow and halo variants drawn on the Effects and Gradients sheet are not built. They arrive as fx classes, not props (ADR 0023 §8).
docs.motion: None. A sparkline renders its final shape on the server and does not animate in; a new `data` array simply redraws.

contrast.role: the line, dot and columns on a card (every slot 1–8 is audited on base and surface in NONTEXT_CONTRAST_PAIRS)
the same marks on the page

changes.summary: Sparkline size="xs" is 64×20, for a trend inside a table row (the stand-in's keyword table). Every mark stays inside the box. The size is not drawn on the Paper sheet yet: recorded in needsDesign.

Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

Paper: a new 'Chart --- Rules, shares, dots and bins' sheet draws the P1 parts no sheet had (event rule, 100% stack, scatter with quadrant rules, bubbles, histogram, marker shapes 1–8, Sparkline xs), copied from the shipped components with colours mapped back to tokens, each badged Derived until a designer approves it. The Bar sheet gains 'Focus in a group': grouped, stacked and histogram marks sit 2px apart, so the focus ring 2px off a mark lands on its neighbour at 1.0–1.9:1 light and 1.9–2.9:1 dark; a 6px surface halo under the ring is proposed, not built. The Heatmap sheet's focus ring moves inside the cell (inset 2px focus ink, then a 2px surface gap), since an outside ring spilled onto neighbouring cells. The Anatomy sheet's series 2 now paints --ui-data-cat-2-solid, closing chart.doc.ts's stale --ui-data-div-neg-2 known gap; Paper's cat-1..8 bg/fg tokens are re-pushed from the repo. chart.doc.ts and sparkline.doc.ts needsDesign rows now point at the new sheet.

Sparkline takes an optional `domain` for line and area. By default each sparkline stretches its own min to max over the full height, which is right for one read alone and wrong for a column of them: in the stand-in screen's keyword table, a flat 12 ↔ 13 drew like a crash beside a real rise. Pass one domain to every sparkline in the column so their slopes compare. It is widened to hold every value, so it never clips; columns ignore it, as they stand on zero.

Charts V2 has no product screen to adopt it yet, so registry/screens/market-intelligence rebuilds the charted parts of the service portal's Market intelligence section (Overview, Share of search, Categories) from library parts only, on placeholder data, as Storybook stories under the axe pass. It maps every Recharts call site the portal has to a library part or a recorded gap (docs/charts-and-graphs-plan.md, 'V2 stand-in'), and surfaced three defects now fixed: direct labels painting past the frame, a rule label crossed by its line, and sparklines in a column exaggerating flat series. The plan's axis geometry case is added (chart-plot-column), and the geometry test now waits for a ResizeObserver re-render before measuring. The stand-in does not close V2's exit; a real screen adopting these does.

Sparkline (experimental): an inline, axis-free trend — line, area or columns at 160×40 or 120×32 — in one of the eight categorical data slots. role=img with a required label and a required person-written description, which ADR 0023 lets stand in for the data table. Server-safe and deterministic. Built on the new viz lib (pure maths, no dependency).

ADR 0023 accepts the data-visualisation layer: own chart components on pure maths (ADR 0002 gains a 'layout and scale mathematics' row), SVG as the floor for any Canvas or WebGL tier, data as props, a required description and table alternative, ordinal data slots, solid strokes, deterministic output, and the Paper effect variants as opt-in fx classes.

items.name: stat-tiles
items.title: StatTiles
items.lead: Pairs a key figure with the context needed to read it.

docs.lead: Pairs a key figure with the context needed to read it.
docs.name: StatTiles
docs.summary: A row of headline numbers in one surface frame, tiles separated by hairlines. Each tile is a label, a figure at the fixed `figure` role, a change line whose glyph says which way and whose colour says whether that is good, and an optional sparkline. A block: it composes Skeleton and takes a Sparkline element; it formats and computes nothing.

anatomy.notes: A <dl>. bg-surface, border-subtle hairline, radius-md, one frame for the whole row. className lands here.

A <div> grouping the term and its descriptions. 24px inset; hairlines between tiles that follow the wrap — a start-side line on every column after the first, a top line on the second row. Two columns: the text, and the trend aligned to the foot. aria-busy while loading.

One line only while each tile gets 280px: four tiles from 1120px of row, three from 840px. Below, two by two; a third tile spans the second row. Under 220px of tile content the trend drops under the change line, 16px clear, and the text takes the full width (sheet: Narrow row).
<dt>. label-sm at 400, muted. Stays printed while loading.
<dd>. The `figure` role — 24/30 at 600, tracking-tight — with tabular figures, primary. A 30px row, so a skeleton holds its height.

16px TrendUp / TrendDown / Minus glyph, 4px gap, the change in label-sm 600 in success or danger ink, the comparison in label-sm 400 muted. A zero change is the Minus glyph and "No change vs …", all muted.
Optional. The caller's element — a Sparkline at size sm (120×32) — at the end of the tile, aligned to the foot of the text.
value: null. The figure becomes a muted em dash and the change line becomes `emptyText` ("No reading yet"). Never a zero.

docs.composition:
StatTiles                     <dl> · two to four tiles
└─ StatTiles.Tile             label · value · delta? · trend? · isLoading?
     delta = { change, comparison, polarity?, format? }
     trend = <Sparkline size="sm" … />

StatDelta / StatFigure        the change line, and figure + change in a row (ChartCard's head)

label.notes: Tile. What is measured. Printed while loading so the frame still says what is coming.

value.notes: Tile. Already formatted ("€3,410"). `null` is no reading yet: an em dash and `emptyText`, never a fake 0.

delta.type: { change; comparison; polarity?; unit?; format?; pointsSuffix?; pointsLabel?; locale?; upLabel?; downLabel?; flatLabel? }
delta.notes: Tile. `change` is signed and, with the default percent format, a fraction (0.12). It prints unsigned — the glyph carries the sign. `comparison` is required: a change with no baseline cannot be read. Omit the whole object for a tile with no comparison; no line is drawn.

polarity.notes: Inside delta. The block reads direction from the sign and cannot know whether a rise is welcome; a cost sets down-is-good. Changes colour only, never the glyph.

trend.notes: Tile. A Sparkline size="sm". An element, so the block draws no chart of its own and the sparkline keeps its own accessible label.

isLoading.notes: Tile. The figure and change become bg-sunken skeletons (96×24, 72×12); the label stays.

emptyText.notes: Tile. Under the dash when value is null.

unit.notes: Inside delta. `points` is a change of a share, printed "2.1 pp" and spoken "2.1 percentage points" (pointsSuffix / pointsLabel): a share from 40% to 42% rose two points, not 5%, and Intl has no unit for it. `change` stays a fraction (0.021). The pp suffix is the library's own reading; no sheet draws it.

upLabel.notes: Inside delta. Spoken before the change, since the glyph is aria-hidden. With downLabel and flatLabel, the block's only strings.

do: Give every change a comparison a person can read: "vs 1971", "vs last month".
Set polarity on every tile where a rise is bad — costs, errors, wait times.
Use one row of two to four tiles; a fifth stops being a glance.
dont: Do not pass a pre-signed string as the figure's change: pass the number, so direction and colour come from one place.
Do not show a zero for a value nobody measured; pass null.
Do not colour the figure itself; the change line carries the judgement.

a11y.role: A <dl>: each tile's label is the term, its figure and change the descriptions, so a reader hears "Posters printed, 1,284, up 12% vs 1971".
a11y.name: None of its own; pass aria-label on the root when the row needs one ("Printing this year"). A Sparkline brings its own label.

keyboard.does: Nothing is focusable. A tile that should open a detail view needs a link inside it, not a click handler on the tile.

contrastPairs.role: the figure
label, comparison, empty state, the flat change
a good change and its glyph
a bad change and its glyph
the frame and the hairlines between tiles
contrastPairs.why: The tiles are separated by their own whitespace and content; the hairline groups, it carries nothing a reader needs.

forwarding.className: StatTiles: root (the <dl>). StatTiles.Tile: the tile <div>.
forwarding.ref: StatTiles: root. StatTiles.Tile: the tile.
forwarding.rest: Each to the element its className lands on.

needsDesign: Forced colours: both intent inks become CanvasText, so good and bad read the same; the glyph and the words carry the rest. Described, not drawn (sheet Gaps: Derived).
knownGaps: No tabular figures: Aspekta ships no `tnum` feature and its digits are proportional (367–602 units), so `tabular-nums` is a no-op in this face — figures right-align on their last digit but do not line up digit by digit, and a figure that changes in place changes width. Filed against the face (ADR 0011 item 5); pinned by registry/fonts/aspekta/aspekta.test.ts.

The row's thresholds are container queries on the row itself (four across from 1120px, three from 840px), so they hold in any panel; the tile's sparkline moves under the text below 220px of tile content, which is read from the tile. A label longer than the sheet's 84px text column still wraps in a tile that keeps its sparkline beside it.
The good/bad judgement is colour only for a screen reader: the direction is spoken ("Up 12%") and the polarity is not. A reader who needs it reads the label.
Label, comparison and empty text are label-sm at 400, declared as type-role deviations as Chart's ticks are.

contrast.role: the figure
label, comparison, empty state, the flat change
a good change and its glyph
a bad change and its glyph
the frame and the hairlines between tiles

changes.summary: StatDelta takes `unit="points"` for a change of share: it prints "+2.1 pp" (the suffix aria-hidden) and reads "percentage points" to assistive technology, instead of formatting the change as a relative percent. `pointsSuffix` and `pointsLabel` localise it.

The row is a container: one line only while each tile gets 280px (four from 1120px, three from 840px), else two by two with the hairlines following the wrap and a third tile spanning the second row. Each tile is a container too: under 220px of content its sparkline drops 16px under the change line. Replaces tiles shrinking side by side until their text wrapped.

Label, figure at text-figure, a change line (TrendUp / TrendDown / Minus, success or danger ink by polarity, a muted comparison), and an optional Sparkline element. A <dl>; loading, no-value and no-comparison states. Installs to components/blocks/, which every components.json already maps. Exports StatDelta and StatFigure.

The plan's axis geometry case is added (chart-plot-column), and the geometry test now waits for a ResizeObserver re-render before measuring. The gate now requires a case for every ui and block item, and both blocks have one, in both schemes. items.name: status-matrix
items.title: StatusMatrix
items.lead: Gives a running process a small, recognisable signal.

docs.lead: Gives a running process a small, recognisable signal.
docs.name: StatusMatrix
docs.summary: The dot-matrix status mark: a 5×5 screen of dots at four levels (Off, Ember, Glow, Lit) on which every state is a signal. Live states loop on one shared clock — waiting, typing, thinking, working, streaming, progress — and the endings draw once and hold: done, failed, stopped. Each tick every dot fades one level and the signal re-lights what it touches, so trails, echoes and hand-overs all fall out of one rule. It never carries a state alone: a status line in words sits beside it, or `label` names it.

anatomy.notes: The <svg>, viewBox 0 0 16 16, at 16px (md) or 14px (sm). className and ref land here (§5). Carries data-status, data-size and data-held. aria-hidden unless `label` makes it role=img.
25 circles, r=1, centres at 2 + 3n. data-level 0–3 maps to opacity 0.1 / 0.15 / 0.35 / 1. Fill is the ink of the signal that last lit the dot; an unlit dot takes the current status's ink.

docs.composition:
StatusMatrix
├─ status           waiting | typing | thinking | working | streaming | progress | done | failed | stopped
├─ value / max      progress only — value required there, refused elsewhere; max default 100
├─ size?            md (16px) | sm (14px)
├─ isHeld?          draw the key frame and keep still — every matrix but the live edge
└─ label?           an accessible name; omit when a status line sits beside it

Status line (caller-owned)
├─ StatusMatrix     status="thinking"
└─ text             "Thinking" — body-sm, muted

status.notes: Changing it hands over IN PLACE: on the next tick the outgoing figure fades a level while the incoming one lights from its own tick 0 — a one-tick lead, so there is never a beat with no figure. One matrix at every instant, never a second one or a jump.

value.notes: Progress only, and required there: a level meter that cannot say how full it is is not a meter. Read against `max`; 4% of the range lights one dot, columns fill bottom-up, left to right, and the next dot breathes.

max.notes: Progress only. The same value/max vocabulary as Progress and Meter.

size.notes: md beside a body-sm status line; sm in a step list, a lane or a dock row, where the sheet draws 14.

isHeld.notes: One matrix moves per turn — the deepest running node in a chain, the root of a parallel or folded run, the first row of a ChatRunDock — and every other matrix in that turn is held on its key frame, so the eye has one place to go. Which matrix is the live edge is a fact about the whole turn, so the caller decides it.

label.notes: Makes the matrix role=img with this name. Leave it out when a visible status line already says the state in words — the matrix is then decorative and aria-hidden.

do: Pair it with a status line in words — 'Thinking', 'Running 3 tools', 'Uploading · 48%'.
Hold every matrix in a turn but the live edge (`isHeld`).
Let a status change hand over in the same matrix: change `status`, never swap one StatusMatrix for another.
Keep settled list glyphs as icons — a finished step is a CheckCircle, a pending one a ring. The matrix's endings are for the turn's own status line.
dont: Do not use it as a generic page spinner: it is the chat run's status, and its shapes mean specific kinds of wait.
Do not animate two matrices in one turn — two moving signals compete for the same glance.
Do not use progress without a real measurement; a value that is a guess is Working.

a11y.role: Decorative by default (aria-hidden, focusable=false): the status line beside it carries the state in words, which is SC 1.4.1's requirement — the shape and the motion are never the only channel. With `label`, role=img named by it.
a11y.name: `label`, when the matrix stands alone. Otherwise the adjacent text.
a11y.forcedColors: The Off grid drops out (opacity 0) and every lit dot draws in CanvasText: the accent means nothing in that mode, and the figure alone carries the shape.

keyboard.does: Not focusable. A status mark is output, not a control.

contrastPairs.role: a Lit dot of a live status on the thread
a Lit dot of a live status on an elevated card, lane pill or dock — the ground every chat surface paints
the Done check
the Failed cross
Typing's dots and the Stopped square

forwarding.className: root (the svg)
forwarding.ref: root — an SVGSVGElement; there is no inner control
forwarding.rest: root — every SVG attribute except children, role and viewBox, which the component owns

docs.motion: A JavaScript tick, because the frames are computed rather than keyed: one shared clock steps every moving matrix on the page together, at --ui-stagger-step (100ms) divided by --ui-fx-ambient-speed — the effects layer's one knob for every ambient loop, read as 1 where that layer is not loaded — so two matrices can never beat against each other. A loop is 10 or 20 ticks — 1000ms or 2000ms at the default step. The 20-tick loop matches --ui-duration-loop at that step, but it is counted in ticks rather than read from that token, so a brand that retunes the step retunes the loop with it. The subscription lives as long as the matrix moves: a status or value change rewrites what the next tick draws instead of re-subscribing, so updates arriving faster than a tick cannot stall the clock. Each dot's opacity and fill then transition on --ui-duration-fast — Typing on --ui-duration-base — which is what turns the four discrete levels into a soft phosphor trail. The first render is the key frame (the frame the sheet draws), and motion continues from it after mount. An ending arrived at draws on — Done a cell a tick along its stroke, Failed from the centre out, Stopped in one — and then the clock lets go of it; an ending MOUNTED is already drawn. `isHeld` and prefers-reduced-motion both render the key frame and never subscribe: the clock is JavaScript, which the token layer's duration collapse cannot reach, so the component asks the media query itself. A page without --ui-stagger-step gets a still matrix rather than an invented tempo.
needsDesign: Listening (the voice variant) is on the sheet but not here: its bars should follow a real input level, and a component that takes a level per tick is a different API from a status. Built when a voice surface exists to drive it.
No 32px or 48px size: the sheet draws those as specimens only, and no composition places the matrix above 16px.
knownGaps: The level opacities (0.1 / 0.15 / 0.35 / 1) are opacity utilities rather than tokens: they are the matrix's own four-step scale and nothing else in the system shares it.
Endings are not announced. A caller that needs 'Done' read out says so in its own live region — Chat Progress's role=status is the model.

contrast.role: a Lit dot of a live status on the thread
a Lit dot of a live status on an elevated card, lane pill or dock — the ground every chat surface paints
the Done check
the Failed cross
Typing's dots and the Stopped square

changes.summary: StatusMatrix: the dot-matrix status mark — live states loop on one shared clock, endings draw once, hand-overs happen in place

Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

ChatTasks: the plan the agent works to, written, ticked off and revised in place. A chat-widget card with a disclosure header; proposed plans show numbered rows with Run / Change it and a per-row drop; running, complete and stopped plans show six row statuses (done, current, pending, needsYou, failed, skipped) and fold to a header whose glyph is the plan's status. The current task holds StatusMatrix Working's key frame — the plan never moves.

ChatSources: inline citation markers, a hover/focus preview anchored to each, and a sources block under the answer — folded to kind discs and a count, open to numbered link rows, or led by source cards. Numbers are list positions shared through ChatSources.Provider; a working StatusMatrix while sources gather; a disabled marker while the answer streams. The marker is allowlisted in check:controls as an inline pill no Button size describes.

ChatRunDock and ChatRunMark: background runs that outlive their turn. The dock sits behind the composer's pill (bg-elevated, radius-lg, inset space-xl), one 32px row per run with a 14px StatusMatrix (Progress when measured, Working otherwise), name, truncating activity, a 40px tabular clock and a named Stop; the mark is the run's line in the thread — started, finished with an action, failed with Retry, or stopped. A named region, never a toast. The rows' matrices hold while the thread has a live edge (`isHeld`), and even when the thread is idle only the FIRST row moves — one live matrix per region, however many runs.

ChatProgress gains form="typing": PEOPLE's presence, the sheet's Gaps row made real. One line — the Typing matrix at 16px in muted ink (a person, never the agent's accent), gap-sm, then a caption line in which `who` truncates and the verb never does, so the longest name gives way first. It is not progress and never competes for the turn's live edge: it is placed on the composer's top edge, never in the thread. The type refuses every run prop on it — clock, receipt, Stop, Retry, failure, disclosure, icon — and requires `who`. Placing it on the composer is the caller's for now; ChatComposer has no slot for it.

Chat Progress rebuilt on StatusMatrix with ONE moving mark per turn. The CSS ring spinner is gone. New forms: waiting and streaming status rows (the thinking row's matrix hands over in place to its ending — failed and stopped keep the same element); reasoning under a five-line capped, faded body; a thought chain on a 16px node lane with kind glyphs, chips, prose, one level of branches, a failed status with Retry and a 40px tabular clock; parallel lanes drawn as the activity pill's box (glyph, 104px name, activity, clock, chevron) that open to their own chain. Only the deepest running node moves — the root when parallel or folded, none when isHeld — and a run that finishes while mounted folds to its receipt. Stop past ~30 s and a stoppedText ending. The geometry spec now measures the lane pill (sheet 4040-0) instead of the old step list.

migration.manual: BREAKING: steps take `status: "done" | "current" | "pending" | "failed"` with optional icon, duration, chips, detail and one level of `steps`; the spinner and its data-slot are gone (the row's mark is a StatusMatrix with data-slot="status-matrix"). Pass isHeld to every ChatProgress in a turn except the live edge. Rows are 17.55px at the body-sm role's leading rather than the old 16px.

items.name: switch
items.title: Switch
items.lead: Changes a setting as soon as you turn it on or off.

docs.lead: Changes a setting as soon as you turn it on or off.
docs.name: Switch
docs.summary: A control that takes effect immediately, unlike a Checkbox, which states an intention the surrounding form later submits. A native input with role=switch, so it is announced as on/off.

anatomy.notes: The <label>. Carries data-state (on | off) and data-disabled, and IS the target — padded to 24px while the track stays 20px.
The real <input type="checkbox" role="switch">, clipped but focusable and in the form. The forwarded ref lands here (§5).
36x20 pill. aria-hidden — the input carries the semantics.
16px circle. Travels by transform, so the track's geometry never changes.
children. The accessible name, natively.

docs.composition:
Switch
├─ children           ReactNode (required) — the label AND the accessible name
├─ isChecked?         controlled
├─ defaultIsChecked?  uncontrolled
└─ isDisabled?

children.notes: Required. The row is one <label>, so the name comes from the DOM rather than an aria-label that can drift.

isChecked.notes: Controlled. Omit and the component owns its state, through the shared useControllableState hook (§4).

isLabelHidden.notes: Visually hides the label without removing it from the accessibility tree.

isDisabled.notes: Sets the `disabled` attribute — never pointer-events-none, which would kill an explaining tooltip.

labelPlacement.notes: Which side of the control the label sits on. end is the shipped inline row. start is the SETTINGS ROW: full width, label first, the control pinned to the end in a fixed lane, so a stack of rows forms one column of controls (#9 Proposals sheet, 03). Visual order only (flex-row-reverse): the input stays first in the DOM, so the peer styling and the reading order hold, and in RTL the sides mirror with the text.

description.notes: A line under the label: body-sm in --ui-text-muted (5.93:1 light, 4.94:1 dark), gap-xs below, --ui-text-disabled when disabled. Inside the <label>, so it is part of the hit target; announced as the input's DESCRIPTION (aria-describedby), with the name pinned to the label text (aria-labelledby) so a long description is never read as the name. A caller's own aria-describedby is kept beside it. With a description the row aligns to the top and the control sits on the label's first line.

onCheckedChange.notes: Fires on every change in both modes. The raw onChange is forwarded and runs after ours (§5).

do: Use a Switch for something that takes effect the moment it is flipped; use a Checkbox inside a form that is submitted later.
Pass the visible label as children — it becomes the accessible name for free.
Keep the label a statement of what is ON ('Show job title'), not an instruction.
dont: Do not put a Switch in a form that needs saving; that is a Checkbox.
Do not render one without children — there is no nameless form, and the type requires it.
Do not add on/off text inside the track; the label already says what it does, and the role announces the state.

a11y.role: switch, on a native checkbox input. The role changes only how it is ANNOUNCED — 'on/off' rather than 'checked' — which is the entire difference from Checkbox at this layer.
a11y.name: The children, via the wrapping <label>. No aria-label is used or needed.

keyboard.does: Moves focus to the input, which is clipped but never out of the tab order.
Toggles. Native implicit activation — no JS key handler exists.
Nothing, per the platform, exactly as for Checkbox.

a11y.target: The track is 36x20; the <label> is padded to min-h-6 so the row clears the 24px floor of WCAG 2.5.8.

contrastPairs.role: the ON track against the page
the OFF track against the page
the label

knownGaps: The off track uses `edge-strong` — a border role used as a fill. The sheet used `--ui-text-placeholder`, a TEXT role as a background, which is worse; both are category errors. A dedicated track role is probably the right answer, and Slider will want the same thing. Raised, not decided.
One size. The sheet draws a single 36x20 track.
labelPlacement and description are CLOSED (2026-11-02, #9): drawn on the #9 Proposals sheet, light and dark. start is the settings row a Switch is most often asked for.
No loading or pending state for a switch whose effect is asynchronous — the commonest real need, and not drawn.
The sheet's thumb shadow is a raw #9EDBF30D; this uses --ui-shadow-sm.
Thumb travel is CLOSED (2026-11-03, Audit #9 "Measured"): 17px instead of translate-x-4, so the ON thumb sits 1px from its edge like the OFF thumb. Asserted in switch.browser.test.tsx.
needsDesign: THUMB IN DARK (Audit #9 "Measured", re-measured 2026-11-03 on the warm-ink ramp). The thumb is --ui-bg-surface, which is DARK in dark (#1E1B18): a dark knob on a light track, the inverse of light's white knob on a dark track. It reads (6.56:1 on the off track) but it is not the same object in both schemes. Disabled is the weak case in both: the thumb on the --ui-bg-sunken track is 1.19:1 light / 1.41:1 dark, so a disabled switch's POSITION is barely readable (the state is exempt from 1.4.11, the information is not). Options: a fixed light thumb role in both schemes, or a disabled thumb drawn in --ui-border-default. Belongs with the dedicated track-role question in knownGaps.
docs.motion: The track transitions `background-color`, `border-color` and `box-shadow`; the thumb travels on `transition-transform`. Both at --ui-duration-fast with --ui-ease-out, so the thumb moves rather than teleports, and the transform keeps the travel on the compositor and the track's geometry untouched. Note this is invisible to the visual gate: a Switch track is under 1% of its frame, which is below `allowedMismatchedPixelRatio` — the track could change colour entirely without tripping a diff.

the OFF track against the page
the label

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

Switch's thumb travels 17px instead of translate-x-4 (16). The inner track is 34 (36 less two 1px borders) and the thumb 16, so the OFF thumb sat 1px from its edge and the ON thumb 2px from its own — measured on the Audit #9 sheet (Paper, Components - Handoff). Both now sit 1px in. Off the spacing scale on purpose, commented at the class. switch.browser.test.tsx asserts the symmetry. Visual: every checked Switch moves 1px.

Checkbox, Radio and Switch draw their checked/selected look from the native input's :checked (peer-checked:) rather than from React state, so they work as plain form controls on a statically rendered page and before hydration (#34). The check glyph and radio dot are always in the DOM and revealed by the same selector. Checkbox's indeterminate state is still render-time (it has no HTML attribute).

Checkbox and Switch gain labelPlacement ("end" default, "start" = the settings row: full width, label first, control pinned to the end) and description (body-sm muted under the label, inside the <label> so it is part of the hit target). The description is announced as the input's description: the name is pinned to the label text with aria-labelledby so a long description is never read as the name, and a caller's own aria-describedby is kept. With a description the row aligns to the top and the control sits on the label's first line; placement is visual only (flex-row-reverse), so the input stays before the control for every peer-* selector and RTL mirrors with the text (#9; approved on the Audit #9 sheet).

check:motion joins the gate list, and every animating component now documents its motion. The gate rejects a literal duration or easing in registry/ (a discipline that was already perfect — zero hard-coded durations across 26 files — and had nothing keeping it that way), transition-all (CONVENTIONS section 6 has said this since the beginning and nothing enforced it), a keyframe with no reduced-motion guard, and an animating component with no top-level motion: note in its doc. It reads lib recipes alongside components as check:overlays does, so Header's motion is found in @/lib/chrome-control where it actually lives rather than reported as absent. 27 doc files gain a motion: note describing what moves, what drives it and what reduced motion does to it; Sheet's and ImageUpload's existing notes are PROMOTED out of a11y to the top level, where Button already had its, because motion is a description of what a component does rather than solely an accessibility concern and a field meaning one thing at two depths stops being findable. ImageUpload's note is corrected while being promoted: it credited the token layer with stopping its spinner, and what actually stops it is the motion-safe: variant. Two findings are recorded in the notes rather than fixed: Sidebar's collapsible section snaps via the hidden attribute where Accordion animates the identical interaction against Base UI's published height, and Banner reaches for transition-colors where the rest of the library enumerates properties. No component's rendered motion changes; no .tsx is touched.

migration.manual: Documentation only — every change is inside a *.doc.ts, and no component's classes or rendered motion moved. If you consume the doc files and read `a11y.motion`, it has moved to the top-level `motion` key on Sheet and ImageUpload; Button was already there and the other 27 are new.

changes.summary: Protect switch state contracts

Switch — the control that takes effect immediately, as against Checkbox, which states an intention a form later submits. Built on a native input with role=switch rather than a div, so Space activation, form participation and :disabled come from the platform and the role changes only how it is ANNOUNCED (on/off rather than checked), which is the entire difference from Checkbox at the a11y layer. Reuses useControllableState, proving the hook generalises past its first consumer. The row is one label carrying the 24px target while the track stays 36x20, and the thumb travels by transform so the track's geometry never changes. Two design defects corrected: the ON track used the --ui-blue-80 palette step, and the OFF track used --ui-text-placeholder — a TEXT role as a background. The ON track now uses the accent role. The OFF track uses edge-strong, which is the same value on a non-text role and clears the 3:1 a control boundary needs, but is still a border role used as a fill; that compromise is recorded in knownGaps rather than hidden, because Slider will want the same thing and a dedicated track role is probably the right answer. Review found a light-scheme contrast issue: the white thumb on the pale accent track measures 1.48:1, under SC 1.4.11's 3:1. Position still distinguishes on from off, and dark is fine at 9.17:1, but the thumb is barely discernible against the fill in light. Recorded as open rather than papered over — the sheet draws the same pale pair.

migration.manual: None — new component. Replaces the Toggle artboard, which the sheet renamed.

items.title: Table
items.lead: Makes structured information easy to compare, sort and scan.

docs.lead: Makes structured information easy to compare, sort and scan.
docs.name: Table
docs.summary: A data surface built from hairlines, not fills. A real <table> with fixed lanes and one flexing column, three densities, sortable headers, row selection with a mixed select-all, and loading and empty bodies that keep the header and the lane widths. It sorts nothing and filters nothing — it reports what the reader asked for.

anatomy.notes: The frame: a bg-elevated mat, 1px subtle edge, radius-lg and 4px of padding. Owns className, the ref, data-size, and --ui-table-body-radius.

The node that rounds the header's top corners and the last row's bottom ones, clipping at max(0, radius-lg minus padding minus border). The frame's border counts in the inset, so the corrected theme-zero radius is 11px. It exists because neither of the alternatives works: clipping on the FRAME cuts along the frame's own curve offset by its padding, which is a different curve from the explicit inner clip, and a <tr> cannot carry a border-radius in either border model.

The <table>: table-fixed, border-SEPARATE at zero spacing, with a <colgroup> carrying the lane widths and an sr-only <caption>. Separate rather than collapse because border-radius does not apply in the collapsing model at all, and the first data row is rounded.
The <thead>. One row, at the size's own height, filled bg-elevated so it reads as part of the mat.
A <th scope="col">. Carries aria-sort when the column is sortable.
The sort control, which IS the header cell — full-bleed inside the <th> so its hover fill covers the lane. data-state is none/ascending/descending.
A ChevronDown, always in the layout at opacity 0 so revealing it moves nothing. 40% on hover or focus, solid when sorted, rotated for ascending.
The <tbody>. Carries aria-busy while loading.

A <tr>. Carries data-state selected/default, data-disabled, the press target and, for selectable rows, the focus ring — but NOT the fill, the divider or the corners. Those are on its cells: a <tr> renders no border-radius in either border model, and the separate model ignores a border on a row.
The header's select lane. Holds a Checkbox whose mixed state resolves to ALL.
A row's select lane. Holds the row's own Checkbox, which is the non-colour half of what a selected row communicates.

A <td>. Primary ink and medium weight on the primary column, secondary and regular elsewhere. Also carries the row's fill and hover/press states, the 1px bg-elevated divider, and — on the first row's outer two cells — the radius-md top corners.
Optional row immediately after its owner. Its table-details cell spans all columns, including selection. The caller owns disclosure controls and state.
Full-width context on the owner row's surface, with the divider after the content. Content does not toggle row selection.
A placeholder row at the real row's height, in the real lanes.

A composed Skeleton at h-2.5, the denser row's height rather than the component's 16px default. Widths still ripple deterministically by row and column — a visual baseline has to be reproducible, which the harness now achieves by pausing the pulse at its first keyframe rather than by the bar being static. Requires the skeleton item.
One cell spanning every lane, marked aria-live="polite". Renders whatever `empty` was given.

docs.composition:
Table<Row>
├─ caption        string (required) — the sr-only accessible name
├─ columns        TableColumn<Row>[]
│   ├─ key          string
│   ├─ header       string          isHeaderHidden?  boolean
│   ├─ width?       number          — omit on ONE column and it flexes
│   ├─ align?       "start" | "end" isNumeric?  boolean
│   ├─ isSortable?  boolean         isPrimary?  boolean
│   └─ cell         (row: Row) => ReactNode
├─ rows           Row[]             getRowId  (row: Row) => string
├─ size?          "sm" | "md" | "lg"   — md is the drawn default
├─ sort? / defaultSort?   TableSort | null      onSortChange?  (sort) => void
├─ isSelectable?  true — then getRowLabel AND selectAllLabel are REQUIRED
│   ├─ selectedIds? / defaultSelectedIds?   string[]
│   └─ onSelectionChange?  (ids: string[]) => void
├─ rowDetails?    (row: Row) => ReactNode — null when absent or collapsed
├─ isRowDisabled? (row: Row) => boolean
├─ isLoading?     boolean           loadingRowCount?  number
└─ empty?         ReactNode — an EmptyState, typically

caption.notes: The table's accessible name, in a visually hidden <caption>. Required for the reason a field's label is: an unnamed table announces as 'table', and a page with three announces three of those. No visible caption is drawn on the sheet, so none is offered — inventing one would mean designing it here.

columns.notes: The lane system. `width` in px pins a lane; omitting it on exactly one column makes that column flex, which is the sheet's 'lanes are fixed, the primary column flexes'. Density never touches these — it moves row height, inline padding and body size only.

rows.notes: Rendered in the order given. Table sorts nothing: `onSortChange` reports the intent and the data stays with the caller (§9 — no data layer). A component that sorted its own copy would be a second source of truth for the order.

getRowId.notes: Stable identity: the React key, and the value the selection API speaks in. Index-based keys break selection the moment rows reorder, which is the first thing sorting does.

rowDetails.notes: Full-width content immediately after a data row. Return null when absent or collapsed. Compose a disclosure button in a cell with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing to an ID in the detail content. The caller owns expansion state; Table preserves lanes, surface, and selection boundaries.

size.notes: Row 36/44/56, header 32/40/48, inline padding 12/16/24, body 13/14/16. md is the value the sheet labels 'default'. The select lane follows as 2 x inline + 16 — 40/48/64, exactly as drawn.

isSortable.notes: Per column. Offers a real <button> filling the header cell. The indicator is latent (opacity 0) until the column is hovered, focused or sorted — it is present in the layout throughout, so nothing reflows when it appears.

isNumeric.notes: Sets the lane in tabular figures and right-aligns it unless `align` overrides. Figures that do not line up are figures nobody can compare down the page.

isPrimary.notes: The sheet's darker, medium-weight lane. Defaults by position because that is what the sheet draws ('primary · flex'); set it false there, or true elsewhere, to move the emphasis.

isHeaderHidden.notes: Per column. The sheet draws the trailing action lane with an EMPTY header cell — this keeps the name for assistive tech and hides the paint, the same shape a field's isLabelHidden uses.

isSelectable.notes: Turns on the select lane and the select-all box, and REQUIRES getRowLabel and selectAllLabel by the type. A row checkbox with no accessible name announces as 'checkbox', and eight of them announce as eight of those.

getRowLabel.notes: Required whenever isSelectable is set. 'Select Jan Tschichold' — the state is already readable; this is what supplies the subject.

selectAllLabel.notes: Required whenever isSelectable is set. Names the header checkbox.

onSelectionChange.notes: Fires with the whole selection, controlled or not. A mixed select-all resolves to ALL — see a11y.keyboard.

isRowDisabled.notes: The row cannot be selected: its checkbox is genuinely `disabled`, its press affordance is gone, and its ink drops to muted. NOT text-disabled, which the sheet draws and which measures 2.09:1 — see needsDesign.

isLoading.notes: The frame keeps its shape and the header stays; only the body changes. aria-busy goes on the <tbody>, so assistive tech is told the region is updating rather than told there are three rows of nothing.

layout.notes: How the lanes are sized. `fixed` is the sheet's model and stays the DEFAULT even though the browser's own default is auto — under `auto` the lanes shift between loading and loaded, because the skeleton's placeholder text is not the data's, and lane agreement across header, rows, skeleton and empty state is the whole reason the lane system exists. `auto` hands sizing back to the browser: every lane fits its content, `width` becomes a hint, and the grid grows past its frame rather than squeezing. Reach for it when the content is unknown, which is most tables that were never drawn.

minWidth.notes: A floor for the grid in px, below which the frame scrolls horizontally instead of compressing. Unset by default — a table that fits should not invent a scrollbar. With `auto` it is usually unnecessary; with `fixed` it is the ONLY way to scroll, because `w-full` means the lanes always add up to the container.

empty.notes: What the body shows when `rows` is empty — an EmptyState, typically. The header and the lane widths stay, because a table that collapses to a sentence loses the one thing that said what was being filtered.

do: Reach for layout="auto" when the content is unknown, and keep `fixed` when the sheet drew the lanes. The trade is lane stability between loading and loaded, not correctness.

Give a wide table a `minWidth` so it scrolls rather than compressing. The scroll region names itself from the caption and becomes a tab stop only while it actually scrolls, which is SC 2.1.1 without a tab stop in front of every table that fits.
Give exactly one column no `width` — that is the lane that flexes.
Mark money, counts and years `isNumeric` so the figures form a column.
Hold the sort state and do the sorting yourself; `onSortChange` reports, it does not act.
Put row actions in a column of their own with `isHeaderHidden`, a fixed width and `align: "end"` — the sheet's trailing lane is a column like any other.
Pass an EmptyState to `empty` so a filtered-to-nothing table still says what to do next.
dont: Do not sort `rows` inside a render function passed to `cell` — the cell is called per row and cannot see the set.
Do not use the row index as `getRowId`; sorting reorders rows and the selection follows the wrong ones.
Do not put a second interactive control in the primary cell expecting the row press to ignore it — it will, but a row that both navigates and selects is two contracts on one target.
Do not set `isLoading` and pass `empty` expecting both; loading wins, which is the correct order — an empty state shown while data is in flight tells the reader the search failed.
Do not reach for a Table to lay out a form or a card grid. This is tabular data; the semantics are the product.

a11y.role: A native <table> with <caption>, <thead>, <th scope="col"> and <tbody>. No ARIA table roles: a grid of divs with ARIA bolted on can only re-describe what the elements already say.
a11y.name: The `caption` prop, in a visually hidden <caption> element.

keyboard.does: Moves through the select-all box, then each row's checkbox and each row's own controls, in visual order.
Toggles the focused checkbox. Native behaviour — nothing here re-implements it.
Activates a column's sort control, flipping to descending if that column is already ascending.
Toggles selection, when the table is selectable. A pointer convenience for what the checkbox already does; a click that came from a control inside the row is left alone.

a11y.targetSize: Every checkbox is a Checkbox, whose label row is padded to a 24px target around an 18px box — SC 2.5.8's floor. The sort control fills its header cell: 32px tall at the smallest size, and the full lane wide.
a11y.focus: Each control owns its own indicator. A selectable ROW additionally draws a 2px inset outline whenever a control inside it has focus-visible, which is what the sheet's focus row is describing — it says which row you are standing in while tabbing down a column of checkboxes. An outline rather than a box-shadow, so it survives forced-colors mode.
a11y.selection: A selected row is its wash plus its checked box — no leading edge, no marker. Rows are not tab stops and carry no aria-selected. Everything a row does is reachable from the checkbox inside it, and aria-selected on a row is only meaningful inside role="grid" — which would mean full APG grid navigation, not an attribute. A mixed select-all resolves to ALL, never to none: at three of eight chosen, 'the rest too' is the far more common intent and the undo for guessing wrong is eight clicks.

contrastPairs.role: the primary column's ink on a resting row
every other column's ink on a resting row
a disabled row's ink — the sheet's text-disabled measures 2.09:1 here, see needsDesign
a resting column header, on the mat
the hovered row's primary ink, and a sortable header's label under the pointer
the hovered row's other lanes
the other column headers while one of them is hovered
the pressed row's primary ink
the pressed row's other lanes
the selected row's primary ink
the selected row's other lanes
the selected row under the pointer
the same row's other lanes
the row's focus outline. Every other ring pair in this system is measured against the page; a row is one surface step off it

contrastPairs.why: The row divider, which is the mat itself showing between rows that float on it — 1.08:1 light, 1.15:1 dark. It separates rows that are already separated by their content and their lane alignment; a conformant hairline here would draw a grid, which is the thing the sheet is explicitly not doing.
The loading placeholder bars. They carry no information — aria-busy on the body is what tells anyone anything — and a conformant bar would read as content that has arrived.

forwarding.ref: The outermost node, the frame. Table is not a form control, so the §5 default applies — and it is a plain `ref` prop rather than forwardRef, which erases the `Row` type parameter. React 19 takes ref as a prop natively.
forwarding.className: Lands on the frame, so width, margin and a max-height wrapper behave predictably. The <table> itself is data-slot="table-grid".
forwarding.rest: Not spread. Table's surface is its named props; reaching an inner part is what the data-slots are for.

needsDesign: Hover and pressed rows are painted the SAME value (--ui-neutral-95) while the sheet's own gutter annotates them bg-hover and bg-active. Two states that render identically give a press no feedback at all. Shipped per the annotation. Confirm.

The frame, the header fill and the row divider are all drawn as the raw palette step --ui-neutral-95. Shipped as --ui-bg-elevated, the role that resolves to it — a palette step in a component is a role that has not been named.
The selected+hover row is a raw hex (#C3DBE7), annotated 'new token'. Shipped as --ui-bg-accent-subtle-hover, pinned to that hex in light and derived at the matching alpha in dark.

The sortable-hover and sorted-descending header rows appear SWAPPED: the sheet's hover row is weight 600 with a solid arrow and its sorted row is 550 with a muted one, the opposite of the gutter. Shipped per the gutter — which is also the version that does not reflow the header on hover.
The header-state matrix types its labels 550 / 0.02em / leading-flat; five other header rows on the sheet use label-sm / 500 / leading-normal. Shipped as the majority. Confirm the outlier.
sm is annotated 'radius-md 8' and painted radius-lg, like md and lg. Shipped uniform at radius-lg.

The selected row's '3px accent-legible edge' is annotated in the gutter and never painted. NOT shipped: selection is only reachable through the select lane, so a selected row always carries a checked box, which is the non-colour channel SC 1.4.1 asks for. Building it also floored --ui-bg-accent-legible against the accent wash and darkened the Switch, the Slider, Progress and ImageUpload — a table row costing four other components a shade. Confirm the annotation is stale.

The disabled row is annotated text-disabled, which measures 2.09:1 in light. WCAG exempts an inactive CONTROL's label; a row's DATA is content. Shipped at text-muted, the quietest ink that clears AA here.

The checkbox is scaled 16/18/20 with radii 4/4/5 across the three sizes, and the Checkbox sheet defines exactly one 18px box at radius-sm — 5px is off the radius scale. Shipped at 18 everywhere. If Checkbox should grow a size axis that is Checkbox's change, with its own sheet.
The gap between a header label and its sort arrow is 6px, which is off the spacing scale (4/8/12). Shipped at space-xs.
The latent sort arrow and the visible one are DIFFERENT glyphs on the sheet — a stemmed down-arrow at opacity 0, a chevron when shown. Shipped as ChevronDown throughout.

No scroll behaviour is drawn. Lanes shrink proportionally below their declared widths rather than overflowing, because the frame clips to draw its corners. Confirm what a table narrower than its lane sum should do.

No focused-ROW behaviour is drawn beyond the ring: the sheet shows a focus ring on a row containing no focusable element. Rows are not tab stops here. Confirm whether a row should be activatable, which would make this a grid.
No sticky header is drawn, and the frame clips, so one cannot be added without changing the frame.
knownGaps: No tabular figures: Aspekta ships no `tnum` feature and its digits are proportional (367–602 units), so `tabular-nums` is a no-op in this face — figures right-align on their last digit but do not line up digit by digit, and a figure that changes in place changes width. Filed against the face (ADR 0011 item 5); pinned by registry/fonts/aspekta/aspekta.test.ts.

The row fill, the divider and the first row's corners live on the CELLS, not the row. A consumer styling the table-row slot with a background paints behind the cells and sees nothing; reach for the table-cell slot instead.
With `rows` empty and no `empty` passed, the body is one blank row at the lane widths. That is deliberate — the frame never collapses — but it says nothing, so pass an EmptyState.
A selected row is distinguished by its wash and by its checked box, and by nothing else. There is no leading edge or marker; a consumer who needs one adds it to a cell through the table-cell slot.
Table sorts and filters nothing. `onSortChange` reports the intent; ordering the rows is the caller's.
Row selection has no shift-click range. The checkbox and the row press each toggle one row.
The row press has no keyboard counterpart of its own — the checkbox inside the row is that path. There is no way to activate a row from the keyboard without moving to its checkbox first.

Under the default `fixed` layout a table still fits its container by squeezing, because `w-full` makes the lanes add up to it — `minWidth` or `layout="auto"` is what makes it scroll instead. What no longer happens is the frame CLIPPING the overflow away, which is what it used to do: columns past the edge disappeared with no affordance at all. When the declared widths alone exceed the frame, the flexing column gets 0px and its text paints over its neighbour — the charts V2 stand-in screen hit this at 320px. Nothing warns; set `minWidth` to the declared lanes plus what the primary column needs.

Column widths are px numbers. Percentages and fr units are not supported — the lane system exists so the header, the rows, the skeleton and the empty state agree, and mixed units make that agreement conditional on the container. `layout="auto"` is the escape hatch, and it trades exactly that agreement away: the lanes will move when the data arrives.

No column-priority hiding and no card/stacked view. The two other standard responsive strategies are compositions rather than props — a caller narrows `columns` at a breakpoint, or renders something else entirely below one.
`isLoading` wins over `empty`. There is no state that shows both.
The focus ring on a row is square; the sheet draws it at radius-sm. A <tr> cannot reliably take a border-radius in either border model, and the ring is drawn on the row rather than on its cells.
docs.motion: Rows transition `background-color` on hover; sortable header cells transition `background-color` and `color`; the sort indicator transitions `opacity` and `rotate`, so it fades in when a column is asked about and flips between ascending and descending. All at --ui-duration-fast with --ui-ease-out. `rotate` is named individually — Tailwind v4 writes it standalone. The glyph is always in the layout, so revealing it moves nothing.

contrast.role: the primary column's ink on a resting row
every other column's ink on a resting row
a disabled row's ink — the sheet's text-disabled measures 2.09:1 here, see needsDesign

the hovered row's other lanes

the pressed row's primary ink
the pressed row's other lanes
