changes.summary: Reserve row focus rings for selectable rows
Compose full-width row details without changing lanes
Account for frame borders in nested table corners

Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

Three failures found by checking the market-intelligence stand-in screen at 320px against the better-layout reflow rule. Category names on a chart's x axis ran together ("PostersTypographyWayfinding…"): the axis now spaces its labels by the widest name plus 8px, guessed from the character count so the server agrees and corrected by measurement after paint, and a name thinned away is still in the tooltip, the announcement and the table view. A horizontal bar chart's fixed 168px name lane left the bars 8px: the lane is now capped at 40% of the row, which only binds below a 420px row, and a truncated name carries its full text as a title. And Table's scroll clip was not a containing block, so visually hidden text in a cell (the screen's "Not ranked") was placed against the page and scrolled it 33px sideways; the clip is now relative. Table's knownGaps also records that a fixed table whose declared lanes exceed its frame gives the flexing column 0px — the screen now sets minWidth.

ADR 0011 item 5 checked: Aspekta ships no `tnum` feature and its default digits are proportional (367–602 units), so `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` is a no-op wherever the library uses it. Figures still right-align on their last digit; they do not line up digit by digit, and a figure that changes in place (tooltip, meter reading, slider readout) changes width. Filed against the face as ADR 0011 directs, not answered with a second family. Chart, ChartCard, StatTiles, Meter, Table and RangeSlider list the gap; registry/fonts/aspekta/aspekta.test.ts pins the measurement and fails when a font update adds the feature. No code or visual change.

Table's loading body composes the Skeleton component instead of drawing its own bar. It drew a static `block h-2.5 rounded-sm bg-sunken` span, and the recorded reason for it being static rather than pulsing was that a visual baseline has to be reproducible. That reason no longer holds: the visual harness pauses infinite animations at their first keyframe rather than banning them, so a pulsing bar is now as reproducible as a still one — and the proof is that Table's baseline did not move by a single pixel, because frame zero of the pulse is full opacity, which is exactly what the static bar was. The library therefore stops having two placeholder treatments for one idea. The remaining difference is height, which is a real one and is passed at the call site: h-2.5 for a dense table row rather than Skeleton's 16px body-text default. Widths still ripple deterministically by row and column.

migration.manual: Table now requires the `skeleton` item — `npx @bydiorama/ui add table` pulls it in. Nothing renders differently at rest; the bars breathe while loading where they previously sat still.

changes.summary: check:motion joins the gate list, and every animating component now documents its motion. The gate rejects a literal duration or easing in registry/ (a discipline that was already perfect — zero hard-coded durations across 26 files — and had nothing keeping it that way), transition-all (CONVENTIONS section 6 has said this since the beginning and nothing enforced it), a keyframe with no reduced-motion guard, and an animating component with no top-level motion: note in its doc. It reads lib recipes alongside components as check:overlays does, so Header's motion is found in @/lib/chrome-control where it actually lives rather than reported as absent. 27 doc files gain a motion: note describing what moves, what drives it and what reduced motion does to it; Sheet's and ImageUpload's existing notes are PROMOTED out of a11y to the top level, where Button already had its, because motion is a description of what a component does rather than solely an accessibility concern and a field meaning one thing at two depths stops being findable. ImageUpload's note is corrected while being promoted: it credited the token layer with stopping its spinner, and what actually stops it is the motion-safe: variant. Two findings are recorded in the notes rather than fixed: Sidebar's collapsible section snaps via the hidden attribute where Accordion animates the identical interaction against Base UI's published height, and Banner reaches for transition-colors where the rest of the library enumerates properties. No component's rendered motion changes; no .tsx is touched.

migration.manual: Documentation only — every change is inside a *.doc.ts, and no component's classes or rendered motion moved. If you consume the doc files and read `a11y.motion`, it has moved to the top-level `motion` key on Sheet and ImageUpload; Button was already there and the other 27 are new.

changes.summary: Table gains `layout="auto"` and a real scroll region. An adversarial review flagged the table as not responsive, and the investigation corrected the premise on the way: `width` was ALREADY optional on every column — the colgroup only emits one where it is declared — so a table with no widths has always rendered. What it did was split the space EQUALLY, because `table-fixed` was hard-coded, so an ID lane and a name lane got the same room. The sharper finding was underneath it: the frame was `overflow-clip`, so a grid wider than its container lost its right-hand columns SILENTLY, with no scrollbar and no affordance. That was in knownGaps ("wrap it yourself if you need a scroll container") and it is the worse half of the two — squeezing is ugly, clipping loses data. `overflow-x-auto` fixes it and keeps the concentric corner, because any non-visible overflow clips at the border box. `fixed` stays the DEFAULT against the ecosystem's grain (shadcn, Radix Themes, Carbon and Primer all default to auto) for a reason those libraries do not have: lane agreement across the header, the rows, the skeleton and the empty state is the whole point of the lane system, and under `auto` the lanes move when the data lands because the skeleton's placeholder text is not the data's. The scroll region is a tab stop ONLY while it actually scrolls — measured with a ResizeObserver rather than hard-coded — because SC 2.1.1 needs a scrollable region to be keyboard-reachable, and the unconditional version most implementations ship puts a silent, nameless stop in front of every table that fits. role, aria-labelledby and tabIndex are applied together or not at all: a named region nobody can reach is as useless as a reachable one with no name.

migration.manual: No caller changes required; `fixed` remains the default and every existing column definition behaves as before. The one behavioural change is that a grid wider than its frame now scrolls instead of being clipped — if you wrapped a Table in your own scroll container to work around that, the wrapper is now redundant and will produce a nested scroll area.

changes.summary: A real <table> with fixed lanes and one flexing column, three densities (row 36/44/56, inline 12/16/24, body 13/14/16), sortable headers that report rather than sort, row selection whose labels the type requires, and loading and empty bodies that keep the header and the lane widths. The frame carries three corner values, all as drawn: radius-lg outside, the concentric calc(radius-lg - space-xs) on the body's clip — the sheet's 12px, which is not a step on the radius scale — and radius-md on the body's top edge. The row fill, the dividers and the first row's corners all sit on the CELLS — border-radius does not apply in the collapsing border model and a <tr> renders none in either, so the sheet's rounded first row forces the separate model. The dividers are border-b-elevated — the mat itself showing between rows that float on it, rather than a border role free to drift from the surface it imitates. Rows are not tab stops: everything a row does is reachable from the checkbox inside it, and the sheet's focus row is drawn with has-[:focus-visible] on the row. The design corrections are recorded in the doc's needsDesign, the two largest being hover and press painted the same value (shipped per the sheet's own annotation as bg-hover and bg-active, so a press has feedback at all) and the disabled row's text-disabled ink, which measures 2.09:1 in light — a row's data is content, not an inactive control's label, so it ships at text-muted. The gutter's annotated 3px selection edge is NOT shipped: selection is only reachable through the select lane, so a selected row always carries a checked box.

migration.manual: New item — nothing to migrate. `npx shadcn add @bydiorama/table`; it pulls in `cn`, `checkbox` and `use-controllable-state`, and expects react and griddy-icons as peers. Table sorts nothing: hold the sort state and order the rows yourself, and give getRowId a stable id rather than an index or selection follows the wrong rows the first time a column is sorted.

changes.summary: Adds --ui-bg-accent-subtle-hover, the accent wash under the pointer. The Table sheet drew a selected+hovered row as a raw hex (#C3DBE7) and annotated it 'new token', and neither existing role could stand in: bg-hover is a neutral and would drop the selection colour on hover, while bg-accent would make one hovered row louder than the button that submits the page. Derived as withAlpha(accent, 0.20) — the same step --ui-intent-danger-bg-hover takes over its own tint — and pinned in ZERO_AUTHORED in BOTH schemes, to the sheet's hex in light and to the matching alpha in dark. Also lists ten contrast pairs a table row is the first thing to render: secondary and muted ink on the accent wash, on bg-hover and on bg-active; the focus ring on bg-surface rather than on the page; and secondary ink on the sunken well. Declaring them moved one shipped token toward more contrast: dark's --ui-text-secondary steps lighter, raising every dark secondary-ink pair in the library (6.97 to 7.91 on the page, 9.13 to 10.36 on a control). Deliberately NOT listed is --ui-bg-accent-legible against those washes. It was, briefly, for a 3px selection edge the sheet annotates and never paints — and flooring the token against the wash as well as the sunken well darkened it from #518CA2 to #458096, deepening the Switch track, the Slider fill and thumb ring, the Progress fill and ImageUpload's, none of which are tables. The edge is not shipped, so the pair is not declared: an unlisted pair is an unchecked pair, but a pair nothing renders is a constraint on every component that does. The four browser tests that failed while the token moved were each named 'uses the ROLE, not the palette step' and each asserted a hard-coded rgb() copy of what the role resolved to the day it was written; they now read the role, which is the fix that outlives this.

migration.manual: A resolver that enumerates BRANDABLE_TOKENS gains one entry and will fail to type-check until it derives it — that is intended. Re-emit your theme CSS (`pnpm tokens` in the storybook app, or your own emitter) or `bg-accent-subtle-hover` compiles to nothing. One existing token moves: dark's secondary ink lightens. Nothing in light changes. If you have pinned a token's value in a test, read the token instead.

docs.name: Tabs
docs.summary: A segmented control that switches which panel is shown, in two orientations and two variants. Roving tabindex, arrow navigation and the tab-to-panel ARIA pairing come from the Base UI behaviour layer (ADR 0012) — and so does the arrow AXIS, which is why `orientation` is forwarded rather than expressed in CSS.

anatomy.notes: The wrapper. className lands here (§5).
role=tablist. Carries data-orientation and data-variant. Enclosed is a bordered bg-surface track at radius-md with a 2px inset and a 32px height; ghost drops fill and edge entirely.

role=tab. min-h-6 for the target floor. Enclosed is flex-1, with its radius derived from the track radius minus padding and stroke, so brand corners remain concentric; ghost sizes to its label at radius-md, because there is no track to divide.
Optional number beside the label. A 16px circle — min-h as well as min-w, or one digit renders as a lozenge. 12px type, not the sheet's 11px.
role=tabpanel, paired with its tab both ways.

docs.composition:
Tabs                     value? / defaultValue? / onValueChange?
                         orientation? / variant?
├─ Tabs.List
│  ├─ Tabs.Tab value="…" count? isDisabled?
│  └─ …
└─ Tabs.Panel value="…"

value.notes: Controlled selection, by tab value. Omit and Tabs owns it.

onValueChange.notes: Narrowed from Base UI's (value, eventDetails) and its loose value type, so no third-party shape reaches the signature.

orientation.notes: Forwarded to the behaviour layer, so vertical swaps the arrow keys to Up/Down and sets aria-orientation. Stacking the boxes in CSS and leaving the arrows horizontal is the usual half-implementation, and it reads as broken to anyone not using a mouse — the browser test drives Right in a vertical strip and asserts nothing moves.

variant.notes: enclosed is the sheet's bordered track. ghost drops fill and edge and lets the selected tab's own fill carry it, for a strip inside a surface that already has an edge.

Tab.value.notes: Pairs the tab with its panel.

Tab.count.notes: A count beside the label, as the sheet draws on the selected tab.

Tab.isDisabled.notes: Skipped by arrow navigation and not selectable.

do: Give every Tabs.Tab a matching Tabs.Panel with the same value; the ARIA pairing is generated from it.
Keep labels short — the strip divides evenly, so one long label squeezes the rest.
Use Tabs for switching views of the same subject, not for navigation between pages.
dont: Do not use Tabs as a router. A tab does not change the URL; a link should.
Do not put more than a handful in one strip — flex-1 makes each narrower, and a crowded strip is a menu wearing a costume.
Do not expect arrowing to select. Activation is MANUAL — see the keyboard table.

a11y.role: tablist / tab / tabpanel, from Base UI, with aria-controls and aria-labelledby paired in both directions — asserted in Chromium.
a11y.name: Each tab's own text. Its panel is named by the tab through aria-labelledby.

keyboard.does: Enters the strip at the SELECTED tab only. Roving tabindex leaves the others at -1, so a keyboard user is not forced through every tab to reach the content — the classic hand-rolled failure.
Move FOCUS between tabs without selecting. Left/Right when horizontal, Up/Down when vertical — the axis follows `orientation`.
Selects the focused tab. Manual activation, which is the ARIA-approved pattern when a panel is expensive to render.
Focus the first and last tab.

a11y.target: Each tab is min-h-6, clearing SC 2.5.8. The sheet's 6px vertical padding is off the spacing scale and would have produced a 20px target.

contrastPairs.role: selected tab ink on its fill
unselected tab ink on the strip
count ink on its pill
the strip boundary
contrastPairs.why: ADR 0010 keeps a resting surface quiet; the strip separates by fill, not edge

needsDesign: The 3px inset is off the spacing scale entirely (the scale starts at 4). It is what the sheet lays out and what closes §6's concentric arithmetic, so it ships — but a control-scale inset the scale cannot express is a gap in the scale, not in this component.

The ghost strip draws its SELECTED tab at radius-md and its unselected ones at radius-sm. Only the selected one has a fill, so the difference is invisible — shipped as radius-md for all of them. Confirm.
No hover state is drawn for an unselected tab; the ink shift to secondary is derived.
The vertical strip has no fixed height and no fixed width in the sheet, so it stretches to its container.
knownGaps: One size. The sheet draws a single scale for both orientations.
No overflow handling — a strip with many tabs squeezes rather than scrolling. Not drawn.
The sheet gives the count only to the selected tab; the component allows it on any, which is the more useful behaviour but is not what is drawn.
No Base UI Indicator (the sliding highlight); the sheet fills the selected tab instead.
docs.motion: Triggers transition `background-color` and `color` at --ui-duration-fast with --ui-ease-out. There is no travelling indicator: the active tab is marked by its fill, so nothing slides between tabs, and a panel change is instant rather than a cross-fade.

contrast.role: selected tab ink on its fill
unselected tab ink on the strip
count ink on its pill
the strip boundary

The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.
Derive enclosed tab corners from track radius, padding and stroke so brand themes remain concentric without changing density.
Tabs.Panel takes `isAlwaysMounted`: an unselected panel stays in the DOM (hidden), so static HTML carries every panel's content (#34).

The enclosed track was inset 3px at the sides and 4px at the top and bottom; the sheet lays out 4px on all four. The source read symmetric — `p-[2px]`, one padding, four sides — and was not on screen: 24px rows plus 2 + 2 plus a 1.5px border the browser USES as 1px is 31, `h-8` demanded 32, and `items-center` paid the spare pixel out of the vertical gaps. A fixed height is a second author of an inset and the two agree only by arithmetic accident, so the height is gone: it is now 24 + 3 + 3 + 1 + 1 = the same 32px, derived. `items-center` is gone too, so every tab stretches to the content box and all four gaps are the padding whatever a tab contains. The inset is 3px, the sheet's own, which also closes CONVENTIONS §6 against the PADDING box (8 − 1 border = 7 = radius-sm 4 + 3) — the previous 2px never did, and the component's comment said so and shipped anyway. Second fix in the same component: the ghost strip stretched full-width and `justify-center` centred it, against both the sheet (a 280px box at x=0) and Tab's own docstring ("ghost sizes to its content and sits left"); it hugs now. Third: `doc.design` pointed at D7G-0, the Text Area artboard. The browser test that asserted `padding === "2px"` and called it "the sheet's own inset" had been written from the component rather than the design, so it pinned the drift rather than catching it — corrected, and the four-sided inset is now asserted against Paper's own world coordinates.

ADR 0019. The design's numbers were never in this repository — `design/paper/` holds PNGs and its own README calls them evidence, not values — so "does this match the design?" could only be answered by a person comparing two pictures, and a person cannot see one pixel. Tabs' track was inset 3px at the sides and 4px top and bottom for its whole life and every gate passed it: the class list reads symmetric, the asymmetry does not exist until layout, and the visual baselines admit in their own header that a small element can change ENTIRELY under `allowedMismatchedPixelRatio`. Each half fails if the other is missing a case. A case must declare every law or excuse it by name, so an unenforced law is distinguishable from one nobody thought of. The neural half is bounded on purpose: looking at a render beside a sheet produces a HYPOTHESIS, discharged either as a new law (arithmetic, permanent) or a spec `deviation` (reason required, 40-char floor) — never as a comment. Coverage is Tabs and its three cases; the other 34 components have no spec and the gate reports the count rather than implying coverage.

changes.summary: Two reported defects, both real, both invisible to the existing tests. FIRST: `isDisabled` had never had any visual effect. Base UI's Tab renders `aria-disabled="true"` and `data-disabled` and deliberately never sets the native `disabled` attribute — so the tab stays focusable and announceable, the same choice Calendar makes for unavailable dates — which meant every `disabled:` class in the component matched nothing. A disabled tab painted identically to an enabled one, same ink and same pointer cursor, in both schemes. The refusal worked, so the behaviour test passed; only the appearance was missing, which is the half no behaviour test could see. Now `aria-disabled:`, asserted as a DIFFERENCE from the enabled tab beside it. SECOND: the selected tab used `--ui-bg-sunken`, which measured 1.10:1 against the track in dark — 'recessed' is a RELATIVE role and the surface scale inverts between schemes, so below the surface there is room on a light page and almost none on a dark one. A new `--ui-bg-selected` role steps AWAY from the surface in whichever direction the scheme reads: light is pinned to the drawn neutral so nothing moves there, and dark goes from 1.10 to 1.68. A resolver test asserts the separation across every stress seed, in both schemes.

Tabs gains `orientation` and `variant`, the two axes the redrawn sheet adds. `orientation` is FORWARDED to the behaviour layer rather than expressed in CSS, so vertical swaps the arrow keys to Up/Down and sets aria-orientation; the browser test drives Right in a vertical strip and asserts nothing moves, because stacking the boxes with flex-direction and leaving the arrows horizontal is the usual half-implementation and it reads as broken to anyone not using a mouse. `ghost` drops the track and lets the selected fill carry the strip; the test compares the two variants TO EACH OTHER on fill, edge and tab width, since two variants that differ in the type and not on screen is a defect this repo has shipped twice. Geometry corrected to the sheet: a 1.5px edge, a 2px inset and a 32px height, replacing a 1px edge and a 4px inset. The count pill gains min-h so a single digit renders as a circle rather than a lozenge. The 2px inset does NOT close §6's concentric arithmetic and is off the spacing scale — recorded in needsDesign, because it is the number the drawn height depends on.

Tabs — a segmented control on the Base UI behaviour layer. The parts worth not hand-rolling are the ones asserted: roving tabindex, so only the SELECTED tab is in the tab order and a keyboard user is not forced through every tab to reach the content; arrow navigation with Home/End; and the two-way aria-controls/aria-labelledby pairing between each tab and its panel. Activation is MANUAL — arrows move focus and Enter or Space selects — which is the ARIA-approved pattern when a panel is expensive to render; the browser test was rewritten to assert that contract after it caught the assumption that arrowing selects. Two implementation defects the browser suite found: the selected tab was styled with data-[selected], which Base UI does not set (it marks aria-selected), so the fill never painted; and py-xs around a 12px flat-leading label gives a 20px target, under SC 2.5.8, now floored with min-h-6. Design defects corrected in Paper: four raw hexes (#FDFCFC, #E8E2D9 twice, #F8F6F2) replaced with bg-surface, border-subtle, bg-sunken and bg-elevated; an off-scale 6px vertical padding replaced with the space scale plus a height floor; a raw 4px radius replaced with radius-sm; and an 11px count label raised to 12px, the floor ADR 0009 set after an 11px label pushed a control under the WCAG target size. Also: the optimizeDeps pre-bundle list added last commit was INCOMPLETE — it is explicit, so Tabs importing a new Base UI subpath reintroduced the story flake until that subpath was added. The list now says so in a comment.

migration.manual: New peer dependency on @base-ui-components/react, the same range the other overlay components declare.

docs.lead: Multi-line text field with its label, helper text and error message as one accessible unit.
docs.name: Textarea
docs.summary: Multi-line text field with its label, helper text and error message as one accessible unit. Three sizes matching Input's, so the two stack in a form without a seam. Height is set by rows and grown by a vertical drag.

anatomy.notes: The wrapper. Owns the vertical rhythm between label, control and messages.
Always rendered. isLabelHidden makes it visually hidden, never absent.
The bordered surface. Carries the border, background, focus ring and data-invalid/data-disabled. It has no height of its own — the textarea's height is the box's height, so a resize drag grows it.
The native <textarea>. Transparent and borderless, and it carries the INSET padding — Input puts that on the control instead. See forwarding.
Rendered before helper so the correction is read first.
Persistent guidance; stays visible alongside an error.

docs.composition:
Textarea
├─ label        string (required) — visually hidden via isLabelHidden
├─ control
│  └─ textarea  native <textarea> — rows, maxLength, placeholder go here
├─ errorText?   string — presence marks the field invalid
└─ helperText?  string

label.notes: Required by the type system, not by review. A placeholder is not a label — it vanishes the moment the user types, taking the field's name with it.

isLabelHidden.notes: Visually hidden, still in the accessibility tree and still a click target.

size.notes: Input's scale, minus the part that cannot carry over. Inset and type step exactly as Input's do (px-md py-sm / p-sm / px-sm py-xs, 14 / 14 / 12px), and the browser test asserts each step against a real Input at that size. The HEIGHT does not carry over: Input's is a constant, this one is rows line boxes, so the same rows gives 127 / 127 / 104px — lg and md are one box with a different inline inset, since md's value moved from caption to body-md with the rest of the field family (#16). A size changes the line, never the count.

isDisabled.notes: Native disabled: blocked, out of the tab order, and the resize grip is withdrawn with it.

isRequired.notes: Sets the native required attribute and appends an aria-hidden asterisk to the visible label.

isInvalid.notes: Only needed when the error is reported elsewhere (a form-level summary); errorText implies it.

isResizable.notes: Vertical only, never horizontal — a field that can be dragged wider breaks the layout containing it. Turn it off inside a surface that cannot reflow: a fixed panel, a Drawer, a table cell.

rows.notes: The native attribute, not a re-spelling of it. 6 is the sheet's 128px box at lg: 6 line boxes of 18.2px over py-sm and the 1.5px border. Changing it changes the content area and nothing else.

cols.notes: OMITTED from the type on purpose. It is a real textarea attribute that this component makes inert — the control is w-full, so a character count never reaches layout (measured: cols={5} rendered at the same 412px as no cols). Refusing it at compile time is the difference between a prop that is unsupported and one that looks supported. Width comes from the field's own className.

helperText.notes: Announced via aria-describedby. Kept alongside an error rather than replaced.

errorText.notes: Presence sets aria-invalid and the danger border. Announced first when both messages exist.

do: Always pass a real label, even when the design shows none — use isLabelHidden.
Set rows to the number of lines the content usually needs; it is the only height knob and it is native.
Put the error in errorText rather than styling the field yourself; it wires aria-invalid and aria-describedby together.
Pass isResizable={false} when the field sits in a surface whose height cannot change.
Control the value with value + onChange, or leave it uncontrolled with defaultValue.
dont: Do not use a placeholder as the label — it disappears on input and is announced inconsistently.
Do not set a height with className; it fights rows and the resize drag, both of which set the box.
Do not set aria-invalid by hand alongside errorText; the component derives it and the two drift apart.
Do not rely on the red border alone to convey an error — errorText is the non-colour channel WCAG 1.4.1 requires.
Do not add outline-none to the control; the focus ring lives there and suppressing it removes the indicator entirely.

a11y.role: textbox with aria-multiline (native textarea)

keyboard.does: Moves in and out. Enter does NOT submit here, so Tab is the only way out — the one keyboard difference from Input.
Inserts a newline. Native; the component adds no key handling.
Native.

a11y.labelling: label is a real <label htmlFor>, so clicking it focuses the field. The id is generated with useId when not supplied, which keeps multiple instances on a page distinct.
a11y.describedBy: helperText and errorText each get an id and both are joined into aria-describedby, error first, so a screen reader reads the correction before the guidance.
a11y.focus: Drawn on the control via focus-within: border moves to --ui-border-focus AND the --ui-focus-ring halo renders. Focus-within rather than focus-visible is deliberate for a text field — a pointer click must show where typing will land.
a11y.target: The default box is 128px and the smallest the field can be is rows={1}, which is one 18.2px line box over py-sm and the border — about 36px, past SC 2.5.8's 24px floor. The inset padding sits on the textarea rather than the wrapper, so the whole box is the target with no dead border zone around it.

contrastPairs.role: the value
the placeholder
the value, on a chrome ground (surface="chrome")
the placeholder, on a chrome ground
a disabled field's value on a chrome ground
contrastPairs.why: WCAG 1.4.3 exempts disabled controls, and a disabled field has to READ as unavailable — holding its ink to 4.5:1 would make it indistinguishable from an available one, which is the real failure. Declared rather than omitted because ADR 0017 added a second ground and an unlisted pair is an unchecked pair: this is the exact ink-on-fill combination the new pair exists to keep distinct.

contrastPairs.role: the label
the helper text
the focus ring
the invalid border — the boundary that says the control is in error (SC 1.4.11)

contrastPairs.why: The resting hairline is quiet BY DECISION (ADR 0010, CONVENTIONS §7b) and measures 1.47:1. Declared rather than omitted because in light --ui-bg-field and --ui-bg-base are the same value, so on the page this hairline is the only thing drawing the field's boundary — which is a live question for SC 1.4.11 across every field in the library, not a Textarea choice. It is recorded here so the next reader sees the number rather than assuming it was checked.

forwarding.ref: Goes to the <textarea>, not the outermost node — the documented form-control exception in CONVENTIONS §5. A ref to the wrapper cannot focus the field, read its value, or be handed to a form library.
forwarding.className: Lands on the outermost field wrapper, so `className="w-64"` sizes the whole field and the control follows. Target an inner part with data-slot.
forwarding.rest: Native props (rows, placeholder, value, maxLength…) go to the <textarea> that owns them.
forwarding.padding: The one place this diverges from Input: the inset lives on the <textarea>, not on the control. The native resize grip is painted at the textarea's own corner, and the drag sets an inline height on the textarea — so padding on the wrapper would float the grip 12px inside the box and clip the drag. The inset a user sees is identical; the browser test asserts it against a real Input.

needsDesign: No character-count or max-length affordance. 'Up to 120 words' is helper prose, not a live counter — a counter is a second live region (it must announce sparingly rather than on every keystroke) and wants designing before it is built.
derivations: The three sizes. The sheet drew one box, matching Input's lg. Inset and type step exactly as Input's do; the height does NOT, because Input's is a constant and this one is `rows` line boxes — so the same rows gives 127 / 127 / 104px. Now drawn on the sheet as its own size row.

The line. The sheet stored a raw 18px on 14px type — 1.286, off the --ui-leading-* scale entirely (tight 1.25, snug 1.3). Shipped as leading-snug, the nearest role, 0.2px per line larger, which lands the 6-row lg box on the sheet's own 128px. The sheet is now bound to var(--ui-leading-snug) rather than to the literal.
The value ink. The sheet drew --ui-text-secondary; Input ships --ui-text-primary, and a form holding both must not show two inks for the same thing. The sheet now carries --ui-text-primary.

Hover, error and disabled. None was drawn. Each is Input's, which takes them from Button's secondary variant: hover moves the edge subtle -> default, error moves it to --ui-border-danger, disabled fills --ui-bg-sunken with --ui-text-disabled ink and withdraws the resize grip. All are now drawn on the sheet.
knownGaps: No leading or trailing slots. Input has icon/iconEnd; nothing in the sheet puts an adornment in a textarea, and a slot with no drawn placement would be a guess about where it sits on a multi-line box.

No auto-grow. `field-sizing: content` would do it in one declaration but is not drawn, is not in every engine yet, and interacts with the resize drag — it is a design decision before it is an implementation one.

Errors are announced via aria-describedby, which a screen reader reads on focus. An error appearing while focus is elsewhere (after a submit) is NOT announced — that belongs to a form-level error summary with focus management, not to this component.
No read-only visual state; native readOnly renders as default today. Same as Input.

A DISABLED field's placeholder does not change ink. Measured: the value drops from rgb(29,27,25) to rgb(183,176,169) as it should, while the placeholder stays at rgb(105,99,93) in both states — `disabled:text-ink-disabled` sets the colour property, and the ::placeholder pseudo has its own from `placeholder:text-ink-placeholder`. So an EMPTY disabled field is distinguished only by its sunken fill and its cursor. It is a one-class fix (disabled:placeholder:text-ink-disabled) and is deliberately NOT applied here, because Input, Select and DatePicker all behave the same way and fixing one field alone would reintroduce exactly the seam the size scale was added to remove. It wants doing across the four together.
The resize grip is the browser's, so it is drawn in the UA's colours rather than the theme's. Styling it means ::-webkit-resizer, which is one engine only.
docs.motion: Transitions `border-color`, `box-shadow` and `background-color` at --ui-duration-fast with --ui-ease-out — the same list as Input, deliberately, because it is the same field wearing a different height.

changes.summary: Public library pages follow the manifest and typed documentation, with article-inspired copy and no changing library totals. Public leads and categories feed generated HTML references, Markdown twins, gallery and search entries, agent indexes and registry routes. The optional NetworkCanvas renderer now has its own typed reference. New freshness, source-boundary, route/link and browser checks keep the public reader in step. Interactive specimens are a featured subset; hosting and the remaining release gates stay open.

Closes #16. A field's value at md is now body-md (14px) in Input, Textarea, Select and Multiselect, where it was caption (12px); lg stays body-md and sm stays caption. Two defects, one decision. First, Select's trigger, and Multiselect's, ignored their size map for text: `SIZE[size]` carried the caption step, then a hard-coded `text-body-md` on the next line won the merge, so every Select rendered 14px at every size while the Input beside it rendered 12 at md and sm. The boxes matched (40px at md), so the geometry relationship test passed for the bug's whole life; only the text inside differed. The hard-coded class is gone and the map is the only thing on either trigger that names a type role. Second, the direction: the maintainer decided md settles at 14px, not 12, because the owner's Paper frames draw every 40px field value at body-md, and service-portal had to patch `[data-slot="control"][data-size="md"]` to get there. sm stays caption because the field tokens carry no type step at all (ADR 0020 §4 keeps type out of density), so the map is the only authority, and a 14px value's 21.7px line in a compact 28px field leaves 3px of block padding. Textarea's md box is now lg's box (127px at 6 rows) with the narrower inline inset. DatePicker draws lg only and does not change. Select's and Multiselect's browser tests now compare the VALUE's font-size and line-height to a real Input's at every size; both fail against the old trigger (probed). Deliberate visual change: the `select` matrix baseline moves (its md and sm rows) and the `textarea` baseline moves (its md row), light and dark, darwin and linux. The input, multiselect and date-picker cases draw lg only and do not move for this. Weight is NOT yet one relationship: Input's value is font-medium (500) at every size, while Select, Multiselect, DatePicker and Textarea take their role's weight (body-md 400, caption 600), so a Select at sm now renders 600 where it rendered 400. Recorded for a maintainer decision rather than changed here.

migration.manual: Remove any local override that forced field text to one size (for example a rule on [data-slot="control"][data-size="md"] setting body-md); md renders body-md on its own now. A form that relied on Select rendering 14px at sm will see 12px there, matching Input; pass size="md" if you meant the larger value.

changes.summary: check:motion joins the gate list, and every animating component now documents its motion. The gate rejects a literal duration or easing in registry/ (a discipline that was already perfect — zero hard-coded durations across 26 files — and had nothing keeping it that way), transition-all (CONVENTIONS section 6 has said this since the beginning and nothing enforced it), a keyframe with no reduced-motion guard, and an animating component with no top-level motion: note in its doc. It reads lib recipes alongside components as check:overlays does, so Header's motion is found in @/lib/chrome-control where it actually lives rather than reported as absent. 27 doc files gain a motion: note describing what moves, what drives it and what reduced motion does to it; Sheet's and ImageUpload's existing notes are PROMOTED out of a11y to the top level, where Button already had its, because motion is a description of what a component does rather than solely an accessibility concern and a field meaning one thing at two depths stops being findable. ImageUpload's note is corrected while being promoted: it credited the token layer with stopping its spinner, and what actually stops it is the motion-safe: variant. Two findings are recorded in the notes rather than fixed: Sidebar's collapsible section snaps via the hidden attribute where Accordion animates the identical interaction against Base UI's published height, and Banner reaches for transition-colors where the rest of the library enumerates properties. No component's rendered motion changes; no .tsx is touched.

migration.manual: Documentation only — every change is inside a *.doc.ts, and no component's classes or rendered motion moved. If you consume the doc files and read `a11y.motion`, it has moved to the top-level `motion` key on Sheet and ImageUpload; Button was already there and the other 27 are new.

changes.summary: Input and Textarea gain `surface: "page" | "chrome"`, and the field fill becomes a GROUND x STATE matrix (ADR 0017). A review flagged the editor inspector for drawing its fields on `bg-sunken` — the value a DISABLED field is filled with. The reading was half right: the drawing was correct and the library was incomplete. Those fields sit on a `bg-elevated` panel, not on the page, and a field is a well cut from whatever contains it, so the same fill means different things on different floors. `resolve.ts` already said so — the comment above `--ui-bg-field` reads 'a field is RECESSED from whatever contains it' — while the derivation reads the page, so the role only held when the page was the container and there was no name for the other case. Four roles now: `--ui-bg-field` / `--ui-bg-field-disabled` on the page, `--ui-bg-field-chrome` / `--ui-bg-field-chrome-disabled` on chrome. `--ui-bg-field-disabled` and `--ui-bg-field-chrome` resolve to the SAME VALUE in theme zero and that is the finding rather than a slip: neutral-90 under a white page reads as unavailable, the identical neutral-90 inside a neutral-95 inspector reads as a well you can type into. So the assertion is not that the four differ — it is that each PAIR separates on its own ground, in both schemes across every stress seed, plus the chrome field reading as a well against the panel. The mechanism of the original collision was a state pointing at a surface role (`isDisabled && "bg-sunken"`); both components now take the enabled and disabled fills TOGETHER from one map, so they cannot be picked apart. The ground is a prop rather than inference because a panel knows it is a panel and an input does not — and the tempting alternative, having chrome surfaces re-point `--ui-bg-field` for their subtree, breaks on exactly the components that need it most, since a Popover, Menu or Select panel is portalled to document.body and inherits nothing. Every value is floored by measurement rather than authored as a step, so a brand whose surfaces sit close together cannot collapse a pair. Light is unchanged; two dark baselines moved, and the dark disabled fill now separates from its field at 1.237 where it used to manage 1.127.

migration.manual: Nothing to change at a call site: `surface` defaults to "page" and every light value is byte-identical. Pass surface="chrome" for a field inside an inspector, island, drawer or bottom sheet — anything floored with bg-elevated — and both its enabled and disabled fills move together. In dark, a DISABLED field's fill changes from #282522 to #2F2C29; if you pinned that value in a test or an override, it moves. Two dark visual baselines were regenerated. Select, Multiselect and Combobox still fill from bg-field directly and want the same prop.

changes.summary: The 'Component --- Text Area' sheet reconciled with the code, so the two now agree on every value the component renders. Token flow stays repo -> Paper: where the sheet and the code disagreed, the code's value was the one drawn. Four changes. (1) The focused row's value carried a raw 14px while the two rows above bound the same value to var(--ui-text-body-md); rebound to the token. They resolve to the same number today, so nothing looked wrong and nothing would have until a brand seed moved the base size and one of three rows stayed behind. (2) Line-height was a raw 18px on 14px type -- 1.286, off the --ui-leading-* scale entirely (tight 1.25, snug 1.3). All three field texts are now bound to var(--ui-leading-snug), the role the component ships; it is 0.2px per line larger and lands the 6-row lg box on the sheet's own 128px. (3) The typed value was --ui-text-secondary; Input ships --ui-text-primary and a form holding both must not show two inks for the same thing, so the sheet now carries --ui-text-primary. (4) Two sections ADDED, for states the sheet had never drawn and a scale it had never shown: 'Text Area Sizes' (lg/md/sm at their real 128/113/105 boxes, each captioned with its type, inset and height) and 'Text Area States' (hover = border-subtle -> border-default, error = the --ui-intent-danger-fg edge with its caption, disabled = bg-sunken with text-disabled ink and no grip; focus was already drawn). The artboard is now height: fit-content rather than a guessed fixed height. Nothing in the sheet is now derived-but-undrawn, which is why textarea.doc.ts's needsDesign is down to one entry -- the character counter, which is a live-region design question rather than a value.

migration.manual: No code change -- the code was the source. The sheet now resolves its type through tokens, so a brand seed that moves the base size or the leading moves every row together, and the sizes and states a reader needs are on the sheet rather than in a doc's derivation list.

changes.summary: Added Textarea, the multi-line field, from the approved 'Component --- Text Area' sheet. It is a separate component rather than a prop on Input because the two differ on the keyboard (Enter submits an Input and inserts a newline here) and on how height is expressed (rows, not a size step) -- one component would have to branch on both. What it DOES share is the control surface: rounded-md, border-[1.5px] border-edge-subtle, bg-field, the inset and type of the matching size, the focus-within border+ring with its forced-colors outline fallback, and the derived hover/invalid/disabled states, all identical to Input. That claim is asserted as a RELATIONSHIP in the browser test -- it mounts a real Input at the SAME SIZE beside the Textarea and compares computed radius, border width, border colour, fill, inset and type size -- rather than as numbers, which would pass while the two drifted apart. Sizes lg/md/sm are DERIVED from Input's table rather than drawn: inset and type step exactly as Input's do (px-md py-sm / p-sm / px-sm py-xs, 14/12/12px), while the height cannot carry over, because Input's is a constant and this one is `rows` line boxes -- the same rows gives 127.125 / 111.5625 / 103.5625px, measured. The three are asserted to differ from each other and to be monotonic, which is the assertion Badge lacked when its two sizes shipped pixel-identical. Leading is leading-snug at every size: the sheet stored a raw 18px on 14px type, a ratio of 1.286 off the --ui-leading-* scale entirely, and snug is the nearest role at 0.2px per line -- it also lands the 6-row lg box on the sheet's own 128px. One deliberate divergence from Input, documented in the doc's forwarding block: the inset padding sits on the <textarea> rather than on the control wrapper. The native resize grip is painted at the textarea's own corner and the drag sets an inline height on it, so padding on the wrapper would float the grip 12px inside the box and clip the drag instead of growing with it; the inset a user sees is identical, and clicking it now lands on the field rather than on dead wrapper padding. `cols` is OMITTED from the props type rather than forwarded: the control is w-full, so a character count never reaches layout -- measured, cols={5} rendered at the same 412px as no cols at all -- and a prop that is accepted, set as an attribute and inert reads as supported. isResizable (default true) is vertical-only, since a field draggable wider breaks the layout containing it, and is withdrawn along with the field when isDisabled. Label, helperText, errorText, isRequired, isInvalid and the aria-invalid/aria-describedby wiring are Input's contract unchanged, error announced before helper.

migration.manual: Nothing to migrate -- this is a new item. A multi-line field previously had to be hand-rolled or an Input stretched with className, both of which lost the label/error wiring; replace those with <Textarea label="..." rows={n} />. `size` matches Input's, so a form already using size="md" fields gets a matching textarea. `cols` is a TYPE ERROR rather than a no-op: size the field with className on the outermost node.

items.lead: Shows a small image with room to identify or remove it.

docs.name: Thumbnail
docs.summary: A 48px attachment tile with an optional remove control on its corner. Thumbnail.Group lays several out as a spaced row or as an overlapping stack that spreads back out on hover, with an overflow counter. Called 'Image Thumbnail' on the sheet.

anatomy.notes: The outermost node. Owns the 48px box, className and the ref, and is the positioning context for the remove control. It does NOT clip, and it is the hover group the control listens to.
The clipped tile: well, radius and the 1.5px inset hairline. Everything that takes the radius lives inside it.
A real , so alt text exists and a broken URL degrades to it. Absent while isLoading.
role=status, named after the file. Replaces the picture rather than sitting over it.
CSS, not an icon — griddy has no spinner glyph and check:icons forbids a private SVG. Stops under prefers-reduced-motion at the token layer.
A real button on the corner. 16px of paint, 24px of target (a pseudo-element), revealed on hover AND on focus. A sibling of the frame, not a child, because the frame clips.
The row or the stack. Spacing comes from the container rather than from rewriting children.
The '+N' tile. Deliberately the same tile as a thumbnail with no picture.

docs.composition:
Thumbnail
├─ src           string (required)
├─ isLoading?    boolean — spinner on the well, picture withheld
├─ alt           string (required) — what the attachment is
├─ onRemove?     () => void
└─ removeLabel   string — REQUIRED whenever onRemove is set

Thumbnail.Group
├─ children      Thumbnail elements, as direct siblings
├─ isStacked?    boolean — overlap instead of space; spreads on hover/focus
├─ max?          number — show this many, the rest become "+N"
└─ overflowLabel string — REQUIRED whenever max is set

src.notes: The picture. A real , so a broken URL degrades to the alt text rather than to an empty square.

isLoading.notes: The picture is still arriving: the tile shows a centred spinner on the well and the is not rendered at all, because one arriving under a spinner reads as a broken one. A prop rather than something inferred from src — an image that has not loaded yet and one whose URL is wrong are indistinguishable from inside the component, and only the caller knows which it has. It is announced as role=status named after the file, so a row of five loading tiles is five different things rather than five 'Loading's.

alt.notes: What the attachment is. Pass an empty string only when a sibling label already names it — a row of thumbnails with no names is a row of identical grey squares to anyone not looking at it.

onRemove.notes: Renders the remove control. Omit it and no control exists at all — a cross that does nothing is worse than no cross.

removeLabel.notes: REQUIRED by the type whenever onRemove is set, the same shape isIconOnly uses for aria-label. A cross with no accessible name announces as 'button', and five of them announce as five buttons called 'button'. Name the thing: 'Remove Brand guidelines.pdf'.

isStacked.notes: Thumbnail.Group only. Overlaps the tiles by 4px instead of spacing them. The two answer different questions — a spaced row is a gallery, a stack is 'there are attachments here'. A stack SPREADS to the spaced layout on hover and on focus-within, which is what keeps it usable: an overlapped tile's remove control is underneath its neighbour.

max.notes: Thumbnail.Group only. How many to show before the rest become a '+N' tile. Counts DIRECT children, so a component that returns three thumbnails counts as one — pass them as siblings.

overflowLabel.notes: Thumbnail.Group only, REQUIRED whenever max is set. A prop rather than a derived string — there is no i18n runtime here (§9) and pluralisation is not guessable.

do: Name the attachment in alt, and name it again in removeLabel — they are read in different places.
Use isStacked when the point is 'there are attachments', and the spaced row when the point is the pictures themselves.
Pass Thumbnail children to Thumbnail.Group as direct siblings.
Reach for AspectRatio instead when the media is content rather than an attachment; a Thumbnail is a 48px chip with a remove control.
dont: Do not render the remove control conditionally on hover — it is opacity, not mounting, precisely so it stays in the tab order and focus is never lost.
Do not shrink the tile below 48px; the remove control's 24px target is already the whole top-right quadrant.
Do not wrap Thumbnail.Group's children to space them — the spacing comes from the container so slot contents are never rewritten (§3).
Do not put anything inside the frame that must escape the radius; the frame clips, which is why the remove control is a sibling.

a11y.role: The tile is a plain span; the remove control is a real <button>.
a11y.name: The picture carries the alt text. The remove control carries removeLabel, which the type requires — a cross alone announces as 'button'.

keyboard.does: Moves to the remove control. It is in the tab order whether or not it is visible, and becomes visible when it takes focus.
Activates the remove control. Native button behaviour — nothing here re-implements it.

a11y.targetSize: The remove control paints 16x16 and targets 24x24 via a pseudo-element (16 + 4 on each side), which is SC 2.5.8's floor exactly. The sheet draws the 16px box only.
a11y.focus: The sheet draws the control on hover alone, which leaves a keyboard user tabbing to something invisible (SC 2.4.7). It is revealed on focus-visible as well. Had it been conditionally rendered instead, it could not have been reached at all (SC 2.1.1).

contrastPairs.role: the remove glyph on its own tile — a graphical object that is the control's only visual channel

contrastPairs.why: The 1.5px inset hairline, and the well behind the picture — the sheet draws both in the same role. Measured 1.22:1 light / 1.50:1 dark against the page (on the 2026-11-03 warm-ink ramp sunken is a fill above the page in dark, not a recess). It is not a boundary anything depends on identifying: the picture itself is what makes a thumbnail visible, and the ring's job is stopping a photograph's own white edge from bleeding into the page. It is in needsDesign, because in a STACKED group the same value means there is no seam between neighbours.

forwarding.ref: Goes to the outermost node — Thumbnail is not a form control, so the §5 default applies. The remove button is reachable through data-slot.
forwarding.className: Lands on the outermost node, so sizing or positioning a thumbnail works. The clipped tile is data-slot="thumbnail-frame".
forwarding.rest: Native span props go to the outermost node.

needsDesign: The remove control is drawn 16x16, under SC 2.5.8's 24px floor. Shipped with a 24px pseudo-element target and the 16px paint unchanged. Confirm — or draw it at 24 and the arithmetic disappears.
The remove control is drawn on hover only. A keyboard user tabs to something invisible (SC 2.4.7). Shipped revealed on focus-visible as well as hover. No focus treatment is drawn for it at all.

The hairline and the well are the SAME role (--ui-bg-sunken), so in a stacked group two overlapping tiles have no seam between them — the ring is invisible against its neighbour's fill. Avatar solves the identical problem with an --ui-bg-surface ring. Confirm which, for both components.

The overflow counter is not drawn for thumbnails at all; it is Avatar.Group's, borrowed, because a stack of attachments truncates for the same reason a stack of people does. Confirm the '+N' tile, its ink and its type role.

The stacked row's hover spreads to TOUCHING rather than to the sheet's +4px gap — half the travel, and eased out over --ui-duration-slow rather than the standard curve, because at 200ms a stack of four read as a snap rather than an unfolding. A zero gap is all the interaction needs: what the overlap hides is the next tile's top-right corner, which is exactly where the remove control sits. Confirm the shorter travel.
No loading state is drawn. Shipped as a centred CSS spinner on the well, with the picture withheld until it is ready.

The stacked row's z-order. The sheet's drawing suggests the FIRST tile sits on top; DOM order paints the last one on top, and reproducing the sheet would mean cloning children to assign z-index, which §3 rules out. Same gap Avatar.Group records.
No hover state is drawn for the tile itself, only for the group and the control. A thumbnail is very often a link to the full asset.
No loading or broken-image state is drawn; a slow attachment shows the bare well.
knownGaps: Thumbnail.Group counts DIRECT children. `{cond && <Thumbnail/>}` is handled (Children.toArray drops it), but a component that returns several thumbnails counts as one and `max` will not see through it.

The stack spreads on hover of the GROUP, so on a touch device — where there is no hover — an overlapped tile's remove control stays under its neighbour. focus-within covers the keyboard path; touch has none.
The '+N' tile is not itself removable and has no press behaviour. It is a counter, not a control.

outline-width AND outline-offset both snap to whole device pixels, so the 1.5px hairline computes to 1px inset 1px at dPR 1 and is exact at dPR 2. Pinned in border-hairline.browser.test.tsx rather than re-investigated.
docs.motion: Three, and they are unusually varied for one component. The image fades in on `opacity` at --ui-duration-fast. The busy spinner is a CSS keyframe under `motion-safe:`, and that variant — not the token layer — is what stops it under prefers-reduced-motion, because `animate-spin` carries its own timing. A stacked group animates `margin-inline-start` at --ui-duration-slow with --ui-ease-out as it unfolds: slow and easing out on purpose, since at --ui-duration-base on the standard curve a stack of four read as a snap rather than a settle.

changes.summary: Three defects found by looking at the built Storybook. (1) ImageEdit drew the picture TWICE — dimmed across the stage and again inside the crop — and the two could never align: each was object-contain inside a different box (384x260 against 240x168), so they resolved to different scales and offsets, and rotating showed both quads at once. Now one image, with the crop dimming everything outside it via a box-shadow whose spread exceeds the stage; that also follows border-radius, so the circular mask gets a circular hole for free. (2) Slider's thumb overhung the track at both extremes, because Base UI centres it on the value — at the minimum half of it sat outside the track and inside the 8px gap to the stepper button. The control is now inset by half a thumb, so the thumb's OUTER edge lands on the control's edge and the track it travels is the track it paints. Reported against Image Edit; it was every slider at 0 and at 100. (3) Thumbnail gains isLoading — a centred CSS spinner on the well, with the withheld, announced as role=status named after the file. Thumbnail.Group's stacked spread now eases out over --ui-duration-slow to a ZERO gap rather than snapping to +4px on the standard curve: half the travel, and all the interaction needs, since what the overlap hides is the next tile's top-right corner where the remove control sits.

migration.manual: Slider renders slightly differently at every size: the track is inset by half a thumb (8px each side; 12px at lg), so a track measures 16-24px narrower than before and the thumb no longer overhangs. No API change. Thumbnail's `isLoading` is additive and defaults to false.

changes.summary: A 48px attachment tile with an optional remove control on its corner, plus Thumbnail.Group as a spaced row or an overlapping stack that spreads back out on hover and focus-within. Two accessibility fixes over the sheet: the control is drawn 16x16, under SC 2.5.8's 24px floor, so its target is extended to 24 with a pseudo-element while the paint stays at 16; and it is drawn hover-only, so it is now revealed on focus-visible as well — as opacity rather than mounting, keeping it in the tab order and never losing focus. removeLabel is required by the type whenever onRemove is passed, and max/overflowLabel travel together, both the same discriminated-union shape Avatar uses. The counter tile is Avatar.Group's, borrowed; the sheet draws none.

migration.manual: New item — nothing to migrate. `npx shadcn add @bydiorama/thumbnail`; it pulls in `cn` and expects react and griddy-icons as peers.

items.name: toast
items.title: Toast
items.lead: Acknowledges an action without taking over the task.

docs.lead: Acknowledges an action without taking over the task.
docs.name: Toast
docs.summary: A transient notification generated by the app, stacked bottom-right of the viewport. Built on Base UI Toast (ADR 0012): the queue, timers, stacking measurements, swipe gesture and announcement come from there; the API, anatomy and every pixel are the sheet's. Toasts collapse into a stack of three; hovering or focusing the viewport expands them.

anatomy.notes: Fixed bottom-right, inset space-xl; width dialog-width-md capped to the viewport minus space-lg each side. A landmark region — F6 jumps to it — named by the required `label` prop.

bg-elevated, a border-subtle hairline, radius-lg, shadow-lg. In dark the fill sits BELOW the page ground, so the hairline and shadow carry the boundary (ADR 0010). Height is clamped to the frontmost toast while collapsed.
The padded row: p-lg, gap-md, overflow-hidden. Hidden (data-behind) while its toast is behind the front one; cross-fades back on expand.

16px griddy glyph in a slot one title line tall (h-[1lh]), top-aligned so it centres on the first line however far the description wraps. Colour is the type's intent ink; the default type renders no icon. Loading renders Button's border-drawn spinner (slot toast-spinner).

16px bold in text-ink-primary. body-lg, NOT title-sm: the title roles are fluid (vw clamp) and a toast is a fixed 416px surface that does not follow the viewport — the browser test asserts the computed 16px.
body-sm medium in text-ink-muted — Banner's message treatment. Carries the announcement when there is no title.
Button — secondary · md, from `action: { label, onClick }`. At most one; pressing it runs onClick and then dismisses the toast.
Banner's dismiss recipe: 24px hit area (SC 2.5.8) around a 16px Close glyph at full ink strength; hover tints the ground with currentColor at 10%. Named by the Viewport's required `dismissLabel`.

docs.composition:
Toast.Provider               limit? timeout?          — once, around the app
├─ <App/>                    anywhere below: useToast().add({ title, description, type, action })
└─ Toast.Viewport            label! dismissLabel! container?
   └─ (renders the stack — per-toast anatomy is not public API)

label.notes: Required. Accessible name of the notifications landmark (the F6 target). A prop, not a default — every user-visible string is one (§9).

dismissLabel.notes: Required. Accessible name of every toast's close button.

container.notes: Where the viewport is portalled. Theme tokens are INHERITED custom properties, so a viewport in the body leaves any brand scope on a wrapper and paints theme zero — pass the themed element to bring it back inside.

limit.notes: Visible toasts before the oldest is hidden — kept mounted, inert, at opacity 0, so it can return if the stack shrinks.

timeout.notes: Default auto-dismiss in ms; 0 never auto-dismisses. Paused while the viewport is hovered or focused and while the window is blurred (Base UI behaviour).

useToast().notes: add / close / update / promise, restated so no Base UI type reaches a consumer signature (ADR 0012). promise() runs one toast through loading → success/danger. add() with an existing id updates in place and resets the clock.

type.notes: Omit for the plain, glyph-less toast. The glyph is the ONLY thing intent changes — the surface never tints, so a stack of mixed types does not read as a traffic light. `danger` is this library's name (shared with Banner/Button); Base UI's promise() stamps `error`, which renders identically.

action.notes: Rendered as Button secondary · md through Base UI's actionProps, so screen readers hear it with the announcement. Runs onClick, then dismisses — an action that should keep the toast open belongs on a surface with room for it.

priority.notes: low announces politely; high assertively — reserve it for danger. Only the title and description strings are announced, so keep both plain text.

do: Mount one Provider + Viewport at the app root and fire everything through useToast() — twelve call sites want exactly this shape.
Give the description the detail and keep the title to a few words; the description carries the announcement when there is no title.
Use promise() for async work — one toast updates through loading → success/danger instead of three stacking up.
Pass the themed element as `container` when the app wraps a brand scope around part of the page.
dont: Do not use a toast for a message that must be acknowledged — that is a Modal; or for one attached to a surface — that is a Banner.
Do not set priority high for routine confirmations; an assertive announcement interrupts whatever the reader was in the middle of.
Do not put a second action in a toast. One action plus Close is the whole vocabulary; more is a dialog.
Do not import Base UI's Toast directly for custom internals — compose a request to design instead (the per-toast anatomy is deliberately not public API).

a11y.role: The viewport is a landmark region (Base UI), named by `label`; each toast announces via the manager's live region.
a11y.name: Viewport: `label` (required). Close buttons: `dismissLabel` (required). Both required at the type level because an unnamed landmark and a nameless icon button are the two failures nothing visual ever catches.

keyboard.does: Moves focus into the toast viewport; the stack expands and timers pause while focus is inside.
Walks the focused toast's controls — action, then close.
Activates the focused control — native, both are real buttons.
Closes the focused toast (Base UI behaviour; asserted in Chromium — F6, Tab into the toast, Escape, gone).

contrastPairs.role: the title — 15.53:1 light / 13.90:1 dark
the description, the Close glyph and the loading spinner — 5.36:1 light / 5.68:1 dark
the info glyph — 5.39:1 light / 9.82:1 dark; the glyph is the only channel carrying the type (SC 1.4.11)
the success glyph — 5.62:1 light / 9.91:1 dark
the warning glyph — 5.48:1 light / 8.67:1 dark
the danger glyph — 5.38:1 light / 6.98:1 dark
the toast against the page
contrastPairs.why: the boundary is the border-subtle hairline plus shadow-lg, not the fill (ADR 0010); in dark the fill sits below the page ground and the hairline is a 14%-alpha light line

a11y.dismissal: Timeout (paused on hover/focus/window blur), the Close button, Escape from within, or a swipe down/right. Toasts over the limit are hidden but stay mounted and inert rather than being destroyed under a screen reader.

forwarding.Toast.Viewport: className and remaining div props land on the viewport element (the outermost node this component owns). label → aria-label; dismissLabel is threaded to every toast's close button. No refs are exposed — there is no stable per-toast node to hold one on.

docs.motion: Enter from translateY(150%) + fade; exit reverses toward the bottom edge, or along the swipe axis after a swipe. Transforms run duration-enter with ease-spring (the sheet's motion-choreographed pair), opacity on duration-slow, the stack's height settle on duration-fast — written as longhand transition properties because the split cannot be expressed in one shorthand. Behind-content cross-fades on duration-base. The loading spinner is animate-spin with the motion-reduce guard; every transition collapses under prefers-reduced-motion at the token layer.
needsDesign: Anchored toasts (Base UI's Toast.Positioner — transient 'Copied' chips on a trigger) are out of scope for the sheet and this component; they need their own design pass if a consumer asks.
A shared Spinner primitive: loading reuses Button's private border-drawn spinner recipe for the third time. Three copies is the chrome-control story again.
knownGaps: The toast width reuses --ui-dialog-width-md (416px) — recorded as a Conflict on the sheet: if Toast should ever size independently of Modal, a --ui-toast-width token must be minted first.
No global manager outside React (Base UI's createToastManager). All twelve measured call sites fire from components; add the wrapper when one does not.

Exit-while-expanded uses the collapsed exit transform (the Base UI demo duplicates every ending transform under data-expanded; this component does not) — visible only when a toast times out at the exact moment the pointer is over the stack.
swipeDirection is fixed to Base UI's default (down, right), matching the bottom-right placement; a viewport placement prop would need the sheet's Custom position pass first.

the description, the Close glyph and the loading spinner — 5.36:1 light / 5.68:1 dark
the info glyph — 5.39:1 light / 9.82:1 dark; the glyph is the only channel carrying the type (SC 1.4.11)
the success glyph — 5.62:1 light / 9.91:1 dark
the warning glyph — 5.48:1 light / 8.67:1 dark
the danger glyph — 5.38:1 light / 6.98:1 dark
